现译: 于是小鸟去摆桌子，老鼠来做菜。她也想照香肠的办法，在菜里滚几滚，好让菜里有油有盐，便纵身跳进锅里。可还远没碰到锅底，她就再也动不了了。丢了皮，丢了毛，连命也丢了。
修改判断: 保留烫死的结局和原文冷冷的三个落点，使灾祸仍由前面的分工发展出来。

中文章名: 老鼠、小鸟和香肠
英文证据: In his alarm and flurry
原译: 目前鸟儿进来想送饭但他看不到厨师。在他的警报器和风笛里他把木头扔到这地板上打电话搜查但找不到厨师。然后，一些被粗心地扔下来的木材被烧了，开始燃烧。这只鸟急着取水，但他的水桶掉进井里，然后他又钻了下去，由于自己无法恢复，他淹死了。
现译: 过了一会儿，小鸟进来要端饭，却哪儿也见不着掌勺的伙伴。他慌了手脚，四下里又喊又找，把柴火丢得满地都是，还是找不着。几根随手扔下的柴着了火，火苗蹿了起来。小鸟赶忙去打水。水桶掉进井里，他也跟着掉了下去，没能再上来，就这样淹死了。
修改判断: 清除“警报器和风笛”等错译。结尾原样收在小鸟溺死处。

中文章名: 霍勒婆婆
英文证据: Once upon a time there was a widow who had two daughters; one of them was beautiful and industrious, the other ugly and lazy. The mother, however, loved the ugly and lazy one best, because she was her own daughter, and so the other, who was only her stepdaughter, was made to do all the work of the house, and was quite the Cinderella of the family. Her stepmother sent her out every day to sit by the well in the high road, there to spin until she made her fingers bleed. Now it chanced one day that some blood fell on to the spindle, and as the girl stopped over the well to wash it off, the spindle suddenly sprang out of her hand and fell into the well. She ran home crying to tell of her misfortune, but her stepmother spoke harshly to her, and after giving her a violent scolding, said unkindly, ‘As you have let the spindle fall into the well you may go yourself and fetch it out.’
原译: 从前，有一个寡妇有两个女儿，其中一人漂亮，勤劳，另一人丑陋，懒惰。但是，母亲最喜欢丑陋懒惰的，因为她是她自己的女儿，所以另一个，只是她的继女，被迫做房子的所有工作，而且相当是家庭灰姑娘。她的继母每天都把她送出去坐在水井旁高高的路上，在那里旋转直到她使她的手指出血。有一天，有些血流到脊椎上，当女孩停下来洗井的时候，脊椎突然从她的手中冒出来，掉进井里。她哭着跑回家说她的不幸，但她的继母对她说粗鲁的话，在对她大吼大叫之后，她又说：'你让脊椎掉进井里，你就可以自己去取出来。'，爱丽丝
现译: 从前有一位寡妇，有两个女儿，一个漂亮又勤快，一个既丑又懒。母亲偏疼那个又丑又懒的，因为那是她亲生的。另一个只是继女，全家上下的活儿都压在她身上，她活脱脱是这家里的灰姑娘。继母天天打发她去大路边的井沿上纺线，一直纺到手指出血。有一天，血滴在纺锤上，她俯到井边想把血洗掉，纺锤忽然从手里一滑，掉进井里。她哭着回家，把这桩倒霉事说给继母听。继母劈头盖脸骂了她一通，又恶狠狠地说：“既然是你让纺锤掉进井里的，你就自己去捞上来。”

Then she carefully gathered the apples together in a heap and walked on again.

中文章名: 霍勒婆婆
英文证据: The next thing she came to was a little house, and there she saw an old woman looking out, with such large teeth, that she was terrified, and turned to run away. But the old woman called after her, ‘What are you afraid of, dear child? Stay with me; if you will do the work of my house properly for me, I will make you very happy. You must be very careful, however, to make my bed in the right way, for I wish you always to shake it thoroughly, so that the feathers fly about; then they say, down there in the world, that it is snowing; for I am Mother Holle.’ The old woman spoke so kindly, that the girl summoned up courage and agreed to enter into her service.
原译: 然后她来到一个小房子，在那里，她看到一个老女人看着外面，这么大的牙齿，她害怕，转身逃跑。但那个老妇人对她说：你怕什么，孩子？你留在我身边吧！如果你为我做好我的房子的工作，我一定使你快乐。你必须非常小心，使我的床用正确的方式铺好，因为我希望你始终摇动它，使羽毛飞扬；然后他们说：这是下雪的，因为我是霍尔尔母亲。那个老妇人说得那么好以至于那个女孩鼓起勇气同意加入她的行列。
现译: 接着她来到一所小房子前。一个老婆婆正往外张望，牙齿大得吓人，姑娘转身便想跑。老婆婆在后面叫她：“好孩子，你怕什么？留下来陪我吧。只要你把我屋里的活儿好好做完，我包你过得快活。有一样可要格外留心，就是给我铺床。每回都得把铺盖用力抖一抖，抖得羽毛四下里飞，下面人间就会说，下雪啦。因为我就是霍勒婆婆。”老婆婆说得这样和气，姑娘壮起胆子，答应留下来帮佣。

英文证据: So she stayed on with Mother Holle for some time, and then she began to grow unhappy. She could not at first tell why she felt sad, but she became conscious at last of great longing to go home; then she knew she was homesick, although she was a thousand times better off with Mother Holle than with her mother and sister. 原译: 所以她和霍勒妈妈在一起一段时间然后她开始不开心了。她一开始不能说明为什么她感到悲伤，但最后她意识到她非常渴望回家；然后她知道自己想家，尽管她与霍勒母亲在一起比与母亲和妹妹在一起要好上千倍。等待了一段时间之后，她去了霍勒母亲那里，说，“我好想家，我不能再跟你住在一起了，因为虽然我在这里很开心，但我必须回到自己的人民身边。'，爱丽丝

修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 大拇指汤姆
英文证据: One day, as the woodman was getting ready to go into the wood to cut fuel, he said, ‘I wish I had someone to bring the cart after me, for I want to make haste.’ ‘Oh, father,’ cried Tom, ‘I will take care of that; the cart shall be in the wood by the time you want it.’ Then the woodman laughed, and said, ‘How can that be? you cannot reach up to the horse’s bridle.’ ‘Never mind that, father,’ said Tom; ‘if my mother will only harness the horse, I will get into his ear and tell him which way to go.’ ‘Well,’ said the father, ‘we will try for once.’

中文章名: 大拇指汤姆
英文证据: When the time came the mother harnessed the horse to the cart, and put Tom into his ear; and as he sat there the little man told the beast how to go, crying out, ‘Go on!’ and ‘Stop!’ as he wanted: and thus the horse went on just as well as if the woodman had driven it himself into the wood. It happened that as the horse was going a little too fast, and Tom was calling out, ‘Gently! gently!’ two strangers came up. ‘What an odd thing that is!’ said one: ‘there is a cart going along, and I hear a carter talking to the horse, but yet I can see no one.’ ‘That is queer, indeed,’ said the other; ‘let us follow the cart, and see where it goes.’ So they went on into the wood, till at last they came to the place where the woodman was. Then Tom Thumb, seeing his father, cried out, ‘See, father, here I am with the cart, all right and safe! now take me down!’ So his father took hold of the horse with one hand, and with the other took his son out of the horse’s ear, and put him down upon a straw, where he sat as merry as you please.
原译: 当时间到来时，母亲把马扶到马车上，把汤姆放在他的耳朵上；当他坐在那的时候，那个小个子告诉野兽怎么走，喊着说：你走吧！你快住手！”他想骑马就骑马，就像木匠自己把马开进木头一样。当马走得太快时汤姆喊道：“温柔点！” 两个陌生人来了。他说：这真是怪事！有人说：有人开车去，我听到有一只木匠对马说话，我却看不见任何人。他说：这确是奇事。我们跟着车走，看看它往哪去。于是他们进入了木头，直到他们终于来到了木工所在的地方。汤姆·拇指，看见他的父亲，就喊道：我的父亲啊！我拿着推车来了，你把我拉下去吧！他父亲用一只手抓住了马，另一只手把他的儿子从马的耳朵里挖出来，把他放在稻草上，他在那里坐着，你高兴也高兴。
现译: 到时候，母亲把马套上车，把汤姆放进马耳朵。小人儿坐在里头，要走就喊一声“驾”，要停就喊一声“吁”。马车往林子里走，跟樵夫自己赶得一样好。有一阵马走快了些，汤姆正喊“慢点！慢点！”恰巧两个外乡人走来。“怪事！”一个说，“有辆车往前走，我明明听见车夫吆喝马，可怎么一个人影都看不见？”“真怪，”另一个说，“咱们跟着，看这车去哪儿。”他们一路跟进林子，终于来到了樵夫干活的地方。大拇指汤姆看见父亲，喊道：“爸爸瞧，我把车赶来了，人和车都平安！快抱我下来吧。”父亲一手牵住马，一手从马耳朵里捧出儿子，把他放在一根干草上。小汤姆坐在那儿，要多快活有多快活。

中文章名: 大拇指汤姆
英文证据: The two strangers were all this time looking on, and did not know what to say for wonder. At last one took the other aside, and said, ‘That little urchin will make our fortune, if we can get him, and carry him about from town to town as a show; we must buy him.’ So they went up to the woodman, and asked him what he would take for the little man. ‘He will be better off,’ said they, ‘with us than with you.’ ‘I won’t sell him at all,’ said the father; ‘my own flesh and blood is dearer to me than all the silver and gold in the world.’ But Tom, hearing of the bargain they wanted to make, crept up his father’s coat to his shoulder and whispered in his ear, ‘Take the money, father, and let them have me; I’ll soon come back to you.’
原译: 两位陌生人一直盯着我看不知该说些什么。终于有一个人把另一个人拉到一边，他说：如果我们抓住他，那个小厄尔钦将使我们发财，他将带着他从一个城市到另一个城市，我们必定要买他。于是他们去见那个伐木工问他他会拿什么给那个小家伙。他们说：他将享受更好的待遇。他说：他与我们在一起，胜过与你在一起。他的父亲说：我绝不出卖他。我的血肉，比全世界的银子和金子，还可爱。但是汤姆，听到他们想做的交易，爬到他父亲的外套肩膀上，对他耳边低语，“拿起钱，父亲，让他们拥有我，我很快会回到你身边。”

中文章名: 大拇指汤姆
英文证据: They journeyed on till it began to be dusky, and then the little man said, ‘Let me get down, I’m tired.’ So the man took off his hat, and put him down on a clod of earth, in a ploughed field by the side of the road. 中文章名: 大拇指汤姆
英文证据: Just as he was falling asleep, he heard two men passing by, chatting together; and one said to the other, ‘How can we rob that rich parson’s house of his silver and gold?’ ‘I’ll tell you!’ cried Tom. ‘What noise was that?’ said the thief, frightened; ‘I’m sure I heard someone speak.’ They stood still listening, and Tom said, ‘Take me with you, and I’ll soon show you how to get the parson’s money.’ ‘But where are you?’ said they. ‘Look about on the ground,’ answered he, ‘and listen where the sound comes from.’ At last the thieves found him out, and lifted him up in their hands. ‘You little urchin!’ they said, ‘what can you do for us?’ ‘Why, I can get between the iron window-bars of the parson’s house, and throw you out whatever you want.’ ‘That’s a good thought,’ said the thieves; ‘come along, we shall see what you can do.’

Meantime the thieves were frightened, and ran off a little way; but at last they plucked up their hearts, and said, ‘The little urchin is only trying to make fools of us.’ So they came back and whispered softly to him, saying, ‘Now let us have no more of your roguish jokes; but throw us out some of the money.’ Then Tom called out as loud as he could, ‘Very well! hold your hands! here it comes.’

中文章名: 大拇指汤姆

But alas! how woefully he was undone! what crosses and sorrows happen to us all in this world! The cook got up early, before daybreak, to feed the cows; and going straight to the hay-loft, carried away a large bundle of hay, with the little man in the middle of it, fast asleep. He still, however, slept on, and did not awake till he found himself in the mouth of the cow; for the cook had put the hay into the cow’s rick, and the cow had taken Tom up in a mouthful of it. ‘Good lack-a-day!’ said he, ‘how came I to tumble into the mill?’ But he soon found out where he really was; and was forced to have all his wits about him, that he might not get between the cow’s teeth, and so be crushed to death. At last down he went into her stomach. ‘It is rather dark,’ said he; ‘they forgot to build windows in this room to let the sun in; a candle would be no bad thing.’
原译: 这小个子爬到干草洞里终于找到一个地方来完成他晚上的休息他躺下意思是睡到天亮然后回到父亲和母亲身边。哀哉！他确已失败了。在今世，我们所有人都遭遇过什么苦难呢？厨师在黎明前早起来喂奶牛直接到干草洞带走一大堆干草中间那个小个子睡得很快。然而，他仍然睡着，直到他发现自己在牛的嘴里；因为厨师把干草放在牛的车厢里，牛把汤姆放在嘴里。他说：我怎么跌倒在磨坊里呢？但是他很快发现他的真实身份，并被迫拥有他所有的智慧，他可能不会得到牛的牙齿之间，所以被压死。终于下到她的肚子里。他说：天黑了。他们忘记在这间屋子里盖窗户，让太阳进来；蜡烛不是一件坏事。
现译: 小人儿在干草楼上爬了一阵，终于找到一处舒服地方，可以接着睡下半夜。他躺下来，打算一觉睡到天亮，然后找路回家见爹娘。唉，他的好打算落了空，多么可怜！我们活在世上，谁能躲得开种种坎坷和烦恼！天还没亮厨娘就起床喂牛，径直上干草楼，抱走一大捆干草，小人儿在草捆中央睡得正香。他一直没醒，睁眼一看，自己已在牛嘴巴里。原来厨娘把干草放进牛的草架，牛嚼起一大口，连汤姆也卷进去了。“我的天哪！”他说，“我怎么掉进磨坊来了？”他很快弄明白自己究竟在哪儿，打起十二分精神，免得落到牛的上下牙齿之间，给活活嚼碎。终于，他滑进了牛肚子。“这儿有点黑，”他说，“他们盖这间屋子的时候忘了开窗，阳光都照不进来。要有根蜡烛倒也不错。”

英文证据: Tom soon set himself to work to get out, which was not a very easy task; but at last, just as he had made room to get his head out, fresh ill-luck befell him. A hungry wolf sprang out, and swallowed up the whole stomach, with Tom in it, at one gulp, and ran away.

中文章名: 大拇指汤姆
英文证据: Tom, however, was still not disheartened; and thinking the wolf would not dislike having some chat with him as he was going along, he called out, ‘My good friend, I can show you a famous treat.’ ‘Where’s that?’ said the wolf. ‘In such and such a house,’ said Tom, describing his own father’s house. ‘You can crawl through the drain into the kitchen and then into the pantry, and there you will find cakes, ham, beef, cold chicken, roast pig, apple-dumplings, and everything that your heart can wish.’
原译: 然而，汤姆仍然不感到沮丧；认为狼不会不喜欢和他交谈当他正在走动，他喊道，“我的好朋友，我可以给你们看一个著名的奖品。“那在哪里？”狼说。汤姆说，“在这样一个房子里，” 描述他父亲的房子。你可以爬进厨房的排水管然后爬进储藏室在那里你会发现蛋糕火腿牛肉冷鸡烤猪苹果豆还有你心愿的一切。

中文章名: 侏儒怪
英文证据: By the side of a wood, in a country a long way off, ran a fine stream of water; and upon the stream there stood a mill. The miller’s house was close by, and the miller, you must know, had a very beautiful daughter. She was, moreover, very shrewd and clever; and the miller was so proud of her, that he one day told the king of the land, who used to come and hunt in the wood, that his daughter could spin gold out of straw. Now this king was very fond of money; and when he heard the miller’s boast his greediness was raised, and he sent for the girl to be brought before him. Then he led her to a chamber in his palace where there was a great heap of straw, and gave her a spinning-wheel, and said, ‘All this must be spun into gold before morning, as you love your life.’ It was in vain that the poor maiden said that it was only a silly boast of her father, for that she could do no such thing as spin straw into gold: the chamber door was locked, and she was left alone.

The fowls began to turn brown, and were nearly ready, but the guest had not yet arrived. Then Gretel called out to her master: ‘If the guest does not come, I must take the fowls away from the fire, but it will be a sin and a shame if they are not eaten the moment they are at their juiciest.’ The master said: ‘I will run myself, and fetch the guest.’ When the master had turned his back, Gretel laid the spit with the fowls on one side, and thought: ‘Standing so long by the fire there, makes one sweat and thirsty; who knows when they will come? 现译: 有一天，主人吩咐她：“格蕾特尔，今晚来客人。给我好好做两只鸡，越鲜美越好。”“交给我，老爷。”格蕾特尔答道。她杀了两只鸡，烫过，拔净毛，穿到烤叉上。快傍晚了，她把它们架到火前烤。鸡皮渐渐焦黄，都快好了，可客人还没到。格蕾特尔便喊主人：“客人再不来，我可得把鸡从火前撤下了。鸡最多汁的时候居然没人吃，那真是造孽，太可惜啦！”主人说：“我亲自跑一趟，把客人请来。”主人一转身，格蕾特尔就把叉着鸡的烤叉搁到一旁，心想：“在火前站了这么久，汗也出来了，嘴也渴了。谁知道他们什么时候回来？趁这工夫，我去地窖喝一口吧。”她跑下楼，举起酒壶，说：“格蕾特尔，愿上帝赐福给你这口酒！”痛痛快快喝了一大口。又想，好好的酒流起来就得让它流到底，哪里好中途截断呢？便又结结实实喝了一大口。

But as the roast meat smelt so good, Gretel thought: ‘Something might be wrong, it ought to be tasted!’ She touched it with her finger, and said: ‘Ah! how good fowls are! It certainly is a sin and a shame that they are not eaten at the right time!’ She ran to the window, to see if the master was not coming with his guest, but she saw no one, and went back to the fowls and thought: ‘One of the wings is burning! I had better take it off and eat it.’ So she cut it off, ate it, and enjoyed it, and when she had done, she thought: ‘The other must go down too, or else master will observe that something is missing.’ When the two wings were eaten, she went and looked for her master, and did not see him. It suddenly occurred to her: ‘Who knows? They are perhaps not coming at all, and have turned in somewhere.’ Then she said: ‘Well, Gretel, enjoy yourself, one fowl has been cut into, take another drink, and eat it up entirely; when it is eaten you will have some peace, why should God’s good gifts be spoilt?’ So she ran into the cellar again, took an enormous drink and ate up the one chicken in great glee. When one of the chickens was swallowed down, and still her master did not come, Gretel looked at the other and said: ‘What one is, the other should be likewise, the two go together; what’s right for the one is right for the other; I think if I were to take another draught it would do me no harm.’ So she took another hearty drink, and let the second chicken follow the first.
原译: 然后她又去把鸡放火堆里压扁他们使吐口水飞快地转过来。但正像烤肉的味道一样，格莱特尔想道：“有些事可能不对劲，应该尝尝！”她用手指摸它，说：唉！鸟儿真优美！那确是罪过，也确是耻辱，因为他们在适当的时候没有被吃了。她跑到窗户边，看主人是不是和客人一起来，但她没看见任何人，回到鸡身上，想着：一只翅膀在燃烧，我最好把它摘下来吃。于是她切掉它，吃了它，享受它，当她做了它的时候，她想：“另一个必须下去，否则主人就会发现，有东西不见了。”两翼被吃掉后，她去寻找主人，没有看见他。她忽然猜想：谁知道呢？他们或许没有来，但他们已归依了。她说：格雷特尔啊！你享受吧！一只禽兽被割了，你再饮吧，你应当完全吃它。当它被吃的时候，你将享受一点宁静，为什么真主的佳美的恩典被破坏呢？于是她又跑进地窖喝了一大杯酒吃了那只鸡。当一只鸡被吞下，而她的主人却未来的时候，格雷特尔看着另一只鸡说：那只鸡是什么，另一只鸡应该一起吃；那只鸡对另一只鸡是合适的；我想如果我再吃一只，那对我是毫无害处的。所以她又喝了一杯心地饮料让第二只鸡跟着第一只。
现译: 然后她回去，把鸡重新架到火前，浇着油汁，快快活活转动烤叉。鸡肉烤得太香，格蕾特尔便想：“说不定还有哪里不对，得尝尝才知道！”她伸指头沾了沾，说：“哎呀，鸡怎么这么好吃！不趁时候吃，真是造孽，太可惜啦！”她跑去窗前，看主人是否领着客人回来了。一个人影也没见着。她又回到鸡旁边，心想：“有一只翅膀要烧焦了！最好割下来吃掉。”她割下鸡翅，美美地吃了。吃完又想：“另外那只也得进肚，不然主人一瞧就知道缺了点什么。”两只翅膀吃光，她又去望主人，还是没望见。她忽然想到：“谁说得准？兴许他们压根儿不来了，路上在哪儿坐下了呢。”于是她说：“好吧，格蕾特尔，你就好好享用吧。一只鸡既已动了刀，再喝一口酒，干脆整只吃光。吃完了心里就清静了。上帝赏的好东西，何苦让它糟蹋掉？”她又跑进地窖，咕咚喝了一大口，把那只鸡吃得高高兴兴。一只鸡都吞下去了，主人还没来。格蕾特尔瞧着另一只，说：“这一只什么样，那一只也该什么样，它们原是一对儿。对一只说得通的道理，对另一只也该说得通。依我看，再来一口酒也没什么坏处。”她又痛痛快快喝了一口，让第二只鸡陪第一只去了。

中文章名: 聪明的格蕾特尔
英文证据: While she was making the most of it, her master came and cried: ‘Hurry up, Gretel, the guest is coming directly after me!’ ‘Yes, sir, I will soon serve up,’ answered Gretel. Meantime the master looked to see that the table was properly laid, and took the great knife, wherewith he was going to carve the chickens, and sharpened it on the steps. Presently the guest came, and knocked politely and courteously at the house-door. Gretel ran, and looked to see who was there, and when she saw the guest, she put her finger to her lips and said: ‘Hush! hush! go away as quickly as you can, if my master catches you it will be the worse for you; he certainly did ask you to supper, but his intention is to cut off your two ears. Just listen how he is sharpening the knife for it!’ The guest heard the sharpening, and hurried down the steps again as fast as he could. Gretel was not idle; she ran screaming to her master, and cried: ‘You have invited a fine guest!’ ‘Why, Gretel? What do you mean by that?’ ‘Yes,’ said she, ‘he has taken the chickens which I was just going to serve up, off the dish, and has run away with them!’ ‘That’s a nice trick!’ said her master, and lamented the fine chickens. ‘If he had but left me one, so that something remained for me to eat.’ He called to him to stop, but the guest pretended not to hear. Then he ran after him with the knife still in his hand, crying: ‘Just one, just one,’ meaning that the guest should leave him just one chicken, and not take both. The guest, however, thought no otherwise than that he was to give up one of his ears, and ran as if fire were burning under him, in order to take them both with him.
原译: 当她正在充分利用它的时候，她的主人来了，她喊道：“快起来，格雷特尔，客人正直接来追我！” “是的，先生，我马上就来，格雷特尔回答说。”主人看着桌子摆好拿走了一把大刀然后他准备把鸡切了并磨磨在台阶上。目前客人来了礼貌和礼貌地敲门。格雷特尔跑去，看谁在那里，当她看见客人的时候，她把她的手指放在嘴唇上，她说：你快出去吧！如果我的主人发现你，那对你是更恶劣的。他的确请你吃晚饭，但他要割掉你的两只耳朵。你看看他怎样磨刀子吧！客人听到尖锐的声音并尽快地再次下台。格雷特尔不是无所事事，她向主人大喊大叫，她喊道：你确已邀请了一位好客人了。 格莱特尔，你什么意思？她说：他把那些我本来要喂的鸡都摘下来，然后带着他们跑了。她主人说：这是个不错的把戏。她为那些小鸡哀号。“如果他留下一个给我，留下的东西给我吃。”他叫停了，但客人假装没听到。然后他拿着刀跑来，哭着说：“只有一只，只有一只，” 意思是客人应该只留下一只鸡，而不是两只。然而，这位客人却认为，他要放弃他的一只耳朵，他跑去，好像他身下着着火，以便把他们都带走。
现译: 她正吃得兴起，主人回到家，喊道：“快点，格蕾特尔！客人就在我后头，马上就到！”“是，老爷，马上就上菜。”格蕾特尔答道。主人去看桌子摆妥没有，又拿来那把准备切鸡的大刀，在门阶上磨起来。不一会儿客人也来了，客客气气地敲门。格蕾特尔跑去一看，见是来客，立即把手指放在嘴唇上：“嘘，嘘！快走，越快越好。要是让我们老爷捉到，您可要倒霉啦。他是请您来吃晚饭不错，心里却打算把您的两只耳朵割掉。您听听，他不是正磨着刀吗？”客人果然听见磨刀声，赶紧转身，飞也似的奔下门阶。格蕾特尔可没闲着，她尖叫着跑去找主人，喊道：“您请的好客人！”“怎么啦，格蕾特尔？这话是什么意思？”“可不是，”她说，“我要端上桌的鸡，他从盘子里一把抄走，两只都带着跑了！”“好一手！”主人心疼起那两只好鸡来，“好歹留给我一只，让我也有口吃的呀！”他喊客人站住，客人装作没听见。主人手里还拿着刀，拔腿就追，口中喊着：“就一只！就一只！”他的意思是客人不该两只鸡都拿走，怎么也给他留下一只。客人听来，可只当他非要自己割一只耳朵下来。为了两只耳朵都带着走，他跑得跟脚底着了火似的。

英文证据: There was a certain village wherein no one lived but really rich peasants, and just one poor one, whom they called the little peasant. He had not even so much as a cow, and still less money to buy one, and yet he and his wife did so wish to have one. One day he said to her: ‘Listen, I have a good idea, there is our gossip the carpenter, he shall make us a wooden calf, and paint it brown, so that it looks like any other, and in time it will certainly get big and be a cow.’ the woman also liked the idea, and their gossip the carpenter cut and planed the calf, and painted it as it ought to be, and made it with its head hanging down as if it were eating.
原译: 有个村子里，除了富人之外，没人住，只有一个穷人，他们叫他们小农民。他甚至没有一头牛，更没有钱买一只，然而他和他的妻子却希望有一只。有一天，他对她说：“听着，我有个好主意，有我们关于木匠的八卦，他要把我们做成一头木牛，把它漆成棕色的，以便它看起来像任何其他的一样，然后它就会变大，变成一头牛。”这个女人也喜欢这个想法，他们的八卦是木匠剪切和计划小牛，并照应该做的画，用它的头挂在下面，好像它正在吃东西一样。
现译: 有这么一个村子，住的尽是富得流油的农民，独独一个穷，他们叫他小农夫。他连一头牛都没有，更别说拿钱买牛了，可他和妻子偏偏一心想要一头牛。有一天他对妻子说：“听着，我想出一个好主意。咱们的老相识木匠，让他给咱们做一头木头小牛，漆成褐色，跟别的小牛一个样。过些日子，它一定会长大，变成一头母牛。”妻子也觉得这个想法妙。他们的老相识木匠又削又刨，做好了小牛，漆上应有的颜色，还让它低垂着脑袋，好像正在吃草。

中文章名: 小农夫
英文证据: Next morning when the cows were being driven out, the little peasant called the cow-herd in and said: ‘Look, I have a little calf there, but it is still small and has to be carried.’ The cow-herd said: ‘All right,’ and took it in his arms and carried it to the pasture, and set it among the grass. The little calf always remained standing like one which was eating, and the cow-herd said: ‘It will soon run by itself, just look how it eats already!’ At night when he was going to drive the herd home again, he said to the calf: ‘If you can stand there and eat your fill, you can also go on your four legs; I don’t care to drag you home again in my arms.’ But the little peasant stood at his door, and waited for his little calf, and when the cow-herd drove the cows through the village, and the calf was missing, he inquired where it was. The cow-herd answered: ‘It is still standing out there eating. It would not stop and come with us.’ But the little peasant said: ‘Oh, but I must have my beast back again.’ Then they went back to the meadow together, but someone had stolen the calf, and it was gone. The cow-herd said: ‘It must have run away.’ The peasant, however, said: ‘Don’t tell me that,’ and led the cow-herd before the mayor, who for his carelessness condemned him to give the peasant a cow for the calf which had run away.
原译: 第二天早晨，牛群被赶出，那小农民叫牛群来，说：我有一个小牛，但小牛只，小牛只，须要被抬起来。牛群说：你们来吧！你们就把它抬进他的怀里，然后，把它抬到草地上，放在草地上。小牛只总是像吃牛一样站立着，牛群说：它不久就会自己跑动，你看它怎么吃。晚上，他要再次驱赶牛群回家，他对小牛说：如果你能站在那里吃东西，你也可以用四条腿走，我不想用我的怀抱把你拖回家。但是那个小农民站在他的门口，等着他的小牛，当牛牧人把牛开过村子，牛牛不见了，他问它在哪里。牛群说：它仍然站在那里吃东西，它不会停下来和我们一起来。但是那个小农民说：“哦，我必须把我的野兽还回来。”然后他们一起回到草原上但有人偷走了小牛，它不见了。牛群说：它必定是奔跑的。农民说：不要告诉我。他把牛牛领到市长面前，市长因粗心大意而责骂他，要他把母牛送给已逃之夭夭的小牛。
现译: 第二天早晨，人们往外赶牛时，小农夫把牧牛人叫进来，说：“瞧，我这儿有一头小牛，还小呢，得抱着走。”牧牛人说：“行。”他抱起小牛，带到牧场，放在草丛里。小牛始终站着，好像一直在吃草。牧牛人说：“很快就会自己跑了。瞧，它这不已经会吃草了吗！”傍晚要赶牛回家，他对小牛说：“既然你站在这里吃得那么饱，也能用四条腿走路了。我才懒得再抱你回家。”小农夫站在门口等着小牛，牛群进村，唯独没有它。他问小牛去哪儿了。牧牛人答道：“它还在那儿站着吃草，怎么也不肯停下来跟我们走。”“那可不行，”小农夫说，“我一定要把牲口领回来。”两人同去草地。小牛已经不见了，原来有人把它偷走了。牧牛人说：“它准是跑了。”“少跟我说这套。”小农夫把牧牛人领到村长面前。村长判牧牛人有失照料，必须拿一头母牛赔偿那头跑掉的小牛。

中文章名: 小农夫
英文证据: And now the little peasant and his wife had the cow for which they had so long wished, and they were heartily glad, but they had no food for it, and could give it nothing to eat, so it soon had to be killed. They salted the flesh, and the peasant went into the town and wanted to sell the skin there, so that he might buy a new calf with the proceeds. On the way he passed by a mill, and there sat a raven with broken wings, and out of pity he took him and wrapped him in the skin. But as the weather grew so bad and there was a storm of rain and wind, he could go no farther, and turned back to the mill and begged for shelter. The miller’s wife was alone in the house, and said to the peasant: ‘Lay yourself on the straw there,’ and gave him a slice of bread and cheese. The peasant ate it, and lay down with his skin beside him, and the woman thought: ‘He is tired and has gone to sleep.’ In the meantime came the parson; the miller’s wife received him well, and said: ‘My husband is out, so we will have a feast.’ The peasant listened, and when he heard them talk about feasting he was vexed that he had been forced to make shift with a slice of bread and cheese. Then the woman served up four different things, roast meat, salad, cakes, and wine.
原译: 现在那个小农民和他妻子有了他们许愿已久的奶牛，他们很高兴，但他们没有食物，没有东西可以吃，所以它很快就要死了。他们把肉给盐了农民进城去想要卖掉那里的皮毛这样他就可以买一头新牛了。在路上，他经过一个磨坊，坐着一只乌鸦，翅膀断了，他出于怜悯把他带走，把他包在皮肤里。但是当天气变得如此糟糕暴雨和风雨，他无法继续前进，转过身去磨坊求救。磨坊主的妻子独自一人在房子里，对农夫说：你们在稻草上坐着吧！他就给他一块面包和奶酪。农夫吃了它，然后，在他旁边躺着，那个女人说：他已疲倦了，已入睡了。同时，牧师来了；磨坊主的妻子对他很好，他说：我丈夫出门了，所以我们有一个宴会。农民听了，当他听到他们谈论吃东西时，他感到很烦恼，他被迫用一块面包和奶酪换班。然后那个女人做了四样不同的东西烤肉沙拉蛋糕酒。
现译: 这下小农夫和妻子总算有了盼望已久的母牛，两个人真心欢喜。可他们没给牛备下饲料，一口吃的也拿不出，很快只好把牛杀了。他们腌下牛肉，小农夫拿着牛皮进城，打算卖了再买一头小牛。路过一座磨坊，他瞧见一只断了翅膀的渡鸦，心生怜悯，便把它抱起，用牛皮裹好。不料天气变坏，暴风骤雨中赶不了路，他只得折返磨坊求宿。磨坊主的妻子独自在家，对他说：“就睡那边的稻草吧。”又给了他一片面包配奶酪。他吃完躺下，把牛皮搁在身旁。女人想：“他累了，已经睡着了。”这时牧师来了。磨坊主的妻子热情迎他进来，说：“我丈夫出了门，咱们好好吃一顿。”小农夫听见他们要摆酒席，想到自己只混到一片面包配奶酪，心里挺不痛快。女人端出四样东西：烤肉、拌菜、糕饼和葡萄酒。

中文章名: 小农夫
英文证据: Just as they were about to sit down and eat, there was a knocking outside. The woman said: ‘Oh, heavens! It is my husband!’ she quickly hid the roast meat inside the tiled stove, the wine under the pillow, the salad on the bed, the cakes under it, and the parson in the closet on the porch. Then she opened the door for her husband, and said: ‘Thank heaven, you are back again! There is such a storm, it looks as if the world were coming to an end.’ The miller saw the peasant lying on the straw, and asked, ‘What is that fellow doing there?’ ‘Ah,’ said the wife, ‘the poor knave came in the storm and rain, and begged for shelter, so I gave him a bit of bread and cheese, and showed him where the straw was.’ The man said: ‘I have no objection, but be quick and get me something to eat.’ The woman said: ‘But I have nothing but bread and cheese.’ ‘I am contented with anything,’ replied the husband, ‘so far as I am concerned, bread and cheese will do,’ and looked at the peasant and said: ‘Come and eat some more with me.’ The peasant did not require to be invited twice, but got up and ate. After this the miller saw the skin in which the raven was, lying on the ground, and asked: ‘What have you there?’ The peasant answered: ‘I have a soothsayer inside it.’ ‘Can he foretell anything to me?’ said the miller. ‘Why not?’ answered the peasant: ‘but he only says four things, and the fifth he keeps to himself.’ The miller was curious, and said: ‘Let him foretell something for once.’ Then the peasant pinched the raven’s head, so that he croaked and made a noise like krr, krr. The miller said: ‘What did he say?’ The peasant answered: ‘In the first place, he says that there is some wine hidden under the pillow.’ ‘Bless me!’ cried the miller, and went there and found the wine. ‘Now go on,’ said he. The peasant made the raven croak again, and said: ‘In the second place, he says that there is some roast meat in the tiled stove.’ ‘Upon my word!’ cried the miller, and went thither, and found the roast meat. The peasant made the raven prophesy still more, and said: ‘Thirdly, he says that there is some salad on the bed.’ ‘That would be a fine thing!’ cried the miller, and went there and found the salad. At last the peasant pinched the raven once more till he croaked, and said: ‘Fourthly, he says that there are some cakes under the bed.’ ‘That would be a fine thing!’ cried the miller, and looked there, and found the cakes.
原译: 他们正要坐下来吃饭外面有个敲门声。那个女人说：我的丈夫啊！她快把烤肉藏在瓷炉里了，把酒藏在枕头下面，把沙拉放在床上，把蛋糕藏在床底下，把壁橱藏在门廊上。她为她的丈夫开门说：谢天谢地，你确已回来了。有一场暴风雨，那阵风好像世界将灭亡一样。磨坊主看见那个农夫躺在稻草上，他问他：那个农夫在那里做什么呢？他说：那可怜虫在暴风雨中奔来求庇，所以我给他一点面包和芝士，指示他稻草在哪里。那个人说：我不反对，你快去给我买点吃的吧！那女人说：我只吃面包和奶酪。他说：我对于任何事物都满意。他说：我对于面包和奶酪是心甘情愿的。你看那农夫说：你们来和我多吃一点吧！农民不需要被邀请两次，但起床吃东西。在那之后，磨坊主看见那只乌鸦躺在地上，他问：你们在那里做什么？农夫说：我有一个占卜者在里面。他能预言一件事吗？“为什么不呢？”回答农民说，“但他只说了四件事，而第五次是他自己做的。”磨坊主好奇地说：请他预言一件事。然后农民捏住乌鸦的头，所以他哭喊，发出像KRR，KRR的噪音。磨坊主说：他说了什么？农夫说：首先，他说：在枕头下隐藏着酒，求你饶了我吧！他喊着那个磨坊主去见酒。“现在继续，'他说。农夫又做了乌鸦，他说：第二，他说：在瓷炉里，有烤肉。我说：你们来吧！」他喊着磨坊主说：你们去吃烤肉吧！农民又编造了乌鸦预言，他说：第三，他说床上有沙拉。“那将是一个很好的事情！”他喊着磨坊主，走到那里，发现沙拉。农民终于再次捏住乌鸦，直到他哭泣，他说：“第四，他说床底下有一些蛋糕。“那将是一个很好的事情！”他哭着磨坊主，然后看着那里，发现蛋糕。
现译: 两人正要落座，外面响起敲门声。“天哪！我丈夫回来了！”女人赶紧把烤肉藏进瓷砖炉，把酒藏在枕头底下，拌菜藏在床上，糕饼藏到床下，牧师藏进门廊的小储物间。这才去给丈夫开门：“谢天谢地，你回来了！好大的风雨，活像世界要到末日了。”磨坊主看见稻草上躺着小农夫，就问：“那人在这里干什么？”“咳，”妻子说，“可怜的家伙冒着暴雨来求宿，我给了他一点面包和奶酪，指给他看哪儿有稻草。”“我倒没意见，”丈夫说，“快点给我也弄些吃的吧。”“可我只有面包和奶酪。”“有什么吃什么，我有面包和奶酪就行。”他看着小农夫说：“来，再陪我吃点。”小农夫哪用请第二遍，当即起来吃。磨坊主瞧见地上那张裹着渡鸦的牛皮，问：“你带的是什么？”“里头有个预言家。”小农夫答道。“他能给我预言点什么吗？”“怎么不能？不过他只肯说四桩，第五桩留在自己肚里。”磨坊主好奇地说：“那就让他预言一回吧。”小农夫捏捏渡鸦的脑袋，渡鸦呱啦、呱啦叫了起来。“他说什么？”磨坊主问。“第一，他说枕头底下藏着酒。”“我的天！”磨坊主过去一找，果然有酒。“接着来。”小农夫又弄得渡鸦叫起来，说：“第二，他说瓷砖炉里有烤肉。”“真神了！”磨坊主过去，果然找到了烤肉。小农夫让渡鸦接着预言：“第三，他说床上有拌菜。”“那敢情好！”磨坊主过去，真找到了拌菜。最后，小农夫又捏一下渡鸦，让它叫了一声，说：“第四，他说床底下有糕饼。”“那敢情好！”磨坊主一瞧，果然找到了糕饼。

The miller would have liked much to know the fifth, but the little peasant said: ‘First, we will quickly eat the four things, for the fifth is something bad.’ So they ate, and after that they bargained how much the miller was to give for the fifth prophecy, until they agreed on three hundred talers. Then the peasant once more pinched the raven’s head till he croaked loudly. The miller asked: ‘What did he say?’ The peasant replied: ‘He says that the Devil is hiding outside there in the closet on the porch.’ The miller said: ‘The Devil must go out,’ and opened the house-door; then the woman was forced to give up the keys, and the peasant unlocked the closet. The parson ran out as fast as he could, and the miller said: ‘It was true; I saw the black rascal with my own eyes.’ The peasant, however, made off next morning by daybreak with the three hundred talers.
原译: 现在他们俩一起坐在桌子上但是磨坊主的妻子吓得要死上床把钥匙都带走了。磨坊主很想知道第五件事，但那个小农民说：首先，我们要快地吃这四件事，第五件事是坏事。于是他们吃了，然后他们讨价还价磨坊主给了第五个预言多少钱，直到他们同意了三百个故事。然后农民又把乌鸦的头捏了到他大声叫喊。磨坊主问：“他说了什么？”农民回答说：“他说，魔鬼躲在门廊的壁橱里。”磨坊主说：恶魔必须出去。她打开了门。然后，那个女人被迫交出钥匙，那个农民打开了衣柜。牧师跑得越快，磨坊主说：这是真的，我亲眼看见那黑流氓。然而，农民第二天早晨与三百个传说家一起离开。
现译: 两人一同入席。磨坊主的妻子吓得要命，带着所有钥匙，上床睡了。磨坊主很想知道第五桩是什么，小农夫说：“先赶快把这四样吃了吧。第五桩可不是好事。”他们吃完，便商量磨坊主该出多少钱听第五个预言，最后说定是三百塔勒。小农夫又一捏渡鸦脑袋，它大叫一声。磨坊主问：“他说什么？”“他说，魔鬼躲在外面门廊的储物间里。”“得把魔鬼赶出去！”磨坊主一把拉开屋门。妻子只好交出钥匙，小农夫打开储物间的锁，牧师飞也似的逃了出去。“果然不假，”磨坊主说，“我亲眼看见那个一身黑的坏家伙了。”第二天一破晓，小农夫便带着三百塔勒上路了。

中文章名: 小农夫
英文证据: At home the small peasant gradually launched out; he built a beautiful house, and the peasants said: ‘The small peasant has certainly been to the place where golden snow falls, and people carry the gold home in shovels.’ Then the small peasant was brought before the mayor, and bidden to say from whence his wealth came. He answered: ‘I sold my cow’s skin in the town, for three hundred talers.’ When the peasants heard that, they too wished to enjoy this great profit, and ran home, killed all their cows, and stripped off their skins in order to sell them in the town to the greatest advantage. The mayor, however, said: ‘But my servant must go first.’ When she came to the merchant in the town, he did not give her more than two talers for a skin, and when the others came, he did not give them so much, and said: ‘What can I do with all these skins?’
原译: 在家里，小农民逐渐地搬出；他建造了一座美丽的房屋，农民们说：小农民的确去过金雪落下的地方，人们用铲子把金子搬回家。然后那个小农夫被带到市长面前要求他说出他的财产来自何方。他说：我把牛皮卖了，卖了三百个传说家。当农民听到这个消息时，他们也希望享受这一巨大的利润，然后跑回家，杀死他们的牛，剥光他们的皮，以便把他们卖到城里去，以获得最大的利益。但市长说：我的仆人必须先走。当她来到城里的商人面前的时候，他只给她两个说客，当别人来的时候，他没有给她们这么多，他说：这些皮革，我能做什么呢？
现译: 小农夫回家后，渐渐阔气起来，还盖了座漂亮房子。农民们说：“他一定去了下金子雪的地方，那里的人拿铲子就能把金子往回铲。”他们把他带到村长面前，要他说出钱财的来历。“我把那张牛皮拿到城里，卖了三百塔勒。”他答道。农民们听了，也想赚这笔大利，跑回家杀掉所有的牛，剥了皮要进城卖个好价钱。村长却说：“得让我家女仆先去。”女仆找到城里的商人，一张皮最多只卖了两个塔勒。等旁人也来了，连这个数都不给，商人说：“这么多牛皮，我拿来做什么？”

中文章名: 小农夫
英文证据: Then the peasants were vexed that the small peasant should have thus outwitted them, wanted to take vengeance on him, and accused him of this treachery before the mayor. The innocent little peasant was unanimously sentenced to death, and was to be rolled into the water, in a barrel pierced full of holes. He was led forth, and a priest was brought who was to say a mass for his soul. The others were all obliged to retire to a distance, and when the peasant looked at the priest, he recognized the man who had been with the miller’s wife. He said to him: ‘I set you free from the closet, set me free from the barrel.’ At this same moment up came, with a flock of sheep, the very shepherd whom the peasant knew had long been wishing to be mayor, so he cried with all his might: ‘No, I will not do it; if the whole world insists on it, I will not do it!’ The shepherd hearing that, came up to him, and asked: ‘What are you about? What is it that you will not do?’ The peasant said: ‘They want to make me mayor, if I will but put myself in the barrel, but I will not do it.’ The shepherd said: ‘If nothing more than that is needful in order to be mayor, I would get into the barrel at once.’ The peasant said: ‘If you will get in, you will be mayor.’ The shepherd was willing, and got in, and the peasant shut the top down on him; then he took the shepherd’s flock for himself, and drove it away. The parson went to the crowd, and declared that the mass had been said. Then they came and rolled the barrel towards the water. When the barrel began to roll, the shepherd cried: ‘I am quite willing to be mayor.’ They believed no otherwise than that it was the peasant who was saying this, and answered: ‘That is what we intend, but first you shall look about you a little down below there,’ and they rolled the barrel down into the water.
原译: 农民们感到愤怒，认为这帮小农民应该愚弄他们，想报复他，并向市长控告他这种背叛行为。无辜的小农民被一致判处死刑，并被卷进水里，桶里充满了洞。他被领了出来，一个牧师被带去说为他的灵魂弥撒。其他人都被迫离家远一点，当农民看着牧师时，他认出了与磨坊主妻子在一起的男人。他说：我使你从衣柜里出来，我从桶里出来。在同一时刻，农夫们知道牧羊人长年希望当市长，他带着羊群上山，大喊大叫：不，我不会做；如果全世界坚持做，我绝不做。牧人听见了声音，就来到他面前说：你们为甚么而工作呢？你们怎么不工作呢？农民说：他们想任命我为镇长，如果我想的话，请把自己放在枪管里，但我不会这样做。牧羊人说：“如果再多的话，我就要马上上船了。”农夫说：如果你进去，你就是镇长。牧羊人愿意进去农民关了上面自己把牧羊人的羊群赶走了。牧师去人群中，并宣布弥撒已经说。然后他们就来了把桶子卷到水边。当枪管开始滚动时，牧羊人喊道：“我愿意当市长。”他们只信那农夫的话，他们说：这是我们所意欲的。你们先在下面观望一下。他们就把桶子翻到水里。
现译: 农民们气小农夫把他们全算计了，一心想报仇，就到村长面前告他耍诈。大家一致判这个无辜的小农夫死刑，要把他装进一个凿满窟窿的木桶，滚进水里。他被押出去，又请来一个牧师，为他的灵魂做弥撒。众人都要退到远处。小农夫看看牧师，认出正是跟磨坊主妻子一道的那个人，便对他说：“我放你出了储物间，你也放我出木桶吧。”这时恰好有个牧羊人赶着羊群经过。小农夫知道他早想当村长，就放声大叫：“不干，我不干！哪怕全天下的人都逼我，我也不干！”牧羊人听见，上前问道：“怎么了？你不愿干什么？”小农夫说：“他们要我当村长，只消钻进这木桶，可我不干。”牧羊人说：“要是当村长只消这么一下，我立刻就钻进去。”“你要肯钻进去，”小农夫说，“你就是村长了。”牧羊人十分乐意，钻进木桶，小农夫把桶盖一扣，接过羊群，赶着走了。牧师回到众人中间，宣布弥撒已经做完。农民们就把木桶往水边滚。木桶一转，牧羊人便喊：“我愿意当村长！我十分愿意！”大家只当喊话的是小农夫，便答道：“咱们也是这个意思。不过，你先下去四面瞧瞧吧。”便把木桶滚进了水里。

中文章名: 小农夫
英文证据: After that the peasants went home, and as they were entering the village, the small peasant also came quietly in, driving a flock of sheep and looking quite contented. Then the peasants were astonished, and said: ‘Peasant, from whence do you come? Have you come out of the water?’ ‘Yes, truly,’ replied the peasant, ‘I sank deep, deep down, until at last I got to the bottom; I pushed the bottom out of the barrel, and crept out, and there were pretty meadows on which a number of lambs were feeding, and from thence I brought this flock away with me.’ Said the peasants: ‘Are there any more there?’ ‘Oh, yes,’ said he, ‘more than I could want.’ Then the peasants made up their minds that they too would fetch some sheep for themselves, a flock apiece, but the mayor said: ‘I come first.’ So they went to the water together, and just then there were some of the small fleecy clouds in the blue sky, which are called little lambs, and they were reflected in the water, whereupon the peasants cried: ‘We already see the sheep down below!’ The mayor pressed forward and said: ‘I will go down first, and look about me, and if things promise well I’ll call you.’ So he jumped in; splash! went the water; it sounded as if he were calling them, and the whole crowd plunged in after him as one man. 中文章名: 弗雷德里克和凯瑟琳
英文证据: When she reached home, she bolted the back door, but the front door she took off the hinges, and said, ‘Frederick told me to lock the door, but surely it can nowhere be so safe if I take it with me.’ So she took her time by the way; and when she overtook her husband she cried out, ‘There, Frederick, there is the door itself, you may watch it as carefully as you please.’ ‘Alas! alas!’ said he, ‘what a clever wife I have! I sent you to make the house fast, and you take the door away, so that everybody may go in and out as they please--however, as you have brought the door, you shall carry it about with you for your pains.’ ‘Very well,’ answered she, ‘I’ll carry the door; but I’ll not carry the nuts and vinegar bottle also--that would be too much of a load; so if you please, I’ll fasten them to the door.’

中文章名: 弗雷德里克和凯瑟琳
英文证据: Frederick of course made no objection to that plan, and they set off into the wood to look for the thieves; but they could not find them: and when it grew dark, they climbed up into a tree to spend the night there. Scarcely were they up, than who should come by but the very rogues they were looking for. 中文章名: 弗雷德里克和凯瑟琳

中文章名: 心上人罗兰

The stepdaughter once had a pretty apron, which the other fancied so much that she became envious, and told her mother that she must and would have that apron. ‘Be quiet, my child,’ said the old woman, ‘and you shall have it. Your stepsister has long deserved death; tonight when she is asleep I will come and cut her head off. Only be careful that you are at the far side of the bed, and push her well to the front.’ It would have been all over with the poor girl if she had not just then been standing in a corner, and heard everything. All day long she dared not go out of doors, and when bedtime had come, the witch’s daughter got into bed first, so as to lie at the far side, but when she was asleep, the other pushed her gently to the front, and took for herself the place at the back, close by the wall. In the night, the old woman came creeping in, she held an axe in her right hand, and felt with her left to see if anyone were lying at the outside, and then she grasped the axe with both hands, and cut her own child’s head off.

现译: 从前有个女人，是个货真价实的女巫。她有两个女儿，一个丑陋又狠毒，她喜欢，因为是亲生的；一个美丽又善良，她偏恨，因为是继女。继女有条漂亮围裙，另一个姑娘喜欢得眼红，对母亲说，这条围裙她想要，非要不可。“别出声，我的孩子，”老婆子说，“这就给你。你那没血缘的姊妹早就该死。今晚等她睡着，我来砍掉她的脑袋。你只消当心，自己睡到床里边去，把她好好推到外边。”可怜的姑娘本来难逃一死，亏得这时正站在角落里，把什么都听了去。她整天没敢出门。到了睡觉时候，女巫的亲女儿先上床，抢了里边的位置。等她睡熟，继女轻轻把她移到外边，自己换到里边紧挨墙的地方。半夜老婆子偷偷摸进屋，右手拿斧，伸出左手摸摸，看看床外沿有没有人，随即双手握斧一砍，把亲生女儿的脑袋砍了下来。

When he came out, she said to him: ‘Listen, dearest Roland, we must fly in all haste; my stepmother wanted to kill me, but has struck her own child. 中文章名: 心上人罗兰
英文证据: When the old witch got up next morning, she called her daughter, and wanted to give her the apron, but she did not come. Then the witch cried: ‘Where are you?’ ‘Here, on the stairs, I am sweeping,’ answered the first drop of blood. The old woman went out, but saw no one on the stairs, and cried again: ‘Where are you?’ ‘Here in the kitchen, I am warming myself,’ cried the second drop of blood. She went into the kitchen, but found no one. Then she cried again: ‘Where are you?’ ‘Ah, here in the bed, I am sleeping,’ cried the third drop of blood. She went into the room to the bed. What did she see there? Her own child, whose head she had cut off, bathed in her blood. The witch fell into a passion, sprang to the window, and as she could look forth quite far into the world, she perceived her stepdaughter hurrying away with her sweetheart Roland. ‘That shall not help you,’ cried she, ‘even if you have got a long way off, you shall still not escape me.’ She put on her many-league boots, in which she covered an hour’s walk at every step, and it was not long before she overtook them. The girl, however, when she saw the old woman striding towards her, changed, with her magic wand, her sweetheart Roland into a lake, and herself into a duck swimming in the middle of it. The witch placed herself on the shore, threw breadcrumbs in, and went to endless trouble to entice the duck; but the duck did not let herself be enticed, and the old woman had to go home at night as she had come. At this the girl and her sweetheart Roland resumed their natural shapes again, and they walked on the whole night until daybreak. Then the maiden changed herself into a beautiful flower which stood in the midst of a briar hedge, and her sweetheart Roland into a fiddler. It was not long before the witch came striding up towards them, and said to the musician: ‘Dear musician, may I pluck that beautiful flower for myself?’ ‘Oh, yes,’ he replied, ‘I will play to you while you do it.’ As she was hastily creeping into the hedge and was just going to pluck the flower, knowing perfectly well who the flower was, he began to play, and whether she would or not, she was forced to dance, for it was a magical dance. The faster he played, the more violent springs was she forced to make, and the thorns tore her clothes from her body, and pricked her and wounded her till she bled, and as he did not stop, she had to dance till she lay dead on the ground.

中文章名: 白雪公主
英文证据: Then poor Snowdrop wandered along through the wood in great fear; and the wild beasts roared about her, but none did her any harm. In the evening she came to a cottage among the hills, and went in to rest, for her little feet would carry her no further. Everything was spruce and neat in the cottage: on the table was spread a white cloth, and there were seven little plates, seven little loaves, and seven little glasses with wine in them; and seven knives and forks laid in order; and by the wall stood seven little beds. As she was very hungry, she picked a little piece of each loaf and drank a very little wine out of each glass; and after that she thought she would lie down and rest. So she tried all the little beds; but one was too long, and another was too short, till at last the seventh suited her: and there she laid herself down and went to sleep.
原译: 然后，可怜的雪地，在极度恐惧的情况下，在树林中徘徊，野兽围着她咆哮，但她没有遭受任何伤害。晚上，她来到山中的一个小屋，并进去休息，因为她的小脚将不再抱她。房子里的东西都很整洁：桌子上铺着白布，有七块小盘子，七块小面包，七块小杯子，上面装着葡萄酒；七把刀和叉子，墙上铺着七张小床。她非常饿，从每块面包中摘了一块，从每杯中喝了一小杯葡萄酒；之后，她以为她会躺下休息。于是她尝试了所有的小床；但有一个太长，另一个太短，直到最后第七个床适合她：她躺着睡觉。
现译: 可怜的白雪公主独自在林子里游荡，怕得要命。野兽在她四周吼叫，却没有一只伤她。傍晚，她走到群山间的一间小屋，进去歇脚，因为一双小脚再也走不动了。屋里处处整齐洁净。桌上铺着白桌布，摆着七只小盘子、七个小面包、七只盛着酒的小玻璃杯，七副刀叉放得整整齐齐。墙边还有七张小床。她实在饿了，每个面包掰下一小口，每只杯子抿了一小口酒，接着想躺下歇会儿。她把小床一张张试过去，这张太长，那张又太短，只有第七张正合适，她便躺下睡着了。

The first said, ‘Who has been sitting on my stool?’ The second, ‘Who has been eating off my plate?’ The third, ‘Who has been picking my bread?’ The fourth, ‘Who has been meddling with my spoon?’ The fifth, ‘Who has been handling my fork?’ The sixth, ‘Who has been cutting with my knife?’ The seventh, ‘Who has been drinking my wine?’ Then the first looked round and said, ‘Who has been lying on my bed?’ And the rest came running to him, and everyone cried out that somebody had been upon his bed. But the seventh saw Snowdrop, and called all his brethren to come and see her; and they cried out with wonder and astonishment and brought their lamps to look at her, and said, ‘Good heavens! what a lovely child she is!’ And they were very glad to see her, and took care not to wake her; and the seventh dwarf slept an hour with each of the other dwarfs in turn, till the night was gone.

现译: 过了一阵，小屋的主人回来了。原来是七个小矮人，住在群山间，在山里探矿挖金。他们点亮七盏小灯，立刻发觉有些不对劲。头一个说：“谁坐过我的凳子？”第二个说：“谁动过我盘子里的东西？”第三个说：“谁掰过我的面包？”第四个说：“谁碰过我的勺子？”第五个说：“谁拿过我的叉子？”第六个说：“谁用我的小刀切过东西？”第七个说：“谁喝过我的酒？”头一个往旁边一瞧，又说：“谁躺过我的床？”其余几个闻声跑来，人人都嚷自己的床叫人躺过。第七个却看见了白雪公主，连忙叫弟兄们都来看。他们惊讶得叫出声来，举灯凑近看了又看，说：“天哪，好一个可爱的孩子！”他们很高兴见到她，小心不去吵醒她。第七个矮人轮流同别的矮人合睡，每张床睡一个钟头，就这么过了一夜。

Then she knocked at the door, and cried, ‘Fine wares to sell!’ Snowdrop looked out at the window, and said, ‘Good day, good woman! what have you to sell?’ ‘Good wares, fine wares,’ said she; ‘laces and bobbins of all colours.’ ‘I will let the old lady in; she seems to be a very good sort of body,’ thought Snowdrop, as she ran down and unbolted the door. ‘Bless me!’ said the old woman, ‘how badly your stays are laced! Let me lace them up with one of my nice new laces.’ Snowdrop did not dream of any mischief; so she stood before the old woman; but she set to work so nimbly, and pulled the lace so tight, that Snowdrop’s breath was stopped, and she fell down as if she were dead. ‘There’s an end to all thy beauty,’ said the spiteful queen, and went away home.
原译: 女王非常害怕，因为她知道玻璃总是说真话，并且确信仆人背叛了她。她无法忍受有人比她更美丽。 所以她打扮成老小马车，走到山上，走到矮人居住的地方。然后她敲了门哭着说：“好东西要卖！”雪滴向窗外望望着窗子 、 说 、 好女子阿 、 你要卖甚么呢 。 她说 、 好器具 、 好器物 。 〔 有古卷作一样 〕 她说 、 百色的鞋和花子 、 我必容婆进去 、 他似乎是极美的身子 、 也思思思子 、 正向下去 、 解了了门。那个老妇人说：求你饶恕我，你所逗留的地方真恶劣，求你让我用我的新的部分来宽慰他们。雪滴没有作恶的梦，所以她站在那个老妇人面前，她忙碌地工作，紧紧拉紧丝带，使雪滴的呼吸停止，她摔倒，仿佛她死了一样。“你的美貌已经终结了” 恶毒的女王说，然后就回家了。

中文章名: 石竹花
英文证据: The cook, however, thought to himself: ‘If the child has the power of wishing, and I am here, he might very easily get me into trouble.’ So he left the palace and went to the boy, who was already big enough to speak, and said to him: ‘Wish for a beautiful palace for yourself with a garden, and all else that pertains to it.’ Scarcely were the words out of the boy’s mouth, when everything was there that he had wished for. After a while the cook said to him: ‘It is not well for you to be so alone, wish for a pretty girl as a companion.’ Then the king’s son wished for one, and she immediately stood before him, and was more beautiful than any painter could have painted her. The two played together, and loved each other with all their hearts, and the old cook went out hunting like a nobleman. The thought occurred to him, however, that the king’s son might some day wish to be with his father, and thus bring him into great peril. So he went out and took the maiden aside, and said: ‘Tonight when the boy is asleep, go to his bed and plunge this knife into his heart, and bring me his heart and tongue, and if you do not do it, you shall lose your life.’ Thereupon he went away, and when he returned next day she had not done it, and said: ‘Why should I shed the blood of an innocent boy who has never harmed anyone?’ The cook once more said: ‘If you do not do it, it shall cost you your own life.’ When he had gone away, she had a little hind brought to her, and ordered her to be killed, and took her heart and tongue, and laid them on a plate, and when she saw the old man coming, she said to the boy: ‘Lie down in your bed, and draw the clothes over you.’ Then the wicked wretch came in and said: ‘Where are the boy’s heart and tongue?’ The girl reached the plate to him, but the king’s son threw off the quilt, and said: ‘You old sinner, why did you want to kill me? Now will I pronounce thy sentence. You shall become a black poodle and have a gold collar round your neck, and shall eat burning coals, till the flames burst forth from your throat.’ And when he had spoken these words, the old man was changed into a poodle dog, and had a gold collar round his neck, and the cooks were ordered to bring up some live coals, and these he ate, until the flames broke forth from his throat. The king’s son remained there a short while longer, and he thought of his mother, and wondered if she were still alive. At length he said to the maiden: ‘I will go home to my own country; if you will go with me, I will provide for you.’ ‘Ah,’ she replied, ‘the way is so long, and what shall I do in a strange land where I am unknown?’ As she did not seem quite willing, and as they could not be parted from each other, he wished that she might be changed into a beautiful pink, and took her with him. Then he went away to his own country, and the poodle had to run after him. He went to the tower in which his mother was confined, and as it was so high, he wished for a ladder which would reach up to the very top. Then he mounted up and looked inside, and cried: ‘Beloved mother, Lady Queen, are you still alive, or are you dead?’ She answered: ‘I have just eaten, and am still satisfied,’ for she thought the angels were there. Said he: ‘I am your dear son, whom the wild beasts were said to have torn from your arms; but I am alive still, and will soon set you free.’ Then he descended again, and went to his father, and caused himself to be announced as a strange huntsman, and asked if he could offer him service. The king said yes, if he was skilful and could get game for him, he should come to him, but that deer had never taken up their quarters in any part of the district or country. Then the huntsman promised to procure as much game for him as he could possibly use at the royal table. So he summoned all the huntsmen together, and bade them go out into the forest with him. And he went with them and made them form a great circle, open at one end where he stationed himself, and began to wish. Two hundred deer and more came running inside the circle at once, and the huntsmen shot them. Then they were all placed on sixty country carts, and driven home to the king, and for once he was able to deck his table with game, after having had none at all for years.
原译: 但是厨师自己想：“如果孩子有愿望的能力，而我在这里，他可能会很容易地给我带来麻烦。”他离开宫殿，去见那个已经够大可以说话的男孩，对他说：你们希望有一个美丽的宫殿，有一个花园，和它的其他一切。当他想要的一切都在那里时男孩的嘴里说的话就可怕了。过了一段时间，厨师对他说：你们为自己的妻子而孤单，并祈求一个美丽的女孩做他的伴侣，这对你们是不妥的。然后国王的儿子希望有一个，她立刻站在他面前，比任何画家都更美丽。两个人一起玩耍，用心爱对方老厨师像贵族一样出去打猎。然而，他想到，国王的儿子可能有一天想和他父亲在一起，从而把他带入巨大的危险之中。他出去把那个少女拉到一边，他说：当男孩睡着的时候，你到他的床上去，把这把刀插入他的心脏，把他的心和舌头拿来给我，如果你不这样做，你必丧失生命。他走了，他第二天回来的时候，她没有做过这件事，他说：我为什么要流一个无辜的男孩的血呢？他没有伤害任何人。厨师们说：如果你不做，那会使你丧失生命。当他离开的时候，她有一个小的后遗症，拿起她的心和舌头，把她们放在盘子上，当她看见那个老头子来的时候，她对那个男孩说：你躺下，你把衣服拿过来吧！恶人进来说：那男孩的心和舌呢？那女孩就到了他面前，国王的儿子就把那个衣服扔下了，他说：你们这个罪人，为什么要杀我呢？现在我要宣布你们的判决，你们要变成一只黑狗，颈上有金领，要吃烧煤，直到你们喉咙中的火焰。当他讲这些话的时候，那个老人被换成一只小狗，脖子上戴着金领，厨师们被命令拿起一些活煤，他们吃这些煤，直到火焰从他的喉咙中冒出来。国王的儿子在那呆了一会儿他想起了母亲想知道她是否还活着。他对那个女孩说：我必定要回家去。如果你们要同我一道去，我必定要供给你们。她说：我的道路是那么长的，我在一个陌生的地方，能做什么呢？由于她似乎不太愿意，而且他们不能分开，他希望她能够变成一个美丽的粉红色，并带走她。然后他去了自己的国家狗狗不得不追逐他。他去了他母亲被禁闭的塔，由于塔太高了，他希望有一个梯子能够达到最顶端。然后，他站起来，看着里面，喊着说：亲爱的母亲，女王夫人，你还活着吗？还是你死了？她回答说：我确已吃过了，仍然满意。她以为众天神在。他说：我确是你亲爱的儿子，据传，野兽是从你怀里被撕破的，但我生前是死的，不久我就要释放你。他又降级了，去见他的父亲，然后，他被宣布为奇人，他问他能否为他服务。国王答应了，如果他有技巧，可以为他打球，他应该去找他，但是那头鹿从未在任何地区或国家占过他们的位子。然后猎人答应给他买多少和他可能在皇室餐桌上用的一样多的游戏。于是他召集了所有的猎人并把他们都召集到森林里去。他和他们一道，使他们变成一个伟大的圆圈，他从一个端开始，他在那里站着，并开始许愿。两百头鹿和更多的鹿一次跑进圆圈里猎人开枪打死了他们。然后他们都坐上60辆乡村车开车回家见国王一次他能把桌子打得一团糟多年来一无所有。
现译: 老厨子却想：“这孩子什么愿都能许，我再留在这里，他轻而易举就能给我招来祸事。”于是他离开王宫，去找男孩。这时孩子已经会说话了。他说：“你给自己许一座美丽的宫殿吧，要带花园，里头该有的东西样样齐全。”男孩话音才落，所许的一切都出现了。过了一阵，厨子又说：“你一个人待着可不好，许个漂亮姑娘来作伴吧。”王子便许了一个，姑娘立刻站在他面前，再好的画师也画不出她的美丽。两个孩子一起玩耍，打心底里爱着对方，老厨子自己过起了贵族老爷出门打猎的日子。可是他又想到，王子说不定有一天会许愿回父亲身边，那样他可就危险了。他出门把姑娘叫到一旁，说：“今晚男孩睡着，你就去他床前，把这把刀子捅进他的心口，把心和舌头拿来给我。你若不肯，就要你的命。”说完便走了。第二天回来，姑娘并没动手，只说：“一个清白孩子，从没伤过人，我为什么要流他的血？”厨子又说：“你不动手，就赔上自己的命。”他一走，姑娘叫人牵来一头小母鹿，吩咐杀了，取出鹿心和鹿舌摆在盘里。看见老头回来，她对男孩说：“上床躺下，拿被子把自己盖好。”坏家伙进来就问：“男孩的心和舌头呢？”姑娘递上盘子，王子却掀开被褥，说：“你这老恶人，为什么要杀我？现在我要宣判了：你将变成一只黑鬈毛狗，颈上戴一个金项圈。你要吞食烧红的木炭，直到喉咙里喷出火焰。”话一出口，老头果然成了一只戴金项圈的鬈毛狗。王子叫厨房端来炽热的木炭，狗吃下去，喉咙里直喷火。王子又在那里住了一小阵，想起母亲，不知道她是否还活着。终于他对姑娘说：“我要回自己的国家了。你要是愿跟我走，我会照料你。”“唉，”她说，“路这么远，到了人生地不熟的异国，我怎么办？”她似乎不大情愿，可两人又分不开，他便许愿把她变成一朵美丽的石竹花，带在身边。他动身回国，鬈毛狗也只得跟在后头跑。王子到了囚禁母亲的高塔下。塔实在太高，他就许愿要一架直通塔顶的梯子。他爬上去，探头往里看，喊道：“亲爱的母后，您还活着，还是已经死了？”她回答：“我刚吃过，还饱着呢。”她以为天使来了。他说：“我是您疼爱的儿子，就是那个据说从您怀里给野兽叼走的孩子。我还活着，很快就能放您出去。”说完他下来，去见父亲，让人通报说来了一位外乡猎人，想问能不能在陛下手下效力。国王答应，只要他有本事，能替国王打到野味，就来供职。只是这一带，乃至全国，向来都没有鹿落脚。猎人保证，御膳需要多少野味，他就能弄来多少。他召集所有猎人，同去森林，叫他们围成一大圈，一头敞开，自己站在开口处许愿。立刻有两百多头鹿跑进圈里，猎人们射中了它们。猎物足足装了六十辆乡间大车，送回给国王。隔了那么多年，国王总算又能在御膳桌上摆出野味来了。

中文章名: 石竹花
英文证据: Now the king felt great joy at this, and commanded that his entire household should eat with him next day, and made a great feast. When they were all assembled together, he said to the huntsman: ‘As you are so clever, you shall sit by me.’ He replied: ‘Lord King, your majesty must excuse me, I am a poor huntsman.’ But the king insisted on it, and said: ‘You shall sit by me,’ until he did it. Whilst he was sitting there, he thought of his dearest mother, and wished that one of the king’s principal servants would begin to speak of her, and would ask how it was faring with the queen in the tower, and if she were alive still, or had perished. Hardly had he formed the wish than the marshal began, and said: ‘Your majesty, we live joyously here, but how is the queen living in the tower? Is she still alive, or has she died?’ But the king replied: ‘She let my dear son be torn to pieces by wild beasts; I will not have her named.’ Then the huntsman arose and said: ‘Gracious lord father she is alive still, and I am her son, and I was not carried away by wild beasts, but by that wretch the old cook, who tore me from her arms when she was asleep, and sprinkled her apron with the blood of a chicken.’ Thereupon he took the dog with the golden collar, and said: ‘That is the wretch!’ and caused live coals to be brought, and these the dog was compelled to devour before the sight of all, until flames burst forth from its throat. On this the huntsman asked the king if he would like to see the dog in his true shape, and wished him back into the form of the cook, in which he stood immediately, with his white apron, and his knife by his side. When the king saw him he fell into a passion, and ordered him to be cast into the deepest dungeon. Then the huntsman spoke further and said: ‘Father, will you see the maiden who brought me up so tenderly and who was afterwards to murder me, but did not do it, though her own life depended on it?’ The king replied: ‘Yes, I would like to see her.’ The son said: ‘Most gracious father, I will show her to you in the form of a beautiful flower,’ and he thrust his hand into his pocket and brought forth the pink, and placed it on the royal table, and it was so beautiful that the king had never seen one to equal it. Then the son said: ‘Now will I show her to you in her own form,’ and wished that she might become a maiden, and she stood there looking so beautiful that no painter could have made her look more so.
原译: 现在国王对这个感到欢乐并命令他的全家第二天与他共进晚餐。当他们被集合的时候，他对狩猎者说：你们真聪明，所以你们坐在我旁边吧！主说：国王啊！我确是一个穷困的狩猎者，你应当恕我直言。但国王坚持说：你们坐在我旁边吧！直到他做了这件事。当他坐在那里的时候，他想到他最亲爱的母亲，并希望国王的一位主要仆人开始谈论她，并会问它是如何在塔里与女王相处的，以及她是否还活着，或者已经死去。他没有象元帅那样形成愿望，他说：我们是快乐的，我们是快乐的，但太后是怎样居住在那座塔里的呢？是她活着呢？还是她死了呢？国王说：她让我的儿子被野兽撕成碎片，我绝不叫她为人命名。猎人就起来说：我的父亲啊！她还活着，我是她的儿子，我不是被野兽带走的，而是被那个老厨师带走的，她睡着时把我从她的怀里撕开，用一只鸡的血洒下她的围裙。他带着那条金领，走来，他说：这确是不轨的。他以炭为生，狗在众目中就被吞噬了，直到火从它的咽喉中冒出来。狩猎者问国王他是否愿意看到狗的真面目，并祝愿他回到厨师的样子。当国王看见他的时候，他沉浸在激情中，命令他投入最深的地牢。猎人又说：我的父亲啊！你告诉我吧，那个使我长大的女子，在她杀死我之后，又是谁呢？她没有杀人，但愿她自己的生命是依恋他的。国王说：是的，我想见她。儿子说：我的父亲啊！我要以一朵美丽的花样昭示你她。他把手伸进口袋，拿出粉色来，放在皇室的桌子上，那件花太美了，国王从未看见过她。儿子说：现在我要以她的形式昭示你们她。她希望她变成一个贞操的少女，她在那里面面容优美，所以没有一位画家能使她更美。
现译: 国王为此十分高兴，下令次日宫中上下都来跟他一道用餐，置办起好大一场宴席。众人到齐，他对猎人说：“你这样能干，坐到我身边来。”“国王陛下，请恕我失礼，我只是个穷猎人。”猎人答道。国王却坚持说“你一定坐我身边”，直到他依从了才罢。猎人坐在那里，想起最亲爱的母亲，便许了个愿，愿国王身边的一位大臣说起她来，问问塔里的王后过得怎样，还活着，还是已经死了。他的心愿才动，宫廷总管就开了口：“陛下，我们在这里过得快活，可王后在塔里过得怎样？她还活着，还是已经死了？”国王却说：“她让野兽撕碎了我的爱子。我不准人提起她！”猎人站起来说：“仁慈的父王，她还活着，我就是她的儿子。把我带走的不是野兽，是那个恶棍老厨子，在她熟睡时把我从她怀里夺走，再往她围裙上洒了鸡血。”他把戴金项圈的狗带上来，说：“那恶棍就在这里！”他命人取来炽热的木炭，让狗当着众人吞下去，一直吞到口中喷火。接着猎人问国王要不要看看狗的本相，便许愿让它恢复老厨子的模样。它立刻就变成了厨子，身围白围裙，腰侧还挂着把刀。国王见了，大发雷霆，下令把他打入最深的地牢。猎人又说：“父亲，您可愿见见那个一直悉心照看我长大的姑娘？后来人家要她杀我，她即便冒着性命之险，也没肯下手。”国王回答：“愿意，我想见她。”儿子说：“尊贵的父亲，我先让您看她变成的一朵鲜花。”他把手伸进口袋，取出石竹花，放在御桌上。那花如此美丽，国王还没见过哪一朵比得上。儿子说：“现在请看她本来的模样。”他许愿让她变回姑娘，她立即亭亭立在眼前，再好的画师也不能把她画得更美。

中文章名: 石竹花
英文证据: And the king sent two waiting-maids and two attendants into the tower, to fetch the queen and bring her to the royal table. But when she was led in she ate nothing, and said: ‘The gracious and merciful God who has supported me in the tower, will soon set me free.’ She lived three days more, and then died happily, and when she was buried, the two white doves which had brought her food to the tower, and were angels of heaven, followed her body and seated themselves on her grave. The aged king ordered the cook to be torn in four pieces, but grief consumed the king’s own heart, and he soon died. His son married the beautiful maiden whom he had brought with him as a flower in his pocket, and whether they are still alive or not, is known to God.
原译: 国王派了两个侍女和两个侍女进入塔里带女王到皇室。当她被引导而未吃东西的时候，她说：在塔里扶助我的仁慈的真主，将使我自由。她活了三天，然后幸福地死去，当她被埋葬时，将食物带到塔上的两只白鸽子，它们是天上的天使，跟着她的身体，坐在她的坟墓上。年老的国王命令厨师被撕成四块但悲痛吞噬了国王的心不久他就死了。他的儿子娶了他带给他的美丽少女，他把那个少女当花朵放在他的口袋里，而无论她们是否还活着，真主都是知道的。
现译: 国王派了两名侍女、两名随从到塔里去，请王后来御桌旁。王后被迎进来，却什么也没吃，说：“仁慈宽厚的上帝在塔里养活了我，不久就要赐我解脱。”她又活了三天，随后安然离世。下葬时，两只曾在塔中给她送食的白鸽，也就是天上的两位天使，跟着灵柩，停在她的坟头。老国王下令把厨子分尸四块，自己却伤心欲绝，也很快死了。他的儿子娶了那位美丽的姑娘，就是化作花朵盛在他口袋里，和他一道来到这里的姑娘。至于他们如今可还活着，只有上帝知道。

中文章名: 聪明的埃尔茜
英文证据: There was once a man who had a daughter who was called Clever Elsie. And when she had grown up her father said: ‘We will get her married.’ ‘Yes,’ said the mother, ‘if only someone would come who would have her.’ At length a man came from a distance and wooed her, who was called Hans; but he stipulated that Clever Elsie should be really smart. ‘Oh,’ said the father, ‘she has plenty of good sense’; and the mother said: ‘Oh, she can see the wind coming up the street, and hear the flies coughing.’ ‘Well,’ said Hans, ‘if she is not really smart, I won’t have her.’ When they were sitting at dinner and had eaten, the mother said: ‘Elsie, go into the cellar and fetch some beer.’ Then Clever Elsie took the pitcher from the wall, went into the cellar, and tapped the lid briskly as she went, so that the time might not appear long. When she was below she fetched herself a chair, and set it before the barrel so that she had no need to stoop, and did not hurt her back or do herself any unexpected injury. Then she placed the can before her, and turned the tap, and while the beer was running she would not let her eyes be idle, but looked up at the wall, and after much peering here and there, saw a pick-axe exactly above her, which the masons had accidentally left there.
原译: 有一次有个女儿叫聪明埃尔西。当她长大的时候，她的父亲说：我们把她娶了。她说：是的。她的母亲说：只有有人来娶她。一个男人从远处来追求她，叫汉斯但他规定聪明的埃尔西应该很聪明。父亲说：啊！她有理智。母亲说：她能看见风吹到街上，听见苍蝇咳嗽。汉斯说：如果她不聪明，我就不拥有她。当他们坐着吃晚饭时，母亲说：“艾尔西，去地窖拿些啤酒来。”然后聪明的埃尔西从墙上拿起投手走进地窖冲进地窖时不时地挖出盖子这样时间就不会长了。她在楼下时，自己拿了把椅子，放在桶前，这样她就不需要踩，而且没有伤到她的背，也没有造成任何意外的伤害。然后她把罐子放在她面前，打开了水龙头，当啤酒开着的时候，她不会让她的眼睛闲晃，但是她看着墙，和经过多次的观察，看见一个接轴完全在她上面，泥瓦匠们不小心离开那里。
现译: 从前有个人，女儿名叫聪明的埃尔茜。姑娘长大了，父亲说：“该给她办婚事了。”“是啊，”母亲说，“只盼有人肯来娶她。”终于从远地来了个汉斯向她求婚。可他有个条件：聪明的埃尔茜得是真聪明才行。“噢，”父亲说，“她的心眼可够使的。”“噢，”母亲说，“风打街上来，她能看见，苍蝇咳嗽，她能听见。”“好，”汉斯说，“若不是真聪明，我可不娶。”几个人坐下来吃饭，饭吃得差不多了，母亲说：“埃尔茜，到地窖去打些啤酒来。”聪明的埃尔茜从墙上取下酒罐，下地窖去。她怕走着走着嫌时间长，一路笃笃地敲着罐盖。到了下面，她先搬来一把椅子，放在酒桶前。这样她就不必弯下腰，免得伤腰，也免得遇上什么意外。然后她把罐子摆在面前，拧开龙头。啤酒往外淌的时候，她也不肯叫眼睛闲着，便仰脸望着墙。在这儿看看，在那儿看看，看了好一阵，终于瞧见自己头顶上正好搁着一把鹤嘴锄，是泥瓦匠不小心落在那里的。

中文章名: 聪明的埃尔茜
英文证据: Then Clever Elsie began to weep and said: ‘If I get Hans, and we have a child, and he grows big, and we send him into the cellar here to draw beer, then the pick-axe will fall on his head and kill him.’ Then she sat and wept and screamed with all the strength of her body, over the misfortune which lay before her. Those upstairs waited for the drink, but Clever Elsie still did not come. Then the woman said to the servant: ‘Just go down into the cellar and see where Elsie is.’ The maid went and found her sitting in front of the barrel, screaming loudly. ‘Elsie why do you weep?’ asked the maid. ‘Ah,’ she answered, ‘have I not reason to weep? If I get Hans, and we have a child, and he grows big, and has to draw beer here, the pick-axe will perhaps fall on his head, and kill him.’ Then said the maid: ‘What a clever Elsie we have!’ and sat down beside her and began loudly to weep over the misfortune. After a while, as the maid did not come back, and those upstairs were thirsty for the beer, the man said to the boy: ‘Just go down into the cellar and see where Elsie and the girl are.’ The boy went down, and there sat Clever Elsie and the girl both weeping together. Then he asked: ‘Why are you weeping?’ ‘Ah,’ said Elsie, ‘have I not reason to weep? If I get Hans, and we have a child, and he grows big, and has to draw beer here, the pick-axe will fall on his head and kill him.’ Then said the boy: ‘What a clever Elsie we have!’ and sat down by her, and likewise began to howl loudly. Then said the mother likewise: ‘What a clever Elsie we have!’ and sat down and wept with them. The man upstairs waited a short time, but as his wife did not come back and his thirst grew ever greater, he said: ‘I must go into the cellar myself and see where Elsie is.’ But when he got into the cellar, and they were all sitting together crying, and he heard the reason, and that Elsie’s child was the cause, and the Elsie might perhaps bring one into the world some day, and that he might be killed by the pick-axe, if he should happen to be sitting beneath it, drawing beer just at the very time when it fell down, he cried: ‘Oh, what a clever Elsie!’ and sat down, and likewise wept with them. 现译: 聪明的埃尔茜便哭了起来，说：“要是我嫁了汉斯，咱们生个孩子，孩子渐渐长大，咱们打发他下地窖接啤酒，这把锄头就会砸到他的脑袋，把他砸死。”她坐在那里，为这桩等在前头的惨事使出全身的力气，哭啊，叫啊。楼上的人等酒喝，聪明的埃尔茜迟迟不来。母亲对女佣说：“你下地窖看看埃尔茜在哪里。”女佣下去，看见她坐在桶前放声大哭。“埃尔茜，为什么哭呀？”女佣问。“唉，”她回答，“我能不哭吗？要是我嫁了汉斯，咱们生个孩子，孩子渐渐长大，得来这里接啤酒，这把锄头说不定会掉在他脑袋上，把他砸死。”“咱们的埃尔茜可真聪明！”女佣说着，坐到她身边，为这桩惨事放声哭了起来。又过了一会儿，女佣还没回来，上头的人渴得想喝啤酒。父亲便对小伙计说：“你下地窖看看，埃尔茜和女佣都去哪儿了。”小伙计下去，看见聪明的埃尔茜和女佣并排坐着哭。他问：“你们为什么哭？”“唉，”埃尔茜说，“我能不哭吗？要是我嫁了汉斯，咱们生个孩子，孩子渐渐长大，得来这里接啤酒，这把锄头就会掉在他脑袋上，把他砸死。”“咱们的埃尔茜可真聪明！”小伙计坐到她身边，也扯开嗓子号哭。上头的人等着小伙计，可他迟迟不回，父亲便对母亲说：“你下地窖看看埃尔茜在哪儿！”母亲下楼，发现三个人正哭成一团，便打听缘故。埃尔茜也告诉她，将来的孩子长大了，得来接啤酒，锄头一掉，就要叫锄头砸死。母亲也说：“咱们的埃尔茜可真聪明！”便坐下来一同哭。父亲在上面等了一小阵，妻子还是不回来，自己却越来越渴，便说：“我得亲自下地窖看看埃尔茜在哪儿。”到了地窖，他见众人围坐痛哭，又听说了缘故，起因原来是埃尔茜的孩子，也就是埃尔茜将来说不定会生的一个孩子，他要是恰好在那把锄头掉下来的时候，坐在它底下接啤酒，说不定就给砸死。父亲喊道：“哎哟，埃尔茜可真聪明！”便也坐下跟他们哭。准新郎独自留在楼上，等了很久也不见一个人回来，便想：“他们一定在下面等我。我也得下去看看，他们究竟在做什么。”他一下楼，只见五个人坐在那里，叫得凄惨，哭得伤心，一个赛过一个。“到底遇上了什么祸事？”他问。“唉，亲爱的汉斯，”埃尔茜说，“要是我们俩成了亲，有了个孩子，孩子长大了，说不定我们会叫他来这儿接点喝的。上面落着的那把锄头要是掉下来，他的脑袋说不定就开花了。你说，我们能不哭吗？”“来吧，”汉斯说，“要操持我的家，有这么多见识就够了。你既是这么聪明的埃尔茜，我娶你。”他抓住她的手，领她一道上楼，和她结了婚。

中文章名: 聪明的埃尔茜
英文证据: After Hans had had her some time, he said: ‘Wife, I am going out to work and earn some money for us; go into the field and cut the corn that we may have some bread.’ ‘Yes, dear Hans, I will do that.’ After Hans had gone away, she cooked herself some good broth and took it into the field with her. When she came to the field she said to herself: ‘What shall I do; shall I cut first, or shall I eat first? Oh, I will eat first.’ Then she drank her cup of broth and when she was fully satisfied, she once more said: ‘What shall I do? Shall I cut first, or shall I sleep first? I will sleep first.’ Then she lay down among the corn and fell asleep. Hans had been at home for a long time, but Elsie did not come; then said he: ‘What a clever Elsie I have; she is so industrious that she does not even come home to eat.’ But when evening came and she still stayed away, Hans went out to see what she had cut, but nothing was cut, and she was lying among the corn asleep. Then Hans hastened home and brought a fowler’s net with little bells and hung it round about her, and she still went on sleeping. Then he ran home, shut the house-door, and sat down in his chair and worked. At length, when it was quite dark, Clever Elsie awoke and when she got up there was a jingling all round about her, and the bells rang at each step which she took. Then she was alarmed, and became uncertain whether she really was Clever Elsie or not, and said: ‘Is it I, or is it not I?’ But she knew not what answer to make to this, and stood for a time in doubt; at length she thought: ‘I will go home and ask if it be I, or if it be not I, they will be sure to know.’ She ran to the door of her own house, but it was shut; then she knocked at the window and cried: ‘Hans, is Elsie within?’ ‘Yes,’ answered Hans, ‘she is within.’ Hereupon she was terrified, and said: ‘Ah, heavens! Then it is not I,’ and went to another door; but when the people heard the jingling of the bells they would not open it, and she could get in nowhere. Then she ran out of the village, and no one has seen her since.
原译: 汉斯生了她一段时间之后，他说：维夫，我要出去工作，为我们挣些钱；你到田里去切玉米，我们也许有面包。'是的，亲爱的汉斯，我会的。汉斯走了之后她自己煮了些好汤然后带她去田里。当她来到田里的时候，她对自己说：我要做什么呢？还是先剪刀呢？还是先吃呢？不然，我要先吃。然后，她喝了一杯咖啡，当她完全满意的时候，她又说：我该怎么办呢？我先剪刀，还是先睡呢？我先睡呢？然后她躺在玉米里睡着了。汉斯在家里待了很久，但埃尔西没有来，他说：我有一个聪明的埃尔西，她非常勤奋，甚至不回家吃饭。但当晚上到来，她仍然不走，汉斯出去看她切的是什么，但没有切到什么，她躺在玉米里睡觉。然后汉斯匆忙回家带了一只小铃的鸡网围绕她，她仍然在睡觉。然后他跑回家关上门坐在椅子上工作。很长一段时间，当天很黑，聪明的埃尔西醒来，当她起床时，有个响铃响起围绕她，钟声响起每一步她采取。她惊慌失措，不知自己是不是聪明的埃尔西，她说：难道我是聪明的吗？她不知道这件事的答案是什么，她怀疑地坚持了一个时期。她想道：我要回家去问问，如果我不是，他们必定知道。她跑到自己家门口，但门被关上了。 然后她敲着窗户，喊道：“汉斯，艾尔西在里面吗？” “是的，汉斯回答说，她在里面。”于是，她惊恐地说：天呀！那不是我要的，而是我要到另一扇门去。当众人听见铃声的时候，他们不敢打开它，而她不知不觉。然后她从村子里跑出来之后就没人见过她了。
现译: 汉斯娶她过了一阵，对她说：“老婆，我要出去干活，给咱们挣点钱。你去田里割谷子，咱们才有面包吃。”“好呀，亲爱的汉斯，我这就去。”汉斯一走，她先给自己煮了一碗好汤，带到田里去。到了田头，她对自己说：“我怎么办好呢？先割谷子，还是先吃饭？噢，先吃吧。”她喝下那碗汤，肚子饱得不能再饱，又对自己说：“我怎么办好呢？先割谷子，还是先睡觉？先睡吧。”便往谷子中间一躺，睡着了。汉斯已经回家好久，还不见埃尔茜，便说：“我这埃尔茜真聪明！干活这么勤快，饭都顾不上回家吃。”可是到了傍晚还不见她，他就出去看她割了多少。田里一根谷子也没割，埃尔茜正躺在庄稼中间熟睡。汉斯赶回家，取来一张缀着小铃铛的捕鸟网，把她从头到脚罩住。她照睡不误。他又跑回家，关上屋门，坐回自己的椅子上干活。等聪明的埃尔茜终于醒来，天已经全黑了。她一起身，四周叮铃铃地响，走一步，铃铛便响一步。她慌了神，拿不准自己到底是不是聪明的埃尔茜，便说：“是我呢，还是不是我呢？”她不知道该怎么答，站在那里犯了好一阵疑，最后想：“我回家问问，是我，还是不是我。他们准知道。”她跑到自家门口，门却关着，便敲敲窗喊：“汉斯，埃尔茜在家吗？”“在呀，”汉斯回答，“她就在家里。”她吓坏了，说：“啊，天哪！那么就不是我了。”她转去敲别家的门，可人们一听铃铛叮铃铃响，都不肯开门。她哪一户也进不去，便跑出了村子。从那以后，再没有人见过她。

中文章名: 荆棘丛里的吝啬鬼
英文证据: A farmer had a faithful and diligent servant, who had worked hard for him three years, without having been paid any wages. At last it came into the man’s head that he would not go on thus without pay any longer; so he went to his master, and said, ‘I have worked hard for you a long time, I will trust to you to give me what I deserve to have for my trouble.’ The farmer was a sad miser, and knew that his man was very simple-hearted; so he took out threepence, and gave him for every year’s service a penny. The poor fellow thought it was a great deal of money to have, and said to himself, ‘Why should I work hard, and live here on bad fare any longer? I can now travel into the wide world, and make myself merry.’ With that he put his money into his purse, and set out, roaming over hill and valley.
原译: 农民有一个忠诚和勤奋的仆人，他为他辛勤工作了三年，没有领到任何工资。终于有人想到，他不能再这样不领薪水了。他去找他的主人说：我为你们辛苦了很久，我一定信任你们，我要为我的烦恼而赐予我我应得的。农夫是个悲哀的人，他知道自己的男人是心地简洁的。他拿出三便士，每年为他供一分钱。可怜的家伙认为拥有一笔大钱，然后对自己说，“我为什么要努力工作，还要在糟糕的票价上生活下去？我现在可以去环游世界，让我自己快乐。”他把钱放进钱包里跑到山上和山谷里。
现译: 有个庄稼人，雇着一个忠厚勤快的长工。长工为他辛辛苦苦做了三年，一文工钱也没拿到。终于有一天，长工想到，不能再这样白干下去了。他便对主人说：“我替你卖力干了这么久，你看我的辛苦值多少，就给我多少吧。我信得过你。”这个庄稼人是个十足的吝啬鬼，深知长工心眼儿实在，便掏出三枚便士，一年工夫算一枚。可怜的长工还当是一大笔钱，心想：“我何必再在这儿吃粗茶淡饭，做苦工呢？如今我大可以上广阔的世界去走走，快活快活。”他把钱装进钱袋，翻山越谷，四处漫游去了。

中文章名: 荆棘丛里的吝啬鬼
英文证据: As he jogged along over the fields, singing and dancing, a little dwarf met him, and asked him what made him so merry. ‘Why, what should make me down-hearted?’ said he; ‘I am sound in health and rich in purse, what should I care for? I have saved up my three years’ earnings and have it all safe in my pocket.’ ‘How much may it come to?’ said the little man. ‘Full threepence,’ replied the countryman. ‘I wish you would give them to me,’ said the other; ‘I am very poor.’ Then the man pitied him, and gave him all he had; and the little dwarf said in return, ‘As you have such a kind honest heart, I will grant you three wishes--one for every penny; so choose whatever you like.’ Then the countryman rejoiced at his good luck, and said, ‘I like many things better than money: first, I will have a bow that will bring down everything I shoot at; secondly, a fiddle that will set everyone dancing that hears me play upon it; and thirdly, I should like that everyone should grant what I ask.’ The dwarf said he should have his three wishes; so he gave him the bow and fiddle, and went his way.
原译: 当他跑到田地上唱歌跳舞时一个矮人遇见了他问他什么让他这么快乐。他说：为什么我心怀怨恨呢？他说：我身体健康，钱包丰富，我何必关心呢？我已节省了三年的收入，我的口袋里有它。小家伙说：“能赚到多少钱？”“三便士，”回答乡下人。另一个人说：我的确希望你们把它交给我，我确是贫穷的。然后，那人可怜他，并把他的一切赏赐他。那矮人说：你有一个善良的心，我就给你三个愿望，一个是每一分钱。你随便选择吧。然后这位乡下人为他的好运而高兴，他说：“我喜欢许多比钱更好的东西：首先，我将有一个弓，使我射的任何东西落下；其次，一个小提琴，使每个人都能跳舞，听到我弹奏；第三，我希望每个人都能答应我的要求。”矮人说，他应该有他的三个愿望，所以他给了他弓和小提琴，然后走他的路。
现译: 他又唱又跳，快步穿过田野，迎面遇到一个小矮人，问他为什么这样快活。“嗨，我有什么可垂头丧气的？”长工说，“身子骨结实，钱袋又满，有什么可愁的？我三年的工钱都攒下来了，好端端地揣在兜里。”“那一共是多少？”小人儿问。“整整三个便士！”乡下人答道。“求你把它们给我吧，”小人儿说，“我穷得很。”长工可怜他，把全部家当给了他。小矮人回报他说：“你这样老实心善，我准你许三个愿，一个便士算一个。你喜欢什么，只管挑。”“我喜欢的好多东西都比钱强，”乡下人庆幸自己有好运气，说，“头一样，我要一张百发百中的弓。第二样，我要一把提琴，人人一听见我拉琴就得跳舞。第三样，我希望我向谁求一件事，谁就得答应。”小矮人允了他三个心愿，把弓和提琴交给他，走自己的路去了。

中文章名: 荆棘丛里的吝啬鬼
英文证据: Our honest friend journeyed on his way too; and if he was merry before, he was now ten times more so. He had not gone far before he met an old miser: close by them stood a tree, and on the topmost twig sat a thrush singing away most joyfully. ‘Oh, what a pretty bird!’ said the miser; ‘I would give a great deal of money to have such a one.’ ‘If that’s all,’ said the countryman, ‘I will soon bring it down.’ Then he took up his bow, and down fell the thrush into the bushes at the foot of the tree. The miser crept into the bush to find it; but directly he had got into the middle, his companion took up his fiddle and played away, and the miser began to dance and spring about, capering higher and higher in the air. The thorns soon began to tear his clothes till they all hung in rags about him, and he himself was all scratched and wounded, so that the blood ran down. ‘Oh, for heaven’s sake!’ cried the miser, ‘Master! master! pray let the fiddle alone. What have I done to deserve this?’ ‘Thou hast shaved many a poor soul close enough,’ said the other; ‘thou art only meeting thy reward’: so he played up another tune. Then the miser began to beg and promise, and offered money for his liberty; but he did not come up to the musician’s price for some time, and he danced him along brisker and brisker, and the miser bid higher and higher, till at last he offered a round hundred of florins that he had in his purse, and had just gained by cheating some poor fellow. When the countryman saw so much money, he said, ‘I will agree to your proposal.’ So he took the purse, put up his fiddle, and travelled on very pleased with his bargain.
原译: 我们的诚实朋友也在路上旅行；如果他以前快乐的话，现在他比以前多十倍。在他遇见一个古老的乞丐之前，他没有走远，他俩就站在那棵树旁，他俩坐在树上，坐在树上，大笑著唱着。乞丐说：你这只小鸟真美！他说：我要花很多钱才能养一只小鸟。乡下人说：我不久就会把它弄下来。然后他抬起弓来，把树脚上的灌木放下来。流浪汉钻进灌木丛寻找它；但他直接进入了中间，他的同伴拿起他的小提琴玩耍，而流浪汉开始跳舞和跳起来，在空中上上下上下上下。刺很快开始撕裂他的衣服直到他们都挂在布上有关他，他自己被刮伤，血流下来。他说：伤风败俗者啊！师傅啊！请你让小提琴独行吧。我为它做了甚么事呢？他说：你把许多贫穷的人剃得够近了。你说：你只受你的报酬。他就弹奏了另一首曲子。之后，那个乞丐开始乞讨和许诺，为他的自由提供了钱；但他有段时间没有付出音乐家的代价，他用漂浮器和漂浮器跳他，而那个不诚实者出价更高，直到最后他拿出了上百个佛罗林，他从他的钱包里拿出了钱，而且刚刚欺骗了一个可怜的人。当乡下人看到这么多钱时他说：“我同意你的提议。”于是他拿了钱包举起小提琴并带着非常满意的价钱旅行。
现译: 咱们这位老实朋友也继续上路。先前若算快活，这会儿比先前快活了十倍。没走多远，他碰见一个老吝啬鬼。近旁有棵树，树梢最高的一根细枝上停着只歌鸫，唱得正欢。“噢，多漂亮的鸟！”吝啬鬼说，“能弄到这么一只，花多少钱我也乐意。”“要是就这么点事，”乡下人说，“我立刻就把它弄下来。”他举起弓，歌鸫应声落在树脚的灌木丛里。吝啬鬼钻进去找，才钻到当中，同伴便拿起提琴拉起来。他不由自主地又跳又蹦，越蹦越高。荆棘很快扯破他的衣裳，把一条条碎布挂满他全身，他自己也被划得遍体是伤，鲜血直流。“啊，看在上天的分上！”吝啬鬼喊道，“好先生！好先生！求你别拉了。我做了什么，要遭这份罪？”“多少穷人都让你刮光了油水，”对方说，“这不过是你应得的回报。”说着又拉起一个调。吝啬鬼便又哀求，又许愿，开价赎自己出去。琴手起先嫌价钱不够，越拉越欢，逼得他越跳越快，他也只得越出越高，最后答应把钱袋里整整一百弗罗林全给他。这笔钱，他刚从一个可怜鬼那里骗来。乡下人看见这么多钱，说：“好吧，就依你。”他收下钱袋，收起提琴，得意于这桩买卖，继续赶路。

At last he went to the judge, and complained that a rascal had robbed him of his money, and beaten him into the bargain; and that the fellow who did it carried a bow at his back and a fiddle hung round his neck. 中文章名: 荆棘丛里的吝啬鬼
英文证据: So away he was taken; but as he stood on the steps he said, ‘My Lord Judge, grant me one last request.’ ‘Anything but thy life,’ replied the other. ‘No,’ said he, ‘I do not ask my life; only to let me play upon my fiddle for the last time.’ The miser cried out, ‘Oh, no! no! for heaven’s sake don’t listen to him! don’t listen to him!’ But the judge said, ‘It is only this once, he will soon have done.’ The fact was, he could not refuse the request, on account of the dwarf’s third gift.
原译: 他确已被俘虏了。当他站在两座阶梯上的时候，他说：我的主啊！求你再答应我一个请求。他说：除你之外，别的事，你只负你的生命的责任。他说：他说：我的确不求生，只愿我最后一次玩小提琴。那个吝啬鬼喊道：“哦，不！不！看在老天的份上，不要听他的话！不要听他的话！”法官说：这只是一次，他不久就成功了。事实是，他不能拒绝请求，因为侏儒的第三个礼物。
现译: 乡下人就被带走了。站在绞架台阶上，他说：“法官大人，请准我最后一个请求。”“只要别求我饶命，什么都行。”法官答道。“不，”他说，“我不求饶命，只求准我最后再拉一回琴。”吝啬鬼大叫：“不，不！看在老天分上，别听他的！别听他的！”法官却说：“就这一次，他很快就拉完了。”其实，有小矮人的第三件礼物在，他也拒绝不了这个请求。

中文章名: 荆棘丛里的吝啬鬼
英文证据: Then the miser said, ‘Bind me fast, bind me fast, for pity’s sake.’ But the countryman seized his fiddle, and struck up a tune, and at the first note judge, clerks, and jailer were in motion; all began capering, and no one could hold the miser. At the second note the hangman let his prisoner go, and danced also, and by the time he had played the first bar of the tune, all were dancing together--judge, court, and miser, and all the people who had followed to look on. At first the thing was merry and pleasant enough; but when it had gone on a while, and there seemed to be no end of playing or dancing, they began to cry out, and beg him to leave off; but he stopped not a whit the more for their entreaties, till the judge not only gave him his life, but promised to return him the hundred florins.
原译: 不义者说：你们快把我捆起来吧！你们快把我绑起来吧！但乡下人抓住了他的小提琴，敲响了一支曲子，法官，书记员和狱卒在第一个音符上运动起来，所有人都开始捉弄，没人能忍受这不幸。第二张纸条上绞刑犯放走也跳舞了当他演奏第一支曲子的时候所有人都在一起跳舞法官庭上。起初，事情是快乐的，是愉快的；但是当事情持续一段时间，而且游戏或舞蹈似乎没有结束的时候，他们开始喊叫，要求他离开；但他没有为了他们的恩惠而停止任何努力，直到法官不仅给了他生命，而且答应归还他那一百弗罗林。
现译: 吝啬鬼赶紧喊：“把我绑紧点！行行好，把我绑住！”可乡下人一把抄起提琴，奏起一支曲子。第一个音符一响，法官、书记员和看守就都动了起来，人人手舞足蹈，没人还能按住吝啬鬼。第二个音符一响，刽子手松开犯人，也跳起舞来。第一小节还没拉完，所有人已经一齐跳起来了，法官、满庭人等、吝啬鬼，以及一路跟来看热闹的百姓，谁也没落下。起初还挺快活有趣，时间一长，琴声舞步似乎都没个尽头，众人便喊啊、求啊，请他歇歇手。他哪肯因为哀求停上一停！直到法官不但饶了他的命，还答应把一百弗罗林还给他。

英文证据: Then he called to the miser, and said, ‘Tell us now, you vagabond, where you got that gold, or I shall play on for your amusement only,’ ‘I stole it,’ said the miser in the presence of all the people; ‘I acknowledge that I stole it, and that you earned it fairly.’ Then the countryman stopped his fiddle, and left the miser to take his place at the gallows.
原译: 他喊叫不义的人们说：你们告诉我吧，你们从那里获得黄金，或者我只为你们娱乐而游戏。不义的人们说：我偷黄金，我承认你们曾偷它，你们曾公平报酬它。然后那个乡下人停了小提琴任由那个混蛋在绞刑架上取代他的位置。

中文章名: 灰姑娘
英文证据: The wife of a rich man fell sick; and when she felt that her end drew nigh, she called her only daughter to her bed-side, and said, ‘Always be a good girl, and I will look down from heaven and watch over you.’ Soon afterwards she shut her eyes and died, and was buried in the garden; and the little girl went every day to her grave and wept, and was always good and kind to all about her. And the snow fell and spread a beautiful white covering over the grave; but by the time the spring came, and the sun had melted it away again, her father had married another wife. This new wife had two daughters of her own, that she brought home with her; they were fair in face but foul at heart, and it was now a sorry time for the poor little girl. ‘What does the good-for-nothing want in the parlour?’ said they; ‘they who would eat bread should first earn it; away with the kitchen-maid!’ Then they took away her fine clothes, and gave her an old grey frock to put on, and laughed at her, and turned her into the kitchen.
原译: 富人的妻子病了。当她觉得自己的结局临近的时候，她叫她唯一的女儿到她的床边去，她说：你永远是一个善良的女孩，我将从天上俯视你。不久之后，她闭上眼睛死去，被埋在花园里；小女孩每天都去坟墓哭泣，对她的一切总是很好和善良的。雪落下，把美丽的白色遮盖在坟墓上；但等到春天来临，太阳再次融化，她的父亲又娶了另一个妻子。这名新妻子有两个女儿，她带着两个女儿回家；她们面对面很公平，但内心却很脏，现在对这个可怜的小女孩来说，这是一个不幸的时刻。他们说：善人们在酒馆里想干什么呢？他们妄言：谁吃面包，谁先吃；谁以饭为食；谁以饭。然后他们拿走了她漂亮的衣服，给了她一个旧的灰色衣服穿上，并嘲笑她，把她变成了厨房。
现译: 有个富人的妻子生了病。她知道自己快不行了，叫来唯一的女儿，拉到床边对她说：“要永远做个好姑娘，我会从天上望着你，守护你。”不久，她便闭眼死了，葬在花园里。小姑娘每天都去坟前哭，对身边的人始终和善厚道。雪落下来，给坟头盖上一层漂亮的白被。等到春天来临，太阳又把白雪晒化，父亲已经娶了新妻子。新妻把自己生的两个女儿也带了来。两人面容美丽，心地却丑恶。可怜的小姑娘，苦日子到了。“这没用的东西待在起居室干什么？”她们说，“要吃面包，就得先把面包挣来。厨房丫头，还不快滚！”她们夺去她的好衣裳，扔来一件旧灰裙让她穿上，又嘲笑她，把她赶进厨房。

中文章名: 灰姑娘
英文证据: There she was forced to do hard work; to rise early before daylight, to bring the water, to make the fire, to cook and to wash. Besides that, the sisters plagued her in all sorts of ways, and laughed at her. In the evening when she was tired, she had no bed to lie down on, but was made to lie by the hearth among the ashes; and as this, of course, made her always dusty and dirty, they called her Ashputtel.
原译: 在那里，她被迫做艰苦的工作；在白天之前早起，带水，生火，做饭和洗手。除此之外，姐妹们还用各种方式折磨她，嘲笑她。在她疲倦的夜晚，她没有床可以躺下，却被迫躺在骨灰中的灵洞里；当然，这让她总是灰尘和脏兮兮的，他们叫她阿什普特尔。
现译: 她在那里不得不干重活。天还没亮便起身，提水、生火、做饭、洗衣。那对姐妹还百般刁难，事事取笑她。到了晚上，她累坏了，却没有一张床可躺，只能睡在炉边的灰堆里。自然，她总是灰头土脸，脏兮兮的，大家便管她叫灰姑娘。

中文章名: 灰姑娘
英文证据: It happened once that the father was going to the fair, and asked his wife’s daughters what he should bring them. ‘Fine clothes,’ said the first; ‘Pearls and diamonds,’ cried the second. ‘Now, child,’ said he to his own daughter, ‘what will you have?’ ‘The first twig, dear father, that brushes against your hat when you turn your face to come homewards,’ said she. Then he bought for the first two the fine clothes and pearls and diamonds they had asked for: and on his way home, as he rode through a green copse, a hazel twig brushed against him, and almost pushed off his hat: so he broke it off and brought it away; and when he got home he gave it to his daughter. Then she took it, and went to her mother’s grave and planted it there; and cried so much that it was watered with her tears; and there it grew and became a fine tree. Three times every day she went to it and cried; and soon a little bird came and built its nest upon the tree, and talked with her, and watched over her, and brought her whatever she wished for.
原译: 父亲曾经去集市问妻子的女儿他应该带什么来。第一条说 、 衣服好 。 第二条哭著说 、 珍珠 、 钻石。孩子 、 他对自己的女儿说 、 你要甚么呢 。 他说 、 你转脸回家时 、 戴帽子的首枝子。然后，他为前两批人购买了他们要求的精美衣服、珍珠和钻石：在他回家的路上，他骑着一辆绿色的警车，一辆Hazel 树枝刷他，差点脱下他的帽子，他把帽子拆掉，拿掉；他回家后，把帽子给了女儿。然后，她拿起它，走到她母亲的坟墓里，然后把它埋在那里。她大喊大叫，大哭，那棵树就长成一棵美树。她每天到那座乐园来三次喊叫，很快，一只小鸟来到树上筑巢，与她交谈，看着她，把她所希望的带来。
现译: 有一回父亲要去赶集，问妻子的两个女儿，要他带什么回来。“漂亮的衣裳。”第一个说。“珍珠和钻石！”第二个叫道。“孩子，”他又问亲生女儿，“你想要什么？”她说：“亲爱的父亲，在您调头回家的路上，头一根碰着您帽子的树枝。”父亲依前两个女儿所求，买了衣裳、珍珠和钻石。回程骑马穿过一小片绿林，一枝榛树枝擦到他，差点把帽子碰掉。他就折下树枝带走，到家给了亲生女儿。她拿去种在母亲坟前。她流了那么多的泪，泪水浇灌了树枝，它就在那里长成一棵美丽的树。每天她去树下哭三次。不久，一只小鸟飞来，在树上筑了巢。它陪她说话，守护着她，她想要什么，它便给她带来什么。

中文章名: 灰姑娘
英文证据: Now it happened that the king of that land held a feast, which was to last three days; and out of those who came to it his son was to choose a bride for himself.
