原译: 此时此刻女王失去了她最美的戒指被怀疑偷走了落入了那个被允许去任何地方的忠诚的仆人手中。国王命令把他带到他面前并用愤怒的言语威胁他除非他能在明天之前指出小偷否则他应该被看成有罪并被处死。他宣布自己无罪，但未获任何更好的答复。
现译: 偏巧就在这一天，王后丢了自己最漂亮的戒指。心腹仆人哪儿都去得，偷戒指的嫌疑落到了他身上。国王下令叫他来，在他面前发了火，威胁说若是明天以前指不出窃贼，他自己就将被认作罪犯，处以死刑。不论他怎样申明清白，国王只管这么一句，便把他打发了出去。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 白蛇
英文证据: In his trouble and fear he went down into the courtyard and took thought how to help himself out of his trouble. Now some ducks were sitting together quietly by a brook and taking their rest; and, whilst they were making their feathers smooth with their bills, they were having a confidential conversation together. The servant stood by and listened. They were telling one another of all the places where they had been waddling about all the morning, and what good food they had found; and one said in a pitiful tone: ‘Something lies heavy on my stomach; as I was eating in haste I swallowed a ring which lay under the queen’s window.’ The servant at once seized her by the neck, carried her to the kitchen, and said to the cook: ‘Here is a fine duck; pray, kill her.’ ‘Yes,’ said the cook, and weighed her in his hand; ‘she has spared no trouble to fatten herself, and has been waiting to be roasted long enough.’ So he cut off her head, and as she was being dressed for the spit, the queen’s ring was found inside her.
原译: 在他的麻烦和恐惧中，他走进院子，思考如何帮助自己摆脱麻烦。现在有些鸭子静静地坐在溪边休息；当他们用钞票把羽毛弄得平滑时，他们一起进行了秘密谈话。仆人站着听。他们对彼此说：他们为甚么在早晨旅行，他们发现什么食物？有人说：我胃里有重物，我吃得很快，我吞下了一只戒指，它落在女王的窗户下。仆人立刻抓住他的脖子 、 抱着他到厨房 、 对厨师说 、 这是一只好鸭子 、 求你宰了他 。 厨师说 、 是 、 他手中重了他 、 毫不费力 、 使自己肥大 、 等了足够的时间。所以他砍下她的头，当她穿的衣服吐口水，女王的戒指被发现在她体内。
现译: 他又害怕又苦恼，走下庭院，琢磨怎样才能脱身。小溪旁坐着几只鸭子，不声不响地歇脚，一边低头用嘴理顺羽毛，一边凑在一起说私房话。仆人站在一旁听。它们谈起整个早晨摇摇摆摆去了哪些地方，又找到了什么好食物。有一只可怜巴巴地说：“我肚子里坠着个什么东西，好沉！方才我吃得太急，把王后窗子底下的一枚戒指给吞了。”仆人一把抓住它的脖子，提到厨房，对厨子说：“这只鸭子真肥，劳驾把它宰了吧。”“是啊，”厨子托在手上掂了掂，“它养起膘来可真不惜力气，眼巴巴等了够久，该烤熟上桌了。”厨子砍下鸭头，收拾鸭子预备穿烤叉的时候，王后的戒指就在它肚里找到了。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 白蛇
英文证据: The servant could now easily prove his innocence; and the king, to make amends for the wrong, allowed him to ask a favour, and promised him the best place in the court that he could wish for. The servant refused everything, and only asked for a horse and some money for travelling, as he had a mind to see the world and go about a little. When his request was granted he set out on his way, and one day came to a pond, where he saw three fishes caught in the reeds and gasping for water. Now, though it is said that fishes are dumb, he heard them lamenting that they must perish so miserably, and, as he had a kind heart, he got off his horse and put the three prisoners back into the water. They leapt with delight, put out their heads, and cried to him: ‘We will remember you and repay you for saving us!’
原译: 仆人现在可以很容易地证明自己是无辜的；国王为不义而赎罪，允许他求情，并承诺他能在法庭中享有他所希望的最佳地位。仆人拒绝一切，只要求一匹马和一些旅行的钱，因为他有看到世界的头脑，走一点点路。当他的请求获得批准时，他开始在路上走动，有一天他来到一个池塘，在那里他看到三条鱼被渔具捕捉，并喘了气。虽然据说鱼是哑巴，他听到他们哀叹，他们必须如此惨痛地死去，和，因为他有一颗善良的心，他下了马，把三个囚犯放回水里。他们狂喜地跳出来，他们抬头对他说：我们必定要记住你，必定要以拯救我们的态度报答你。
现译: 仆人这下轻易就能证明自己清白。为补偿对他的冤枉，国王准他提一个请求，宫里最好的职位，只要他想要，便许给他。仆人一概谢绝，只求一匹马和些路费，他想出门走走，见识见识世界。国王应允，他便上路。一天，他来到一口池塘边，看见三条鱼困在芦苇间，张着嘴，苦苦盼水。常言道，鱼是哑巴，可他听见它们正在哀叹，眼看就要死得这么惨。他心地好，当即下马，把这三个囚徒放回水中。它们高高兴兴地一跳，探出头来朝他喊：“我们会记得你，要报答你的救命之恩！”
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 白蛇
英文证据: He rode on, and after a while it seemed to him that he heard a voice in the sand at his feet. He listened, and heard an ant-king complain: ‘Why cannot folks, with their clumsy beasts, keep off our bodies? That stupid horse, with his heavy hoofs, has been treading down my people without mercy!’ So he turned on to a side path and the ant-king cried out to him: ‘We will remember you--one good turn deserves another!’
原译: 他骑着马走了过了一段时间他似乎听到他脚边沙子的声音。他听他说：你们怎么不把那些笨拙的野兽从我们的身体里取出来呢？那匹笨马，和他的重蹄，曾不怜悯地踏倒我的宗族。他就转身而奔走，蚂蚁喊叫他说：我们必定要记住你们，一个善功的转折！
现译: 他骑马继续前行。过了一阵，仿佛听见脚下砂土间传来个声音。他仔细听去，是蚂蚁国王在抱怨：“人家就不能牵着那笨重的牲口，绕开我们的身体吗？那匹蠢马，铁沉的蹄子毫不留情地践踏我的臣民！”他便拐到旁边的小道上。蚂蚁国王大声朝他说：“我们会记得你！你帮了我们，我们也要帮你！”
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 白蛇
英文证据: The path led him into a wood, and there he saw two old ravens standing by their nest, and throwing out their young ones. ‘Out with you, you idle, good-for-nothing creatures!’ cried they; ‘we cannot find food for you any longer; you are big enough, and can provide for yourselves.’ But the poor young ravens lay upon the ground, flapping their wings, and crying: ‘Oh, what helpless chicks we are! We must shift for ourselves, and yet we cannot fly! What can we do, but lie here and starve?’ So the good young fellow alighted and killed his horse with his sword, and gave it to them for food. Then they came hopping up to it, satisfied their hunger, and cried: ‘We will remember you--one good turn deserves another!’
原译: 这条路把他引向了木头，在那里，他看到两只老乌鸦站在他们的巢穴旁，扔掉他们年轻的乌鸦。你们这些闲散的、无福的动物，你们出去吧！他们说：我们为你们求得食物，你们是足够大的，你们是能供养的。但可怜的小乌鸦躺在地上，挥舞翅膀，哭着说：我们是何等的无助的小鸡，我们必须为自己而转变，我们却不能飞，只能躺在这里挨饿。所以这位年轻好人用剑把马给人吃了。然后，他们忙着忙忙忙忙忙忙忙地忙忙忙忙忙忙，他们说：我们必定要记住你们，必定有一个更好的归宿。
现译: 小道通进树林。他看见两只老渡鸦守在巢边，把小渡鸦们往外扔。“出去吧，你们这些没用的懒家伙！”它们喊道，“我们再也养不起你们了。你们也够大，该自己找吃的了。”可怜的小渡鸦们伏在地上，扑打着翅膀叫道：“唉，我们这几只雏鸟，一点办法也没有！得靠自己过活，偏偏不会飞！除了躺在这里等着饿死，还能怎么办？”好心的年轻人下了马，用剑杀掉自己的马，给它们充饥。它们一蹦一跳凑过来，填饱肚子，叫道：“我们会记得你！你帮了我们，我们也要帮你！”
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 白蛇
英文证据: And now he had to use his own legs, and when he had walked a long way, he came to a large city. There was a great noise and crowd in the streets, and a man rode up on horseback, crying aloud: ‘The king’s daughter wants a husband; but whoever seeks her hand must perform a hard task, and if he does not succeed he will forfeit his life.’ Many had already made the attempt, but in vain; nevertheless when the youth saw the king’s daughter he was so overcome by her great beauty that he forgot all danger, went before the king, and declared himself a suitor.
原译: 现在他不得不用自己的腿，当他走了很长的路，他来到一个大城市。街上吵闹闹闹，有人骑马大喊：“国王的女儿想要一个丈夫，但凡想得到她的人，必须执行艰难的任务，如果他不成功，他将丧失生命。”许多人已经尝试过，但徒劳无功；然而，当青年看到国王的女儿时，她伟大的美貌使他战胜了她，他忘记了一切危险，来到国王面前，宣布自己是求婚者。
现译: 现在他只有靠自己的两条腿赶路了。他走了很长一段路，来到一座大城。街上人山人海，十分嘈杂。一个人骑马过来，高声宣告：“国王的女儿要招婿。谁来求婚，都得完成一桩难事，办不成，便要赔上性命。”在他以前，许多人都已尝试过，徒然送了性命。可年轻人一见公主，那绝世的美貌便叫他把一切危险忘了个干净。他上前去见国王，宣告自己要向公主求婚。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 白蛇
英文证据: So he was led out to the sea, and a gold ring was thrown into it, before his eyes; then the king ordered him to fetch this ring up from the bottom of the sea, and added: ‘If you come up again without it you will be thrown in again and again until you perish amid the waves.’ All the people grieved for the handsome youth; then they went away, leaving him alone by the sea.
原译: 他被带出海门，然后，他看见一个金戒指，就把它扔在海中。国王命令他从海中取出这个戒指，他又说：如果你再没有这个戒指，你就要被扔在海中，直到你在一个海浪中死亡。所有人都为英俊的青年而悲伤，然后离开，任凭他独自在海边。
现译: 于是人们领他到海边，当面把一枚金戒指扔向大海。国王命令他把戒指从海底捞上来，又说：“你若是空手浮上来，就会一回又一回被扔回海里，直到你葬身波涛。”众人都为这英俊的年轻人难过，随后纷纷离开，只留下他一个人在海边。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 白蛇
英文证据: He stood on the shore and considered what he should do, when suddenly he saw three fishes come swimming towards him, and they were the very fishes whose lives he had saved. The one in the middle held a mussel in its mouth, which it laid on the shore at the youth’s feet, and when he had taken it up and opened it, there lay the gold ring in the shell. Full of joy he took it to the king and expected that he would grant him the promised reward.
原译: 他站在岸边，思考了自己应该做什么，突然，他看到三条鱼游向他，鱼就是他救过的鱼。中间的那个嘴里拿着一只贝壳，放在幼年的脚边，当他拿起它打开它时，把金环放在壳里。他将它带给国王，他满怀喜悦，并期望他获得所应得的报酬。
现译: 他站在岸上，正想着怎么办，忽然看见三条鱼朝自己游过来。正是他救过性命的那三条。中间那条口里衔着一只海蚌，把它放在年轻人脚边。他捡起海蚌，一打开，看见金戒指正躺在壳里。他满心欢喜，把戒指拿去见国王，以为国王这下就会给他许诺的赏赐。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 白蛇
英文证据: But when the proud princess perceived that he was not her equal in birth, she scorned him, and required him first to perform another task. She went down into the garden and strewed with her own hands ten sacksful of millet-seed on the grass; then she said: ‘Tomorrow morning before sunrise these must be picked up, and not a single grain be wanting.’
原译: 但是当骄傲的公主发现自己在出生时不是她一样的时候，她就鄙视他，要求他先执行另一项任务。她走进园圃，亲手把十袋小米撒到草地上，她说：明天早晨之前，必须捡起这些果实，每颗果实，就一粒不缺。'，爱丽丝
现译: 可是高傲的公主发觉他与自己出身悬殊，很瞧不起他，要求他先去完成另一件事。她走下花园，亲手把整整十袋小米撒在草地上，又说：“明早日出以前，把它们全捡回来，一粒都不能少。”
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 白蛇
英文证据: The youth sat down in the garden and considered how it might be possible to perform this task, but he could think of nothing, and there he sat sorrowfully awaiting the break of day, when he should be led to death. But as soon as the first rays of the sun shone into the garden he saw all the ten sacks standing side by side, quite full, and not a single grain was missing. The ant-king had come in the night with thousands and thousands of ants, and the grateful creatures had by great industry picked up all the millet-seed and gathered them into the sacks.
原译: 年轻人坐在花园里，思考着如何完成这项任务，但他什么也想不出来，他在那里悲哀地坐着等待一天的休息，那时他应该被带去死。但是当太阳第一次照射到花园时他看到所有十袋一起完全满满的。蚂蚁在晚上带着成千上万的蚂蚁来到了这里伟大的工业所赐的感恩动物们把所有小米种子都捡起来把它们带到了麻袋里。
现译: 年轻人坐在花园里，想怎样才能办到，横竖想不出办法，只好忧愁地坐等天亮。天一亮，他就要被押去处死了。谁知太阳的第一缕光照进花园，他竟看见十个口袋并排立着，每袋都装得满满的，一粒也不缺。原来蚂蚁国王夜里带着成千上万只蚂蚁赶来，这些知恩的小生灵不辞辛苦，一粒一粒捡起所有的小米，尽数搬进袋中。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 白蛇
英文证据: Presently the king’s daughter herself came down into the garden, and was amazed to see that the young man had done the task she had given him. But she could not yet conquer her proud heart, and said: ‘Although he has performed both the tasks, he shall not be my husband until he had brought me an apple from the Tree of Life.’ The youth did not know where the Tree of Life stood, but he set out, and would have gone on for ever, as long as his legs would carry him, though he had no hope of finding it. After he had wandered through three kingdoms, he came one evening to a wood, and lay down under a tree to sleep. But he heard a rustling in the branches, and a golden apple fell into his hand. At the same time three ravens flew down to him, perched themselves upon his knee, and said: ‘We are the three young ravens whom you saved from starving; when we had grown big, and heard that you were seeking the Golden Apple, we flew over the sea to the end of the world, where the Tree of Life stands, and have brought you the apple.’ The youth, full of joy, set out homewards, and took the Golden Apple to the king’s beautiful daughter, who had now no more excuses left to make. They cut the Apple of Life in two and ate it together; and then her heart became full of love for him, and they lived in undisturbed happiness to a great age.
原译: 目前国王的女儿自己来到花园并惊讶地看到年轻人完成了她交给他的任务。她却不能征服自己的骄傲的心，她说：他确已完成这两件事了，但他不做我丈夫，直到他从生命之树上拿一个苹果来给我。年轻人不知道生命之树的位置，但他离开了，并且会一直继续下去，只要他的腿会抬着他，尽管他没有希望找到它。他经过三个王国之后，有一天晚上来到一棵木头旁，躺在一棵树下睡觉。但他听到树枝里有刺一只金苹果掉在他手里。与此同时，有三只乌鸦飞到他面前，坐在他的膝盖上，他说：我们是你从饥饿中拯救出来的三只年轻的乌鸦。当我们长大了，听说你正在寻找金苹果的时候，我们飞过海洋，飞到生命之树所在的世界尽头，把苹果带来了你。年轻人充满了欢乐回到家把金苹果带到国王的美丽女儿面前她现在没有借口了。他们把生命之苹果切成两半一起吃掉然后她的心充满了爱他，他们生活在一个伟大的时代。
现译: 不一会儿，公主亲自下花园来，见年轻人竟办成了她交代的事，大为惊奇。可她那颗高傲的心仍旧不肯低头，便说：“他虽办成了两桩事，还须给我带来生命之树上的一只苹果，才能做我丈夫。”年轻人不知道生命之树长在什么地方，仍旧动身了。虽然没有寻到的指望，只要双腿还走得动，他就打算走下去。走过三个王国，一天傍晚，他来到一片树林，在树下躺倒，准备睡觉。忽然枝叶窸窣作响，一只金苹果落进他手里。同时有三只渡鸦飞下来，停在他膝头，说：“我们就是你从饥饿中救下的三只小渡鸦。我们长大以后，听说你在找金苹果，就飞过大海，来到生命之树生长的世界尽头，给你把苹果带回来了。”年轻人欢欢喜喜踏上归途，把金苹果送到美丽的公主面前。她终于再没有可推托的借口。两人把生命之果切成两半，一起吃了。从这以后，她心中满是对他的爱。两人相伴到老，幸福的日子从没人来打扰。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 狼和七只小山羊
英文证据: There was once upon a time an old goat who had seven little kids, and loved them with all the love of a mother for her children. One day she wanted to go into the forest and fetch some food. So she called all seven to her and said: ‘Dear children, I have to go into the forest, be on your guard against the wolf; if he comes in, he will devour you all--skin, hair, and everything. The wretch often disguises himself, but you will know him at once by his rough voice and his black feet.’ The kids said: ‘Dear mother, we will take good care of ourselves; you may go away without any anxiety.’ Then the old one bleated, and went on her way with an easy mind.

中文章名: 杜松树

中文章名: 狐狸和马
英文证据: The poor horse was very melancholy, and wandered up and down in the wood, seeking some little shelter from the cold wind and rain. Presently a fox met him: ‘What’s the matter, my friend?’ said he, ‘why do you hang down your head and look so lonely and woe-begone?’ ‘Ah!’ replied the horse, ‘justice and avarice never dwell in one house; my master has forgotten all that I have done for him so many years, and because I can no longer work he has turned me adrift, and says unless I become stronger than a lion he will not take me back again; what chance can I have of that? he knows I have none, or he would not talk so.’
原译: 这匹可怜的马非常忧郁，上下徘徊在树林里，寻找一些避风港和雨点的避风港。现在有只狐狸遇见他，他说：我的朋友，你怎么啦？他说：你为什么把头挂在头上，而变成孤单和忧愁呢？他说：啊！他说：正义和贪婪绝不是同住的。我的主人已忘记了我为他所做的许多年。并且因为我不能再工作了，他让我漂泊，他说：除非我比狮子更强壮，否则他不会再把我带回去。我还能有什么样的机会呢？他知道我一无所有，或他不会说这样的话。
现译: 可怜的马心情低落，在树林里来来回回地走，想找个稍微能遮挡冷风寒雨的地方。不久遇见一只狐狸，问它：“怎么了，朋友？干吗低垂着头，这样孤单、这样愁苦？”“唉，”马回答，“公道和贪心从来不能住在同一屋檐下。我替主人卖了这么多年力气，他全忘了。如今只因我干不动活，他就把我赶出来，还说我非得比狮子强壮才肯让我回去。我哪里办得到？他知道我办不到，要不也不会这样说。”

英文证据: However, the fox bid him be of good cheer, and said, ‘I will help you; lie down there, stretch yourself out quite stiff, and pretend to be dead.’ The horse did as he was told, and the fox went straight to the lion who lived in a cave close by, and said to him, ‘A little way off lies a dead horse; come with me and you may make an excellent meal of his carcase.’ The lion was greatly pleased, and set off immediately; and when they came to the horse, the fox said, ‘You will not be able to eat him comfortably here; I’ll tell you what--I will tie you fast to his tail, and then you can draw him to your den, and eat him at your leisure.’

中文章名: 蓝灯
英文证据: There was once upon a time a soldier who for many years had served the king faithfully, but when the war came to an end could serve no longer because of the many wounds which he had received. The king said to him: ‘You may return to your home, I need you no longer, and you will not receive any more money, for he only receives wages who renders me service for them.’ Then the soldier did not know how to earn a living, went away greatly troubled, and walked the whole day, until in the evening he entered a forest. When darkness came on, he saw a light, which he went up to, and came to a house wherein lived a witch. ‘Do give me one night’s lodging, and a little to eat and drink,’ said he to her, ‘or I shall starve.’ ‘Oho!’ she answered, ‘who gives anything to a run-away soldier? Yet will I be compassionate, and take you in, if you will do what I wish.’ ‘What do you wish?’ said the soldier. ‘That you should dig all round my garden for me, tomorrow.’ The soldier consented, and next day laboured with all his strength, but could not finish it by the evening. ‘I see well enough,’ said the witch, ‘that you can do no more today, but I will keep you yet another night, in payment for which you must tomorrow chop me a load of wood, and chop it small.’ The soldier spent the whole day in doing it, and in the evening the witch proposed that he should stay one night more. ‘Tomorrow, you shall only do me a very trifling piece of work. Behind my house, there is an old dry well, into which my light has fallen, it burns blue, and never goes out, and you shall bring it up again.’ Next day the old woman took him to the well, and let him down in a basket. He found the blue light, and made her a signal to draw him up again. She did draw him up, but when he came near the edge, she stretched down her hand and wanted to take the blue light away from him. ‘No,’ said he, perceiving her evil intention, ‘I will not give you the light until I am standing with both feet upon the ground.’ The witch fell into a passion, let him fall again into the well, and went away.
原译: 曾经有一位军人，多年来忠实地为国王服务，但战争结束后，由于他遭受的许多创伤，他不能再服役了。国王对他说：你们可以回家去，我不需要你们了，你们也不再获得任何报酬。他只获得报酬，他为我服务。士兵不知如何谋生，于是大乱，整天走来走去，直到晚上他进入森林。当黑暗降临的时候，他看见一道光明，就升起它来到一座有女巫居住的房屋。他对我说：你使我有一个晚上，你使我稍稍地吃喝吧！他说：不然，我要饿死。她说：谁以任何物供给一个离家出走的士兵呢？我对于你们是慈悲的，你们可以收养你们，如果你们要做我所欲做的事。他说：你们想吃什么？“明天你应该为我挖遍花园。”该士兵同意，第二天他全力以赴，但未能在晚上完成。女巫说：“我看得够清楚了，” “今天你不能再做下去了，” “但我会留你一个晚上。这名士兵花了一整天时间这样做，在晚上，女巫建议他多呆一晚。明天，你只给我做一件小事。在我家后面，有一个老井，我的光线掉进水里，它烧成蓝色，再不出来，你再把它拿上来。第二天，那个老妇人带他到井里，让他在篮子里躺下。他发现了蓝色的光，并给她一个信号画他再次。她确实画了他，但是当他靠近边缘时，她伸出她的手，想把蓝色的灯从他身上带走。他说：不然！你猜想她有恶念，我就不把光明赏赐你，直到我双脚都站在地上。女巫陷入了激情让他再次掉进井里然后走了。
现译: 从前有个士兵，忠心耿耿为国王效力了许多年。战争结束时，他浑身是伤，再也当不了兵。国王对他说：“你可以回家了，我已经用不着你。往后你也领不到钱，只有为我效力的人才拿得到饷。”士兵不知该靠什么谋生，满怀愁苦地走了。他走了一整天，傍晚进入一座森林。天黑后，他望见一点灯光，循光走去，来到一座房子前，里面住着一个女巫。“请让我借宿一晚，给点吃的喝的，”他说，“不然我就要饿死了。”“哟！”她答道，“谁会给一个逃兵东西？好吧，我也发发慈悲，你要肯照我的意思办，我就收留你。”“你想让我做什么？”士兵说。“明天给我把花园四周的地都挖一遍。”士兵答应了。第二天他用尽全力干活，可直到傍晚也没能干完。“我看得出，”女巫说，“你今天确实干不动了。我再留你一晚。作为报酬，明天你得替我劈一车柴，要劈得细细的。”他花了整天劈柴。傍晚女巫又提议让他多住一晚：“明天只消替我干一桩极小的活。我屋后有一口干涸的老井，我的灯掉在里面了。它发着蓝光，永远不灭。你给我捞上来。”第二天，老婆子领他到井边，用篮子把他放下去。他找到蓝灯，向她打手势，叫她把他拉上去。她倒是往上拉了，可当他将近井沿，她便往下一伸手，想从他手里拿走蓝灯。“不，”他看出她没安好心，说，“两只脚没站稳在地上，我是不会把灯给你的。”女巫大发雷霆，手一松，让他落回井里，自己走了。

中文章名: 蓝灯
英文证据: The poor soldier fell without injury on the moist ground, and the blue light went on burning, but of what use was that to him? He saw very well that he could not escape death. He sat for a while very sorrowfully, then suddenly he felt in his pocket and found his tobacco pipe, which was still half full. ‘This shall be my last pleasure,’ thought he, pulled it out, lit it at the blue light and began to smoke. When the smoke had circled about the cavern, suddenly a little black dwarf stood before him, and said: ‘Lord, what are your commands?’ ‘What my commands are?’ replied the soldier, quite astonished. ‘I must do everything you bid me,’ said the little man. ‘Good,’ said the soldier; ‘then in the first place help me out of this well.’ The little man took him by the hand, and led him through an underground passage, but he did not forget to take the blue light with him. On the way the dwarf showed him the treasures which the witch had collected and hidden there, and the soldier took as much gold as he could carry. When he was above, he said to the little man: ‘Now go and bind the old witch, and carry her before the judge.’ In a short time she came by like the wind, riding on a wild tom-cat and screaming frightfully. Nor was it long before the little man reappeared. ‘It is all done,’ said he, ‘and the witch is already hanging on the gallows. What further commands has my lord?’ inquired the dwarf. ‘At this moment, none,’ answered the soldier; ‘you can return home, only be at hand immediately, if I summon you.’ ‘Nothing more is needed than that you should light your pipe at the blue light, and I will appear before you at once.’ Thereupon he vanished from his sight.
原译: 可怜的士兵在潮湿的地面上跌倒，蓝色的光线继续燃烧，但是对于他有什么用？他非常清楚地看到，他无法逃脱死亡。他坐了一会儿很悲伤的，然后突然感到在他的口袋里，找到了他的烟斗，仍然有一半的烟斗。“这是我最后的荣幸，”他以为，他把它拉出来，点亮它，然后开始吸烟。当烟雾笼罩着洞穴的时候，一个小黑矮人忽然站在他面前说：我的主啊！你有什么命令呢？我的命令是什么？他回答说：这确是令人吃惊的。小家伙说“我必须照你说的做。”兵兵人说 、 好 、 起先帮助我脱井。那个小人牵着他走并带领他穿过地下通道但他没有忘记带走蓝色的光。在途中，矮人向他展示了女巫收集并藏在那里的宝藏，士兵拿走了尽可能多的黄金。当他在天上的时候，他对那个小人说：你们去把那个老巫婆绑起来，你们把她抬到法官那里去。不久，她像风一样过来骑着一只野猫尖叫着。也远未到那个小人重现。他说：事情已经办妥了。女巫们已经悬在绞刑架上。我的主还有别的什么命令呢？他询问了矮人。当时，没有一个士兵回答说：你们可以回家，只要我召唤你们，你们就立刻到场。你们在蓝灯下点燃你们的烟斗，我就立刻来见你们。他忽然从他的眼前消失。
现译: 可怜的士兵跌在潮湿的井底，倒没受伤，蓝灯也依然燃着。可这对他又有什么用？他清楚自己逃不过一死。他忧伤地坐了一阵，忽然往口袋里一摸，摸着了烟斗，斗里还有半斗烟丝。“这算是我最后一点享受吧。”他想。他取出烟斗，就着蓝灯点燃，抽起烟来。烟雾在井底的洞穴里盘旋几圈，忽然，一个黑黢黢的小矮人站在他面前，说：“主人，有什么吩咐？”“我有什么吩咐？”士兵吃惊地反问。“凡是您吩咐的，我都得做。”小人儿说。“好，”士兵说，“那就先把我弄出这口井。”小人儿牵着他的手，领他走过一条地下通道，士兵也没忘记带上蓝灯。沿路小矮人指给他看女巫积攒、私藏在那里的财宝。士兵拿了自己搬得动的那么多金子。到了地面，他对小人儿说：“现在去捆住老女巫，把她押到法官面前。”不多时，女巫骑在一只野公猫背上，像一阵风从旁边刮过，尖叫得十分可怕。小人儿很快也回来了，禀道：“都办好了，女巫已经挂上绞架了。主人还有什么吩咐？”“眼下没有了，”士兵答道，“你可以回去，不过我一叫，你就得来到跟前。”“您只须用蓝灯点燃烟斗，我立刻就会出现在您面前。”说完，他从士兵眼前消失了。

中文章名: 蓝灯
英文证据: The soldier returned to the town from which he came. He went to the best inn, ordered himself handsome clothes, and then bade the landlord furnish him a room as handsome as possible. When it was ready and the soldier had taken possession of it, he summoned the little black manikin and said: ‘I have served the king faithfully, but he has dismissed me, and left me to hunger, and now I want to take my revenge.’ ‘What am I to do?’ asked the little man. ‘Late at night, when the king’s daughter is in bed, bring her here in her sleep, she shall do servant’s work for me.’ The manikin said: ‘That is an easy thing for me to do, but a very dangerous thing for you, for if it is discovered, you will fare ill.’ When twelve o’clock had struck, the door sprang open, and the manikin carried in the princess. ‘Aha! are you there?’ cried the soldier, ‘get to your work at once! Fetch the broom and sweep the chamber.’ When she had done this, he ordered her to come to his chair, and then he stretched out his feet and said: ‘Pull off my boots,’ and then he threw them in her face, and made her pick them up again, and clean and brighten them. She, however, did everything he bade her, without opposition, silently and with half-shut eyes. When the first cock crowed, the manikin carried her back to the royal palace, and laid her in her bed.
原译: 这名士兵返回他从那里来的城镇。他去了最好的客栈自己订了帅气的衣服然后给房东准备一间尽可能帅气的房间。当它准备好了，当那个士兵拿到它的时候，他召唤那个小黑马尼金说：我确已忠实地服侍国王，但他抛弃了我，使我饥渴，现在我要报仇。他说：我要做什么？他说：我要做什么？晚上，当国王的女儿在床上，把她带到这里睡觉，她应该为我做仆人的工作。曼尼金说：这对于我确是一件容易的事，对于你确是一件危险的事。如果那事被发现，你必定要害病。12点时，门开着，马尼金带着公主。“啊哈，你在吗？” 士兵喊着说，“马上去工作，拿扫帚来扫房间。”当她做了这件事的时候，他命令她坐到椅子上，然后，他伸出他的脚来，他说：你们把靴子拿开。他就把靴子扔在她的脸上，使她再捡起来，然后，打干净，弄亮。然而，她做了一切，他没有反对，无声无息地用半裸的双眼骂她。当第一只公鸡叫的时候，马尼金把她带回皇宫，把她放在床上。
现译: 士兵回到自己原先所在的城里，走进最好的客栈，叫人给自己做体面的衣裳，又吩咐店主尽可能给他布置一间华美的客房。房间备好，他住了进去，召来黑黢黢的小人儿，说：“我向来忠心侍奉国王，他却把我赶出来，任我忍饥挨饿。现在我要报仇。”“要我做什么？”小人儿问。“深更半夜，国王的女儿上床睡熟以后，把她带到这儿。我要她像佣人一样为我干活。”小人儿说：“这对我倒是件轻而易举的事，对您却很危险。一旦事情败露，您可没有好果子吃。”午夜十二点一过，房门大开，小人儿抱着公主进来了。“啊哈！你来了？”士兵喝道，“立刻干活！拿扫帚来，把房间扫干净。”她做完，他吩咐她到自己椅子旁边，伸出双脚说：“给我脱靴。”他又把靴子扔在她脸上，叫她捡起来，擦干净，擦亮。公主什么也没说，眼睛半闭着，毫不反抗，把他吩咐的事一件件做完。雄鸡头一遍啼叫，小人儿才把她带回王宫，放回床上。

中文章名: 蓝灯
英文证据: Next morning when the princess arose she went to her father, and told him that she had had a very strange dream. ‘I was carried through the streets with the rapidity of lightning,’ said she, ‘and taken into a soldier’s room, and I had to wait upon him like a servant, sweep his room, clean his boots, and do all kinds of menial work. It was only a dream, and yet I am just as tired as if I really had done everything.’ ‘The dream may have been true,’ said the king. ‘I will give you a piece of advice. Fill your pocket full of peas, and make a small hole in the pocket, and then if you are carried away again, they will fall out and leave a track in the streets.’ But unseen by the king, the manikin was standing beside him when he said that, and heard all. At night when the sleeping princess was again carried through the streets, some peas certainly did fall out of her pocket, but they made no track, for the crafty manikin had just before scattered peas in every street there was. And again the princess was compelled to do servant’s work until cock-crow.
原译: 第二天早上公主醒来时她去找她的父亲告诉他她做了一个很奇怪的梦。她说：我被闪电带去见街，她就说：我被带入一个士兵的房间，我不得不像仆人一样等待他，打扫他的房间，打扫他的靴子，做各种苦差事。那只是一个梦，但我已厌倦了，好像我已做了一切一样。国王说：这个梦或许是真实的。我将给你一个忠告，你应当把满袋的豌豆装满袋，你应当打个洞，如果你再被卷走，他们必定要掉下去，在街上留下一条轨道。但国王看不见，马尼金站在他旁边，他这么说，并听到一切。晚上睡着的公主再次被抬过街道，有些豆子确实从她的口袋里掉下来，但没有留下任何痕迹，因为狡猾的马尼金刚刚在每一条街上撒满了豆子。公主再次被迫做仆人的工作直到公鸡群。
现译: 第二天早晨，公主起来见父亲，说自己做了个很古怪的梦。“有人带着我，快如闪电地穿过一条条街，”她说，“带到一个士兵的房里。我得当他的佣人，服侍他，给他扫屋、擦靴子，干各种杂活。明明只是个梦，我却这么累，好像样样都真的做过。”“那场梦也许是真的，”国王说，“我给你出个主意。把口袋装满豌豆，在袋底弄个小洞。要是再有人把你带走，豌豆就会漏出来，沿街留下踪迹。”小人儿当时就站在旁边，国王看不见他，什么话都让他听见了。夜里，熟睡的公主又被带着穿街而过，口袋里也的确落下一些豌豆，可一点踪迹也没留下：狡猾的小人儿刚刚已经把豌豆撒遍了所有的街道。公主又被迫像佣人一样干活，干到鸡啼。

中文章名: 蓝灯
英文证据: Next morning the king sent his people out to seek the track, but it was all in vain, for in every street poor children were sitting, picking up peas, and saying: ‘It must have rained peas, last night.’ ‘We must think of something else,’ said the king; ‘keep your shoes on when you go to bed, and before you come back from the place where you are taken, hide one of them there, I will soon contrive to find it.’ The black manikin heard this plot, and at night when the soldier again ordered him to bring the princess, revealed it to him, and told him that he knew of no expedient to counteract this stratagem, and that if the shoe were found in the soldier’s house it would go badly with him. ‘Do what I bid you,’ replied the soldier, and again this third night the princess was obliged to work like a servant, but before she went away, she hid her shoe under the bed.
原译: 第二天早晨，国王派他的族人去寻找铁轨，但这一切都是徒劳的，因为每个流浪儿童都坐在那里，捡起豆子，说：昨天晚上，它一定下雨了。国王说：我们必须想些别的事情。他说：你们睡觉的时候，要穿鞋，在你们从被带走的地方回来之前，要先把鞋子穿好，把其中的一只藏起来，我很快就想好办法找到它。黑马尼金听到这个阴谋，当士兵再次命令他带公主来时，他向他透露了这个阴谋，并告诉他，他知道没有什么权宜之计来对付这一阴谋，如果在士兵家中发现鞋子，他就会很坏。“照我说的做” 士兵回答说第三次晚上公主不得不像仆人一样工作但是在她走之前她把鞋藏在床底下。
现译: 次日早晨，国王派人去寻踪迹，却一无所获。每条街上都坐着穷人家的孩子，一边捡豌豆，一边说：“昨天夜里一定下过一场豌豆雨。”“咱们得想别的办法，”国王说，“上床的时候别脱鞋。到了人家把你带去的地方，回来之前把一只鞋藏在那里，我自会很快想法找到。”黑黢黢的小人儿也听见了这个计策。夜里士兵又命他带公主来，他就把计策告诉士兵，说自己想不出破解的方法，要是从士兵的住处搜出那只鞋，士兵就要倒大霉。“照我的吩咐做。”士兵答道。于是第三个夜晚公主又得像佣人一样干活，只是临走前，她把自己的鞋藏在了床下。

中文章名: 蓝灯
英文证据: Next morning the king had the entire town searched for his daughter’s shoe. It was found at the soldier’s, and the soldier himself, who at the entreaty of the dwarf had gone outside the gate, was soon brought back, and thrown into prison. In his flight he had forgotten the most valuable things he had, the blue light and the gold, and had only one ducat in his pocket. And now loaded with chains, he was standing at the window of his dungeon, when he chanced to see one of his comrades passing by. The soldier tapped at the pane of glass, and when this man came up, said to him: ‘Be so kind as to fetch me the small bundle I have left lying in the inn, and I will give you a ducat for doing it.’ His comrade ran thither and brought him what he wanted. As soon as the soldier was alone again, he lighted his pipe and summoned the black manikin. ‘Have no fear,’ said the latter to his master. ‘Go wheresoever they take you, and let them do what they will, only take the blue light with you.’ Next day the soldier was tried, and though he had done nothing wicked, the judge condemned him to death. When he was led forth to die, he begged a last favour of the king. ‘What is it?’ asked the king. ‘That I may smoke one more pipe on my way.’ ‘You may smoke three,’ answered the king, ‘but do not imagine that I will spare your life.’ Then the soldier pulled out his pipe and lighted it at the blue light, and as soon as a few wreaths of smoke had ascended, the manikin was there with a small cudgel in his hand, and said: ‘What does my lord command?’ ‘Strike down to earth that false judge there, and his constable, and spare not the king who has treated me so ill.’ Then the manikin fell on them like lightning, darting this way and that way, and whosoever was so much as touched by his cudgel fell to earth, and did not venture to stir again. The king was terrified; he threw himself on the soldier’s mercy, and merely to be allowed to live at all, gave him his kingdom for his own, and his daughter to wife.
原译: 第二天早上国王让全镇的人都去寻找他女儿的鞋。在士兵家发现，士兵本人，在侏儒堡门外，很快被带回监狱，被扔进监狱。他在飞行中忘记了最有价值的东西蓝光和金子口袋里只有一颗黄油。现在他带着铁链站在地牢的窗户上碰巧看到他的一个同志路过。士兵在玻璃窗旁偷听，当他来见他的时候，他说：请你把我留在客栈里的一小捆东西拿来给我，我一定给你一个做这件事的护身符。他的同志跑来跑去给他带来了他想要的东西。士兵一回来就点燃了烟斗召唤了黑马尼金。“不要害怕，' 后人对他的主人说。他们无论带你到哪里，都随他们的意愿而行动，他们只把蓝光带走。第二天，该士兵受到审判，尽管他没有做坏事，但法官将他判处死刑。当他被带去死的时候，他求国王最后帮个忙。”是什么？“ 问国王。我路上要再抽一根管 。 你可抽三根 。 国王回答说 、 你不可想到我必饶你的命。然后，士兵拔出他的管子，在蓝灯下点燃了烟花，当烟花一升起，马尼金手握着一把小棍子，说：我的主啊！求你把那伪君子和他的治安官打倒在地上，求你不要饶恕对我如此恶毒的国王。然后，马尼金像闪电般落在他们身上，用这样和那样的方式飞翔，凡被他的手杖所动过的人，都掉到地上，不敢再动了。国王很害怕，他把自己扔在士兵的慈悲之下，只允许他活着，把国权交给他，女儿嫁给他。
现译: 第二天早上，国王下令搜遍全城，寻找女儿的鞋。鞋子在士兵屋里找到了，士兵本人虽已听从小矮人的苦劝出了城门，也很快被带回来，投进监狱。他逃走时把最宝贵的东西——蓝灯和金子——全落下了，口袋里仅剩一枚金币。他戴着沉重的锁链，站在牢房窗前，忽然看见一个老战友经过。士兵轻敲玻璃，等那人走近，便说：“劳驾，帮我到客栈取个落下的小包袱。我给你一枚金币做酬劳。”战友跑去，把他要的东西拿来了。四周一没人，士兵就点燃烟斗，叫来黑黢黢的小人儿。“不要怕，”小人儿对主人说，“他们要把您带到哪里，就跟着去。他们要怎么处置，先由他们。只要随身带着蓝灯就行。”次日士兵受审。他虽不曾犯过什么恶行，法官还是判他死刑。被押出去受死时，他请求国王给最后一点恩典。“什么恩典？”国王问。“准我临上路再抽一斗烟。”“抽三斗都行，”国王答道，“可别妄想我会饶你的命。”士兵掏出烟斗，就着蓝灯点燃。才冒起几缕青烟，小人儿就出现了，手里拿着一根小木棒：“主人有何吩咐？”“把那个枉法的法官和他的差役打倒在地，那个亏待我的国王也别放过！”小人儿像闪电一样扑上去，东一窜，西一闪。谁叫木棒轻轻一碰，就倒在地上，动也不再敢动。国王吓破了胆，扑过去向士兵求饶。只求士兵准他活命，他把整个王国都送给了士兵，还把自己的女儿许给他做妻子。

中文章名: 渡鸦
英文证据: There was once a queen who had a little daughter, still too young to run alone. One day the child was very troublesome, and the mother could not quiet it, do what she would. She grew impatient, and seeing the ravens flying round the castle, she opened the window, and said: ‘I wish you were a raven and would fly away, then I should have a little peace.’ Scarcely were the words out of her mouth, when the child in her arms was turned into a raven, and flew away from her through the open window. The bird took its flight to a dark wood and remained there for a long time, and meanwhile the parents could hear nothing of their child.
原译: 曾经有一个女王有一个小女儿，仍然太年轻，无法独自运行。有一天，孩子很麻烦，母亲不能安静下来，做她想做的事。她变得焦急，看到乌鸦在城堡里飞来飞去，她打开窗户说：我的确希望你变成一只乌鸦，然后，我必定要平静下来。她嘴里说的话很可怕当她怀里的孩子变成一只乌鸦并且从窗外飞走。这只鸟飞到黑暗的木头在那里呆了很长时间同时他们的父母听不到他们的孩子的声音。
现译: 从前有一位王后，生了个小女儿，还没长到能独自跑跳的年纪。一天，孩子吵闹得厉害，母亲想尽办法也哄不住。她不耐烦了，望见一群渡鸦绕着城堡飞，便打开窗说：“但愿你也变成一只渡鸦飞走，叫我清静一会儿。”话音未落，怀里的孩子果然变成一只渡鸦，从敞开的窗子飞离了她。鸟儿一直飞到一座黑黝黝的森林，在那里住了很久。其间，父母一点也打听不出孩子的下落。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 渡鸦
英文证据: Long after this, a man was making his way through the wood when he heard a raven calling, and he followed the sound of the voice. As he drew near, the raven said, ‘I am by birth a king’s daughter, but am now under the spell of some enchantment; you can, however, set me free.’ ‘What am I to do?’ he asked. She replied, ‘Go farther into the wood until you come to a house, wherein lives an old woman; she will offer you food and drink, but you must not take of either; if you do, you will fall into a deep sleep, and will not be able to help me. In the garden behind the house is a large tan-heap, and on that you must stand and watch for me. I shall drive there in my carriage at two o’clock in the afternoon for three successive days; the first day it will be drawn by four white, the second by four chestnut, and the last by four black horses; but if you fail to keep awake and I find you sleeping, I shall not be set free.’

中文章名: 渡鸦
英文证据: As it drew towards the appointed hour, he went outside into the garden and mounted the tan-heap to await the raven. Suddenly a feeling of fatigue came over him, and unable to resist it, he lay down for a little while, fully determined, however, to keep awake; but in another minute his eyes closed of their own accord, and he fell into such a deep sleep, that all the noises in the world would not have awakened him. At two o’clock the raven came driving along, drawn by her four white horses; but even before she reached the spot, she said to herself, sighing, ‘I know he has fallen asleep.’ When she entered the garden, there she found him as she had feared, lying on the tan-heap, fast asleep. She got out of her carriage and went to him; she called him and shook him, but it was all in vain, he still continued sleeping.
原译: 当它向规定的时间行进时，他走到花园外面，乘着太阳晒的油堆等待乌鸦。他突然感到疲惫，无法抗拒，他躺了一会儿，但满心决心保持清醒；但到了另一分钟，他自己闭着眼睛，睡得那么沉，以致于全世界的声音都不会唤醒他。两点，乌鸦从她的四匹白马那里走过来，甚至在她到达那个地方之前，她对自己说，叹息着，“我知道他睡着了。”当她进入花园时，她发现他像她所害怕的那样，躺在棕榈地上，睡得很快。她走出马车，走到他身边；她打电话给他，摇晃他，但这一切都是徒劳的，他仍然在睡觉。
现译: 约定的时辰快到了，他走进花园，爬上树皮堆，等候渡鸦。突然一阵困意袭来，他抵挡不了，就躺下歇会儿，却拿定主意要保持清醒。可是又过了片刻，眼睛不由自主地合拢了。他睡得这样沉，世上一切响动加起来也叫不醒他。两点钟，渡鸦驾着四匹白马的车过来了。还没到地方，她就叹着气自语：“我知道他已经睡着了。”一进花园，她看见他果然如她所担心的那样，躺在树皮堆上熟睡。她下车走近，又是呼唤，又是摇晃，全没有用，他只管睡个不停。

中文章名: 渡鸦

As the raven drove along her four chestnut horses, she said sorrowfully to herself, ‘I know he has fallen asleep.’ She went as before to look for him, but he slept, and it was impossible to awaken him.

中文章名: 渡鸦
英文证据: She was sadder than ever as she drove along, and said mournfully, ‘I know he has fallen asleep, and will not be able to set me free.’ She found him sleeping heavily, and all her efforts to awaken him were of no avail. Then she placed beside him a loaf, and some meat, and a flask of wine, of such a kind, that however much he took of them, they would never grow less. After that she drew a gold ring, on which her name was engraved, off her finger, and put it upon one of his. Finally, she laid a letter near him, in which, after giving him particulars of the food and drink she had left for him, she finished with the following words: ‘I see that as long as you remain here you will never be able to set me free; if, however, you still wish to do so, come to the golden castle of Stromberg; this is well within your power to accomplish.’ She then returned to her carriage and drove to the golden castle of Stromberg.
原译: 她开车时比以前更难过，她悲哀地说：我知道他睡着，所以不能释放我。她发现他睡得很沉，她为唤醒他所作的一切努力都徒劳无功。然后她把一个面包，一些肉，和一瓶酒放在他旁边，不论他拿了多少，他们不会长少。在那之后，她画了一枚金戒指，上面刻着她的名字，从她的手指上掉下来，放在他身上。最后，她在他面前写了一封信，在给他她留给他的食品和饮料的细节之后，她用下面的话说：“我看见只要你留在这里，你永远无法让我自由，如果你仍然想这样做，就来见斯特伦伯格的金色城堡，这是你所能完成的。”然后她回到她的马车开车到金色的城堡斯特伦伯格。

中文章名: 渡鸦
英文证据: When the man awoke and found that he had been sleeping, he was grieved at heart, and said, ‘She has no doubt been here and driven away again, and it is now too late for me to save her.’ Then his eyes fell on the things which were lying beside him; he read the letter, and knew from it all that had happened. He rose up without delay, eager to start on his way and to reach the castle of Stromberg, but he had no idea in which direction he ought to go. He travelled about a long time in search of it and came at last to a dark forest, through which he went on walking for fourteen days and still could not find a way out. Once more the night came on, and worn out he lay down under a bush and fell asleep. Again the next day he pursued his way through the forest, and that evening, thinking to rest again, he lay down as before, but he heard such a howling and wailing that he found it impossible to sleep. He waited till it was darker and people had begun to light up their houses, and then seeing a little glimmer ahead of him, he went towards it.

现译: 男人醒来，发觉自己睡过了头，内心十分痛苦，说：“她一定来过，又走了。我如今再想救她，已经太迟。”这时他瞧见身旁放着的东西，读了那封信，一切经过便都明白了。他立刻起身，恨不得马上上路，赶到施特龙贝格的城堡去，却不知道该往哪个方向走。他四处寻访，找了很久，终于到了一座黑暗的森林。他在里头走了十四天，仍找不到出路。夜幕再次降临，他精疲力尽，倒在树丛底下睡去。第二天，他继续在林中赶路。到了晚上，正想像先前一样躺下休息，却听见好一阵哀号哭喊，怎么也睡不着。他等到天又黑了些，人们都开始在屋里点灯，看到前方一丝微光，就朝那里走去。

中文章名: 渡鸦
英文证据: So they went indoors together and sat down, and the man brought out the bread, meat, and wine, which although he had eaten and drunk of them, were still unconsumed. The giant was pleased with the good cheer, and ate and drank to his heart’s content. When he had finished his supper the man asked him if he could direct him to the castle of Stromberg. The giant said, ‘I will look on my map; on it are marked all the towns, villages, and houses.’ So he fetched his map, and looked for the castle, but could not find it. ‘Never mind,’ he said, ‘I have larger maps upstairs in the cupboard, we will look on those,’ but they searched in vain, for the castle was not marked even on these. The man now thought he should like to continue his journey, but the giant begged him to remain for a day or two longer until the return of his brother, who was away in search of provisions. When the brother came home, they asked him about the castle of Stromberg, and he told them he would look on his own maps as soon as he had eaten and appeased his hunger. Accordingly, when he had finished his supper, they all went up together to his room and looked through his maps, but the castle was not to be found. Then he fetched other older maps, and they went on looking for the castle until at last they found it, but it was many thousand miles away. ‘How shall I be able to get there?’ asked the man. ‘I have two hours to spare,’ said the giant, ‘and I will carry you into the neighbourhood of the castle; I must then return to look after the child who is in our care.’

现译: 两人一起进屋坐下，男人拿出面包、肉、葡萄酒。他虽沿路吃过喝过，这些东西依然一点不少。巨人见有好酒好菜，欢喜地尽情吃喝。晚饭吃完，男人问他能不能指点去施特龙贝格城堡的路。巨人说：“我查查地图吧。上面标着所有的城镇、村庄和房子。”他取来地图，查来查去，找不到城堡。“没关系，”他说，“楼上柜子里还有更大的地图，咱们去那些上面找。”可他们仍是白费力气，连那些地图都没标出城堡。男人这下想继续上路，巨人却求他多留一两天，等出门找粮食的兄弟回来。兄弟回来以后，他们问起施特龙贝格的城堡。他说等吃饱了肚子，就查他自己的地图。于是晚餐过后，大家一同上楼，到他房里翻寻地图，还是没有那座城堡。他又拿来几张更早的老地图，接着找，终于找到了，距离这里却有好几千英里。“我怎么去得了？”男人问。“我有两个钟头的空闲，”巨人说，“可以把你送到城堡附近。然后我得回来，我们这里托养的孩子还得有人看顾。”

中文章名: 渡鸦
英文证据: The giant, thereupon, carried the man to within about a hundred leagues of the castle, where he left him, saying, ‘You will be able to walk the remainder of the way yourself.’ The man journeyed on day and night till he reached the golden castle of Stromberg. He found it situated, however, on a glass mountain, and looking up from the foot he saw the enchanted maiden drive round her castle and then go inside. He was overjoyed to see her, and longed to get to the top of the mountain, but the sides were so slippery that every time he attempted to climb he fell back again. When he saw that it was impossible to reach her, he was greatly grieved, and said to himself, ‘I will remain here and wait for her,’ so he built himself a little hut, and there he sat and watched for a whole year, and every day he saw the king’s daughter driving round her castle, but still was unable to get nearer to her.
原译: 巨人就把他带到城堡的一百里范围内留下他的地方说：“你将可以走完剩下的路。”这个人日夜不停地旅行直到他到达金色的斯特伦伯格城堡。但是他发现它位于玻璃山上，从脚上往上看，他看到魔法少女驾车绕过她的城堡，然后进去。他见到她太高兴了渴望爬上山顶但两边很滑每次都想爬上山。当他看见不可能找到她时，他感到非常悲痛，他对自己说：我将留在这里等待她。他就为自己建造了一个小屋，他在那里坐了整整一年，每天看见国王的女儿在她的城堡里开车，但他仍然不能接近她。
现译: 巨人便扛着这个人，一直走到距城堡约一百里格的地方，放下他，说：“剩下的路，你自己就能走过去了。”那人日夜兼程，终于来到施特龙贝格的金城堡前。这才发现，城堡竟建在一座玻璃山上。他站在山脚远望，看见中了魔法的姑娘驾车绕着她的城堡走了一圈，随后进了城堡。见到她，他高兴极了，多想立刻登上山顶！可山坡太滑，每爬一次，便摔回来一次。明白自己上不去，他伤心极了，对自己说：“我就留在这里，等她吧。”他搭起一间小棚屋，整整一年坐在那里守望。每天他都能看见公主驾车绕行城堡，却始终没法离她近一步。

中文章名: 渡鸦
英文证据: Looking out from his hut one day he saw three robbers fighting and he called out to them, ‘God be with you.’ They stopped when they heard the call, but looking round and seeing nobody, they went on again with their fighting, which now became more furious. ‘God be with you,’ he cried again, and again they paused and looked about, but seeing no one went back to their fighting. A third time he called out, ‘God be with you,’ and then thinking he should like to know the cause of dispute between the three men, he went out and asked them why they were fighting so angrily with one another. One of them said that he had found a stick, and that he had but to strike it against any door through which he wished to pass, and it immediately flew open. Another told him that he had found a cloak which rendered its wearer invisible; and the third had caught a horse which would carry its rider over any obstacle, and even up the glass mountain. They had been unable to decide whether they would keep together and have the things in common, or whether they would separate. On hearing this, the man said, ‘I will give you something in exchange for those three things; not money, for that I have not got, but something that is of far more value. I must first, however, prove whether all you have told me about your three things is true.’ The robbers, therefore, made him get on the horse, and handed him the stick and the cloak, and when he had put this round him he was no longer visible. Then he fell upon them with the stick and beat them one after another, crying, ‘There, you idle vagabonds, you have got what you deserve; are you satisfied now!’
原译: 有一天，他从他的棚子里看到三个强盗在战斗，他喊叫他们说：真主与你们同在。当他们听到电话时就停下来了，但是他们环顾四周，看到没有人，他们又继续战斗，现在更加愤怒。他又喊叫说：真主与你同在。他们又停下来，望著他们，但看见没有人再战斗。他第三次喊叫说：真主与你们同在。他想必知道这三人之间争论的起因。他出去问他们，为什么他们互相愤怒地战斗。其中一人说，他找到了一根棍子，他只能用棍子抵挡任何他想穿过的门，而棍子立即打开。另一位代表告诉他，他发现了一件遮盖着面具的外衣，第三匹马抓住了骑马的马，骑马的马将踏过任何障碍，甚至爬上玻璃山。他们无法决定他们是否会保持团结，共同生活，或是否会分开。听到这个消息的时候，他说：我要以这三样东西换取你。我所没有的钱，不能以它换取更贵的。我首先必须证明你所告诉我的三样东西，是不是真实的。因此，强盗逼他上马，把棍子和斗篷交给他，在他把棍子和斗篷放在他身上时，他已不可见了。然后，他用棍子打他们，然后，他喊叫说：你们这些闲散的流浪者，已获得你们所应得的，你们已满足了。
现译: 一天，他从小屋往外看，瞧见三个强盗正在打架，便喊道：“愿上帝与你们同在！”他们听见喊声停了手，四处张望，不见人，便又打了起来，比先前还凶。“愿上帝与你们同在！”他又喊。几个人又站住张望，还是不见谁，便又扭打起来。他第三次喊：“愿上帝与你们同在！”这回他也想弄清三人为何争执，便走出去，问他们为什么彼此打得这么凶。一个说自己捡到一根木棍，想进哪扇门，只须拿它一敲，门马上就开。另一个说他找到一件斗篷，谁披上，谁便能隐身。第三个捉到一匹马，载着骑手能越过一切障碍，就连玻璃山也上得去。三人拿不定主意，到底是一道留下，三件宝物合着用，还是各走各的路。男人听了，说：“我拿点东西跟你们换这三样。钱我没有，我给的却比钱值价得多。不过先得让我试试，你们说的这三样的本领是不是真的。”强盗们就请他上马，把木棍、斗篷交给他。斗篷一披，他就隐去了身影。他举起木棍扑向三人，挨个打了一顿，喝道：“拿着吧，游手好闲的坏蛋，这是你们应得的！如今满意了吧？”

中文章名: 渡鸦

英文证据: Then Dummling said: ‘Father, do let me go and cut wood.’ The father answered: ‘Your brothers have hurt themselves with it, leave it alone, you do not understand anything about it.’ But Dummling begged so long that at last he said: ‘Just go then, you will get wiser by hurting yourself.’ His mother gave him a cake made with water and baked in the cinders, and with it a bottle of sour beer.

中文章名: 金鹅
英文证据: When he came to the forest the little old grey man met him likewise, and greeting him, said: ‘Give me a piece of your cake and a drink out of your bottle; I am so hungry and thirsty.’ Dummling answered: ‘I have only cinder-cake and sour beer; if that pleases you, we will sit down and eat.’ So they sat down, and when Dummling pulled out his cinder-cake, it was a fine sweet cake, and the sour beer had become good wine. 中文章名: 金鹅

Is that seemly?’ At the same time he seized the youngest by the hand in order to pull her away, but as soon as he touched her he likewise stuck fast, and was himself obliged to run behind.

中文章名: 金鹅

中文章名: 生命之水
英文证据: Long before you or I were born, there reigned, in a country a great way off, a king who had three sons. This king once fell very ill--so ill that nobody thought he could live. His sons were very much grieved at their father’s sickness; and as they were walking together very mournfully in the garden of the palace, a little old man met them and asked what was the matter. They told him that their father was very ill, and that they were afraid nothing could save him. ‘I know what would,’ said the little old man; ‘it is the Water of Life. In the same manner he befriended two other countries through which they passed on their way.
原译: 然后他们三人一起骑马回家来到一个被战争和可怕的饥荒所毁灭的国家因此人们担心所有人都会因为匮乏而死。但王子把食物和他所有的国度都给了大地的国王。他借给国王一把美妙的剑用它杀死了敌人的军队因而王国再次平平安安。他以同样的方式与另外两个国家结为朋友，他们通过这两个国家。
现译: 三兄弟一起骑马回家。途中，他们来到一处被战乱和大饥荒摧残的国家，人人都怕老百姓全要活活饿死。小王子把面包交给那里的国王，全国人民都有了吃的。他又把那把神剑借给国王，国王用它消灭敌军，这个国家终于重享太平富足。归途上他们经过另外两个国家，他也同样伸手相助。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 生命之水
英文证据: When they came to the sea, they got into a ship and during their voyage the two eldest said to themselves, ‘Our brother has got the water which we could not find, therefore our father will forsake us and give him the kingdom, which is our right’; so they were full of envy and revenge, and agreed together how they could ruin him. Then they waited till he was fast asleep, and poured the Water of Life out of the cup, and took it for themselves, giving him bitter sea-water instead.
原译: 当他们来到海边的时候，他们乘船进去了。在航行期间，两个长辈对自己说：我们的哥哥获得我们所不能找到的水，所以我们的父亲要抛弃我们，要把我们的国权赏赐他。他们嫉妒，要惩罚，要毁灭他，要他们共同判决。然后他们等他睡着，把生命之水从杯子里倒出来，然后自己把它取下来，给他苦水。
现译: 到了海边，他们上了一艘船。航行中，两位哥哥暗想：“咱们找不到的水，弟弟倒找到了。这一来，父亲就要撇下咱们，把理应归咱们的王国给他。”他们满怀嫉妒和怨恨，商定要毁了他。等他睡熟，两人把杯里的生命之水倒出来据为己有，另给他换上又苦又咸的海水。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 生命之水
英文证据: When they came to their journey’s end, the youngest son brought his cup to the sick king, that he might drink and be healed. Scarcely, however, had he tasted the bitter sea-water when he became worse even than he was before; and then both the elder sons came in, and blamed the youngest for what they had done; and said that he wanted to poison their father, but that they had found the Water of Life, and had brought it with them. He no sooner began to drink of what they brought him, than he felt his sickness leave him, and was as strong and well as in his younger days. Then they went to their brother, and laughed at him, and said, ‘Well, brother, you found the Water of Life, did you? You have had the trouble and we shall have the reward. Pray, with all your cleverness, why did not you manage to keep your eyes open? Next year one of us will take away your beautiful princess, if you do not take care. You had better say nothing about this to our father, for he does not believe a word you say; and if you tell tales, you shall lose your life into the bargain: but be quiet, and we will let you off.’
原译: 当他们走到旅途的尽头时，最小的儿子把他的杯子带到病态的国王那里，以便他饮酒和痊愈。然而，当他比以前更难受的时候，他尝到了苦海的滋味，那两个大儿子就进来，把小儿子的所作所为归罪于他们。他说：他要毒害他们的父亲，但他们发现有生命之水，并且把它带来了。他毫不迟疑地开始喝他们给他带的酒，因为他觉得自己病了，而且身体健壮，年幼。然后，他们去找他们的哥哥，嘲笑他，他说：我的兄弟啊！你确已发现生命之水了。你惹了麻烦，我们会得到奖励。祈祷吧，你这么聪明为什么不睁大眼睛？明年，我们中的一个会带走你美丽的公主，如果你不照顾。你最好不要对我们的父亲说这件事，因为他不信你所说的一句话；如果你讲故事，你将在交易中丧失生命。你应当安静，我们将使你离开。'，爱丽丝
现译: 旅程结束，小儿子把杯子捧到病中的父王面前，想让父亲喝下去治好病。可是苦海水刚一沾唇，国王病得比先前更重了。两个哥哥随即进屋，把自己所做的事全栽在弟弟身上，说小王子想毒死父亲，幸亏他们寻到了生命之水，已经带来。国王才喝下他们送的水，便觉得病痛退去，身体又像年轻时一样健康有力。他们去找弟弟，笑着说：“喂，老弟，是你找到生命之水的，对吧？辛苦归你，奖赏归我们。请问你这样聪明，怎么就没想法让眼睛别合上呢？你要不当心，到明年，那位美丽的公主也会叫我们中的一个带走。最好别跟父亲说，一个字他也不会信你。你敢说长道短，连命都得搭上。你只管闭嘴，我们就放你一马。”
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 生命之水
英文证据: The old king was still very angry with his youngest son, and thought that he really meant to have taken away his life; so he called his court together, and asked what should be done, and all agreed that he ought to be put to death. The prince knew nothing of what was going on, till one day, when the king’s chief huntsmen went a-hunting with him, and they were alone in the wood together, the huntsman looked so sorrowful that the prince said, ‘My friend, what is the matter with you?’ ‘I cannot and dare not tell you,’ said he. But the prince begged very hard, and said, ‘Only tell me what it is, and do not think I shall be angry, for I will forgive you.’ ‘Alas!’ said the huntsman; ‘the king has ordered me to shoot you.’ The prince started at this, and said, ‘Let me live, and I will change dresses with you; you shall take my royal coat to show to my father, and do you give me your shabby one.’ ‘With all my heart,’ said the huntsman; ‘I am sure I shall be glad to save you, for I could not have shot you.’ Then he took the prince’s coat, and gave him the shabby one, and went away through the wood.
原译: 老国王仍然很生他小儿子的气，认为他真的想夺走他的生命，所以他召集法庭，询问应该做什么，大家都同意要把他处死。王子对事情一无所知直到有一天国王的首领猎人和他一起猎杀并且他们独自一人在树林里猎人看起来很悲伤王子说：“我的朋友，你怎么了？” 他说：“我不能也不敢告诉你。”但王子向你求苦 、 说 、 只要告诉我 、 不要以为我必生怒 。 我必饶恕你 。 狩猎人说 、 君王已命我杀你。王子说：你让我活下去吧！我要和你一起换衣服，你把我的皇室外套给我父亲看看，你把你的破烂的外套给我。猎人说：我诚心诚意地说：我必定要拯救你，因为我不能射杀你。然后他拿了王子的外套给了他破旧的一件穿过了树林。
现译: 老国王仍十分恼怒小儿子，以为他真的想要父亲的命，便召集大臣商议怎么处置，众口一词，都说该判死。王子对这一切毫不知情。一天，国王的首席猎人同他出猎，林中只剩下两人。猎人满面愁容，王子便问：“朋友，你怎么了？”“我不能也不敢说。”猎人说。王子苦苦请求：“只管告诉我是什么事，别怕我生气，我会宽恕你。”“唉，”猎人说，“国王下令，要我把您射死。”王子猛吃一惊，说：“让我活命吧。我跟你换衣裳，你拿我的王袍去给父亲看，把你那件破衣裳给我。”“我一万个愿意，”猎人说，“我很高兴能救您，我本来也下不了手射您。”他接过王子的外衣，把自己的破衣服给他，独自穿过森林走了。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 生命之水
英文证据: Some time after, three grand embassies came to the old king’s court, with rich gifts of gold and precious stones for his youngest son; now all these were sent from the three kings to whom he had lent his sword and loaf of bread, in order to rid them of their enemy and feed their people. This touched the old king’s heart, and he thought his son might still be guiltless, and said to his court, ‘O that my son were still alive! how it grieves me that I had him killed!’ ‘He is still alive,’ said the huntsman; ‘and I am glad that I had pity on him, but let him go in peace, and brought home his royal coat.’ At this the king was overwhelmed with joy, and made it known throughout all his kingdom, that if his son would come back to his court he would forgive him.
原译: 不久后，三个大大使馆来到老国王的宫廷，送给他最小的儿子金子和宝石的丰厚礼物；现在所有这些都是他借刀子和面包给的三个国王寄来的，以便让他们摆脱敌人，养活他们的人民。这触动了老国王的心，他猜想他的儿子是无罪的，他对他的官司说：我的儿子是活着的，我为他被杀死而忧愁。猎人说：他还活着。我的确为怜悯他而高兴，求你让他平安地走，并把他的首饰拿回来。国王如此的喜悦 、 使他遍了他的国度 、 都知道 、 若他的儿子回到庭上 、 他必原谅他。
现译: 过了一阵，三个盛大的使团来到老国王的朝廷，指明给小王子送来厚礼，满是黄金宝石。他把宝剑和面包借给三位国王，帮他们赶走敌人、喂饱百姓，如今正是那三位国王派了人来。这些事打动了老国王，他想到儿子也许本来无辜，对朝臣说：“啊，我的儿子要是还活着多好！我叫人杀他，心里多么难受！”“他还活着，”猎人说，“我很庆幸自己当时怜惜他，平安放他走了，只带回他的王袍。”国王喜不自胜，立刻通告全国，只要儿子肯回朝见他，他就宽恕他。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 生命之水
英文证据: Meanwhile the princess was eagerly waiting till her deliverer should come back; and had a road made leading up to her palace all of shining gold; and told her courtiers that whoever came on horseback, and rode straight up to the gate upon it, was her true lover; and that they must let him in: but whoever rode on one side of it, they must be sure was not the right one; and that they must send him away at once.
原译: 同时，公主急切地等待拯救者回来；她有一条道路，通向她的宫殿。她对臣仆们说，骑马上门的人，确是她的爱人，他们必须让他进去；但骑马的人，必须确信不是正确的；他们必须立刻将他送走。
现译: 另一头，公主正热切地等待恩人回来。她命人铺了一条通往宫门的路，从头到尾全用亮闪闪的金子铺成。她吩咐朝臣，谁要是骑马笔直踏上金路，一路驰到大门前，那便是她真正的心上人，一定要放他进来。谁要是沿着路的旁边走，准不是真正的那个人，马上就得打发他走。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 生命之水
英文证据: The time soon came, when the eldest brother thought that he would make haste to go to the princess, and say that he was the one who had set her free, and that he should have her for his wife, and the kingdom with her. As he came before the palace and saw the golden road, he stopped to look at it, and he thought to himself, ‘It is a pity to ride upon this beautiful road’; so he turned aside and rode on the right-hand side of it. But when he came to the gate, the guards, who had seen the road he took, said to him, he could not be what he said he was, and must go about his business.
原译: 时间很快就到了当大哥哥以为他会匆忙去见公主说是他让她自由的并且他应该把她留给妻子和王室和她在一起。当他来到宫殿前，看见那条金色的道路的时候，他停下来看一看，他对自己说：在这条美丽的道路上骑行，真可惜！他就转过身去，顺着那条金色的道路而奔驰。但是，当他来到大门时，看到他走的路的警卫对他说，他不可能像他所说的那样，必须去处理他的事情。
现译: 约定的日子快到了。大哥想抢先赶去找公主，自称是把她救出来的人，好把她娶回家，连王国也一并接收。他来到宫前，望见那条金路，停下来瞧了瞧，心想：“这么漂亮的路，骑马踩在上头未免可惜。”他便转了方向，从路右边一路骑去。可到了大门，守卫早已看清他走的路线，对他说，他决不是他自称的那个人，请他上别处忙自己的事去。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 生命之水
英文证据: The second prince set out soon afterwards on the same errand; and when he came to the golden road, and his horse had set one foot upon it, he stopped to look at it, and thought it very beautiful, and said to himself, ‘What a pity it is that anything should tread here!’ Then he too turned aside and rode on the left side of it. But when he came to the gate the guards said he was not the true prince, and that he too must go away about his business; and away he went.
原译: 第二位王子不久就出发去办同样的事情。 当他来到金色的路上，他的马踏上一条脚，他停下来看它，觉得它非常美丽，对自己说，“真可惜，任何东西都踏在这里了！”然后，他转过身去，骑在左边。但是当他来到门前时卫兵说他不是真正的王子他必须离开他的生意。
现译: 不久二王子也打着同样的主意动身了。到了金路前，他的马一只蹄子已经踏了上去，他却停下来观看，觉得这路实在太美，心想：“要叫谁在上面踩上一脚，那真可惜！”他也拐到旁边，从路左边骑去。到了大门，守卫说他不是真王子，也请他另往别处忙去。他只好走了。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 生命之水
英文证据: Now when the full year was come round, the third brother left the forest in which he had lain hid for fear of his father’s anger, and set out in search of his betrothed bride. So he journeyed on, thinking of her all the way, and rode so quickly that he did not even see what the road was made of, but went with his horse straight over it; and as he came to the gate it flew open, and the princess welcomed him with joy, and said he was her deliverer, and should now be her husband and lord of the kingdom. When the first joy at their meeting was over, the princess told him she had heard of his father having forgiven him, and of his wish to have him home again: so, before his wedding with the princess, he went to visit his father, taking her with him. Then he told him everything; how his brothers had cheated and robbed him, and yet that he had borne all those wrongs for the love of his father. And the old king was very angry, and wanted to punish his wicked sons; but they made their escape, and got into a ship and sailed away over the wide sea, and where they went to nobody knew and nobody cared.
原译: 当整年到来的时候，第三兄弟离开他躺着的森林害怕他父亲的愤怒出发寻找他的未婚妻。他一路走来，想着她，骑得如此之快，他甚至看不到路是用什么造的，而是骑着他的马走过去。 当他来到大门前，门就打开了，公主欢乐地欢迎他，说他是她的救世主，现在应该是她的丈夫和王国的主人。当他们见面的第一次欢乐结束时，公主告诉他，她听说他的父亲原谅了他，并说他希望他能再次回家：因此，在他与公主结婚之前，他去探望他的父亲，带她去见他的父亲。然后，他告诉他一切；他的兄弟们怎样欺骗他，怎样抢劫他，他为爱他的父亲而承受了一切罪恶。老国王非常愤怒，想惩罚他的邪恶的儿子，但他们逃到船上，在大海中航行，他们去的地方无人知晓，无人关心。
现译: 足足一年期满，老三终于离开躲藏的森林。他一直是为躲避父王的怒火才藏在那里，如今要动身寻找订了亲的新娘。他一路走，一路想着她，马骑得那么快，根本没留意路是什么铺的，就直直沿路骑了过去。一到大门，门立刻敞开。公主欢喜地迎他，说他就是自己的救命恩人，如今该做她的丈夫和王国的主人了。团聚时最初的喜悦过后，公主告诉他，她听说父王已经宽恕了他，仍盼他回家。于是，他在成亲前先带上公主，去探望父亲。他把一切都说出来，两个哥哥如何欺骗他、偷他的东西，自己又如何因为爱父亲，默默忍下了所有冤屈。老国王怒不可遏，要惩罚两个恶子。可是两人早已逃走，上船驶过茫茫大海。他们到底去了哪里，谁也不知道，谁也不在意。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 生命之水
英文证据: And now the old king gathered together his court, and asked all his kingdom to come and celebrate the wedding of his son and the princess. And young and old, noble and squire, gentle and simple, came at once on the summons; and among the rest came the friendly dwarf, with the sugarloaf hat, and a new scarlet cloak.
原译: 现在老国王聚集了自己的宫殿要求他所有的王国都来庆祝他儿子和公主的婚礼。年轻又老高尚谦卑温柔又简单立刻赶来其余的都来了。
现译: 老国王召集群臣，邀请全国百姓来为儿子与公主的婚礼庆祝。老的少的，贵族和乡绅，体面人和平民，听见召唤，一齐赶来。来客中还有那个友善的小矮人，戴着尖尖的糖锥帽，披着一件崭新的猩红斗篷。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 生命之水
英文证据:
And the wedding was held, and the merry bells run.

中文章名: 十二个猎人
英文证据: There was once a king’s son who had a bride whom he loved very much. And when he was sitting beside her and very happy, news came that his father lay sick unto death, and desired to see him once again before his end. Then he said to his beloved: ‘I must now go and leave you, I give you a ring as a remembrance of me. When I am king, I will return and fetch you.’ So he rode away, and when he reached his father, the latter was dangerously ill, and near his death. He said to him: ‘Dear son, I wished to see you once again before my end, promise me to marry as I wish,’ and he named a certain king’s daughter who was to be his wife. The son was in such trouble that he did not think what he was doing, and said: ‘Yes, dear father, your will shall be done,’ and thereupon the king shut his eyes, and died.
原译: 曾经有一个国王的儿子有个他非常爱的新娘。当他坐在她身边，非常高兴，传来的消息说，他的父亲病倒在地上，希望在他死前再次见到他。他对他的爱人说：我现在必须离开你，我以戒指给你，以纪念我。当我是国王的时候，我必定回来接你。于是他骑马走了，当他到达他的父亲那里的时候，他的父亲病得很重，几乎要死了。他对他说：亲爱的儿子，在我临终之前，我想再次见到你，向我保证，我愿意结婚。他为国王指定了一位女儿，她是他的妻子。儿子遭遇重重麻烦，不敢思考自己的行为，他说：是的，亲爱的父亲，你的意愿必定实现。国王就闭了眼而死。
现译: 从前有个王子，有位十分相爱的未婚妻。一天，他正快快活活坐在她身边，忽然传来消息，说父亲病危，想在临终前再见儿子一面。他对心上人说：“现在我得离开你了。我给你一枚戒指，留作思念。等我做了国王，一定回来接你。”他骑马走了。赶到父亲那里时，老人已病入膏肓，气息奄奄，开口对他说：“好儿子，我只盼最后能再见你一面。答应我，依我的心意娶妻吧。”父亲说出了一位公主的名字，要王子娶她。儿子心里乱极了，没顾得上想自己在做什么，便回答：“好，亲爱的父亲，一切依您的心愿。”国王就此合上双眼，死了。

中文章名: 十二个猎人

His first betrothed heard of this, and fretted so much about his faithfulness that she nearly died. Then her father said to her: ‘Dearest child, why are you so sad? You shall have whatsoever you will.’ She thought for a moment and said: ‘Dear father, I wish for eleven girls exactly like myself in face, figure, and size.’ The father said: ‘If it be possible, your desire shall be fulfilled,’ and he caused a search to be made in his whole kingdom, until eleven young maidens were found who exactly resembled his daughter in face, figure, and size.
原译: 当他的儿子被宣布为国王，哀悼的时候，他被迫履行他父亲的诺言，使国王的女儿被邀约，她也受约约。他第一次订婚听说这件事，并担心这么多他的忠诚，她差点死了。她的父亲对她说：亲爱的孩子啊！你为什么忧愁呢？你必定获得你所希望的。她想了一会儿，说：“亲爱的父亲，我希望有11个女孩和我一样的面孔，身材和体型。”父亲说：如果你们的愿望实现，那末，你们的愿望必定实现。他使那十一个年轻少女，在他们面前、身材上和身材上，都像他的女儿。
现译: 儿子登基做了国王。丧期一过，他只得履行向父亲许下的诺言，派人向那位公主求婚，对方也同意将她许配给他。他原先的未婚妻听说了，为心上人是否还忠于旧约，忧心得几乎死去。她父亲便对她说：“我最亲爱的孩子，你为什么这样悲伤？你想要什么，我都给你。”她想了片刻，说：“亲爱的父亲，我想要十一个与我面容、身形、高矮全都相同的姑娘。”父亲说：“只要办得到，一定如你所愿。”他下令找遍全国，直到寻到十一位年轻姑娘，面容、身形、高矮都跟他的女儿一模一样。

中文章名: 十二个猎人
英文证据: When they came to the king’s daughter, she had twelve suits of huntsmen’s clothes made, all alike, and the eleven maidens had to put on the huntsmen’s clothes, and she herself put on the twelfth suit. Thereupon she took her leave of her father, and rode away with them, and rode to the court of her former betrothed, whom she loved so dearly. Then she asked if he required any huntsmen, and if he would take all of them into his service. The king looked at her and did not know her, but as they were such handsome fellows, he said: ‘Yes,’ and that he would willingly take them, and now they were the king’s twelve huntsmen.
原译: 当他们来到国王的女儿，她有12套西装狩猎者的衣服一样，11个少女不得不穿上狩猎者的衣服，她自己穿上第十二套西装。于是，她请了父亲的假，带着父亲们离开，来到她以前订婚的宫廷，她深爱着她。然后她问他是否需要任何猎人以及他是否愿意带他们去服役。国王看着她，却不认识她，但他们都是英俊的人。他说：是的。他要自愿地带走他们，现在他们是国王的12个猎人。
现译: 那十一个姑娘来到公主面前，公主叫人做了十二套猎人的衣服，款式完全相同。她让姑娘们各换一套，自己穿上第十二套，随后向父亲告别，带着她们骑马出发，去到先前那个未婚夫的朝廷。她仍是那样爱他。她上前问他缺不缺猎人，肯不肯把他们这一行人全收来当差。国王打量了她，却没认出来。见是这么一群英俊的小伙子，他说愿意，很乐意把他们留下。就这样，她们成了国王的十二个猎人。

中文章名: 十二个猎人
英文证据: The king, however, had a lion which was a wondrous animal, for he knew all concealed and secret things. It came to pass that one evening he said to the king: ‘You think you have twelve huntsmen?’ ‘Yes,’ said the king, ‘they are twelve huntsmen.’ The lion continued: ‘You are mistaken, they are twelve girls.’ The king said: ‘That cannot be true! How will you prove that to me?’ ‘Oh, just let some peas be strewn in the ante-chamber,’ answered the lion, ‘and then you will soon see. Men have a firm step, and when they walk over peas none of them stir, but girls trip and skip, and drag their feet, and the peas roll about.’ The king was well pleased with the counsel, and caused the peas to be strewn.
原译: 然而，国王有一只狮子，是一种奇妙的动物，因为他知道一切隐藏和秘密的东西。有天晚上，他对国王说：你们以为你们有十二个猎人吗？国王说：他们是十二个猎人。狮子接着说：你错了，她们是12个女孩。国王说：这绝不是真实的。你怎么向我证明呢？你说：你们让些豆子在前院里飘动吧！你们就对狮子说：你们不久就知道了。人将踏上坚固的步伐，当他们踏上豌豆的时候，没有一个人会搅动他们，但女孩们会游荡，她们会溜走，她们会摇动。国王对建议很满意，并导致豆子被粉碎。
现译: 国王养着一头神异的狮子，什么隐藏的、秘而不宣的事，它全知道。一天晚上，它对国王说：“您以为您有十二个猎人？”“对呀，”国王说，“他们是十二个猎人。”狮子接着说：“您弄错啦，她们是十二个姑娘。”国王说：“这不可能！你有什么证据？”“噢，您只须叫人撒些豌豆在前厅，很快就有分晓。男人脚步稳，踏上豌豆，没有一颗会动。姑娘们却一蹦一跳，拖着脚走，豆子就该四面滚了。”国王对这主意很满意，叫人把豌豆撒下去。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 十二个猎人
英文证据: There was, however, a servant of the king’s who favoured the huntsmen, and when he heard that they were going to be put to this test he went to them and repeated everything, and said: ‘The lion wants to make the king believe that you are girls.’ Then the king’s daughter thanked him, and said to her maidens: ‘Show some strength, and step firmly on the peas.’ So next morning when the king had the twelve huntsmen called before him, and they came into the ante-chamber where the peas were lying, they stepped so firmly on them, and had such a strong, sure walk, that not one of the peas either rolled or stirred. Then they went away again, and the king said to the lion: ‘You have lied to me, they walk just like men.’ The lion said: ‘They have been informed that they were going to be put to the test, and have assumed some strength. Just let twelve spinning-wheels be brought into the ante-chamber, and they will go to them and be pleased with them, and that is what no man would do.’ The king liked the advice, and had the spinning-wheels placed in the ante-chamber.
原译: 但是，有一个国王的仆人偏爱猎人，当他听说他们要接受这个考验时，他走到他们面前，重复了一切，说：“狮子想让国王相信你们是女孩。”然后，国王的女儿感谢他，对她的众仆说：你们拿出一点力量来，你们要坚定地踏在豌豆上。第二天早晨，国王叫来十二个猎人，他们来到了豆子躺着的安眠室，他们踏得如此坚定，行得非常有力，以致没有一只豆子滚动或搅动。他们又走了，国王对狮子说：你对我撒谎了，他们象男人一样走路。狮子说：他们确已被告知要受考验，而且有所力量了。你们让十二辆旋转的轮子进入安眠院吧，他们就去他们那里享受，那确是无人能做的。国王喜欢这个建议，并且把旋转轮放在前厅。
现译: 不过国王手下有个仆人，十分偏爱这群猎人。一听说要用这法子试探他们，便去把话一五一十转告了，说：“狮子想让国王相信，你们是姑娘。”公主谢过他，对姑娘们说：“使出力气来，在豌豆上走得稳稳的。”第二天清早，国王召十二个猎人觐见，她们走进撒着豌豆的前厅，每一步都踏得这样稳，步子这样坚实笃定，竟没有一颗豆子滚动或挪位。等她们离去，国王便对狮子说：“你向我撒了谎。他们的走相跟男人一模一样。”狮子说：“她们事先听说要受考验，故意使足了力气。再请人搬十二架纺车到前厅去，她们准会凑上前表示喜欢。这可不是男人会做的。”国王喜欢这个主意，便让人把纺车摆到前厅。

So when they were alone the king’s daughter said to her eleven girls: ‘Show some constraint, and do not look round at the spinning-wheels.’ And next morning when the king had his twelve huntsmen summoned, they went through the ante-chamber, and never once looked at the spinning-wheels. 中文章名: 十二个猎人
英文证据: The twelve huntsmen always followed the king to the chase, and his liking for them continually increased. Now it came to pass that once when they were out hunting, news came that the king’s bride was approaching. When the true bride heard that, it hurt her so much that her heart was almost broken, and she fell fainting to the ground. The king thought something had happened to his dear huntsman, ran up to him, wanted to help him, and drew his glove off. Then he saw the ring which he had given to his first bride, and when he looked in her face he recognized her. Then his heart was so touched that he kissed her, and when she opened her eyes he said: ‘You are mine, and I am yours, and no one in the world can alter that.’ He sent a messenger to the other bride, and entreated her to return to her own kingdom, for he had a wife already, and someone who had just found an old key did not require a new one. Thereupon the wedding was celebrated, and the lion was again taken into favour, because, after all, he had told the truth.
原译: 十二个猎人总是跟着国王追逐并且他对他们的爱心不断提高。现在传闻说，当他们出去打猎时国王的新娘正在接近。当真正的新娘听到这个消息时，她很伤心，心几乎碎了，她昏倒在地。国王以为他亲爱的猎人出了什么事跑到他身边想帮他摘下手套。然后他看到了他送给第一个新娘的戒指，当他看着她的脸时，他认出了她。然后，他的心被触动，以致亲吻她。当她睁开眼睛的时候，他说：你是我的，我是你的，世界上没有一个人能改变这件事。他派了一个信使到另一个新娘，折磨她回到自己的王国，因为他已经有妻子了，刚刚找到一把旧钥匙的人不需要新的钥匙。婚礼就庆祝了狮子又被收买了因为毕竟他说的是实话。
现译: 十二个猎人一直跟随国王出猎，他也一日比一日喜欢他们。有一回打猎途中传来消息，说国王的新娘已经快要到了。原来的新娘一听见，痛得几乎心碎，当场昏倒在地。国王以为自己心爱的猎人出了事，奔上前，想帮帮他，便脱下他的手套。他看见了那枚戒指，那是他给头一位新娘的。再仔细打量她的脸，终于认出了她。他深受感动，低头吻了她。等她睁开眼睛，他说：“你属于我，我也属于你，世上没有谁能改变这一点。”他派使者去见另一位新娘，恳请她返回自己的国度，因为他已经有妻子了。刚刚找回旧钥匙的人，就不需要配一把新的了。于是婚礼举行了。狮子也重新得了宠爱，毕竟它当初说的都是实话。

中文章名: 金山国王

He had two richly laden ships then making a voyage upon the seas, in which he had embarked all his wealth, in the hope of making great gains, when the news came that both were lost. Thus from being a rich man he became all at once so very poor that nothing was left to him but one small plot of land; and there he often went in an evening to take his walk, and ease his mind of a little of his trouble.

中文章名: 金山国王
英文证据: One day, as he was roaming along in a brown study, thinking with no great comfort on what he had been and what he now was, and was like to be, all on a sudden there stood before him a little, rough-looking, black dwarf. ‘Prithee, friend, why so sorrowful?’ said he to the merchant; ‘what is it you take so deeply to heart?’ ‘If you would do me any good I would willingly tell you,’ said the merchant. ‘Who knows but I may?’ said the little man: ‘tell me what ails you, and perhaps you will find I may be of some use.’ Then the merchant told him how all his wealth was gone to the bottom of the sea, and how he had nothing left but that little plot of land. ‘Oh, trouble not yourself about that,’ said the dwarf; ‘only undertake to bring me here, twelve years hence, whatever meets you first on your going home, and I will give you as much as you please.’ The merchant thought this was no great thing to ask; that it would most likely be his dog or his cat, or something of that sort, but forgot his little boy Heinel; so he agreed to the bargain, and signed and sealed the bond to do what was asked of him.
原译: 有一天，当他在一个棕色的书房里漫步时，思考着他曾经和现在是什么样子，并感到很不自在，突然间，站在他面前的是一个小的，粗糙的，黑色的侏儒。朋友阿 、 为何如此忧愁呢 。 他对商人说 、 你如此深心 、 甚么事呢 。 商人说 、 你若肯向我行善 、 我便自愿告诉你。他说：你们告诉我吧！你们所遭遇的是什么，你们或许发现我对于你们有所裨益。然后那个商人告诉他他所有的财富都流到海底了他除了那块小地什么都没有了。侏儒说：不要自找麻烦。只许你带我来这里，十二年之后，无论你回家时遇到什么，我会尽你所能。商人认为这不是件好事；很可能是他的狗或猫，或类似的东西，但忘记了他的小男孩海奈尔；于是他同意了交易，签了字并封了保证书。
现译: 有一天，他正漫无目的地踱着，陷在沉思里。想想自己的从前、如今和往后，越想越不舒坦。忽然面前冒出一个黑黢黢的小矮人，相貌粗野。“请问，朋友，你为什么这样忧愁？”他问商人，“什么事叫你这么放不下？”“你若能帮得上忙，我很愿意告诉你。”商人说。“谁说我帮不上呢？”小人儿说，“说说烦恼吧，说不定你会发现我还有些用处。”商人便说出，自己的财产如何沉入海底，如今剩下的又如何只有这么一小块土地。“哦，别为这个发愁，”矮人说，“只要答应我，在你回家时最先来迎接你的，不论是什么，十二年后把它带到这里来。你想要多少，我就给你多少。”商人心想，这个要求不难办，先迎上来的多半是他家的狗或猫之类。他把自己的小儿子海内尔忘了个干净。于是他答应这桩买卖，在契约上签名盖印，保证依约行事。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 金山国王
英文证据: But as he drew near home, his little boy was so glad to see him that he crept behind him, and laid fast hold of his legs, and looked up in his face and laughed. Then the father started, trembling with fear and horror, and saw what it was that he had bound himself to do; but as no gold was come, he made himself easy by thinking that it was only a joke that the dwarf was playing him, and that, at any rate, when the money came, he should see the bearer, and would not take it in.
原译: 当他走向家门的时候，他的儿子很高兴看到他躲在他身后，紧握着他的双腿，抬起头来笑他。父亲开始以恐惧和恐惧颤抖，看到自己注定要做的事；但是，由于没有金子来，他以为侏儒在耍他只是个玩笑，他觉得不管怎样，当钱来的时候，他应该看到持票人，而不会接受。
现译: 可是他快到家时，小儿子见了他，欢喜得很，在他身后一摇一晃爬上来，牢牢抱住他两条腿，仰起脸冲他笑。父亲猛地一惊，吓得浑身发抖，这才明白自己立约答应了什么。不过还没见到金子，他又安慰自己，说不定那矮人只是开了个玩笑。退一步说，钱来的时候，总能看见是谁送来的，自己只要拒收就是了。

中文章名: 金山国王
英文证据: About a month afterwards he went upstairs into a lumber-room to look for some old iron, that he might sell it and raise a little money; and there, instead of his iron, he saw a large pile of gold lying on the floor. At the sight of this he was overjoyed, and forgetting all about his son, went into trade again, and became a richer merchant than before.
原译: 大约一个月后，他上楼到一个木材房寻找一些旧的铁，以便他可以卖掉它，筹集一点钱；在那里，他看到地上埋着一大堆金子，而不是他的铁。看见这个，他太高兴了，忘记了他儿子的一切，重新进入了贸易，成为一个比以前更富有的商人。
现译: 约莫一个月后，他上楼去杂物间找些旧铁，预备拿去卖了，换几个钱。谁知在放铁的地方，他却看见地板上堆着一大堆黄金。他一见大喜，又把儿子的事忘得一干二净，拿金子重做买卖，成了比从前更富有的商人。

中文章名: 金山国王
英文证据: Meantime little Heinel grew up, and as the end of the twelve years drew near the merchant began to call to mind his bond, and became very sad and thoughtful; so that care and sorrow were written upon his face. The boy one day asked what was the matter, but his father would not tell for some time; at last, however, he said that he had, without knowing it, sold him for gold to a little, ugly-looking, black dwarf, and that the twelve years were coming round when he must keep his word. Then Heinel said, ‘Father, give yourself very little trouble about that; I shall be too much for the little man.’
原译: 同时，小海内尔长大了，随着十二年的结束，商人们开始牢记他的纽带，变得非常悲伤和体贴；这样，他的关心和悲伤就写在他脸上。有一天，男孩问出了什么问题，但他父亲一段时间不说；然而，他最后说，他不知道这一点，就把他卖给了一个小的、丑陋的、黑色的矮人，12年即将来临，他必须信守诺言。海内尔说：我的父亲啊！你为那件事给自己一点小麻烦吧！我对于这个小人来说，是太过分了。'，爱丽丝
现译: 这期间小海内尔渐渐长大。眼看十二年的期限将满，商人才又想起所立的契约，天天闷闷不乐，心事重重，满面都写着忧愁。男孩一天问他出了什么事，父亲起初不肯说，末了只好招认，自己曾经在不知情的时候，把他卖给一个丑陋的黑矮人换了金子。现在十二年就要到期，他非守信不可。海内尔说：“父亲，这事你不用太操心。我有办法对付那个小人儿。”
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 金山国王
英文证据: When the time came, the father and son went out together to the place agreed upon: and the son drew a circle on the ground, and set himself and his father in the middle of it. The little black dwarf soon came, and walked round and round about the circle, but could not find any way to get into it, and he either could not, or dared not, jump over it. At last the boy said to him. ‘Have you anything to say to us, my friend, or what do you want?’ Now Heinel had found a friend in a good fairy, that was fond of him, and had told him what to do; for this fairy knew what good luck was in store for him. ‘Have you brought me what you said you would?’ said the dwarf to the merchant. The old man held his tongue, but Heinel said again, ‘What do you want here?’ The dwarf said, ‘I come to talk with your father, not with you.’ ‘You have cheated and taken in my father,’ said the son; ‘pray give him up his bond at once.’ ‘Fair and softly,’ said the little old man; ‘right is right; I have paid my money, and your father has had it, and spent it; so be so good as to let me have what I paid it for.’ ‘You must have my consent to that first,’ said Heinel, ‘so please to step in here, and let us talk it over.’ The old man grinned, and showed his teeth, as if he should have been very glad to get into the circle if he could. Then at last, after a long talk, they came to terms. Heinel agreed that his father must give him up, and that so far the dwarf should have his way: but, on the other hand, the fairy had told Heinel what fortune was in store for him, if he followed his own course; and he did not choose to be given up to his hump-backed friend, who seemed so anxious for his company.
原译: 到了那个时候，父子们走到一个约定的地方。 儿子在地上画了一个圆圈，然后把自己和父亲放在中间。小黑矮人很快来了环绕圈子走来走去但找不到任何办法进入圈子他要么不能要么不敢跳过圈子。终于那个男孩对他说了。“你有什么要说的吗，我的朋友，还是你想说什么？”现在海妮儿在一个爱他的好仙子里找到了一个朋友告诉他该怎么做因为这个仙子知道他的好运是什么。“你带给我你说过要的东西了吗？” “矮人对商人说。”老头一直守口如瓶但海内尔又说：“你在这里想干什么？”侏儒说 、 我来是要和你父亲说话 、 而不是要和你说话 。 他儿子说 、 你作了弊 、 收买了我的父 。 他说 、 求你立即交出他的捆绑 。 小老头说 、 公平 、 温和 。 事实如此 、 我付我的钱 、 你父也得了 、 也花了；所以最好让我得到我付的钱。'你必须先得到我的同意，'海内尔说，'请进来，让我们好好谈谈。'老头笑了露出了牙齿仿佛他应该很高兴能进入圈子。最后，经过长时间的谈话，他们终于有了条件。海内尔同意他父亲必须放弃他，到目前为止矮人应该有他的方式：但另一方面，仙子告诉Heiner，如果他按照自己的路线行事，他将获得多少财富；他没有选择放弃他的背包朋友，他似乎非常渴望他的陪伴。
现译: 日子到了，父子一同赶赴约定的地点。儿子在地上画了个圈，同父亲站在圈心。小黑矮人很快来了，围着圆圈走了一圈又一圈，找不到进来的路。他要么不能，要么不敢跳过圈线。男孩终于开口：“朋友，有什么话要跟我们说吗？你想要什么？”原来海内尔有一位善良的仙女朋友。仙女喜爱他，知道前头有怎样的好运在等他，先前已经教过他怎么办。“你答应的东西带来了吗？”矮人问商人。父亲闭口不言。海内尔又说：“你来这里要什么？”矮人说：“我来跟你父亲谈话，没问你。”“你算计我父亲，叫他上了当，”儿子说，“请立刻把契约还给他。”“且慢，有话好说，”小老头说，“该怎样就怎样。我付了钱，你父亲收了钱，也花了钱。既然这样，就劳驾把我付钱买的东西交给我吧。”“那得先问我同不同意，”海内尔说，“请进来，咱们商量商量。”小老头龇牙咧嘴地干笑，看样子要是进得去，他倒再乐意不过。两人谈了很久，终于讲定条件。海内尔承认父亲得放弃他，这一点照矮人的意思办。可是仙女早已告诉海内尔，假如照自己的路走下去，怎样的好运会等着他。他可不打算把自己交给这位驼背朋友，随对方多么巴不得有他作伴都不成。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 金山国王
英文证据: So, to make a sort of drawn battle of the matter, it was settled that Heinel should be put into an open boat, that lay on the sea-shore hard by; that the father should push him off with his own hand, and that he should thus be set adrift, and left to the bad or good luck of wind and weather. Then he took leave of his father, and set himself in the boat, but before it got far off a wave struck it, and it fell with one side low in the water, so the merchant thought that poor Heinel was lost, and went home very sorrowful, while the dwarf went his way, thinking that at any rate he had had his revenge.
原译: 所以，为了对这件事进行一场激烈的战斗，已经确定海内尔应该被置于一艘开阔的船上，硬硬地躺在海岸上；父亲应该用自己的手把他推下去，这样他应该被拖下水，任由风和天气的厄运或运气好。然后他离开他父亲，把自己放在船上，但在船远走高飞之前，船撞了它，船掉在水里，商人们以为可怜的海奈尔输了，回到了非常悲伤的家里，而侏儒走在路上，以为他已经报仇了。
现译: 两边各让一步，算成了个平局。大家议定，把海内尔放进近旁海边的一艘敞篷小船，由父亲亲手推船离岸，此后任他漂流，风吹雨打，是福是祸，一切看天。海内尔告别父亲，登上小船。没漂出去多远，一个浪头打来，船向一边倾斜，半边几乎没进水里。商人只当可怜的海内尔已然没命，万分悲伤地回家。矮人也走了，心想不管怎样，自己这口气算出了。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 金山国王
英文证据: The boat, however, did not sink, for the good fairy took care of her friend, and soon raised the boat up again, and it went safely on. The young man sat safe within, till at length it ran ashore upon an unknown land. As he jumped upon the shore he saw before him a beautiful castle but empty and dreary within, for it was enchanted. ‘Here,’ said he to himself, ‘must I find the prize the good fairy told me of.’ So he once more searched the whole palace through, till at last he found a white snake, lying coiled up on a cushion in one of the chambers.
原译: 但是，船没有沉没，因为好仙子照顾了她的朋友，很快又把船抬起来，船安全上船。年轻人坐在里面很安全，直到它长途飞到未知的土地上。当他跳上岸时，他看到了一个美丽的城堡，里面空虚沉闷，因为它被施了魔法。“这里，”他说，“我必须找到奖品，好仙子告诉我。”所以他再次搜查了整个宫殿直到最后他发现了一条白蛇躺在一个房间的垫子上。
现译: 然而船并没有沉。善良的仙女照看着她的朋友，很快扶正小船，让它平稳向前。年轻人安坐在里面，终于在一片陌生土地上靠岸。他一跃上岸，面前是一座美丽的城堡，里面空空荡荡，毫无生气，因为它被施了魔咒。“仙女告诉我的奖赏，”他想，“我一定要在这里把它找出来。”于是他又把整座宫殿从头搜到尾，最后在一间屋的软垫上发现一条白蛇，正盘在那里。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 金山国王
英文证据: Now the white snake was an enchanted princess; and she was very glad to see him, and said, ‘Are you at last come to set me free? Twelve long years have I waited here for the fairy to bring you hither as she promised, for you alone can save me. This night twelve men will come: their faces will be black, and they will be dressed in chain armour. They will ask what you do here, but give no answer; and let them do what they will--beat, whip, pinch, prick, or torment you--bear all; only speak not a word, and at twelve o’clock they must go away. The second night twelve others will come: and the third night twenty-four, who will even cut off your head; but at the twelfth hour of that night their power is gone, and I shall be free, and will come and bring you the Water of Life, and will wash you with it, and bring you back to life and health.’ And all came to pass as she had said; Heinel bore all, and spoke not a word; and the third night the princess came, and fell on his neck and kissed him. Joy and gladness burst forth throughout the castle, the wedding was celebrated, and he was crowned king of the Golden Mountain.
原译: 白蛇曾是一个迷人的公主，她很高兴见到他，她说：你终于来拯救我了吗？十二年来，我一直在这里等待仙女象她所应许的那样把你带来，你独自拯救我。今夜，十二个人将来，他们的脸将变成黑色的。他们将穿著铁链的盔甲，他们问你在这里做什么；他们不答应你；他们将做他们所欲做的事；他们将做他们所意欲的事，他们鞭打、鞭打、捏打、刺杀、或刑罚。他们只说一句话，他们将在十二点钟离开。第二晚，将有十二个人来。第三晚，二十四人来。他将砍掉你的头，但在那个夜间的十二点，他俩的权柄已逝去了，我将自由，我将带来生命之水，而以它洗涤你，使你复返于生命和健康。一如她说的，希内尔无话可说。第三个晚上，公主来了，他摔倒在脖子上，吻了他。欢乐和欢乐在整个城堡爆发，婚礼庆祝，他加冕了金山的国王。
现译: 白蛇原是一位中了魔的公主。她见了他，欢喜极了，说：“你终于来救我了吗？我在这里等了漫长的十二年，等仙女依她所许，把你带来，只有你能救我。今夜会来十二个人，脸庞黝黑，身穿锁子甲。他们会问你来这里做什么，你不要回答。不管他们要怎么处置你——打你，鞭你，掐你，扎你，折磨你——都得忍住，一个字也别说，等到十二点他们就非走不可。第二夜还要再来十二个，第三夜要来二十四个，甚至会砍掉你的脑袋。可是那一夜钟敲十二下，他们的力量就没了，我也将获得自由。我会带着生命之水来，用它洗濯你，让你恢复生命和健康。”一切果然照她所说的发生了。海内尔全都忍了，一个字也没说。第三天夜里，公主来了，搂住他的脖子吻他。欢声笑语传遍整座城堡。人们为他俩举行婚礼，并为他加冕。从此，他就是金山国王。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 金山国王
英文证据: They lived together very happily, and the queen had a son. And thus eight years had passed over their heads, when the king thought of his father; and he began to long to see him once again. But the queen was against his going, and said, ‘I know well that misfortunes will come upon us if you go.’ However, he gave her no rest till she agreed. At his going away she gave him a wishing-ring, and said, ‘Take this ring, and put it on your finger; whatever you wish it will bring you; only promise never to make use of it to bring me hence to your father’s house.’ Then he said he would do what she asked, and put the ring on his finger, and wished himself near the town where his father lived.
原译: 他们一起生活很幸福女王有个儿子。国王想到他的父亲，他们已逝去了八年，他又开始长相见。但皇后反对他的行动，他说：我知道，如果你们去，那末，灾难必定降临我们。但是，她同意之前，他不让她休息。他走了之后，她就为他说：你拿这个戒指去，你把它戴在你的手指上，无论你希望它带给你什么，你都不要用它来带我到你父亲的家里去。然后他说他会照她的要求去做，把戒指放在他的手指上，并祝愿自己靠近他父亲居住的小镇。
现译: 他们快活地住在一起，王后生了个儿子。八年过去，国王想起父亲，越来越盼望能再见他一面。王后却不赞成他说走就走：“我知道，你这一去，有祸事要降到我们头上。”可是他不停求她，终于求得她答应。临行时，王后给了他一枚许愿戒指，说：“拿着这戒指，戴在手上。你想要什么，它都能带给你。只答应我，千万别用它把我从这里带到你父亲家去。”他说一定照她的意思办，戴上戒指，许愿让自己来到父亲居住的城镇附近。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 金山国王
英文证据: Heinel found himself at the gates in a moment; but the guards would not let him go in, because he was so strangely clad. So he went up to a neighbouring hill, where a shepherd dwelt, and borrowed his old frock, and thus passed unknown into the town. When he came to his father’s house, he said he was his son; but the merchant would not believe him, and said he had had but one son, his poor Heinel, who he knew was long since dead: and as he was only dressed like a poor shepherd, he would not even give him anything to eat. The king, however, still vowed that he was his son, and said, ‘Is there no mark by which you would know me if I am really your son?’ ‘Yes,’ said his mother, ‘our Heinel had a mark like a raspberry on his right arm.’ Then he showed them the mark, and they knew that what he had said was true.
原译: 海内尔在一瞬间就发现自己在门口，但卫兵不让他进去，因为他是那么的奇怪。于是，他走到一个邻近的山丘上，有一个牧羊人住在那里，他借去了他的旧衣服，然后不知名地进入了这个城市。当他来到他父亲家的时候，他说他是他的儿子，但商人不相信他，他说他只有一个儿子，就是他可怜的海奈尔，他早就知道这个儿子已经去世了；他只是穿得像一个可怜的牧羊人，他甚至不给他任何食物。但王仍誓 、 以他是他的子 、 说 、 我是你的子 、 你知道我的分 、 岂不是么 。 他的母亲说 、 我的海牛 、 右臂上有像草莓那样的分 、 是的。然后，他昭示他们这个迹象，他们就知道他所说的是真实的。
现译: 转眼海内尔已经站在城门口，守卫见他穿着奇异，却不肯放他进城。他便上了附近一座山，找住在那里的牧羊人借了件旧罩衫，这才没叫人认出来，顺利进了城。到了父亲家，他说自己就是他的儿子，商人却坚决不信，说他只有一个儿子，可怜的海内尔，老早就死了，这是他知道的。这人一副穷牧羊人的打扮，他连一口吃的也不肯给他。国王却仍坚持自己正是他的儿子，说：“倘若真是我，难道身上没有一处记号，是你们认得出的吗？”“有，”母亲答道，“我们海内尔右胳膊上有块像覆盆子的胎记。”他给他们看了胎记。他们这才知道他的话是真的。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 金山国王
英文证据: He next told them how he was king of the Golden Mountain, and was married to a princess, and had a son seven years old. But the merchant said, ‘that can never be true; he must be a fine king truly who travels about in a shepherd’s frock!’ At this the son was vexed; and forgetting his word, turned his ring, and wished for his queen and son. In an instant they stood before him; but the queen wept, and said he had broken his word, and bad luck would follow. 中文章名: 万事通大夫

When the money was being counted out to him, it so happened that the doctor was sitting at table, and when the peasant saw how well he ate and drank, his heart desired what he saw, and would willingly have been a doctor too. So he remained standing a while, and at length inquired if he too could not be a doctor. ‘Oh, yes,’ said the doctor, ‘that is soon managed.’ ‘What must I do?’ asked the peasant. ‘In the first place buy yourself an A B C book of the kind which has a cock on the frontispiece; in the second, turn your cart and your two oxen into money, and get yourself some clothes, and whatsoever else pertains to medicine; thirdly, have a sign painted for yourself with the words: “I am Doctor Knowall,” and have that nailed up above your house-door.’ The peasant did everything that he had been told to do. When he had doctored people awhile, but not long, a rich and great lord had some money stolen. Then he was told about Doctor Knowall who lived in such and such a village, and must know what had become of the money. So the lord had the horses harnessed to his carriage, drove out to the village, and asked Crabb if he were Doctor Knowall. Yes, he was, he said. Then he was to go with him and bring back the stolen money. ‘Oh, yes, but Grete, my wife, must go too.’ The lord was willing, and let both of them have a seat in the carriage, and they all drove away together. When they came to the nobleman’s castle, the table was spread, and Crabb was told to sit down and eat. ‘Yes, but my wife, Grete, too,’ said he, and he seated himself with her at the table. The servant, however, thought he intended by that to say: ‘That is the first thief,’ and as he actually was so, he was terrified, and said to his comrade outside: ‘The doctor knows all: we shall fare ill, he said I was the first.’ The second did not want to go in at all, but was forced. So when he went in with his dish, the peasant nudged his wife, and said: ‘Grete, that is the second.’ This servant was equally alarmed, and he got out as fast as he could. The third fared no better, for the peasant again said: ‘Grete, that is the third.’ The fourth had to carry in a dish that was covered, and the lord told the doctor that he was to show his skill, and guess what was beneath the cover. The doctor looked at the dish, had no idea what to say, and cried: ‘Ah, poor Crabb.’ When the lord heard that, he cried: ‘There! he knows it; he must also know who has the money!’

中文章名: 生菜

原译: 然后，他离开他的朋友们，把他的包挂在脖子上，然后走向他的道路。有一天他的路穿过了一根厚木头，树的尽头是一座绿色草原上的一座大城堡，在一个窗户上，站在一个老妇人旁边，一位非常美丽的年轻女士看着他们。那个老妇人曾是一个巫婆，对那个年轻女子说：有一个青年男子从树林里出来，拿起一个很棒的奖品，我们必须把它从他身上拿走，我的孩子，因为那比他更适合我们。他有一个鸟的心，每天早晨把一块金子放在他的枕头下。狩猎者走近了看这位女士，对自己说，“我旅行了那么久，我想进城堡休息，因为我有足够的钱来支付我想要的一切。” 但真正的原因是，他想多见一位美丽的女士。然后他走进房子受到欢迎不久他就会爱上她了他除了看着她的眼睛做她想做的事。然后那个老妇人说：现在是时候去取鸟的心了。所以这位女士偷走了它，他从没有在他的枕头下找到任何更多的金子，因为现在它躺在这位年轻女士的下面，每天早上，这位老妇人拿走了它；但他深爱着它，所以他从来没有错过过他的奖品。
现译: 他辞别朋友，把猎袋和弓往脖子上一挂，上了路。一天，他沿路穿过密林，林子尽头是一片青翠的草地，草地上耸立着一座大城堡。一扇窗边站着一个老妇人，身旁有位极美的年轻姑娘，两人正在向外张望。原来老妇人是女巫，对姑娘说：“有个年轻人正从林子里出来，身上带着一件极好的宝贝。亲爱的孩子，咱们得把它夺过来。那东西归咱们，可比归他合适。他有颗鸟心，每天清早都会给他在枕底送来一块金子。”这时猎人走近，看见了姑娘，自言自语：“我旅行了这么久，很想进城堡歇歇。反正我要什么都有钱付。”其实真正的缘故是他想多看那美丽姑娘几眼。他进了门，得到热情接待。不久他便爱她爱得什么也顾不上，心里只想望着她的眼睛，为她做一切她要他做的事。老婆子便说：“眼下正是取到鸟心的时候。”姑娘偷偷拿走了鸟心。猎人再没在自己的枕下见到金子，因为金子现在躺在姑娘的枕底下，每天早上都被老婆子取了去。可他爱得如此深，竟连宝物不见了也没在意。

中文章名: 生菜
英文证据: ‘Well,’ said the old witch, ‘we have got the bird’s heart, but not the wishing-cloak yet, and that we must also get.’ ‘Let us leave him that,’ said the young lady; ‘he has already lost his wealth.’ Then the witch was very angry, and said, ‘Such a cloak is a very rare and wonderful thing, and I must and will have it.’ So she did as the old woman told her, and set herself at the window, and looked about the country and seemed very sorrowful; then the huntsman said, ‘What makes you so sad?’ ‘Alas! dear sir,’ said she, ‘yonder lies the granite rock where all the costly diamonds grow, and I want so much to go there, that whenever I think of it I cannot help being sorrowful, for who can reach it? only the birds and the flies--man cannot.’ ‘If that’s all your grief,’ said the huntsman, ‘I’ll take you there with all my heart’; so he drew her under his cloak, and the moment he wished to be on the granite mountain they were both there. The diamonds glittered so on all sides that they were delighted with the sight and picked up the finest. But the old witch made a deep sleep come upon him, and he said to the young lady, ‘Let us sit down and rest ourselves a little, I am so tired that I cannot stand any longer.’ So they sat down, and he laid his head in her lap and fell asleep; and whilst he was sleeping on she took the cloak from his shoulders, hung it on her own, picked up the diamonds, and wished herself home again.
原译: 那个老巫婆说：我们已获得鸟儿的心，但还没有获得希望，我们也必须获得希望。(他已获得希望了。)他说：我们已获得希望了。女巫非常生气，说：这件斗篷是一件稀有而美妙的事，我必定要拥有它。她照老妇人所说的话做了，她把自己放在窗户边，看一看这个国家，看起来很悲伤。后来，猎人说：你为什么这么伤心？她说：唉，亲爱的先生，她说：(她)是花岗岩，那里生长着所有昂贵的钻石，我想去那里。当我想起这件事的时候，我感到悲伤，谁能达到它呢？只有鸟儿和苍蝇才能达到。狩猎者说：如果那是你的悲伤，那末，我誓必带着你到那个地方去。他就把她拉在斗篷下，那一刻他想在花岗岩山上他们俩都在那里。钻石的光亮在所有方面，他们很高兴的目光并捡起最好的。但是那个老巫婆睡了一会儿，对这位年轻女士说：“让我们坐下来休息一会，我太累了，我再也站不住了。”于是他们坐下，他把头放在她的腿上，睡着了；他睡在她的肩膀上时，她把斗篷从肩膀上拿下来，自己挂起来，捡起钻石，希望自己再次回家。
现译: “好啦，”老女巫说，“鸟心到手了，许愿斗篷还没有。咱们也得把它弄来。”“就把斗篷留给他吧，”姑娘说，“他已经失去了财富。”女巫大为生气，说：“这样一件斗篷何等稀罕奇妙，我非得到不可！”于是姑娘照她吩咐，坐在窗前，向郊野眺望，露出一副十分忧伤的样子。猎人便问：“什么事叫你这么难过？”“唉，好先生，”她说，“远处那座花岗石山上长着种种名贵的钻石。我多想去看看，可每回想起，免不了伤心。谁上得去呢？只有鸟儿和飞虫能飞到，人可去不了。”“你若只为这个发愁，”猎人说，“我心甘情愿带你上去。”他把她往斗篷底下一揽，心里才想着要去花岗石山，两人已经站在那儿了。四面钻石灿灿发光，这景色令他们满心愉悦，便挑最好的拾了起来。可是老女巫使了法术，让一阵浓重的睡意落在猎人身上。他对姑娘说：“咱们坐下歇会儿吧。我累得站都站不稳了。”两人坐下，他枕着她的膝头睡着了。趁他熟睡，她把斗篷从他肩上解下来，披到自己身上，捡起钻石，许愿回到了家里。
