Besides the soreness in my mouth, and the pain in my neck, it always made my windpipe feel bad, and if I had stopped there long I know it would have spoiled my breathing; but I grew more and more restless and irritable, I could not help it; and I began to snap and kick when any one came to harness me; for this the groom beat me, and one day, as they had just buckled us into the carriage, and were straining my head up with that rein, I began to plunge and kick with all my might. 中文章名: 第一部 / 第9章　快腿儿
英文证据: “Of course not; I would not do such a thing for the best oats that ever came into the stable; why, I am as careful of our young ladies as the master could be, and as for the little ones it is I who teach them to ride. When they seem frightened or a little unsteady on my back I go as smooth and as quiet as old pussy when she is after a bird; and when they are all right I go on again faster, you see, just to use them to it; so don't you trouble yourself preaching to me; I am the best friend and the best riding-master those children have. It is not them, it is the boys; boys,” said he, shaking his mane, “are quite different; they must be broken in as we were broken in when we were colts, and just be taught what's what. The other children had ridden me about for nearly two hours, and then the boys thought it was their turn, and so it was, and I was quite agreeable. They rode me by turns, and I galloped them about, up and down the fields and all about the orchard, for a good hour. They had each cut a great hazel stick for a riding-whip, and laid it on a little too hard; but I took it in good part, till at last I thought we had had enough, so I stopped two or three times by way of a hint. Boys, you see, think a horse or pony is like a steam-engine or a thrashing-machine, and can go on as long and as fast as they please; they never think that a pony can get tired, or have any feelings; so as the one who was whipping me could not understand I just rose up on my hind legs and let him slip off behind--that was all. He mounted me again, and I did the same. Then the other boy got up, and as soon as he began to use his stick I laid him on the grass, and so on, till they were able to understand--that was all. They are not bad boys; they don't wish to be cruel. I like them very well; but you see I had to give them a lesson. When they brought me to James and told him I think he was very angry to see such big sticks. He said they were only fit for drovers or gypsies, and not for young gentlemen.”
原译: “当然不是，我不会做这样的事情最好的燕麦，曾经来到马厩；为什么，我对我们年轻的女士可能像主人一样小心，至于那些幼童，我教他们骑马。当他们似乎害怕或有点不稳的时候，我像老猫一样顺畅安静，当她追逐一只鸟的时候；当他们平安的时候，我走得更快，你看，只是用它们来教它；所以不要烦恼你对我说教；我是那些孩子最好的朋友和最好的骑师。不是他们，而是男孩。男孩们摇晃着他的马蹄，他说：“他们很不一样。我们必须打破他们，就像我们被打碎的时候，并且教他们什么是。其他的孩子骑了我近两个小时。男孩们以为轮到他们了，所以他们就来了，我也很讨人喜欢。他们轮流骑我，我把他们赶到田地上，在果园里，在一整小时里，我把他们赶到地上。他们每人都割了一根大哈泽尔棍子做骑马的鞭子，并且把它打得有点硬。但我把它放在了很好的一部分，直到最后我以为我们已经受够了，所以我停下来了两三次，作为提示。 男孩们，你看，认为马或小马像蒸汽发动机或打马机一样，并且可以继续，只要他们愿意，他们不会认为小马会疲倦，或有任何感觉。因为鞭打我的那个人，我无法理解，我只是站起来，让他从后面溜走。他又把我抬起来，我也做了同样的动作。然后，另一个男孩站起来，一开始用他的棍子，我就把他放在草地上，等等，直到他们能了解。他们不是恶人，他们不希望残酷。我的确喜欢他们，但你们知道我必须给他们一个教训。当他们把我带到詹姆斯面前，并且告诉他，我以为他很生气看到这样的大棒的时候，他说他们只适合驾车者或吉卜赛人。而不是为年轻的绅士们。”
现译: “当然没有！就是把这马厩里进过的最好的燕麦都给我，我也不干那种事。哎，我对咱们两位小姐，小心起来绝不比主人差。那些小一点的孩子，更是由我教他们骑马的。他们露出害怕的样子，或者在我背上坐得不够稳，我走得就跟老猫悄悄跟着鸟儿那样又轻又稳。等他们坐安稳，我才渐渐快起来，你懂吧，正好叫他们习惯一点。所以不劳你来教训我。我是那些孩子最好的朋友，也是他们最好的骑术老师。我说的哪是他们，是那几个大男孩。男孩子呀，”他说着，摇动鬃毛，“全然不同。我们做马驹时得受调教，他们也得好好调教一番，教教他们怎么回事。别的孩子已经骑我兜了快两个钟头，男孩们觉得该轮到他们了。这当然没说错，我也完全同意。他们轮流骑，我驮着他们驰骋，在地里跑上跑下，在果园里四处兜圈，足足跑了一个钟头。他们各自砍了根粗榛树条当马鞭，下手重了些，我也没太放在心上。后来觉得彼此都该歇了，我便停下两三回，想给点暗示。你瞧，大男孩以为大马小马都是蒸汽机、打谷机，只要他们乐意，要多快有多快，要走多久就走多久。他们从不想，小矮马也会疲倦，也会有感觉。那个正抽我的人既不懂，我就往后腿上一立，让他从我身后滑下去，如此而已。他又骑上来，我就照做一次。换另一个男孩上来，才开始动棍子，我便把他安放到草地上。就这样，一直到他们弄懂为止。没别的。他们不是坏孩子，并没存心残忍。我还挺喜欢他们呢。可你知道，这堂课我非给他们上不可。他们把我带回詹姆斯跟前，告诉他出了什么事。我看他一看到那些粗棍子就很生气。他说这种棍子只配赶牲口的人或流浪的吉卜赛人使，不是有教养的小绅士该拿的东西。”

英文证据: “No doubt you would,” said Merrylegs; “but then I am not quite such a fool (begging your pardon) as to anger our master or make James ashamed of me. Besides, those children are under my charge when they are riding; I tell you they are intrusted to me. Why, only the other day I heard our master say to Mrs. Blomefield, 'My dear madam, you need not be anxious about the children; my old Merrylegs will take as much care of them as you or I could; I assure you I would not sell that pony for any money, he is so perfectly good-tempered and trustworthy;' and do you think I am such an ungrateful brute as to forget all the kind treatment I have had here for five years, and all the trust they place in me, and turn vicious because a couple of ignorant boys used me badly? No, no! you never had a good place where they were kind to you, and so you don't know, and I'm sorry for you; but I can tell you good places make good horses. I wouldn't vex our people for anything; I love them, I do,” said Merrylegs, and he gave a low “ho, ho, ho!” through his nose, as he used to do in the morning when he heard James' footstep at the door.

现译: “你准会，”快腿儿说，“不过，恕我说一句，我还没傻到要惹主人发火，叫詹姆斯为我羞愧。而且孩子们一上马，就归我照管。我告诉你，是人家把他们托付给我的。就前几天，我还听见主人跟布洛姆菲尔德太太说，‘亲爱的太太，您不用为孩子们担心。我们家老快腿儿会照看好他们，跟您亲自看着，或我亲自看着，一样用心。我敢向您保证，给多少钱我也不会卖掉那匹矮马，他的脾气那么好，简直再可靠不过。’难道你以为我是个不知感恩的畜生，能忘掉在这里五年来受的善待，忘掉他们多么信任我，只因为两个不懂事的孩子亏待了我，就动起坏脾气？不，不！你没赶上过人家好好待你的好地方，所以你不明白。我为你难过。可我告诉你，好地方能养出好马来。为了什么，我都不肯叫这一家子烦心。我爱他们，我真的爱他们。”快腿儿说着，用鼻子轻轻发出“呵，呵，呵”的低鸣，就像早晨在门外听见詹姆斯的脚步声时一样。

中文章名: 第一部 / 第10章　果园里的谈话
英文证据: Ginger and I were not of the regular tall carriage horse breed, we had more of the racing blood in us. We stood about fifteen and a half hands high; we were therefore just as good for riding as we were for driving, and our master used to say that he disliked either horse or man that could do but one thing; and as he did not want to show off in London parks, he preferred a more active and useful kind of horse. As for us, our greatest pleasure was when we were saddled for a riding party; the master on Ginger, the mistress on me, and the young ladies on Sir Oliver and Merrylegs. It was so cheerful to be trotting and cantering all together that it always put us in high spirits. I had the best of it, for I always carried the mistress; her weight was little, her voice was sweet, and her hand was so light on the rein that I was guided almost without feeling it.
原译: 姜儿和我不是普通的马匹品种我们的血流得更多。我们站着15个半手高高，因此我们同样擅长骑马，我们的主人曾经说，他不喜欢马或人，只做一件事；他不想在伦敦公园炫耀，他更喜欢更积极、更有用的马。至于我们，我们最大的快乐是我们被安排去参加一个骑马派对；姜儿的主人，我的情妇，奥利弗爵士和快腿儿的年轻女士。快乐地一起漫步一起滑雪使我们永远充满了激情。我拥有最好的东西，因为我总是抱着情妇；她的体重很小，她的声音很甜美，她的手是如此的轻，以至于我几乎没有感觉到它。
现译: 姜儿和我都不是通常那一类高大的挽车马，我们身上赛马的血统更多些。我们肩高约十五掌半，既适合驾车，也一样适合骑乘。主人常说，无论是马还是人，他都不喜欢只会做一样事的。他又不打算去伦敦的公园里炫耀，比起一味要体面，他情愿养行动灵活而实用的马。至于我们，最高兴的时候莫过于全家出骑，给我们套上鞍，主人骑姜儿，夫人骑我，小姐们分别骑奥利弗爵士和快腿儿。大家一同小跑，一同轻驰，好不畅快，每回都让我们精神大振。我得的差事最好，因为我总是驮夫人。她身子轻，声音柔和，握缰的手又轻得很，我几乎觉察不到，她已经把路指给我了。

中文章名: 第一部 / 第10章　果园里的谈话
英文证据: Oh! if people knew what a comfort to horses a light hand is, and how it keeps a good mouth and a good temper, they surely would not chuck, and drag, and pull at the rein as they often do. Our mouths are so tender that where they have not been spoiled or hardened with bad or ignorant treatment, they feel the slightest movement of the driver's hand, and we know in an instant what is required of us. My mouth has never been spoiled, and I believe that was why the mistress preferred me to Ginger, although her paces were certainly quite as good. She used often to envy me, and said it was all the fault of breaking in, and the gag bit in London, that her mouth was not so perfect as mine; and then old Sir Oliver would say, “There, there! don't vex yourself; you have the greatest honor; a mare that can carry a tall man of our master's weight, with all your spring and sprightly action, does not need to hold her head down because she does not carry the lady; we horses must take things as they come, and always be contented and willing so long as we are kindly used.”
原译: 如果人们知道轻手骑马有多舒服如何保持口好口好脾气他们肯定不会像他们经常做的那样摇摆拖拉拉。我们的嘴是如此温柔，以至于在他们没有被坏或无知的对待所宠坏或硬化的地方，他们感到驾驶者的手一动不动，我们立刻就知道需要我们做什么。我的嘴从来没有被宠坏过，我相信这就是为什么情妇喜欢我比姜儿，尽管她的步伐肯定相当不错。她经常羡慕我，并说这是所有的错闯入，和在伦敦的口香糖咬，她的嘴并不如我的那么完美；然后老奥利弗爵士会说，“在那里，不要自欺欺人；你拥有最大的荣誉；尽管你充满生机、行动敏捷，却不必低着头，因为你并非女士。我们马儿只需接受现实，只要得到善用，永远保持满足与乐意即可。
现译: 唉，要是人们知道，一只手放得轻些能叫马多么舒服，多么能保住一张灵敏的嘴和一副好脾气，想必就不会像平常那样对缰绳又拽又扯又猛抽。我们的嘴何等娇嫩，只要没让坏手法或不懂行的人弄伤，弄得麻木，车夫的手再轻微不过的一个动作也能感觉到，我们立刻就会懂得他要什么。我的嘴从没被弄坏。我想，夫人爱骑我胜过姜儿，就为这个，虽然她的步法一点也不比我的差。姜儿常常羡慕我，说她的嘴不如我的好，全怪小时候的调教，再加上伦敦用的那副强提马嘴的衔铁。这时候老奥利弗爵士便会说：“好啦，好啦，不必烦心。你的差事可更有荣耀。一位像我们主人这样高大沉重的男人，你驮得动，动作又那么轻快有弹性。哪有必要只因没驮夫人就低着脑袋？做马的，该来的事来了就受着，只要人家善待我们，便该知足，也该乐意干活。”

英文证据: I had often wondered how it was that Sir Oliver had such a very short tail; it really was only six or seven inches long, with a tassel of hair hanging from it; and on one of our holidays in the orchard I ventured to ask him by what accident it was that he had lost his tail. “Accident!” he snorted with a fierce look, “it was no accident! it was a cruel, shameful, cold-blooded act! When I was young I was taken to a place where these cruel things were done; I was tied up, and made fast so that I could not stir, and then they came and cut off my long and beautiful tail, through the flesh and through the bone, and took it away.
原译: 我经常想，奥利弗爵士的尾巴怎么这么短；实际上只有六到七英寸长，上面挂着一副头发；在果园的一个节日，我冒昧地问他，他的尾巴是因什么意外而失去的。意外！他用凶狠的眼神打呼噜，“这不是偶然的，那是残忍的，可耻的，冷血的！”当我年轻时，我被带到一个地方在那里这些残酷的事情做；我被绑起来，并快速地使我无法搅动，然后他们来了切掉我的长长和美丽的尾巴，通过肉和骨头。
现译: 我一直好奇，奥利弗爵士怎么会有一条那样短的尾巴。它真的只有六七英寸长，上头垂着一小绺毛，像个穗子。一个假日，我们在果园里，我壮着胆问他，是出了什么意外，把尾巴给弄没了。“意外！”他猛喷一声响鼻，神情凶得很，“哪是什么意外！那是桩残忍、可耻、冷血的事！年轻时，人家把我带到专做这种残忍事的地方，把我绑住，再牢牢固定好，让我一下也动不了。他们走过来，把我又长又漂亮的尾巴，连肉带骨地切下，带走了。

英文证据: “Dreadful, ah! it was dreadful; but it was not only the pain, though that was terrible and lasted a long time; it was not only the indignity of having my best ornament taken from me, though that was bad; but it was this, how could I ever brush the flies off my sides and my hind legs any more? 中文章名: 第一部 / 第15章　老马夫
英文证据: “Practice makes perfect,” said the crooked little hostler, “and 'twould be a pity if it didn't; forty years' practice, and not perfect! ha, ha! that would be a pity; and as to being quick, why, bless you! that is only a matter of habit; if you get into the habit of being quick it is just as easy as being slow; easier, I should say; in fact it don't agree with my health to be hulking about over a job twice as long as it need take. Bless you! I couldn't whistle if I crawled over my work as some folks do! You see, I have been about horses ever since I was twelve years old, in hunting stables, and racing stables; and being small, ye see, I was jockey for several years; but at the Goodwood, ye see, the turf was very slippery and my poor Larkspur got a fall, and I broke my knee, and so of course I was of no more use there. But I could not live without horses, of course I couldn't, so I took to the hotels. And I can tell ye it is a downright pleasure to handle an animal like this, well-bred, well-mannered, well-cared-for; bless ye! I can tell how a horse is treated. Give me the handling of a horse for twenty minutes, and I'll tell you what sort of a groom he has had. Look at this one, pleasant, quiet, turns about just as you want him, holds up his feet to be cleaned out, or anything else you please to wish; then you'll find another fidgety, fretty, won't move the right way, or starts across the stall, tosses up his head as soon as you come near him, lays his ears, and seems afraid of you; or else squares about at you with his heels. Poor things! I know what sort of treatment they have had. If they are timid it makes them start or shy; if they are high-mettled it makes them vicious or dangerous; their tempers are mostly made when they are young. Bless you! they are like children, train 'em up in the way they should go, as the good book says, and when they are old they will not depart from it, if they have a chance.”
原译: 邪恶的小主人说：“实践是完美的，” “如果它没有，那就不算遗憾了，40年的实践，而不是完美的！” 哈哈哈！那太可惜了。 至于快速，为什么，保佑你！这只是个习惯而已。如果你习惯了快速，它就像慢一点一样简单，我应该说，事实上，我的身体并不同意做一份需要两倍的工作。 祝福你！如果我像其他人一样爬过工作，我就不能吹口哨！从十二岁起，我就一直在马场工作，既在狩猎马厩，也在赛马厩里。由于我身材矮小，好几年都担任骑师。但在古德伍德，地面非常滑，我可怜的拉克斯珀摔了一跤，结果我的膝盖也受伤了。当然，我在那里没有用处。但是，我没有马，我当然不能，所以我带了旅馆。我可以告诉你，处理这样的动物是一件非常愉快的事，它很健康，有教养，有教养，有照顾，有照顾。上帝保佑你们！我看得出马是如何被对待的。给我20分钟的马的处理方式，我会告诉你他有什么样的新郎。看看这个，愉快，安静，转身，就像你想要他一样，举起他的脚来清理，或者你想要的任何东西；然后你会发现另一个小矮人，费蒂，你走错路了，或者跨过摊位，你一靠近他，就把他的头抬起来，打他的耳朵，看你怕你，或者用他的脚跟对着你，可怜的东西！我知道他们有什么样的待遇。如果他们胆怯，那会使他们开始，或害羞。如果他们是高贵的，那使他们变成恶人或危险的人；他们的情状，在他们年轻的时候，大半是陈腐的。你应当保佑他们吧！他们确是像儿童一样，故你应当把他们训练成自己的行为。他们既老了，又不会离开。如果他们有希望的话。

英文证据: “I don't often speak of myself,” said John, “but as you are going away from us out into the world to shift for yourself I'll just tell you how I look on these things. I was just as old as Joseph when my father and mother died of the fever within ten days of each other, and left me and my cripple sister Nelly alone in the world, without a relation that we could look to for help. I was a farmer's boy, not earning enough to keep myself, much less both of us, and she must have gone to the workhouse but for our mistress (Nelly calls her her angel, and she has good right to do so). She went and hired a room for her with old Widow Mallet, and she gave her knitting and needlework when she was able to do it; and when she was ill she sent her dinners and many nice, comfortable things, and was like a mother to her. Then the master he took me into the stable under old Norman, the coachman that was then. I had my food at the house and my bed in the loft, and a suit of clothes, and three shillings a week, so that I could help Nelly. Then there was Norman; he might have turned round and said at his age he could not be troubled with a raw boy from the plow-tail, but he was like a father to me, and took no end of pains with me. When the old man died some years after I stepped into his place, and now of course I have top wages, and can lay by for a rainy day or a sunny day, as it may happen, and Nelly is as happy as a bird. So you see, James, I am not the man that should turn up his nose at a little boy and vex a good, kind master. No, no! I shall miss you very much, James, but we shall pull through, and there's nothing like doing a kindness when 'tis put in your way, and I am glad I can do it.”
原译: 约翰说：“我并不常提到自己，但当你离开我们到外面去为自己而改变自己的时候，我告诉你我是如何看待这些事情的。我和约瑟夫一样老，当时我的父亲和母亲在10天之内死于发烧，我和我残废的妹妹内莉独自生活在世界上。与我们没有关系，我们无法寻求帮助。我是一个农民的孩子，挣的钱不足以养活自己，更不能说我们俩了。她一定是去上班了，但是为了我们的情妇(Nelly称她为天使，她有权这样做)。她和老寡妇Mallet一起为她雇了一间房间，当她能做时，她给她织了织衣和针线；当她生病的时候，她给她送了晚餐和许多舒适舒适的东西，就像一个母亲一样。然后，主人把我带到了那个老诺曼的马厩里，那个马厩里，那个当时的教练。我在房子里吃东西，床上在阁楼里，和一件衣服，和三先令一周，以便我助内莉一臂之力。然后，诺曼，他也许转身说，在他这个年纪，他不会为一个从稻尾来的生男孩烦恼，但他对我来说就像一个父亲一样。并且没有结束我的痛苦。当那个老人在我踏入他家之后去世了几年，当然现在我工资很高，并且可以躺过一个雨天或阳光明媚的日子，可能发生，尼莉就像一只鸟一样快乐。你看，詹姆斯，不，不，不，我会非常想你的，詹姆斯，但是我们会挺过来的，没有什么比做善事好的时候，“我很高兴我能做到。”

We came through a village, then through a dark wood, then uphill, then downhill, till after eight miles' run we came to the town, through the streets and into the market-place. It was all quite still except the clatter of my feet on the stones--everybody was asleep. The church clock struck three as we drew up at Dr. White's door. Then he gave me a pailful of water to drink; it was cold and very good, and I drank it all; then he gave me some hay and some corn, and thinking he had done right, he went away. The colts were wild and frolicsome, and one of them bolted across the road and blundered up against Lizzie's hind legs, and whether it was the stupid colt, or the loud cracking of the whip, or both together, I cannot say, but she gave a violent kick, and dashed off into a headlong gallop. 中文章名: 第二部 / 第25章　鲁本·史密斯
英文证据: Now I must say a little about Reuben Smith, who was left in charge of the stables when York went to London. No one more thoroughly understood his business than he did, and when he was all right there could not be a more faithful or valuable man. He was gentle and very clever in his management of horses, and could doctor them almost as well as a farrier, for he had lived two years with a veterinary surgeon. He was a first-rate driver; he could take a four-in-hand or a tandem as easily as a pair. He was a handsome man, a good scholar, and had very pleasant manners. I believe everybody liked him; certainly the horses did. The only wonder was that he should be in an under situation and not in the place of a head coachman like York; but he had one great fault and that was the love of drink. He was not like some men, always at it; he used to keep steady for weeks or months together, and then he would break out and have a “bout” of it, as York called it, and be a disgrace to himself, a terror to his wife, and a nuisance to all that had to do with him. He was, however, so useful that two or three times York had hushed the matter up and kept it from the earl's knowledge; but one night, when Reuben had to drive a party home from a ball he was so drunk that he could not hold the reins, and a gentleman of the party had to mount the box and drive the ladies home. Of course, this could not be hidden, and Reuben was at once dismissed; his poor wife and little children had to turn out of the pretty cottage by the park gate and go where they could. Old Max told me all this, for it happened a good while ago; but shortly before Ginger and I came Smith had been taken back again. York had interceded for him with the earl, who is very kind-hearted, and the man had promised faithfully that he would never taste another drop as long as he lived there. He had kept his promise so well that York thought he might be safely trusted to fill his place while he was away, and he was so clever and honest that no one else seemed so well fitted for it.
原译: 现在我必须说说鲁本·史密斯当约克去伦敦时由他负责马厩。没有人比他更透彻地了解他的生意，当他没事时，就没有比他更忠诚和有价值的人了。他善于管理马匹，非常聪明，而且几乎可以治好马匹，因为他和兽医住过两年。他是一个一流的司机；他可以像一对一样容易地搭乘四对或双对。他是个英俊的男人，一个优秀的学者，并且有非常愉快的礼仪。我相信每个人都喜欢他，当然马也喜欢他。唯一令人惊讶的是，他应该处于一种处境，而不是取代约克这样的教练长；但他有一个大错，那就是喜欢喝酒。他不像某些男人，总是这样；他曾经保持稳定几个星期或几个月在一起，然后他会打破并有一个“关于”它，如约克称之为，并成为耻辱自己，可怕的他的妻子，和一个骚扰与他有关的一切。不过，他很有用，约克两次或三次都隐瞒了这件事情，不让伯爵知道；但有一天晚上，鲁本不得不从舞会上开车回家，他喝得烂醉，不能握着绳子，而派对的一位绅士必须挂上箱子，把女士们赶回家。当然，这不可能被隐藏，鲁本立即被解雇；他可怜的妻子和孩子不得不从公园大门旁边的漂亮的小屋里出来，走到他们可以去的地方。麦克斯告诉我这一切，因为它发生在好一阵子前，但不久之前，我和姜儿来到史密斯被再次夺回。约克曾为他与耳聋交谈，他非常善良，并且他忠实地承诺，只要他住在那里，他就不再尝一滴。他信守诺言约克认为他可以安全地在他离开的时候填补他的位置他聪明诚实似乎没人能胜任。
现译: 现在我得说几句鲁本·史密斯的事。约克去伦敦的时候，马厩的事就交给他料理。若说通晓本行，没有人能比他更透彻。在他头脑清醒的时候，再找不到比他更忠实、更顶用的人。他待马温和，驾驭起来又有办法，甚至给马看病也几乎不亚于一位马医，因为他曾在兽医手下干过两年。他赶车是一等一的好手。四匹马一起驾，或两匹马一前一后驾，在他手里，都跟两匹并排拉车一样容易。他长得英俊，读过不少书，举止也十分讨人喜欢。我相信人人都喜欢他。至少马是肯定喜欢他的。唯一叫人诧异的是，他怎么还在副手的位置上，没有像约克那样做到车夫领班。原来他有一个很大的缺点，就是嗜酒。他不像有些人那样，整天都在喝，往往连续几个星期甚至几个月都稳稳当当，偏会突然发作，照约克的话说，是要“来上一场”。这时候他给自己丢脸，叫妻子害怕，也给所有跟他共事的人惹麻烦。不过他的确能干，约克已经有过两三回把事情瞒下来，没让伯爵知道。但有一天夜里，鲁本该从舞会接一群客人回家，他竟醉得连缰绳也握不住，只得由其中一位男宾登上车夫座，把女士们送回家。这当然瞒不住了，鲁本当即遭到解雇。可怜的妻子带着几个小孩子，不得不搬出庄园门旁那间漂亮的小屋，到能落脚的地方落脚。这全是老马克斯告诉我的，因为事情发生已经很久了。可就在我和姜儿到庄园之前不久，史密斯又被召了回来。约克替他向伯爵求了情，而伯爵心地又很慈厚。鲁本也庄严保证，只要还在这里做事，再不沾一滴酒。他把承诺守得那么好，约克觉得自己外出这段日子，大可放心把职位交给他代理。而且他如此能干又诚实，似乎没有旁人比他更合适了。

中文章名: 第二部 / 第25章　鲁本·史密斯
英文证据: This could not go on; no horse could keep his footing under such circumstances; the pain was too great. I stumbled, and fell with violence on both my knees. Smith was flung off by my fall, and, owing to the speed I was going at, he must have fallen with great force. I soon recovered my feet and limped to the side of the road, where it was free from stones. The moon had just risen above the hedge, and by its light I could see Smith lying a few yards beyond me. He did not rise; he made one slight effort to do so, and then there was a heavy groan. I could have groaned, too, for I was suffering intense pain both from my foot and knees; but horses are used to bear their pain in silence. I uttered no sound, but I stood there and listened. One more heavy groan from Smith; but though he now lay in the full moonlight I could see no motion. I could do nothing for him nor myself, but, oh! how I listened for the sound of horse, or wheels, or footsteps! The road was not much frequented, and at this time of the night we might stay for hours before help came to us. I stood watching and listening. It was a calm, sweet April night; there were no sounds but a few low notes of a nightingale, and nothing moved but the white clouds near the moon and a brown owl that flitted over the hedge. It made me think of the summer nights long ago, when I used to lie beside my mother in the green pleasant meadow at Farmer Grey's.
原译: 这种情况不能继续下去；在这种情形下，没有匹马能够保持自己的地位；痛苦太大。我跌倒了膝盖上都充满了暴力。史密斯被我摔倒时被甩了，并且，由于我的速度，他一定是以巨大的力量坠落。我很快恢复了脚，脚瘸到路边，没有石头。月亮刚刚升到树篱上光线让我看到史密斯躺在我身外几码处。他没有起身，他稍作努力，然后又大呻吟。我本可以呻吟，因为我从脚和膝盖上都忍受着剧烈的痛苦；但马习惯在沉默中承受痛苦。我没有发声，但我站在那里听。史密斯又大喊大叫虽然他现在躺在月光下我看不到任何动静。我无法为他或我做任何事，但是，哦！我是如何听到马的声音，或轮子的声音，或脚步声的！这条路不太频繁，在这个晚上的这个时候，我们也许在有人来帮忙之前要呆上几个小时。我站着看着，听着。那是一个平静的，甜蜜的四月之夜；没有什么声音，只有几张暗夜鸟的低音，什么都没有移动，只有月亮附近的白云和一只棕色的猫头鹰，在树篱上翻转。它让我想起很久以前的夏夜，当时我常躺在我母亲身边，躺在农夫灰的绿色的好草地上。
现译: 这不可能一直持续下去。在这样的情形下，没有哪匹马站得稳，实在太疼了。我失了脚，两只前膝重重摔在地上。我这一倒，把史密斯摔出老远，以我们当时的速度，他落地一定极重。我很快爬起，一瘸一拐挪到路边一块没有石子的地方。月亮刚在树篱上方升起来。月光下，我看见史密斯躺在离我几码远的前头。他没站起来，只略略挣扎了一下，发出一声沉重的呻吟。其实我也想呻吟，蹄子和两膝都疼得厉害。可马向来习惯默默忍痛。我一声不响地站在那儿，竖耳听着。史密斯又低低呻吟了一声。现在他的全身已经沐在月光里，我却看不见他有半点动作。我帮不了他，也帮不了自己。哦，我多么盼着听见一匹马的蹄声、一辆车的轮声，或是一个人的脚步！这条路平时少有人走，夜里到了这个时候，我们也许得等上好几个钟头才有人来帮忙。我站在那里，望着，听着。那是个静谧而清甜的四月夜，除了夜莺几声低唱，再没有别的声音。一切都不动，只有月亮旁的白云，以及从树篱上方轻轻掠过的一只褐色猫头鹰。它叫我想起了很久以前的夏夜，在格雷农场主家那片可爱的青草地上，我曾经紧挨着妈妈躺着。

中文章名: 第二部 / 第27章　从此走下坡路
英文证据: When I reached the end of my journey I found myself in a tolerably comfortable stable, and well attended to. These stables were not so airy and pleasant as those I had been used to. The stalls were laid on a slope instead of being level, and as my head was kept tied to the manger, I was obliged always to stand on the slope, which was very fatiguing. Men do not seem to know yet that horses can do more work if they can stand comfortably and can turn about; however, I was well fed and well cleaned, and, on the whole, I think our master took as much care of us as he could. He kept a good many horses and carriages of different kinds for hire. Sometimes his own men drove them; at others, the horse and chaise were let to gentlemen or ladies who drove themselves.
原译: 当我到达旅途的终点时，我发现自己处于一个令人忍受的舒适稳定之中，并且受到很好的照顾。这些马厩没有我习惯的那么空气和舒适。摊位是放在斜坡上而不是平平的，当我的头被绑在挖土机上时，我总是被迫站在斜坡上，因为斜坡非常肥。男人们似乎还不知道，如果马能安稳地站着，转身，可以做更多的工作；然而，我吃饱了，干净了，总的来说，我认为我们的主人尽可能地照顾我们。他有很多马和马车可以雇人。有时他自己的人开的马；在其他人身上，马和小马被让给自己开的绅士或女士们。
现译: 抵达以后，等待我的是一座还算舒适的马厩，照应也很周到。比起我从前住惯的地方，这里不够通风，也没那么宜人。马栏地面是倾斜的，不像以前那样平坦，笼头又把我拴在食槽前，只得不停地在斜坡上站着，十分疲累。人好像还不知道，若让马站得舒服，偶尔能转个身，它反倒能做更多的活。不过我吃得不错，身上也能梳洗干净。总的说，我想主人已尽力照料我们了。他养了不少马，还有各式各样的车，专供出租。有时由他自己的车夫赶车，有时则把轻车和马一道租给绅士或女士，由他们自己来驾。

中文章名: 第二部 / 第28章　出租马和它的车夫们
英文证据: Besides, these drivers are often careless altogether, and will attend to anything else more than their horses. I went out in the phaeton one day with one of them; he had a lady and two children behind. He flopped the reins about as we started, and of course gave me several unmeaning cuts with the whip, though I was fairly off. There had been a good deal of road-mending going on, and even where the stones were not freshly laid down there were a great many loose ones about. My driver was laughing and joking with the lady and the children, and talking about the country to the right and the left; but he never thought it worth while to keep an eye on his horse or to drive on the smoothest parts of the road; and so it easily happened that I got a stone in one of my fore feet.

中文章名: 第二部 / 第28章　出租马和它的车夫们
英文证据: Now, if Mr. Gordon or John, or in fact any good driver, had been there, he would have seen that something was wrong before I had gone three paces. But this man went on laughing and talking, while at every step the stone became more firmly wedged between my shoe and the frog of my foot. 中文章名: 第二部 / 第28章　出租马和它的车夫们

中文章名: 第二部 / 第29章　伦敦城里人
英文证据: I well remember one spring evening I and Rory had been out for the day. (Rory was the horse that mostly went with me when a pair was ordered, and a good honest fellow he was.) We had our own driver, and as he was always considerate and gentle with us, we had a very pleasant day. We were coming home at a good smart pace, about twilight. Our road turned sharp to the left; but as we were close to the hedge on our own side, and there was plenty of room to pass, our driver did not pull us in. As we neared the corner I heard a horse and two wheels coming rapidly down the hill toward us. The hedge was high, and I could see nothing, but the next moment we were upon each other. Happily for me, I was on the side next the hedge. Rory was on the left side of the pole, and had not even a shaft to protect him. The man who was driving was making straight for the corner, and when he came in sight of us he had no time to pull over to his own side. The whole shock came upon Rory. The gig shaft ran right into the chest, making him stagger back with a cry that I shall never forget. The other horse was thrown upon his haunches and one shaft broken. Well, you get along for a bit, but soon find yourself in a long train of carts and carriages all obliged to go at a walk; perhaps you come to a regular block-up, and have to stand still for minutes together, till something clears out into a side street, or the policeman interferes; you have to be ready for any chance--to dash forward if there be an opening, and be quick as a rat-dog to see if there be room and if there be time, lest you get your own wheels locked or smashed, or the shaft of some other vehicle run into your chest or shoulder. 原译: 每天中途，在街道上交通繁忙时，很难快速开车，但我们做了可以做的事情；当一个好的司机和一匹好的马，相互了解对方时，他们能够做的很好。我有一个非常好的嘴 -- 也就是说我可以由最小的触摸在伦敦，这是一件伟大的事情，在马车，包球，车，面包车，卡车，出租车，和伟大的马车爬行走的步伐；有些走的一种，另一种，另一种，缓慢的，另一些想通过它们；球体每几分钟就停一下来接乘客迫使后面的马也拉上来或通过并赶在他们之前可能你想通过但只是后来有什么东西冲破了狭窄的开口靠近两边的轮子距离更近半英寸他们就会刮伤。你相处了一会儿，但很快发现自己坐在一辆长长的车和马车都不得不去散步。 也许你来一个普通的阻塞，并不得不站在一起几分钟，直到有东西清空出来在一条街，或者警察干预。如果有开口，你必须做好准备冲向前方，并且像一只老鼠狗一样快速看有没有空间，有没有时间，以免你得到自己的轮子锁上或砸碎，或者其他车辆的轴跑进你的胸部或肩膀。这一切都是你必须准备的。如果你想在中午快速通过伦敦..。 ..。它想要练习。
现译: 正午时分，城市的街道填满了各样车辆，要想赶得快总是很难。可凡是能做的，我们都做了。一位好车夫和一匹好马彼此了解，又一条心，真能做出叫人吃惊的事来。我的嘴很灵，也就是说，缰绳只消轻轻一碰，便能叫我转向。在伦敦可太需要这个了。私家马车、公共马车、货车、厢式车、板车、出租马车，还有慢慢以步行速度爬着的大货车，挤在同一条路上。有的朝这边，有的朝那边，有的走得慢，有的急着超过去。公共马车隔几分钟就要猛停一下让人上车，后面的马不是跟着急停，就是设法超过它，抢到前面。你也许想超车，可一道窄缝里恰好有个什么飞冲进来，你只好又缩回公共马车后头。过一会儿，觉得机会来了，终于抢到前头，身子与两边车轮贴得那样近，只需再近半英寸，轮子就要擦上。好吧，顺当走了一阵，一转眼却落入一长列客车货车里，辆辆车全得慢慢走。说不定来一次彻底的堵塞，在原地一站好几分钟，要等什么车拐进支路，或者警察过来疏导才能动。机会一起，你就得准备好，有空隙立刻冲过去，眼睛还得像捕鼠狗那样快，瞅准地方够不够、时间来不来得及，免得自己的车轮跟别人的缠住，或者撞碎，又或者别的车辕尖端直撞进你的胸口、肩头。这一切，你都得有所准备。大中午想迅速穿过伦敦，需要的经验可真不少。

Now Rann the Kite brings home the night
That Mang the Bat sets free--
The herds are shut in byre and hut
For loosed till dawn are we.
This is the hour of pride and power,
Talon and tush and claw.
Oh, hear the call!--Good hunting all
That keep the Jungle Law!
_Night-Song in the Jungle_
原译:
鸢鹰兰恩带来黑夜，
蝙蝠芒把它放飞。
牛圈、棚屋收起牲口，

此时是骄傲的时辰、力量的时辰，
归弯钩一样的鹰爪、獠牙与利爪。
听啊，召唤响了！愿各位猎有所获，
凡守丛林法则者！
《丛林夜歌》
现译:

蝙蝠芒把黑夜放出。

从现在到天明，轮到我们自由。
这是我们的威风时辰，
鹰有钩爪，兽有尖牙利爪。
听，号令来了！愿狩猎顺遂，

Sometimes Bagheera the Black Panther would come lounging through the jungle to see how his pet was getting on, and would purr with his head against a tree while Mowgli recited the day’s lesson to Baloo. The boy could climb almost as well as he could swim, and swim almost as well as he could run. None of the Jungle People like being disturbed, and all are very ready to fly at an intruder. Then, too, Mowgli was taught the Strangers’ Hunting Call, which must be repeated aloud till it is answered, whenever one of the Jungle-People hunts outside his own grounds. 英文证据: They never meant to do any more--the Bandar-log never mean anything at all; but one of them invented what seemed to him a brilliant idea, and he told all the others that Mowgli would be a useful person to keep in the tribe, because he could weave sticks together for protection from the wind; so, if they caught him, they could make him teach them. Of course Mowgli, as a woodcutter’s child, inherited all sorts of instincts, and used to make little huts of fallen branches without thinking how he came to do it. The Monkey-People, watching in the trees, considered his play most wonderful. This time, they said, they were really going to have a leader and become the wisest people in the jungle--so wise that everyone else would notice and envy them. Therefore they followed Baloo and Bagheera and Mowgli through the jungle very quietly till it was time for the midday nap, and Mowgli, who was very much ashamed of himself, slept between the Panther and the Bear, resolving to have no more to do with the Monkey People.

中文章名: 巨蟒卡阿捕猎
英文证据: The next thing he remembered was feeling hands on his legs and arms--hard, strong, little hands--and then a swash of branches in his face, and then he was staring down through the swaying boughs as Baloo woke the jungle with his deep cries and Bagheera bounded up the trunk with every tooth bared. The Bandar-log howled with triumph and scuffled away to the upper branches where Bagheera dared not follow, shouting: “He has noticed us! Bagheera has noticed us. All the Jungle-People admire us for our skill and our cunning.” Then they began their flight; and the flight of the Monkey-People through tree-land is one of the things nobody can describe. They have their regular roads and crossroads, up hills and down hills, all laid out from fifty to seventy or a hundred feet above ground, and by these they can travel even at night if necessary. Two of the strongest monkeys caught Mowgli under the arms and swung off with him through the treetops, twenty feet at a bound. Had they been alone they could have gone twice as fast, but the boy’s weight held them back. Sick and giddy as Mowgli was he could not help enjoying the wild rush, though the glimpses of earth far down below frightened him, and the terrible check and jerk at the end of the swing over nothing but empty air brought his heart between his teeth. His escort would rush him up a tree till he felt the thinnest topmost branches crackle and bend under them, and then with a cough and a whoop would fling themselves into the air outward and downward, and bring up, hanging by their hands or their feet to the lower limbs of the next tree. Sometimes he could see for miles and miles across the still green jungle, as a man on the top of a mast can see for miles across the sea, and then the branches and leaves would lash him across the face, and he and his two guards would be almost down to earth again. So, bounding and crashing and whooping and yelling, the whole tribe of Bandar-log swept along the tree-roads with Mowgli their prisoner.
原译: 他记得的接下来是双手触碰他的腿和手臂——那是一双坚硬而有力的小手——接着有树枝在脸上刮过，然后他透过摇晃的树枝向下看，此时巴鲁正用低沉的叫声唤醒丛林，而巴希拉则张牙舞口地沿着树干向上跑。巴希拉不敢追随的上部树枝上边，班达尔人大喊着：“他注意到我们了，巴希拉注意到了我们。所有丛林人民都钦佩我们的技巧和狡猾。”然后他们开始飞行猴子人飞过树地是没人能描述的东西之一。他们有正常的道路和十字路口，有上山和下山，在地面上50至70或100英尺处铺设，必要时可以在夜间旅行。两个最强壮的猴子抓住了毛格利并和他一起从树顶上摔下来 20英尺处被捆绑着。如果她们独自一人的话，她们可能走得比她们快两倍，但男孩的体重却挡住了她们。和毛格利一样病态又傻，他无法享受狂野的匆忙，尽管地底的一瞥吓到了他。他的护送者会把他赶上树，直到他感觉到最薄的树枝裂开，弯曲在树下，然后咳嗽，大呼小叫将自己向上和向下投放到空气中，然后抬起，用他们的手或脚挂在下一棵树的下肢上。有时他可以看到长英里和长英里穿过仍然绿绿的丛林，就象一个人在船杆顶上可以看到在海边的几英里，然后树枝和树叶将鞭打他的脸，他和他的两个警卫将几乎再次下到地球。所以，被包围，坠毁，大喊大叫班达罗部落沿着树道扫荡他们的囚犯毛格利。
现译: 他接下来记得的，就是腿上、胳膊上忽然多了些手——硬邦邦、有力气的小手。接着，一片树枝猛地扫过脸。再接着，他已隔着晃荡的枝条往下望了。巴鲁的吼声深沉，把整个丛林都震醒了；巴希拉龇出满口牙，一跃跃地蹿上树干。班达尔族得意地叫着，争先恐后逃到上层细枝，巴希拉不敢追上去了。“他注意到我们了！巴希拉注意到我们了！丛林各族都佩服我们的本领和机智！”他们嚷道。接着他们开始逃跑。猴族在树上的国度里怎样飞逃，谁也说不清楚。他们有固定的大路和岔路，有上坡、有下坡，都铺在离地五十、七十，甚至一百英尺的高处。必要时他们摸黑也走得通。两只最强壮的猴子从腋下架起毛格利，带着他在树梢间飞荡，一跃便有二十英尺。若是空身，他们能快上一倍，这孩子的分量拖慢了他们。毛格利晕得想吐，却也禁不住喜欢这没命的飞奔。偶尔瞥见那么远的地面，他才又害怕起来；凌空荡出去，脚底下什么也没有，到尽头猛地收住一颠，心都快蹦到嘴里。他的两个押送者夹着他蹿上树梢，蹿到最细的梢尖在身下咔嚓作响、弯了下去，才咳一声、叫一声，往外、往下一纵，就用手攀住、或用脚勾住隔壁那株树较低的横枝。有时候，他望过一片静静的绿林，能一眼看出去好几英里，好比人站在桅顶上远望海面。转眼间，枝叶又抽在脸上，他和两个看守又快回到地上了。就这样，一路腾跳，一路冲撞，一路尖啸，一路嚎叫，整个班达尔族带着他们的俘虏毛格利，沿着树上的道路席卷而去。

英文证据: For a time he was afraid of being dropped. Then he grew angry but knew better than to struggle, and then he began to think. The first thing was to send back word to Baloo and Bagheera, for, at the pace the monkeys were going, he knew his friends would be left far behind. It was useless to look down, for he could only see the topsides of the branches, so he stared upward and saw, far away in the blue, Rann the Kite balancing and wheeling as he kept watch over the jungle waiting for things to die. Rann saw that the monkeys were carrying something, and dropped a few hundred yards to find out whether their load was good to eat. He whistled with surprise when he saw Mowgli being dragged up to a treetop and heard him give the Kite call for--“We be of one blood, thou and I.” The waves of the branches closed over the boy, but Rann balanced away to the next tree in time to see the little brown face come up again. “Mark my trail!” Mowgli shouted. “Tell Baloo of the Seeonee Pack and Bagheera of the Council Rock.”

原译: 毛格利之歌 -- -- 我，毛格利，在唱歌。让丛林听听我所做的一切。谢尔·汗说他会杀人 -- -- 会杀人！在黄昏的大门上他会杀了毛格利青蛙！他吃了东西喝了酒。喝多一点，谢利汗，你什么时候再喝？睡觉和梦想的杀戮。我一个人在牧场上。灰哥，过来！来我这里吧，孤狼，因为有大游戏！把大公牛牛蓝皮牛和愤怒的眼睛。按我的命令把他们赶到佛罗。你还睡着吗，谢利·汗？醒来，哦，醒来！我来了公牛们在后面。水牛王拉玛脚踩了下来。温冈加河的水，谢尔汗去了哪里？他不是挖洞的艾基毛孔雀也不应该飞。他不是蝙蝠曼格，挂在树枝上。小竹子一起碎裂，告诉我他跑到哪里去了？呜！他来了。嘘！他来了。拉玛脚下是拉梅一号！起来，谢尔汗！起来杀！这是肉，打破公牛的脖子！嘘！他睡着了。我们不会吵醒他，因为他的力量非常强大。风筝下来看它。黑蚂蚁们已经知道了。他有一个伟大的集会为他。阿拉拉！亚拉拉！我没有衣服可以包扎我。风筝会看到我裸体。见到这些人我很羞耻。把你的外套借给我，谢利·汗。借我你的同性恋条纹大衣，我可能会去理事会摇滚。买下我的公牛我许下承诺小小的承诺。在我信守诺言之前只有你的外套是缺少的。用刀，用人用的刀，用猎人的刀，我会蹲下给我的礼物。温贡加河的水雪儿汗给了我他的外套以换取他怀抱我的爱。拉，灰色兄弟！拉，阿凯拉！雪莉汗的藏身之处很重。人包是愤怒的。他们扔石头，谈论孩子的谈话。我的嘴在出血。 。 。让我逃跑。穿过黑夜，穿过热夜，迅速与我运行，我的兄弟们。我们离开村子的灯光，去低月。华冈加河水人肉袋把我赶出去了。我没有伤害他们但他们怕我。为什么？狼群，你也把我赶出来了。丛林对我关闭村庄大门关闭。为什么？曼格飞在野兽和鸟类之间所以飞在村庄和丛林之间。为什么？我在雪莉汗的藏身处跳舞但我的心很重。我的嘴被村子里的石头割伤了但我的心很轻因为我回到了丛林里。为什么？这两件事在我身中争吵蛇在春天争吵。水从我的眼睛里流出来，我却在水落下的时候笑。为什么？我是两个毛克利人，但雪莉汗的藏身之处在我脚下。所有丛林都知道我杀了谢尔·汗。看..。 看好，欧狼！阿凯！我对一些我不明白的事情很沉痛。
现译:
毛格利的歌——是我毛格利在唱。让丛林来听听我做过的事。谢尔汗说他要杀——要杀！他说黄昏时分，就在村门口，要杀死青蛙毛格利！他吃过了，也喝过了。尽管喝个痛快吧，谢尔汗，你还有哪一天能再喝呢？睡吧，梦里接着捕猎。
放牧的草地上，只有我一个。灰兄弟，到我这儿来！独狼，到我这儿来，大家伙已经出动啦！把高大的公水牛赶过来，那些牛群里的种牛，青皮，怒眼。我叫你们怎么赶，你们就怎么赶。谢尔汗，你还睡着吗？醒醒，醒醒！我来了，公牛们就在我后面。水牛之王罗摩一蹄跺下。瓦因贡加河的水呀，谢尔汗上哪儿去了？他又不是会打洞的豪猪伊基，又不是能飞的孔雀毛奥。他也不是蝙蝠芒，能倒挂在树枝间。一起吱嘎作响的小竹子，快告诉我，他跑到哪里去了？喔！他在那里。啊呜！他在那里。那瘸子，躺在罗摩的蹄子底下！
起来呀，谢尔汗！起来杀呀！肉就在这儿，咬断公牛的脖子呀！嘘！他睡着了。我们别吵醒他，他力气可大呢。鸢鸟飞下来看了。黑蚂蚁也爬上来看个究竟。为了他，好多人都聚到了一块儿。啊啦啦！我没块布遮身。鸢鸟要看见我光着身子了。我害臊，怎能这样见大伙儿。把你的外衣借我穿吧，谢尔汗。借我你那件斑纹漂亮的外衣，好叫我去议事岩。我曾指着赎买我的那头公牛许下诺言，一个小小的诺言。只差你这件外衣，我就能守信了。拿这把刀，用人使的刀，用猎人的刀，我俯下身，取我的礼物。瓦因贡加河的水呀，谢尔汗爱我，把他的外衣送给了我。拉呀，灰兄弟！拉呀，阿克拉！谢尔汗的皮好沉。
人群发了怒。他们扔石头，他们说孩子话。我嘴里在流血。让我跑吧。穿过夜色，穿过这燠热的夜，我的兄弟们，和我一起快跑吧。我们离开村里的灯火，向那低低的月亮跑去。瓦因贡加河的水呀，人群把我赶了出来。我没有害他们，他们却怕我。为什么？狼群，你们也把我赶了出来。丛林不收我，村门也关上了。为什么？就像蝙蝠芒飞在走兽与飞鸟之间，我也飞在村子与丛林之间。为什么？
我踏着谢尔汗的虎皮跳舞，心里却沉甸甸的。村里掷的石头打得我嘴破了，受了伤，可是我心里好轻快，因为我又回到丛林了。为什么？这两样东西在我心里争斗，就像蛇在春天争斗。我的眼睛流出了水，水往下落，我却在笑。为什么？我成了两个毛格利，可我脚下确实踩着谢尔汗的皮。整个丛林都知道我杀了谢尔汗。看吧——狼群，好好看吧！啊嗨！这么多事情我不明白，我的心好沉。
修改判断: 整首歌与前后叙事对读，重译诗节，保留重唱句、视角与行间停顿。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: Ah, weary wee flipperling, curl at thy ease!
原译:
嘘，宝贝，今晚已经过去了
黑色的海水点燃了如此的绿色。
月亮梳子向下看找到我们
休息时，在两难之间的空洞里。
浮标相遇时柔软的枕头
啊，疲惫的毛发，弯曲你的放松！
暴风绝不能使你苏醒，鲨鱼绝不能使你追上。
沉睡在缓慢的海洋的怀抱里！
现译:
嘘，睡吧，我的宝贝，黑夜围在身后，
方才还泛着绿光的海水已是一片墨黑。
月亮越过浪头，低头来把我们找，
我们歇在浪与浪之间，听海水窸窣地响。
两道波浪相接的地方，就是你柔软的枕头，
累坏了的小鳍宝宝，蜷起身来好好睡。
风暴不会吵醒你，鲨鱼也追不上你，
大海轻轻摇着，你就在它怀里安睡。
修改判断: 连读八行，恢复海豹妈妈的摇篮歌，包括浪谷、鲨鱼与小鳍的意象。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: All these things happened several years ago at a place called Novastoshnah, or North East Point, on the Island of St. Paul, away and away in the Bering Sea. Limmershin, the Winter Wren, told me the tale when he was blown on to the rigging of a steamer going to Japan, and I took him down into my cabin and warmed and fed him for a couple of days till he was fit to fly back to St. Paul’s again. Limmershin is a very quaint little bird, but he knows how to tell the truth.
原译: 所有这些事情发生在几年前一个叫诺瓦斯托什纳的地方，或东北点，在圣保罗岛，远离白令海。Limmershin，Winter Wren，告诉了我一个故事，当他被吹向一艘驶往日本的蒸汽船的操纵时，我把他带到我的船舱里，暖和和喂他几天，直到他能再飞回圣保罗。林默申是个很古怪的小鸟但他知道如何说出真相。
现译: 这些事发生在几年前，地点叫诺瓦斯托什纳，又称东北角，在遥远的白令海圣保罗岛上。故事是冬鹪鹩林默申讲给我的。他叫风吹到了开往日本的一艘轮船的索具上。我把他带下去，在船舱里给他暖身子，喂了他两天，直到他有力气再飞回圣保罗岛。林默申是只十分古怪的小鸟，倒是很懂得怎么讲真话。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: Nobody comes to Novastoshnah except on business, and the only people who have regular business there are the seals. They come in the summer months by hundreds and hundreds of thousands out of the cold gray sea. For Novastoshnah Beach has the finest accommodation for seals of any place in all the world.
原译: 除了做生意，没人会来新斯多夏那里只有印章。夏天的月里，他们从寒冷的灰海中来了几百和几十万人。诺瓦斯托什纳海滩拥有世界上任何地方最好的海豹住所。
现译: 要不是有正事，谁也不会去诺瓦斯托什纳。定期到这里办正事的，只有海豹。一到夏季，他们成十万、成十万地从冰冷灰暗的海上赶来。要说哪处最适合海豹落脚，天下再没有胜过诺瓦斯托什纳海滩的地方了。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: Sea Catch knew that, and every spring would swim from whatever place he happened to be in--would swim like a torpedo-boat straight for Novastoshnah and spend a month fighting with his companions for a good place on the rocks, as close to the sea as possible. Sea Catch was fifteen years old, a huge gray fur seal with almost a mane on his shoulders, and long, wicked dog teeth. When he heaved himself up on his front flippers he stood more than four feet clear of the ground, and his weight, if anyone had been bold enough to weigh him, was nearly seven hundred pounds. He was scarred all over with the marks of savage fights, but he was always ready for just one fight more. He would put his head on one side, as though he were afraid to look his enemy in the face; then he would shoot it out like lightning, and when the big teeth were firmly fixed on the other seal’s neck, the other seal might get away if he could, but Sea Catch would not help him.
原译: 捕海队知道，每一个春天都会从任何地方游来..。 将像鱼雷船一样游到诺瓦斯托什纳..。 并花一个月时间和同伴战斗..。海捕获是15岁一只巨大的灰色毛海豹肩膀上几乎有根毛长长的邪恶狗牙。当他用脚踏车抬起时，他站在四英尺外，远离地面，他的体重，如果有谁敢称他体重的话，将近700磅。他被野蛮战斗留下的伤痕一直以来他都准备再打一场。他把头放在一边，好像他害怕看着敌人的脸，然后他像闪电一样射出它，当大牙牢牢固定在另一头海豹的脖子上时，另一只海豹如果可以的话，就会逃走，但海捕获对他没有帮助。
现译: 海猎手就知道这点。每年春天，不管碰巧身在何方，他都像一艘鱼雷艇，笔直向诺瓦斯托什纳游去，再花一个月跟同伴打架，为的是在礁石上抢一块尽可能靠海的好地方。海猎手十五岁，是头庞大的灰色毛皮海豹，两肩几乎长出了鬃毛，犬齿又长又凶。他要是用两只前鳍把上半身撑起来，足有四英尺多高。如果有谁胆敢称称他，体重得有将近七百磅。恶战给他留下满身伤疤，可再加一仗，他也从来都奉陪。他会偏过头去，好像不敢瞧敌手的脸，随即快如闪电地探出脑袋。等到大牙牢牢嵌进对方脖子，那头海豹有本事就逃脱吧，海猎手可不会帮他一把。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: Yet Sea Catch never chased a beaten seal, for that was against the Rules of the Beach. He only wanted room by the sea for his nursery. But as there were forty or fifty thousand other seals hunting for the same thing each spring, the whistling, bellowing, roaring, and blowing on the beach was something frightful.
原译: 但海捕从未追逐过一个被击败的海豹，因为那是违反海滩规则的。他只想在海边为他的托儿所留个房间。但是，因为有四万或五万其他海豹捕猎相同的东西每一个春天，吹口哨，钟声，咆哮，和吹在海滩上是可怕的东西。
现译: 但海猎手绝不追击已经败走的海豹，那有违海滩的规矩。他所求的，不过是海边一块空地，好养育自家的孩子。可是每年春天，另有四五万头海豹也都想要同样的地方。于是尖哨声、低吼声、咆哮声、喷气声响成一团，海滩上真够吓人的。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: From a little hill called Hutchinson’s Hill, you could look over three and a half miles of ground covered with fighting seals; and the surf was dotted all over with the heads of seals hurrying to land and begin their share of the fighting. They fought in the breakers, they fought in the sand, and they fought on the smooth-worn basalt rocks of the nurseries, for they were just as stupid and unaccommodating as men. Their wives never came to the island until late in May or early in June, for they did not care to be torn to pieces; and the young two-, three-, and four-year-old seals who had not begun housekeeping went inland about half a mile through the ranks of the fighters and played about on the sand dunes in droves and legions, and rubbed off every single green thing that grew. They were called the holluschickie--the bachelors--and there were perhaps two or three hundred thousand of them at Novastoshnah alone.
原译: 从一个叫做哈钦森山的小山丘上你可以看到三英里半的地上覆盖着战斗的海豹冲浪到处都是海豹的头。他们打在断路器，他们打在沙子上，他们战斗在光滑的烧烤岩石苗圃，因为他们是一样愚蠢和不适应男人。他们的妻子直到5月底或6月初才来到岛上，因为他们并不想被撕成碎片；那些年幼的两、三、四岁海豹没有开始做家务，他们到内陆去了大约半英里，在战斗机的队伍中，在沙丘上玩耍，开着汽车和军团，擦掉每一件绿色东西。他们被称为霍卢斯奇奇克单身汉可能只有诺瓦斯托什纳有两三十万。
现译: 有座小丘叫哈钦森丘，在上面可以望见整整三英里半的地面，全给打架的海豹铺满了。碎浪里还密密地冒着海豹脑袋，一心赶来上岸，好到这场架里打一份。他们在破浪里打，在沙地上打，也在育幼地早已磨滑的玄武岩上打，在不肯让人这件事上，蠢起来简直就跟人一样。他们的太太们不到五月底六月初不会登岛，谁也不想叫人撕成碎片。那些两岁、三岁、四岁，还没成家的年轻海豹，穿过打架的行列，向内陆走上半英里，在沙丘上成群结队地嬉戏，把地上长出来的每一点绿色都给蹭掉。他们叫“霍卢希基”，就是单身汉的意思。单在诺瓦斯托什纳，怕就有二三十万头。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: Sea Catch had just finished his forty-fifth fight one spring when Matkah, his soft, sleek, gentle-eyed wife, came up out of the sea, and he caught her by the scruff of the neck and dumped her down on his reservation, saying gruffly: “Late as usual. Where have you been?”
原译: 海豹队刚打完第45场比赛在一个春天，马特卡，他的软软的，狡猾的，眼神温柔的妻子，走出海洋，他抓住她的脖子的绞痕把她扔到他的订位上，说：“像往常一样的迟到。你去哪了？”
现译: 有年春天，海猎手刚打完他的第四十五场架，他的妻子玛特卡正好出水。她毛皮柔滑油亮，眼神温和。他一口衔住她后颈的皮，把她往自己占好的地盘上一撂，粗声喝道：“照旧来得迟！上哪儿去了？”
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: It was not the fashion for Sea Catch to eat anything during the four months he stayed on the beaches, and so his temper was generally bad. Matkah knew better than to answer back. She looked round and cooed: “How thoughtful of you. You’ve taken the old place again.”
原译: 海鱼在海滩上呆了四个月却不怎么吃东西所以他的脾气一般都不好。玛特卡知道比回答还好。她四处看说：“你多么体贴，你又占领了老地方。”
现译: 海猎手留在海滩上的四个月，照老规矩一点东西也不吃，所以脾气一向不大好。玛特卡懂得不必顶嘴，向四下一望，柔声说：“你想得真周到，又把咱们的老地方占到手啦。”

中文章名: 白海豹

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: Sea Catch sunk his head proudly between his fat shoulders and pretended to go to sleep for a few minutes, but all the time he was keeping a sharp lookout for a fight. Now that all the seals and their wives were on the land, you could hear their clamor miles out to sea above the loudest gales. At the lowest counting there were over a million seals on the beach--old seals, mother seals, tiny babies, and holluschickie, fighting, scuffling, bleating, crawling, and playing together--going down to the sea and coming up from it in gangs and regiments, lying over every foot of ground as far as the eye could reach, and skirmishing about in brigades through the fog. It is nearly always foggy at Novastoshnah, except when the sun comes out and makes everything look all pearly and rainbow-colored for a little while.
原译: 被海鱼引以为豪地撞到头顶假装睡了几分钟但他一直盯着人看。现在所有的海豹和妻子都在陆地上你可以听到他们在海边的叫声。最起码的计数结果显示，海豹、母海豹、小婴儿和霍卢什奇奇海豹有100多万条海豹，有战斗、打斗、抽打、流泪、爬行、一起到海边玩耍，并组成帮派和团团从海边爬上，趴在每一英尺的地上，眼睛可以达到，还有在雾中小队滑雪。在诺瓦斯托什纳几乎总是雾，除非太阳出来，让一切看起来都珍珠和彩虹颜色一小会儿。
现译: 海猎手傲气十足，把脑袋往肥厚的肩膀中间一缩，装作要打几分钟的盹。其实他一直睁着眼睛，找下一个架打。如今公海豹和太太们都上了岸，哪怕刮着最响的狂风，几英里外的海上仍听得见他们的吵闹声。往最少里算，滩上也超过一百万头海豹。老海豹、当妈妈的海豹、丁点儿大的娃娃和单身汉，一起打架、推挤、咩叫、爬行、玩耍，一队队、一团团地下海，又从海里上来。放眼望去，每寸土地都趴满了海豹，雾中还不时有一拨拨队伍起小冲突。诺瓦斯托什纳几乎总有雾，只偶尔太阳出来一小会儿，给万物披上一层珍珠色和彩虹色的光。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹

修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹

修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: “Empty clam-shells and dry seaweed!” snorted Sea Catch. “There never has been such a thing in the world as a white seal.”

中文章名: 白海豹

中文章名: 白海豹

You mustn’t swim till you’re six weeks old,

Are bad for baby seals.

小海豹，大不该跟它们挨近。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据:
Are bad for baby seals, dear rat,
As bad as bad can be;
But splash and grow strong,
And you can’t be wrong.
Child of the Open Sea!

对小海豹不好亲爱的老鼠

开阔海之子！

你就不会走错路，
大海的孩子！

中文章名: 白海豹

原译: 当然，这个小家伙一开始不理解这些话。他用脚踏在母亲的身边，并学会了打滚路边，当他的父亲与另一海豹战斗，和两个滚动，咆哮上下滑滑的岩石。玛特卡过去常去海边吃东西，婴儿两天内只喂过一次，但是他吃了所有他能吃的，并且用它来加速。
现译: 小家伙起先自然听不懂。他在妈妈身边拨拉着鳍，爬来爬去，还学会了在父亲跟别的海豹打起来的时候赶紧躲开，躲开那两团在滑溜溜的石头上吼着滚上滚下的大家伙。玛特卡常得下海找食物，宝宝两天才吃一顿奶。可每回他敞开肚子吃，照样长得好极了。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: The first thing he did was to crawl inland, and there he met tens of thousands of babies of his own age, and they played together like puppies, went to sleep on the clean sand, and played again. The old people in the nurseries took no notice of them, and the holluschickie kept to their own grounds, and the babies had a beautiful playtime.

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: When Matkah came back from her deep-sea fishing she would go straight to their playground and call as a sheep calls for a lamb, and wait until she heard Kotick bleat. Then she would take the straightest of straight lines in his direction, striking out with her fore flippers and knocking the youngsters head over heels right and left. There were always a few hundred mothers hunting for their children through the playgrounds, and the babies were kept lively. But, as Matkah told Kotick, “So long as you don’t lie in muddy water and get mange, or rub the hard sand into a cut or scratch, and so long as you never go swimming when there is a heavy sea, nothing will hurt you here.”
原译: 当玛特卡从深海钓鱼回来时，她会直接去他们的操场，像只羊叫羊，然后等她听到科蒂克的Blaat的声音。然后，她会采取最直直的直线在他的方向，罢工出她的前额脚踏板和击打年轻人头高高的右和左。始终有几百个母亲在游乐场里寻找孩子，婴儿保持活跃。但是，正如玛特卡对科蒂克所说，“只要你不躺在泥水里，不弄脏了，不把硬沙擦成一块块或刮伤，只要你没有在大海中游泳，这里就没有什么会伤害你。”

修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹

The first time that Kotick went down to the sea a wave carried him out beyond his depth, and his big head sank and his little hind flippers flew up exactly as his mother had told him in the song, and if the next wave had not thrown him back again he would have drowned.

现译: 小海豹不会游泳，跟小孩儿一样；可是没学会之前，他们总觉得不痛快。科蒂克头一回下海，一个浪就把他送进了脚探不到底的深水。他那大脑袋往下一栽，两只小后鳍向上一翘，恰如妈妈的歌里说的。要不是后一个浪头把他送回来，他就已经淹死了。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: After that, he learned to lie in a beach pool and let the wash of the waves just cover him and lift him up while he paddled, but he always kept his eye open for big waves that might hurt. He was two weeks learning to use his flippers; and all that while he floundered in and out of the water, and coughed and grunted and crawled up the beach and took catnaps on the sand, and went back again, until at last he found that he truly belonged to the water.

修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: Then you can imagine the times that he had with his companions, ducking under the rollers; or coming in on top of a comber and landing with a swash and a splutter as the big wave went whirling far up the beach; or standing up on his tail and scratching his head as the old people did; or playing “I’m the King of the Castle” on slippery, weedy rocks that just stuck out of the wash. Now and then he would see a thin fin, like a big shark’s fin, drifting along close to shore, and he knew that that was the Killer Whale, the Grampus, who eats young seals when he can get them; and Kotick would head for the beach like an arrow, and the fin would jig off slowly, as if it were looking for nothing at all.

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: Late in October the seals began to leave St. Paul’s for the deep sea, by families and tribes, and there was no more fighting over the nurseries, and the holluschickie played anywhere they liked. “Next year,” said Matkah to Kotick, “you will be a holluschickie; but this year you must learn how to catch fish.”

修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: They set out together across the Pacific, and Matkah showed Kotick how to sleep on his back with his flippers tucked down by his side and his little nose just out of the water. No cradle is so comfortable as the long, rocking swell of the Pacific. 原译: 科特克游回诺瓦斯托什纳任由海鸥尖叫。在那里，他发现没有人同情他，因为他试图为海豹找到一个安静的地方。他们告诉他，男人们总是开着霍卢斯基..。 ..。这是一天工作的一部分..。 ..。如果他不喜欢看到丑陋的东西，他不应该去杀人场。但其他海豹都没有看到这起杀人案这让他和他的朋友有不同。况且，科特克是个白海豹。
现译: 科蒂克游回诺瓦斯托什纳，让鸥鸟们继续叫去。回到家才发现，对于他初次试着给海豹们寻找安静去处这件事，根本没人同情。他们说，人向来都要把年轻的单身汉赶走，是日常事务的一部分。他要是不爱看丑事，原不该去屠宰场。可是别的海豹都没亲眼见过屠宰，这正是他跟朋友们不一样的地方。再说，科蒂克还是头白海豹。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: “What you must do,” said old Sea Catch, after he had heard his son’s adventures, “is to grow up and be a big seal like your father, and have a nursery on the beach, and then they will leave you alone. In another five years you ought to be able to fight for yourself.” Even gentle Matkah, his mother, said: “You will never be able to stop the killing. Go and play in the sea, Kotick.” And Kotick went off and danced the Fire-dance with a very heavy little heart.
原译: “你必须做什么”，老海渔在听到他儿子的冒险之后说，“长大后要像你父亲一样成为一只大海豹，在海滩上建一个托儿所，然后他们就会离开你。再过五年你就应该能够为自己而战斗了。”他母亲玛特卡说：你绝不能阻止杀戮，你到海里去玩吧，科迪克。科特克用一颗非常沉重的心跳着火舞走了。
现译: “你该做的，”老海猎手听完儿子的经历说，“就是长大，长成像你父亲这样的大海豹，在滩上占块育幼地。到时候他们也就不来碰你了。再过五年，你就该能自己上阵打架了。”连温和的母亲玛特卡都说：“你阻止不了他们杀海豹。科蒂克，去海里玩吧。”科蒂克就去跳火舞了，小小的一颗心沉甸甸的。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: That autumn he left the beach as soon as he could, and set off alone because of a notion in his bullet-head. He was going to find Sea Cow, if there was such a person in the sea, and he was going to find a quiet island with good firm beaches for seals to live on, where men could not get at them. So he explored and explored by himself from the North to the South Pacific, swimming as much as three hundred miles in a day and a night. He met with more adventures than can be told, and narrowly escaped being caught by the Basking Shark, and the Spotted Shark, and the Hammerhead, and he met all the untrustworthy ruffians that loaf up and down the seas, and the heavy polite fish, and the scarlet spotted scallops that are moored in one place for hundreds of years, and grow very proud of it; but he never met Sea Cow, and he never found an island that he could fancy.
原译: 那年秋天他尽快离开海滩独自离开因为他的子弹头有一个概念。他打算找到海牛，如果有这样的人在海上，他打算找到一个安静的岛屿，拥有良好的固定海滩供海豹居住，在那里，人们无法得到它们。他从北太平洋到南太平洋，每天和晚上游300英里。他遇到的冒险比人们所知道的还多，被巴斯金鲨鱼，斑点鲨鱼和锤头捕捉被困住了，他遇到了所有不值得信赖的流浪者游过海面，和厚厚的礼貌的鱼，和红斑斑斑斑被固定在一个地方数百年，并且为此而骄傲但他从未见过海牛也从未找到一个他喜欢的岛。
现译: 那年秋天，他能多早离开海滩就多早离开了，独自出发。他那颗子弹般圆溜溜的小脑袋里装着一个念头。只要海中真有海牛，他就要把海牛找出来；又要找到一个安静的岛，上面有结实的好海滩可供海豹生活，人类却到不了。他就这样独个儿找呀找，从北太平洋一直游到南太平洋，一天一夜有时能游三百英里。他的历险多得讲不完：险些落进姥鲨、斑点鲨和锤头鲨的口中；碰见海上那些南来北往、信不过的恶棍，大块头而有礼貌的鱼，还有长着猩红斑点的扇贝，它们在同一处抛锚几百年，还颇以此为荣。可他没遇见海牛，也没发现中意的岛。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: If the beach was good and hard, with a slope behind it for seals to play on, there was always the smoke of a whaler on the horizon, boiling down blubber, and Kotick knew what that meant. Or else he could see that seals had once visited the island and been killed off, and Kotick knew that where men had come once they would come again.
原译: 如果海滩是好的和硬的，后面有一个斜坡，海豹可以玩弄，总是有烟捕鲸者在地平线上，煮下来的鲸脂，科特克知道这意味着什么。或者他可以看到海豹曾经去过小岛被杀死了科蒂克知道一旦有人来过他们就会再来。
现译: 假若海滩结实又平坦，后面还带一面适合海豹做游戏的斜坡，那么天边总会飘着捕鲸船熬鲸脂的烟。科蒂克知道那意味着什么。要么就是他看得出，昔日有海豹来过，已全叫人猎光；他知道，人来过一回，还会来第二回。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: He picked up with an old stumpy-tailed albatross, who told him that Kerguelen Island was the very place for peace and quiet, and when Kotick went down there he was all but smashed to pieces against some wicked black cliffs in a heavy sleet-storm with lightning and thunder. Yet as he pulled out against the gale he could see that even there had once been a seal nursery. And it was so in all the other islands that he visited.
原译: 他拿着一条老的树枝尾信天翁，他告诉他，凯尔盖伦岛是和平和安静的地方，当科特克下山时，他被打碎了，在暴风雨中，用闪电和雷电击打着一些邪恶的黑悬崖。然而当他拉出对抗大风他可以看到即使曾经有一个海豹苗圃。他访问过的其他岛屿都是如此。
现译: 他结识了一只老短尾信天翁。那鸟告诉他，真要图清静，就该去凯尔盖朗岛。科蒂克游到岛边，却赶上一场雷电交加的雨雪风暴，差一点撞在凶险的黑色峭壁上，撞得粉身碎骨。可就在他迎着狂风拔身离去时，他也看得出来，这地方居然也曾是海豹的育幼地。他去过的其余岛屿，处处如此。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: Limmershin gave a long list of them, for he said that Kotick spent five seasons exploring, with a four months’ rest each year at Novastoshnah, when the holluschickie used to make fun of him and his imaginary islands. He went to the Gallapagos, a horrid dry place on the Equator, where he was nearly baked to death; he went to the Georgia Islands, the Orkneys, Emerald Island, Little Nightingale Island, Gough’s Island, Bouvet’s Island, the Crossets, and even to a little speck of an island south of the Cape of Good Hope. But everywhere the People of the Sea told him the same things. Seals had come to those islands once upon a time, but men had killed them all off. Even when he swam thousands of miles out of the Pacific and got to a place called Cape Corrientes (that was when he was coming back from Gough’s Island), he found a few hundred mangy seals on a rock and they told him that men came there too.
原译: Limmershin给出了一个长长的名单，因为他说科特克花了五个赛季探险，每年有四个月的休息在诺瓦斯托什纳。他去了加拉帕戈斯，这是赤道的一个干燥的地方，他差点被烤死；他去了格鲁吉亚群岛、奥克尼岛、翡翠岛、小奈丁格尔岛、戈夫岛、布韦特岛、十字架，甚至去了好望角以南的一个小岛。但海人到处告诉他同样的事情。海豹曾经来过这些岛屿但人类却把他们全杀了。即使他游了几千英里远的太平洋到达了一个叫科里恩特斯角的地方(当时他正从戈夫岛回来) 他在一块岩石上发现了几百条毛巾。
现译: 林默申给我开过长长一串岛名。他说科蒂克花了五季探寻，每年只回诺瓦斯托什纳歇四个月，年轻的单身汉总笑他和他那些凭空想出来的小岛。他去了赤道上的加拉帕戈斯，那地方干得可怕，险些把他烤死；去了乔治亚群岛、奥克尼群岛、翡翠岛、小夜莺岛、戈夫岛、布韦岛、克罗泽群岛，甚至远远跑到好望角以南一座小不点儿的岛上。可是海洋之民不论到哪儿都告诉他同一件事：从前这些岛上来过海豹，可都给人杀光了。甚至有一回，他从戈夫岛回来，已经游离太平洋几千英里，来到一处叫科连特斯角的地方，在礁石上找见几百头身上长癞的海豹。他们也告诉他，人照样会来。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: That nearly broke his heart, and he headed round the Horn back to his own beaches; and on his way north he hauled out on an island full of green trees, where he found an old, old seal who was dying, and Kotick caught fish for him and told him all his sorrows. “Now,” said Kotick, “I am going back to Novastoshnah, and if I am driven to the killing-pens with the holluschickie I shall not care.”
原译: 差点伤了他的心，他绕着非洲之角回到自己的海滩上；在往北走的路上，他从一个充满绿树的岛上出来，在那里，他发现了一个正在死去的老海豹，科蒂克为他钓到了鱼，并告诉他他所有的悲伤。科特克说：“现在，我要去诺瓦斯托什纳，如果我被赶到杀人犯那里，我不在乎。”
现译: 他差一点心碎，便绕过合恩角，踏上回乡的水路。朝北游的时候，他在一座绿树成片的岛上登岸，找到一头很老很老、快要死去的海豹。科蒂克捉鱼给他吃，又向他诉说自己的一切苦恼。“如今我要回诺瓦斯托什纳了，”科蒂克说，“他们就是把我跟年轻单身汉一道赶进屠宰围栏，我也不在乎了。”
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: The old seal said, “Try once more. I am the last of the Lost Rookery of Masafuera, and in the days when men killed us by the hundred thousand there was a story on the beaches that some day a white seal would come out of the North and lead the seal people to a quiet place. I am old, and I shall never live to see that day, but others will. Try once more.”
原译: 旧海豹说：你再试一次吧！我是马萨富埃拉最后的鲁克里人。当人们以十万计杀死我们的时候，海滩上传来一个故事说，有朝一日，一个白色海豹会从北方出来，带领海豹们到一个安静的地方。我老了，我永远不会活着去见那个日子，但别人会。你再试一次。
现译: 老海豹说：“再试一回吧。马萨富埃拉那座失落的海豹窝，只有我活下来了。当年人十万十万地杀我们，海滩上总传着个故事，说有一天会有头白海豹从北方来，领海豹一族去一个安静的地方。我老了，活不到那一天，可别人会见到的。再试一回吧。”
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: And Kotick curled up his mustache (it was a beauty) and said, “I am the only white seal that has ever been born on the beaches, and I am the only seal, black or white, who ever thought of looking for new islands.”
原译: 科特克卷起他的胡子，说：我是海滩上唯一出生的白海豹，我是唯一想寻找新岛屿的黑白海豹。
现译: 科蒂克卷起胡须——多漂亮的一副胡须呀——说：“从来海滩上长大的白海豹，只有我一个。不管黑的还是白的，想到要去寻找新岛屿的海豹，也只有我一个。”
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: This cheered him immensely; and when he came back to Novastoshnah that summer, Matkah, his mother, begged him to marry and settle down, for he was no longer a holluschick but a full-grown sea-catch, with a curly white mane on his shoulders, as heavy, as big, and as fierce as his father. “Give me another season,” he said. “Remember, Mother, it is always the seventh wave that goes farthest up the beach.”
原译: 这令他欢欣鼓舞；当他夏天回到诺瓦斯托什纳时，他的母亲玛特卡求他结婚和安顿下来，因为他不再是个乡巴佬，而是一只长满的海捞鱼，肩上有卷发白毛，重得像他的父亲一样大，凶猛。他说“再给我一个季节。”“记住，妈妈，总是第七波最远在海滩上。”
现译: 这么一想，他高兴多了。那年夏天回到诺瓦斯托什纳，母亲玛特卡求他娶妻成家，因为他已不再是个年轻单身汉，而是头堂堂正正的大公海豹了。卷曲的白鬃垂在肩头，不论分量、身量还是凶猛，他都不输给父亲。“再给我一季，妈妈，”他说，“你别忘记，冲到沙滩最远处的，总是第七道浪。”
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: Curiously enough, there was another seal who thought that she would put off marrying till the next year, and Kotick danced the Fire-dance with her all down Lukannon Beach the night before he set off on his last exploration. This time he went westward, because he had fallen on the trail of a great shoal of halibut, and he needed at least one hundred pounds of fish a day to keep him in good condition. He chased them till he was tired, and then he curled himself up and went to sleep on the hollows of the ground swell that sets in to Copper Island. He knew the coast perfectly well, so about midnight, when he felt himself gently bumped on a weed-bed, he said, “Hm, tide’s running strong tonight,” and turning over under water opened his eyes slowly and stretched. Then he jumped like a cat, for he saw huge things nosing about in the shoal water and browsing on the heavy fringes of the weeds.
原译: 奇怪的是还有一个海豹以为她会推迟结婚直到下一年科特克和她共舞火舞。这次他向西走因为他掉在一条大沙滩上他每天需要至少一百磅的鱼才能让他保持良好状态。他追着他们，直到他累了，然后他弯了起来，睡在地洞里，形成在铜岛。他对海岸非常了解，所以大约午夜，当他感到自己轻轻地撞到一个杂草床，他说，“嗯，今晚潮水会很强劲，” 然后在水下翻过身来，慢慢地睁开眼睛，伸展。然后他像猫一样跳了下来，因为他看到巨大的东西喷探在沼泽的水和浏览在重的杂草边缘。
现译: 说来也巧，还有一头海豹也打算把婚事推到明年。科蒂克最后一次出发探险的前一晚，就跟她一道，在卢卡农海滩从一头到另一头跳完了火舞。这一趟他往西游，因为正好赶上了一大群比目鱼的踪迹，而要保持体力，他一天至少得吃一百磅鱼。他追得累了，就蜷起身子，在涌向铜岛的长浪之间，躺进浪谷里睡了过去。他对这海岸一清二楚。所以半夜感到自己轻轻撞上一片海藻时，只咕哝了一句“嗯，今晚潮水好急”，便在水里翻身，慢慢睁开双眼，伸个懒腰。随即，他像猫似的一下子蹦了起来，因为浅水里有一群极大的东西正用鼻子东拱西拱，啃着海藻密厚的垂边。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: “By the Great Combers of Magellan!” he said, beneath his mustache. “Who in the Deep Sea are these people?”
原译: 他说：“在麦哲伦大Combers！” 他说，在他的胡子下面。“这些人在深海里是谁？”
现译: “麦哲伦海峡的大浪头在上！”他在胡须底下小声说，“深海里哪来的这些家伙？”
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: They were like no walrus, sea lion, seal, bear, whale, shark, fish, squid, or scallop that Kotick had ever seen before. They were between twenty and thirty feet long, and they had no hind flippers, but a shovel-like tail that looked as if it had been whittled out of wet leather. Their heads were the most foolish-looking things you ever saw, and they balanced on the ends of their tails in deep water when they weren’t grazing, bowing solemnly to each other and waving their front flippers as a fat man waves his arm.
原译: 它们是像没有海象，海狮，海豹，熊，鲸鱼，鲨鱼，鱼，鱿鱼，或扇贝，科蒂克见过。他们有20到30英尺长，没有后脚的脚踏车，但有一个像铲子一样的尾巴，看起来好像是从湿皮革里挖出来的。他们的头是你见过的最愚蠢的东西，他们平衡他们的尾巴在深水当他们不放牧，庄严地向对方鞠躬和挥舞他们的前脚象一个胖子挥动他的手臂。
现译: 科蒂克见过海象、海狮、海豹、熊、鲸、鲨、鱼、鱿鱼和扇贝，眼前这些东西跟哪一样都不像。他们长二三十英尺，没有后鳍，倒有一条铁锹似的尾巴，仿佛是用湿皮革削成的。头的模样说不出地呆。他们不吃草的时候，就在深水里用尾巴尖支起身子，彼此庄重地鞠躬，挥起前鳍，活像胖子挥胳膊。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: “Ahem!” said Kotick. “Good sport, gentlemen?” The big things answered by bowing and waving their flippers like the Frog Footman. When they began feeding again Kotick saw that their upper lip was split into two pieces that they could twitch apart about a foot and bring together again with a whole bushel of seaweed between the splits. They tucked the stuff into their mouths and chumped solemnly.

I see you bow gracefully, but I should like to know your names.” The split lips moved and twitched; and the glassy green eyes stared, but they did not speak.

中文章名: 白海豹

中文章名: 白海豹

But the sea cows did not answer because Sea Cow cannot talk. 中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: By daylight Kotick’s mane was standing on end and his temper was gone where the dead crabs go. Then the Sea Cow began to travel northward very slowly, stopping to hold absurd bowing councils from time to time, and Kotick followed them, saying to himself, “People who are such idiots as these are would have been killed long ago if they hadn’t found out some safe island. And what is good enough for the Sea Cow is good enough for the Sea Catch. All the same, I wish they’d hurry.”
原译: 白天，科迪克的马甲站在尽头他的脾气已经消失死螃蟹去的地方。然后海牛开始慢慢向北走，停下来不时地举行荒谬的鞠躬会，科蒂克跟着他们，对自己说，“这些人，如果他们没有找到一个安全的岛，早就会被杀了。对海牛来说，什么是足够的好东西，足以让海牛捕捉。同样，我希望他们快点。”
现译: 到了天亮，科蒂克连鬃毛都竖起来，脾气也不知同死螃蟹一道去了哪里。海牛群这才缓缓向北出发，时不时停下，鞠着躬，开些滑稽的会议。科蒂克跟在后面，心想：“像他们这样的傻瓜，要是没找着什么安全的岛，早叫人杀光了。海牛住得，大公海豹也住得。不过，真盼他们游快点。”
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: It was weary work for Kotick. The herd never went more than forty or fifty miles a day, and stopped to feed at night, and kept close to the shore all the time; while Kotick swam round them, and over them, and under them, but he could not hurry them up one-half mile. As they went farther north they held a bowing council every few hours, and Kotick nearly bit off his mustache with impatience till he saw that they were following up a warm current of water, and then he respected them more.
原译: 这是为科特克做的苦工。牛群一天不到四、五十英里，在夜间停食，一直停留在岸边。科特克围着牛群游，在牛群的四周游，在牛群的下面游，但他不能使他们快到半英里。当他们走得更远的时候，他们每隔几个小时就举行一个鞠躬会，而科蒂克几乎不耐烦地咬掉了他的胡子，直到他看到他们正在追寻温暖的水流，然后他更加尊敬他们。

中文章名: 白海豹
英文证据: One night they sank through the shiny water--sank like stones--and for the first time since he had known them began to swim quickly. Kotick followed, and the pace astonished him, for he never dreamed that Sea Cow was anything of a swimmer. 原译: 一天晚上，他们沉没在闪亮的水中像石头一样第一次，自从他知道他们很快游泳。科蒂克跟着他，他的步伐令他吃惊，因为他从来没有梦想过海牛是游泳运动员。他们朝悬崖边的岸边去了悬崖冲进深水中滑入深水中。游了很久科蒂克急切地想呼吸新鲜空气之后他走出了黑暗的隧道他们把他带过。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: His mother Radha Pyari,--Radha the darling,--who had been caught in the same drive with Kala Nag, told him, before his little milk tusks had dropped out, that elephants who were afraid always got hurt. Kala Nag knew that that advice was good, for the first time that he saw a shell burst he backed, screaming, into a stand of piled rifles, and the bayonets pricked him in all his softest places. So, before he was twenty-five, he gave up being afraid, and so he was the best-loved and the best-looked-after elephant in the service of the Government of India. He had carried tents, twelve hundred pounds’ weight of tents, on the march in Upper India. He had been hoisted into a ship at the end of a steam crane and taken for days across the water, and made to carry a mortar on his back in a strange and rocky country very far from India, and had seen the Emperor Theodore lying dead in Magdala, and had come back again in the steamer entitled, so the soldiers said, to the Abyssinian War medal. He had seen his fellow elephants die of cold and epilepsy and starvation and sunstroke up at a place called Ali Musjid, ten years later; and afterward he had been sent down thousands of miles south to haul and pile big balks of teak in the timberyards at Moulmein. There he had half killed an insubordinate young elephant who was shirking his fair share of work.
原译: 他的母亲Radha Pyari 和卡拉·纳格一起被困在同一个车道里的Radha Radha 告诉他在他的小牛奶牙掉出来之前害怕的象总是受伤了。卡拉·纳格知道这个建议很好，他第一次看到一个炮弹爆裂，他背上，尖叫，在一个堆积的步枪的摊子。所以，在他25岁之前，他放弃了恐惧，所以他是最可爱和最帅的大象服务于印度政府。他在上印度的游行中携带了1 200磅重的帐篷。他被吊在一艘蒸汽起重机的尽头，并被拖过水面好几天，并被迫背上迫击炮，背部离印度很远的陌生和岩石国家，他看到Theodore皇帝死在Magdala，又回到汽船里，士兵们说，他们有权领取Abyssinian战争奖牌。10年后，他看到其他大象死于寒冷和癫痫，饿死和晒太阳，在阿里·穆希德的一个地方；之后，他被送到南边数千英里处，在穆尔梅因的木材厂里拖走和堆放大块茶叶。在那里，他杀死了一位不服从的年轻大象，他正在逃避他公平的工作份额。
现译: 他的母亲拉达·皮娅莉，也就是“亲爱的拉达”，是跟卡拉·纳格在同一次围捕中落网的。在他那对小乳牙掉落之前，她便告诉过他，胆怯的象总要受伤。他知道这话说得对。第一回见炮弹爆炸，他尖叫着后退，一屁股顶上一架堆起来的步枪，刺刀专扎在他浑身最软的那些地方。于是还不满二十五岁，他就戒了害怕这个毛病，也成了印度政府的服役象中最受喜爱、最受照料的一头。在印度北部随军行进时，他背过帐篷，一千二百磅重的帐篷。他还叫蒸汽吊车吊上过一条船，在水上走了许多天，去一个离印度很远、满地岩石的陌生国度，背着一门臼炮。他在马格达拉亲眼瞧见提奥多尔皇帝死去后躺在地上，又搭轮船回来。士兵们说，他够资格得一枚阿比西尼亚战役勋章。十年后，在一个叫阿里清真寺的地方，他看见同伴们有的冻死，有的癫痫发作而死，有的死于饥饿，有的死于中暑。后来他被送往南边几千英里外的毛淡棉，在木材场上拖运、堆码巨大的柚木方料。那里一头年轻象不听指派，想躲开自己该做的那份工，险些给他打掉半条命。

中文章名: 象童图迈

Elephants are very strictly preserved by the Indian Government. There is one whole department which does nothing else but hunt them, and catch them, and break them in, and send them up and down the country as they are needed for work.
原译: 之后，他被从采伐木材业中摘除，雇用了几头受过商业训练的其他大象，帮助在加罗山中捕捉野生大象。大象受到印度政府的严格保护。整个部门除了猎杀他们之外什么都做不了把他们抓起来把他们打碎然后把他们送到全国。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: Kala Nag stood ten fair feet at the shoulders, and his tusks had been cut off short at five feet, and bound round the ends, to prevent them splitting, with bands of copper; but he could do more with those stumps than any untrained elephant could do with the real sharpened ones. When, after weeks and weeks of cautious driving of scattered elephants across the hills, the forty or fifty wild monsters were driven into the last stockade, and the big drop gate, made of tree trunks lashed together, jarred down behind them, Kala Nag, at the word of command, would go into that flaring, trumpeting pandemonium (generally at night, when the flicker of the torches made it difficult to judge distances), and, picking out the biggest and wildest tusker of the mob, would hammer him and hustle him into quiet while the men on the backs of the other elephants roped and tied the smaller ones.
原译: 卡拉·纳格的肩膀有10英尺高，他的象牙短短5英尺高，并被捆绑在两端，以防止他们与铜团分解；但他对这些树桩所能做的比任何未受过训练的大象对真正的尖锐大象所能做的还要多。当经过数周和数周的小心驾驶分散的大象穿过山丘，四十或五十个野兽被驱赶到最后的棚屋，由树干捆绑在一起，喇叭声(一般在晚上，火炬闪烁使判断距离难于判断)，并挑出暴徒中最大和最野的暴徒。
现译: 卡拉·纳格肩高足足十英尺，两根象牙都截到只有五英尺长，截面箍着铜圈，不叫它们开裂。他用这两截牙干得出的事，没受过训练的象就是长着真正磨尖的长牙也干不了。捕象人谨慎地花上一周又一周，把四散的野象赶过山岭。最后四五十头野生巨兽悉数进了最后一道木栅，那用树干捆成的巨大闸门在他们身后轰然落下。这时只要一声号令，卡拉·纳格便走进那火光闪动、象吼震天的乱场——通常都在夜里，火把忽明忽暗，远近很难看准。他从象群中专挑最大最野的长牙公象，又撞又逼，直到对方安静下来；其余人则骑在别的大象背上，用绳索套住那些较小的野象，绑缚起来。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: There was nothing in the way of fighting that Kala Nag, the old wise Black Snake, did not know, for he had stood up more than once in his time to the charge of the wounded tiger, and, curling up his soft trunk to be out of harm’s way, had knocked the springing brute sideways in mid-air with a quick sickle cut of his head, that he had invented all by himself; had knocked him over, and kneeled upon him with his huge knees till the life went out with a gasp and a howl, and there was only a fluffy striped thing on the ground for Kala Nag to pull by the tail.
原译: 没有什么阻碍战斗的方式，古老的黑蛇卡拉·纳格，不知道，因为他不止一次站出来负责受伤的老虎，并卷起他的软后备箱走出伤害的方式，他曾捏造万物，然后把他击倒，然后用大膝盖跪在地上，直到生命用油气和怒吼扑灭，而卡拉·纳格在地上只留下一条毛巾，靠着尾巴拉。
现译: 要说打架的法门，这条聪明的老黑蛇，没有一样是不懂的。他不止一回迎击过受伤老虎的猛扑。他把柔软的长鼻卷起来，免得受伤，待老虎扑到半空，脑袋如镰刀一般飞快地侧挥过去，就把猛兽从空中撞向一旁。这一招是他自己想出来的。老虎倒了，他便用大膝盖压上去，直到敌手发出最后一声抽气和哀号，咽了气。地上只剩一团毛茸茸、有条纹的东西，任由卡拉·纳格拽着尾巴拖。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: “Yes,” said Big Toomai, his driver, the son of Black Toomai who had taken him to Abyssinia, and grandson of Toomai of the Elephants who had seen him caught, “there is nothing that the Black Snake fears except me. He has seen three generations of us feed him and groom him, and he will live to see four.”

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: “He is afraid of me also,” said Little Toomai, standing up to his full height of four feet, with only one rag upon him. He was ten years old, the eldest son of Big Toomai, and, according to custom, he would take his father’s place on Kala Nag’s neck when he grew up, and would handle the heavy iron ankus, the elephant goad, that had been worn smooth by his father, and his grandfather, and his great-grandfather.

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: He knew what he was talking of; for he had been born under Kala Nag’s shadow, had played with the end of his trunk before he could walk, had taken him down to water as soon as he could walk, and Kala Nag would no more have dreamed of disobeying his shrill little orders than he would have dreamed of killing him on that day when Big Toomai carried the little brown baby under Kala Nag’s tusks, and told him to salute his master that was to be.

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: “Yes,” said Little Toomai, “he is afraid of me,” and he took long strides up to Kala Nag, called him a fat old pig, and made him lift up his feet one after the other.

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: “Wah!” said Little Toomai, “thou art a big elephant,” and he wagged his fluffy head, quoting his father. “The Government may pay for elephants, but they belong to us mahouts. When thou art old, Kala Nag, there will come some rich rajah, and he will buy thee from the Government, on account of thy size and thy manners, and then thou wilt have nothing to do but to carry gold earrings in thy ears, and a gold howdah on thy back, and a red cloth covered with gold on thy sides, and walk at the head of the processions of the King. Then I shall sit on thy neck, O Kala Nag, with a silver ankus, and men will run before us with golden sticks, crying, `Room for the King’s elephant!’ That will be good, Kala Nag, but not so good as this hunting in the jungles.”
原译: 小图迈说，“你是个大象”，他用他父亲的话扯着他的毛头。“政府可以支付大象的费用，但大象属于我们。当你老了，卡拉纳格，就会有一些有钱的拉贾赫，他会以你的大小和举止从政府那里买下你，然后你将无事可做，只能把金耳环塞进你的耳朵里，你背上还有金鞭，你身上盖着金的红布，我必坐在你脖子上，加银的手杖。众人将用金棍在我们面前奔跑，他们喊叫著说：为国王的大象而建造一座房屋。那将是有益的。卡拉纳格，但并不如这个在丛林打猎。“
现译: “哇！你真是头了不起的大象。”小图迈摇晃着蓬松的小脑袋，学起父亲的口吻。“政府出钱买象，可象归我们象夫。卡拉·纳格，等你年纪大了，会有位有钱的王公看上你的身量和礼数，把你从政府手里买去。到那时候，你所要做的，只是耳朵戴金环，背上驮金鞍轿，两肋垂着满绣金线的红布，走在国王仪仗的头里。卡拉·纳格啊，我就拿一把银象钩，坐在你颈上。前头有人手执金杖奔走，高呼：‘给王家的大象让路！’那也很好，卡拉·纳格，可比不上眼下在丛林里狩猎。”
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: “Umph!” said Big Toomai. “Thou art a boy, and as wild as a buffalo-calf. This running up and down among the hills is not the best Government service. I am getting old, and I do not love wild elephants. Give me brick elephant lines, one stall to each elephant, and big stumps to tie them to safely, and flat, broad roads to exercise upon, instead of this come-and-go camping. Aha, the Cawnpore barracks were good. There was a bazaar close by, and only three hours’ work a day.”
原译: “Umph！” 大富人说。“你是一个男孩，野如水牛肉。这在山中奔跑并不是最好的政府服务。我年纪大了，我不喜欢野象。给我砖头大象线，每头大象一个摊位，大树桩，把它们安全地绑在平坦的宽阔的路上运动，库恩波尔营房不错，附近有集市，每天工作三小时。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: Little Toomai remembered the Cawnpore elephant-lines and said nothing. He very much preferred the camp life, and hated those broad, flat roads, with the daily grubbing for grass in the forage reserve, and the long hours when there was nothing to do except to watch Kala Nag fidgeting in his pickets.

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: What Little Toomai liked was to scramble up bridle paths that only an elephant could take; the dip into the valley below; the glimpses of the wild elephants browsing miles away; the rush of the frightened pig and peacock under Kala Nag’s feet; the blinding warm rains, when all the hills and valleys smoked; the beautiful misty mornings when nobody knew where they would camp that night; the steady, cautious drive of the wild elephants, and the mad rush and blaze and hullabaloo of the last night’s drive, when the elephants poured into the stockade like boulders in a landslide, found that they could not get out, and flung themselves at the heavy posts only to be driven back by yells and flaring torches and volleys of blank cartridge.

中文章名: 象童图迈

At last the elephants began to lie down one after another as is their custom, till only Kala Nag at the right of the line was left standing up; and he rocked slowly from side to side, his ears put forward to listen to the night wind as it blew very slowly across the hills. The air was full of all the night noises that, taken together, make one big silence--the click of one bamboo stem against the other, the rustle of something alive in the undergrowth, the scratch and squawk of a half-waked bird (birds are awake in the night much more often than we imagine), and the fall of water ever so far away. Little Toomai slept for some time, and when he waked it was brilliant moonlight, and Kala Nag was still standing up with his ears cocked. Little Toomai turned, rustling in the fodder, and watched the curve of his big back against half the stars in heaven, and while he watched he heard, so far away that it sounded no more than a pinhole of noise pricked through the stillness, the “hoot-toot” of a wild elephant.

中文章名: 象童图迈

中文章名: 象童图迈

That was made already, six feet wide, in front of him, where the bent jungle-grass was trying to recover itself and stand up. Many elephants must have gone that way only a few minutes before. Little Toomai looked back, and behind him a great wild tusker with his little pig’s eyes glowing like hot coals was just lifting himself out of the misty river. Then the trees closed up again, and they went on and up, with trumpetings and crashings, and the sound of breaking branches on every side of them.

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: At last Kala Nag stood still between two tree-trunks at the very top of the hill. They were part of a circle of trees that grew round an irregular space of some three or four acres, and in all that space, as Little Toomai could see, the ground had been trampled down as hard as a brick floor. Some trees grew in the center of the clearing, but their bark was rubbed away, and the white wood beneath showed all shiny and polished in the patches of moonlight. There were creepers hanging from the upper branches, and the bells of the flowers of the creepers, great waxy white things like convolvuluses, hung down fast asleep. But within the limits of the clearing there was not a single blade of green--nothing but the trampled earth.
原译: 终于卡拉·纳格站在山顶两棵树的中间。它们是一圈树木的一部分，这些树木在大约三到四英亩的不正常面积周围生长，在所有这些面积中，正如小图迈所见，地面被像砖地一样被踩碎。有些树生长在空地的中心，但它们的树皮被擦去，而下面的白色木头显示光亮和光亮在月光的斑点上。树枝上挂着爬行者爬行者花的钟声巨大的白蜡像卷轴快速沉睡。但在空旷的限度内，除了被践踏的大地之外，没有一片绿刃。
现译: 到了山巅，卡拉·纳格终于在两棵树之间停下。这两棵树属于环立林边的一大圈树，围着一块形状不规则、三四英亩大的空地。小图迈看得见，整个地面都给踩得像砖地一般硬。地中央长着几棵树，树皮已经磨掉，底下的白木在一块块月光里显得光亮平滑，像打过磨。高枝上垂着藤蔓，藤上的花就像旋花一样，白莹莹的，蜡质的大花钟低垂着，睡得正沉。可在这圈空地内，竟连一根青草都没有，只有踏实了的泥地。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: The moonlight showed it all iron gray, except where some elephants stood upon it, and their shadows were inky black. Little Toomai looked, holding his breath, with his eyes starting out of his head, and as he looked, more and more and more elephants swung out into the open from between the tree trunks. Little Toomai could only count up to ten, and he counted again and again on his fingers till he lost count of the tens, and his head began to swim. Outside the clearing he could hear them crashing in the undergrowth as they worked their way up the hillside, but as soon as they were within the circle of the tree trunks they moved like ghosts.
原译: 月光显示所有的铁灰色，除了一些大象站在它上面，他们的阴影是黑的。小图迈看着，屏住呼吸，眼睛从头开始，当他看着，越来越多的大象从树干之间向外挥舞。小图迈只能数到10，他一次又一次数到手指上，直到他数到10，头开始游泳。在空地外他听到他们从山坡上爬上去时在下层的树丛中坠落但一进入树干圈他们就像鬼一样移动了。
现译: 月光把整块地照成铁灰色，只有站着象的地方，他们的影子黑得像墨。小图迈屏住气，两眼几乎要瞪出来。他望着，望着，从树干之间，更多的象摇晃着走到了空地上，还有更多，还有更多。他只会数到十，屈起手指数了一遍又一遍，最后连数过了几个十都记不得了，脑袋一阵眩晕。空地之外，他能听见来者沿山坡往上闯，闯过灌草的动静。可他们一走进树干的圈子，步子便像鬼影一样安静。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: There were white-tusked wild males, with fallen leaves and nuts and twigs lying in the wrinkles of their necks and the folds of their ears; fat, slow-footed she-elephants, with restless, little pinky black calves only three or four feet high running under their stomachs; young elephants with their tusks just beginning to show, and very proud of them; lanky, scraggy old-maid elephants, with their hollow anxious faces, and trunks like rough bark; savage old bull elephants, scarred from shoulder to flank with great weals and cuts of bygone fights, and the caked dirt of their solitary mud baths dropping from their shoulders; and there was one with a broken tusk and the marks of the full-stroke, the terrible drawing scrape, of a tiger’s claws on his side.
原译: 有白发野生雄性，落叶、坚果和树枝躺在脖子的皱纹和耳朵的折叠中；长长的、慢脚的母象，腹部下只有三、四英尺高，无动于衷，小小小小小小小黑小牛；年轻的大象开始展示，非常骄傲；疯狂的老美大象，空洞的焦虑脸孔，和树干像粗糙的树皮；野蛮的老公象，肩膀和侧翼被伤痕累累，和他们单独泥浴的蛋糕泥从他们的肩膀上掉下来；和有一个有断裂的象牙和标记全面冲击，可怕的画刮痕，老虎爪在他身边。
现译: 有雪白长牙的野公象，颈间的皱皮和耳朵的折缝里搁着落叶、坚果、碎树枝；有胖胖的母象步子迟缓，肚皮底下跑着三四英尺高、粉中透黑、没有一刻安静的小象；有年轻象才冒出象牙，就骄傲得很；有瘦瘦长长、没有成过家的老妇，脸上凹陷忧烦，鼻子像粗糙的树皮；还有凶猛的老公象，从肩到肋，往昔搏斗留下的一道道肿痕、几处深伤全看得清。他们独自洗过泥浴，身上结壳的土正一块块从肩头掉下来。其中一头断了一根牙，身侧还留有猛虎全力挥爪向后一拖所刻下的、骇人的抓痕。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: They were standing head to head, or walking to and fro across the ground in couples, or rocking and swaying all by themselves--scores and scores of elephants.
原译: 他们站着头顶，或走来走去和fro横跨地面在夫妇，或摇摆和摇摆全部自己 - 计分和数十大象。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: Toomai knew that so long as he lay still on Kala Nag’s neck nothing would happen to him, for even in the rush and scramble of a Keddah drive a wild elephant does not reach up with his trunk and drag a man off the neck of a tame elephant. And these elephants were not thinking of men that night. Once they started and put their ears forward when they heard the chinking of a leg iron in the forest, but it was Pudmini, Petersen Sahib’s pet elephant, her chain snapped short off, grunting, snuffling up the hillside. She must have broken her pickets and come straight from Petersen Sahib’s camp; and Little Toomai saw another elephant, one that he did not know, with deep rope galls on his back and breast. He, too, must have run away from some camp in the hills about.
原译: 图迈知道，只要他躺在卡拉·纳格的脖子上，他就不会有事，因为即使在Keddah的匆忙和乱跑中，野象也不会抬起他的后备箱，把一个人从被驯服的大象的脖子上拖下来。那天晚上这些大象没有想到男人。他们听到森林里一只脚铁的下巴时开始把耳朵往前伸出来但是是Pudmini 彼得森老爷的宠物大象她的链条断了向山坡上发出呼噜声窒息。她一定是打破了纠察线，直接从彼得森·萨希布的营地赶来；小图玛伊看到另一头大象，他不知道，背上和胸上还有深处的绳子。他一定也从山上的营地跑了。
现译: 图迈知道，只要静静趴在卡拉·纳格的颈上，自己就没事。哪怕在围栅里最拥挤、最混乱的时候，野象也不会把长鼻伸上去，从驯象颈上扯下一个人来。况且这些象那一晚根本没在人身上转念头。只有一回，林间突然有脚镣叮当一响，他们一惊，一齐把耳朵伸向前去。原来是彼得森老爷的爱象帕德米妮，脚链齐茬断了，正哼哼着、喷着鼻息往山上爬。她一定是挣脱拴桩，从彼得森老爷的营地径直赶来的。小图迈还看见一头自己不认识的象，胸前背上都带着绳子磨出的深痕。想必他也是从近处山里的哪座营地逃出来的。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: At last there was no sound of any more elephants moving in the forest, and Kala Nag rolled out from his station between the trees and went into the middle of the crowd, clucking and gurgling, and all the elephants began to talk in their own tongue, and to move about.

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: Still lying down, Little Toomai looked down upon scores and scores of broad backs, and wagging ears, and tossing trunks, and little rolling eyes. He heard the click of tusks as they crossed other tusks by accident, and the dry rustle of trunks twined together, and the chafing of enormous sides and shoulders in the crowd, and the incessant flick and hissh of the great tails. Then a cloud came over the moon, and he sat in black darkness. But the quiet, steady hustling and pushing and gurgling went on just the same. He knew that there were elephants all round Kala Nag, and that there was no chance of backing him out of the assembly; so he set his teeth and shivered. In a Keddah at least there was torchlight and shouting, but here he was all alone in the dark, and once a trunk came up and touched him on the knee.
原译: 仍然躺着，小图玛伊低头看得分和得分的背部，摇摇晃晃的耳朵，抛下树干，和小滚动的眼睛。他听到海象的点击声，当时它们偶然跨过其他海象，干枯的树干结结成两半，人群中巨大的两面和肩部的磨擦，以及大尾巴的不断闪烁和刺痛。然后一朵云从月球上飞来他坐在黑暗中。但安静的稳稳的推推和凝固都一样。他知道有大象围着卡拉纳格，没有机会支持他出集会，所以他放下牙齿和颤抖。至少在一个凯达有火炬和喊叫，但在这里，他独自在黑暗中，有一次一个后备箱上来触摸他的膝盖。
现译: 小图迈仍旧趴着，俯望几十又几十副宽阔的脊背，摇动的耳朵，甩过来甩过去的长鼻，小小的转动的眼睛。他听见象牙不小心交错时轻轻一叩，长鼻互相缠绕时干涩的磨擦声，庞大的肩与肋在挤作一团的象群中擦过；大尾巴甩过去，嘶一声，又甩过来，没完没了。忽有一朵云掩住月亮，他坐在一团漆黑里。但那安静、有节奏的推推挤挤和咕噜声，依然如故。他知道卡拉·纳格四面全是象，休想倒退着把他从集会中带出去，只好咬住牙关发抖。在围栅里，至少有火把，有人喊叫，这儿他却独自待在暗处。有一回，一条长鼻还探上来碰了碰他的膝盖。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: Then an elephant trumpeted, and they all took it up for five or ten terrible seconds. The dew from the trees above spattered down like rain on the unseen backs, and a dull booming noise began, not very loud at first, and Little Toomai could not tell what it was. But it grew and grew, and Kala Nag lifted up one forefoot and then the other, and brought them down on the ground--one-two, one-two, as steadily as trip-hammers. The elephants were stamping all together now, and it sounded like a war drum beaten at the mouth of a cave. The dew fell from the trees till there was no more left to fall, and the booming went on, and the ground rocked and shivered, and Little Toomai put his hands up to his ears to shut out the sound. But it was all one gigantic jar that ran through him--this stamp of hundreds of heavy feet on the raw earth. Once or twice he could feel Kala Nag and all the others surge forward a few strides, and the thumping would change to the crushing sound of juicy green things being bruised, but in a minute or two the boom of feet on hard earth began again. A tree was creaking and groaning somewhere near him. He put out his arm and felt the bark, but Kala Nag moved forward, still tramping, and he could not tell where he was in the clearing. There was no sound from the elephants, except once, when two or three little calves squeaked together. Then he heard a thump and a shuffle, and the booming went on. It must have lasted fully two hours, and Little Toomai ached in every nerve, but he knew by the smell of the night air that the dawn was coming.
原译: 然后一头大象吹喇叭，他们都把它拿起来 5或10 可怕的秒。上面树上的露水像雨一样喷落在看不见的背部开始发出无趣的声响一开始声音不太响小图迈不知道是什么。但它长大了卡拉纳格举起一只前脚然后又举起另一只脚把他们带到地面上。大象们现在都聚在一起了听起来像是在洞穴口打的战鼓。露水从树上掉下来，直到再没有剩下可以倒下去的了，繁荣继续，地面震动，小图迈把手举到耳朵上，把声音关上。但是，这是所有一个巨大的罐跑过他 -- 这个印章数百重脚在生土。他一两下就能感觉到卡拉纳格其他人都往前冲了几步震动声会改变成充满活力的绿色物质被打碎的声音但一两分钟后硬土上又开始繁荣。有棵树在他附近吱吱作响。他伸出手臂，感觉到了树皮，但是卡拉纳格继续前进，仍然在踩踏，他不知道他在哪里在空地。大象们没有发出任何声音，除了一次，两三个小牛群一起叫叫。然后他听到一声巨响和乱七八糟的响起。它一定持续了整整两个小时小豆木一股神经都发炎了但他从夜空的气味中知道黎明即将来临。
现译: 随后，一头象昂鼻长鸣，所有的象都接了上来。那骇人的呼号响了五秒，也许十秒。头顶的露珠纷纷从树上洒下来，如同下雨，溅在看不见的象背上。这时传来低沉的隆隆声，起初并不很响，小图迈辨不出是什么。可声音渐渐大了，又大了。卡拉·纳格抬起一只前脚，再抬另一只，一下下踏回地面。一、二，一、二，稳得像锻锤。此刻群象都在齐齐踏地，声音就像有人在洞口敲响战鼓。露珠从树上落尽，再没有一滴可落，轰鸣却还在继续，大地摇荡震颤。小图迈举起双手捂住耳朵，不想听这声音。可那整个儿是一场穿过他全身的大震动——几百只沉重的大脚正踏在裸露的泥土上。有一两次，他觉得卡拉·纳格和所有大象一齐向前涌了几步。咚咚声就变作挤压鲜嫩草木的碎裂声，只过一两分钟，象脚踏硬地的轰鸣又起来了。附近有一棵树吱呀呻吟，他伸手摸到了树皮。可卡拉·纳格一边踏一边又向前走，他已经分不清自己在空地的什么地方。象群没有发出别的声音，只有一次，两三头小象一同吱叫了一阵。跟着一声闷响，一阵挪步，轰鸣继续。这样一定足足过了两个钟头。小图迈浑身每一根神经都在作痛，但他从夜风的气味中知道，黎明要来了。
修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: The morning broke in one sheet of pale yellow behind the green hills, and the booming stopped with the first ray, as though the light had been an order. Before Little Toomai had got the ringing out of his head, before even he had shifted his position, there was not an elephant in sight except Kala Nag, Pudmini, and the elephant with the rope-galls, and there was neither sign nor rustle nor whisper down the hillsides to show where the others had gone.
原译: 早上在绿山后面一片黄色的床单中破碎繁荣与第一束光停止仿佛光线是命令。在小图迈还没把那些想法从脑海中抛开，甚至还没改变位置之前，视野中除了卡拉·纳格、普德米尼以及那头有绳伤的大象，就再也没有其他大象了。山坡上既没有任何迹象、沙沙声或低语声表明其他大象去了哪里。

修改判断: 按所附英文全段重译，保留叙事视角、动物说话的身份和前后动作。

中文章名: 象童图迈
英文证据: Little Toomai stared again and again. The clearing, as he remembered it, had grown in the night.
