中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: That was enough for Kotuko. He had been brought up to believe that every rock and boulder had its owner (its inua), who was generally a one-eyed kind of a Woman-Thing called a tornaq, and that when a tornaq meant to help a man she rolled after him inside her stone house, and asked him whether he would take her for a guardian spirit. (In summer thaws the ice-propped rocks and boulders roll and slip all over the face of the land, so you can easily see how the idea of live stones arose.) Kotuko heard the blood beating in his ears as he had heard it all day, and he thought that was the tornaq of the stone speaking to him. Before he reached home he was quite certain that he had held a long conversation with her, and as all his people believed that this was quite possible, no one contradicted him.
原译: 柯图科已经够了。他长大后相信，每一块石头和巨石都有其主人，一般都是独眼女人，叫破碎，当一个龙卷风想帮助一个男人，她就滚进她家的石头屋，并问他，他是否会把她当作守护神。(夏天解冻了冰块和石头滚动滑过陆地表面，这样你就能很容易地看到活石的想法是如何产生的。)。科图科听到他一整天听到的流血声，他以为那是石头的撕裂声。在他回家之前，他非常确信他与她进行了长时间的对话，而且由于他的人民都认为这很有可能，因此没有人反驳他。
现译: 单这一桩，已经够叫科图科相信了。他从小就学到，每一块岩石、每一块巨砾都有自己的主人，叫“伊努阿”，通常是独眼的女子形体的精怪，名为托尔纳克。若一位托尔纳克想帮一个人，就会躲在自己的石头屋里跟着他滚，问他愿不愿收她为护身灵。（夏日解冻，被冰撑着的岩石在地面到处滚落滑行。你很容易明白，石头有生命的信念由此怎样生出。）科图科又听见血在耳中跳动，那声音已响了一整天。他以为是石里的托尔纳克和自己说话。在到家以前，他已确信跟她有过一席长谈。族人都信这样的事大有可能，没有谁反驳他。

中文章名: 奎奎恩

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: Through the village people were shouting: “The tornait have spoken to Kotuko. They will show him open ice. Kotuko insisted that the tornaq of the stone had told him to go north, and north they went under Tuktuqdjung the Reindeer--those stars that we call the Great Bear.

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: No European could have made five miles a day over the ice-rubbish and the sharp-edged drifts; but those two knew exactly the turn of the wrist that coaxes a sleigh round a hummock, the jerk that nearly lifts it out of an ice-crack, and the exact strength that goes to the few quiet strokes of the spear-head that make a path possible when everything looks hopeless.

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: The girl said nothing, but bowed her head, and the long wolverine-fur fringe of her ermine hood blew across her broad, dark face. The sky above them was an intense velvety black, changing to bands of Indian red on the horizon, where the great stars burned like street-lamps. From time to time a greenish wave of the Northern Lights would roll across the hollow of the high heavens, flick like a flag, and disappear; or a meteor would crackle from darkness to darkness, trailing a shower of sparks behind. Then they could see the ridged and furrowed surface of the floe tipped and laced with strange colours--red, copper, and bluish; but in the ordinary starlight everything turned to one frost-bitten gray. The floe, as you will remember, had been battered and tormented by the autumn gales till it was one frozen earthquake. There were gullies and ravines, and holes like gravel-pits, cut in ice; lumps and scattered pieces frozen down to the original floor of the floe; blotches of old black ice that had been thrust under the floe in some gale and heaved up again; roundish boulders of ice; saw-like edges of ice carved by the snow that flies before the wind; and sunken pits where thirty or forty acres lay below the level of the rest of the field. From a little distance you might have taken the lumps for seal or walrus, overturned sleighs or men on a hunting expedition, or even the great Ten-legged White Spirit-Bear himself; but in spite of these fantastic shapes, all on the very edge of starting into life, there was neither sound nor the least faint echo of sound. And through this silence and through this waste, where the sudden lights flapped and went out again, the sleigh and the two that pulled it crawled like things in a nightmare--a nightmare of the end of the world at the end of the world.
原译: 女孩没说什么，只是低头长长的狼人和Fur 头罩吹过她的宽阔，黑暗的脸。上面的天空是一团强烈的天鹅绒黑变成地平线上的印度红带巨大的恒星像街灯一样燃烧。有时，绿色的北极光浪会滚过高空的空洞，像旗子一样闪烁，消失；或者一颗陨石从黑暗到黑暗，在烟花的后面闪烁。然后，他们可以看到花朵的被剥落和被剥落的表面满是奇怪的颜色红色，铜色，和油质；但在普通星光中，一切都变成了一个冰冻的灰色。你将记得，佛罗因在秋天被暴风雪折磨，直到一场冰冻的地震。有沟渠和沟渠，还有像碎石坑一样的洞洞，被切成冰块；有块块块和零散的碎块，被冻在花地板上；有一块旧黑冰块，在花上被挤压，再被堆积起来；有圆圆圆的冰块；在风前的雪所雕刻的冰面，和沉积的坑，30到40英亩的面积低于田地的其余部分。从一小段距离，你可能已经拿块海豹或海象，翻转雪橇或人在狩猎探险，甚至伟大的十脚白色圣灵熊自己；但尽管这些奇妙的形状，在所有开始生命的边缘。通过沉默和浪费，突然的灯光闪烁，又熄灭了，雪橇和两个拉它爬行像在一场噩梦中-- 噩梦世界末日的末日。
现译: 女孩垂头不说话。白鼬皮兜帽镶着狼獾长毛，毛边吹过她宽阔深色的面孔。头顶的天黑得像厚绒，到地平线化作一带带暗红，大星燃烧，像街灯一般。时而一浪浅绿的北极光滚过穹顶空虚的高处，像旗帜抖一下又消失，或者一颗流星劈啪地从黑暗的这一头穿到那一头，身后拖着一阵火花雨。那时他们便能看见浮冰的脊梁和沟纹镶上奇异的色彩，红的，紫铜的，带蓝的。可在寻常星光底下，一切只剩冻伤般的一片灰。你还记得吧，秋天的狂风把冰原捶打、折磨得仿佛一场冻住的地震。冰里刻着沟谷和裂壑，坑洼像砾石采场。碎块和冰团冻在原先平整的冰层上。黑斑是老冰，曾被某一场疾风塞进冰原底下，又重新掀起。还有近圆的冰石，飞雪在风前凿出的锯齿冰缘，以及比其余地面低了整整一层、三四十英亩大的凹坑。稍远处望去，你会把这些冰团当成海豹或海象，翻倒的雪橇，出猎的人，甚至伟大的十足白灵熊本尊。可是这些古怪的形状个个都像立刻要活转来，四下却毫无声息，连一点点回音都没有。雪橇和拉着它的两个人，穿过这片寂静，穿过这片突现的光忽地扑扇又熄灭的荒原，缓缓蠕动，如同噩梦里的东西。这是一个在世界尽头梦见世界末日的噩梦。

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: When they were tired Kotuko would make what the hunters call a “half-house,” a very small snow hut, into which they would huddle with the travelling-lamp, and try to thaw out the frozen seal-meat. When they had slept, the march began again--thirty miles a day to get ten miles northward. The girl was always very silent, but Kotuko muttered to himself and broke out into songs he had learned in the Singing-House--summer songs, and reindeer and salmon songs--all horribly out of place at that season. He would declare that he heard the tornaq growling to him, and would run wildly up a hummock, tossing his arms and speaking in loud, threatening tones. To tell the truth, Kotuko was very nearly crazy for the time being; but the girl was sure that he was being guided by his guardian spirit, and that everything would come right. She was not surprised, therefore, when at the end of the fourth march Kotuko, whose eyes were burning like fire-balls in his head, told her that his tornaq was following them across the snow in the shape of a two-headed dog. The girl looked where Kotuko pointed, and something seemed to slip into a ravine. It was certainly not human, but everybody knew that the tornait preferred to appear in the shape of bear and seal, and such like.
原译: 当他们疲惫的时候科图科会把猎人称之为“半屋” 一个很小的雪棚，他们会围着那条路走，试着解冻冰封的海豹。当他们睡着，游行又开始了..。 每天30英里向北走10英里。这女孩总是很沉默，但科图科自言自语，突然就唱出他在《唱歌 -豪斯 -夏令营》的歌和驯鹿和鲑鱼的歌..。他将宣布，他听到咆哮的旋律，他将狂野地跑到一个喇叭上，抛起他的手臂，大声地说话，威胁地喊叫。说实话，科图科目前几乎是疯了；但女孩确信，他正在以他的守护精神为指导，一切都会好起来。因此，她并不感到惊讶的是，在第四场游行结束时，科图科的眼睛像燃烧的火球一样在头部燃烧，她告诉她，他的龙卷风正以一只双头狗的形状在雪上跟着他们。女孩看着科图科指向的地方似乎有东西滑进了峡谷。它当然不是人类，但每个人都知道拖拉机更喜欢出现以熊和海豹的形式，像这样。
现译: 累了，科图科就搭起猎人们叫作“半间屋”的东西，小得不能再小的雪屋。两人带着行灯挤进去，设法把冻海豹肉化开。睡了一觉，再次上路。要往北挪十英里，一天须绕三十英里路。女孩总是极安静，科图科却喃喃自语，忽而唱出从歌屋学来的调子，唱夏天，唱驯鹿，唱鲑鱼，在这个时节听来何其不合情境。他会宣称听到了石灵向他低吼，疯了般跑上一座冰丘，两臂乱挥，高声威胁着什么。说实话，科图科那一阵差不多失去了理智。可是女孩深信他的守护灵在指引他，一切终究会好。因此到了第四次歇脚时，他那两眼在眼窝里烧成火球，告诉女孩他的托尔纳克变作一条双头狗，一路尾随他们过雪原，女孩并不惊奇。她朝科图科指的地方看，好像真有个东西滑进一条冰沟。那肯定不是人。不过人人都知道，石灵爱借熊、海豹之类的形状现身。

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: It might have been the Ten-legged White Spirit-Bear himself, or it might have been anything, for Kotuko and the girl were so starved that their eyes were untrustworthy. They had trapped nothing, and seen no trace of game since they had left the village; their food would not hold out for another week, and there was a gale coming. A Polar storm can blow for ten days without a break, and all that while it is certain death to be abroad. Kotuko laid up a snow-house large enough to take in the hand-sleigh (never be separated from your meat), and while he was shaping the last irregular block of ice that makes the key-stone of the roof, he saw a Thing looking at him from a little cliff of ice half a mile away. The air was hazy, and the Thing seemed to be forty feet long and ten feet high, with twenty feet of tail and a shape that quivered all along the outlines. The girl saw it too, but instead of crying aloud with terror, said quietly, “That is Quiquern. What comes after?”
原译: 可能是十脚的白种人也可能是任何东西因为科图科和那女孩都饿得眼睛不可信。他们没有困住任何东西，也没有看到他们离开村庄后的任何游戏痕迹；他们的食物再过一周就停不下来了，还有一场大风。极地风暴可以连续十天不停地吹，而这一切，虽然它肯定死在国外。科图科在雪地上盖了一座雪屋，足以把雪橇(从不与你的肉分开)，当他正在塑造最后一块不规则的冰块。空气很模糊，东西似乎有40英尺长，10英尺高，尾巴有20英尺长，外形在轮廓上抖动。那女孩也看到了，但与其大声喊叫，还不如悄悄地说，“这是Quiquen，后来又怎么了？”
现译: 兴许是十足白灵熊自己，兴许是什么都可以。科图科和女孩饿得眼睛已不可信。出村以后，他们的套子一无所获，也没见过猎物留下半点迹象。口粮再撑不过一个星期，风暴且正要来。极地风暴可以一连吹上十天不停，这整个期间留在外面必死无疑。科图科搭了座够大得能放进手橇的雪屋（永远别和你的肉分开）。他正在修整屋顶最后那块不规则的拱顶石时，看见半英里外的小冰崖上有个东西正望着他。空气雾蒙蒙，那东西看起来有四十英尺长、十英尺高，尾巴二十英尺，整圈轮廓都在晃动。女孩也看见了。可她没惊叫，只平静地说：“是奎奎恩。往后又要出什么事呢？”

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: “He will speak to me,” said Kotuko; but the snow-knife trembled in his hand as he spoke, because however much a man may believe that he is a friend of strange and ugly spirits, he seldom likes to be taken quite at his word. Quiquern, too, is the phantom of a gigantic toothless dog without any hair, who is supposed to live in the far North, and to wander about the country just before things are going to happen. They may be pleasant or unpleasant things, but not even the sorcerers care to speak about Quiquern. He makes the dogs go mad. Like the Spirit-Bear, he has several extra pairs of legs,--six or eight,--and this Thing jumping up and down in the haze had more legs than any real dog needed. Kotuko and the girl huddled into their hut quickly. Of course if Quiquern had wanted them, he could have torn it to pieces above their heads, but the sense of a foot-thick snow-wall between themselves and the wicked dark was great comfort. The gale broke with a shriek of wind like the shriek of a train, and for three days and three nights it held, never varying one point, and never lulling even for a minute. They fed the stone lamp between their knees, and nibbled at the half-warm seal-meat, and watched the black soot gather on the roof for seventy-two long hours. The girl counted up the food in the sleigh; there was not more than two days’ supply, and Kotuko looked over the iron heads and the deer-sinew fastenings of his harpoon and his seal-lance and his bird-dart. There was nothing else to do.

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: “Let us follow,” said the girl. “It may know some way that does not lead to Sedna”; but she reeled from weakness as she took the pulling-rope. The Thing moved off slowly and clumsily across the ridges, heading always toward the westward and the land, and they followed, while the growling thunder at the edge of the floe rolled nearer and nearer. The floe’s lip was split and cracked in every direction for three or four miles inland, and great pans of ten-foot-thick ice, from a few yards to twenty acres square, were jolting and ducking and surging into one another, and into the yet unbroken floe, as the heavy swell took and shook and spouted between them. This battering-ram ice was, so to speak, the first army that the sea was flinging against the floe. The incessant crash and jar of these cakes almost drowned the ripping sound of sheets of pack-ice driven bodily under the floe as cards are hastily pushed under a tablecloth. Where the water was shallow these sheets would be piled one atop of the other till the bottommost touched mud fifty feet down, and the discoloured sea banked behind the muddy ice till the increasing pressure drove all forward again. In addition to the floe and the pack-ice, the gale and the currents were bringing down true bergs, sailing mountains of ice, snapped off from the Greenland side of the water or the north shore of Melville Bay. They pounded in solemnly, the waves breaking white round them, and advanced on the floe like an old-time fleet under full sail. A berg that seemed ready to carry the world before it would ground helplessly in deep water, reel over, and wallow in a lather of foam and mud and flying frozen spray, while a much smaller and lower one would rip and ride into the flat floe, flinging tons of ice on either side, and cutting a track half a mile long before it was stopped. Some fell like swords, shearing a raw-edged canal; and others splintered into a shower of blocks, weighing scores of tons apiece, that whirled and skirted among the hummocks. Others, again, rose up bodily out of the water when they shoaled, twisted as though in pain, and fell solidly on their sides, while the sea threshed over their shoulders. This trampling and crowding and bending and buckling and arching of the ice into every possible shape was going on as far as the eye could reach all along the north line of the floe. From where Kotuko and the girl were, the confusion looked no more than an uneasy, rippling, crawling movement under the horizon; but it came toward them each moment, and they could hear, far away to landward a heavy booming, as it might have been the boom of artillery through a fog. That showed that the floe was being jammed home against the iron cliffs of Bylot’s Island, the land to the southward behind them.
原译: “让我们跟着”，女孩说。可能知道一些方法并不导致塞德纳；但她从软弱中退缩，当她采取拉绳。它慢慢地穿过山脊，向西走去，向陆地走来，然后它们跟着，浮线边缘的咆哮雷更近更近地滚动。佛罗尔的嘴唇被撕裂向内陆三四英里处的每一个方向裂开巨大的十英尺厚的冰层从几码到二十英亩方形从几码到20英亩处。可以说，这块冰块是海中第一次向浮舟倾斜的军队。这些蛋糕的不断坠毁和罐子几乎淹没了被肉身驱使的肉床的撕裂声因为卡片被匆忙地推倒在桌布下。在浅水的地方，这些床单会堆在另一张床单上，直到最底部触摸到五十英尺深的泥土，腐烂的海面在泥冰后面，直到不断增大的压力再次推向前进。除了浮冰和冰块之外，风和海流正在降下真正的冰山，漂浮在冰山上，从格陵兰河边或梅尔维尔湾的北岸断裂。他们郑重地敲打，波浪冲破了他们，并像一个老舰队在全帆下前进。一个似乎准备承载世界的冰山将无助地沉入深水中卷起绳子沉入泡沫和泥浆的泥浆中喷洒冰冻的喷雾。一些人像剑一样倒下，割断了一条生化的运河；另一些人则从一块块的淋浴中分裂出来，每块重达几十吨，在蜂窝中摇晃和穿梭。其他人再次从水中身体上站起来当他们游荡，扭曲，就像痛苦，并倒在他们的两侧，而海击打他们的肩膀。冰块的践踏挤压弯曲弯曲和倾斜和倾斜形成各种可能形状正在继续。从科图科和那女孩的身影来看，混乱只是一种令人不安的、 振动的、爬行的地平线下；但是它每时每刻都降临到他们面前，他们都能听到，远至在陆地上发生一次猛烈的爆炸，因为它可能是大炮在雾中爆炸。这说明佛洛被卡在比洛特岛的铁悬崖上南边的土地被卡住了。
现译: “咱们跟着它吧，”女孩说。“也许它知道哪条路不用去见塞德娜。”她握住拉绳时，却虚弱得一个趔趄。那东西笨拙缓慢地越过道道冰脊，一直向西，朝着陆地。他们在后面跟，浮冰边缘雷鸣般的低吼却越来越近。自冰缘往里三四英里，横七竖八全是裂缝。厚达十英尺的大冰盘，小的宽几码，大的整块有二十英亩，彼此颠撞、沉浮、冲涌，又撞上还没破裂的冰原。巨浪托起它们，摇撼它们，从它们之间喷涌。这些像攻城槌的冰块，可以说是大海冲冰野派出的第一支军队。大冰饼一刻不停地相撞，震得几乎听不见另一种撕裂声。那是整张整张的浮冰被推入冰原底下，像纸牌被匆忙塞进桌布下面落出的响动。逢到浅水，那些冰片一层层堆积，直到最底下的一片触到五十英尺深处的淤泥，搅得变色的海水壅在泥冰后面，压力增加，又把一切往前推。除了整片的岸冰和成群的浮冰，风暴和洋流还带来了真正的冰山。它们是从对面的格陵兰岸或梅尔维尔湾北岸断落、漂浮在水上的山。冰山沉稳地重重迫近，四周浪花雪白，像古代的舰队张满帆，压向冰野。有的冰山看去足以把全世界推在前面，却在深水里无可奈何地搁浅，摇晃，倾倒，在泡沫、泥浆和飞到半空便冻住的水雾里打滚。小而低的另一座反倒撕开冰皮，骑上平整的冰原，两边掀起成吨冰块，犁出半英里长的一条路才停。有的冰山像剑劈下来，削出一道边缘生硬的新水渠。有的崩裂成雨点般的冰块，每块少说几十吨，在冰丘间打旋飞掠。还有的在浅处整座耸出水面，像疼极了似的扭动，轰然侧倒，海水在它的肩头鞭打。目力所及，沿冰原北线，到处是这样踩踏、拥挤、弯曲、折叠、拱起，能有的形状全有了。从科图科和女孩所在之处看去，天边的骚乱不过是一线不安的波纹在蠕动。可每过一刻，它就近一些。朝陆地方向的远处传来沉重的轰鸣，像大雾中的炮声。那说明整片浮冰已被结结实实挤向他们身后南方拜洛特岛钢铁般的峭壁。

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: “Follow THAT!” the girl cried, pointing to the Thing half limping, half running distractedly before them. They followed, tugging at the hand-sleigh, while nearer and nearer came the roaring march of the ice. At last the fields round them cracked and starred in every direction, and the cracks opened and snapped like the teeth of wolves. But where the Thing rested, on a mound of old and scattered ice-blocks some fifty feet high, there was no motion. Kotuko leaped forward wildly, dragging the girl after him, and crawled to the bottom of the mound. The talking of the ice grew louder and louder round them, but the mound stayed fast, and, as the girl looked at him, he threw his right elbow upward and outward, making the Inuit sign for land in the shape of an island. And land it was that the eight-legged, limping Thing had led them to--some granite-tipped, sand-beached islet off the coast, shod and sheathed and masked with ice so that no man could have told it from the floe, but at the bottom solid earth, and not shifting ice! The smashing and rebound of the floes as they grounded and splintered marked the borders of it, and a friendly shoal ran out to the northward, and turned aside the rush of the heaviest ice, exactly as a ploughshare turns over loam. There was danger, of course, that some heavily squeezed ice-field might shoot up the beach, and plane off the top of the islet bodily; but that did not trouble Kotuko and the girl when they made their snow-house and began to eat, and heard the ice hammer and skid along the beach. The Thing had disappeared, and Kotuko was talking excitedly about his power over spirits as he crouched round the lamp. In the middle of his wild sayings the girl began to laugh, and rock herself backward and forward.
原译: 女孩哭着说：“跟着！” 指着半瘸半瘸的东西，一半在她们面前分心跑。他们跟着，拖着滑雪梯，而冰雪的咆哮行进则越来越近。终于，圆着的田地裂开，向每个方向裂开，像狼的牙齿一样断裂。但是，当事情平息，在一个堆积的旧的和分散的冰块大约50英尺高，没有运动。科图科狂野地向前冲拖着那女孩跟着他爬到丘陵的底部。冰的传言越来越响亮，但丘陵保持快速，当女孩看着他，他把他的右肘向上和向外，使因努伊特人标记土地的形状一个岛屿。正是那八条腿、一瘸一拐的怪物，把他们带到了——一处海岸边有花岗岩构成的、沙滩覆盖的小岛上。那里被冰覆盖，无法与浮冰区分，但底部是坚实的陆地，而非移动的冰层！水线的粉碎和反弹标志着它的边界一只友善的船跑向北边抛开最重的冰块。当然，有危险，有些挤得要命的冰场可能会在海滩上射击，飞机会从小岛的顶部飞下来；但是，当科图科和那个女孩在雪屋里做饭时，他们没有感到烦恼，他们听到在海滩上打冰锤和滑雪的声音。歌声消失了科图科在压着灯泡的时候兴奋地谈论着自己对灵魂的力量。在他疯狂的言语中女孩开始笑，并摇动自己后退和向前。
现译: “跟着它！”女孩指着前方一瘸一拐又仓皇奔跑的那东西叫道。他们扯着手橇跟了去，冰的行军吼声越来越逼近。终于，身边的冰野朝各方放射出星形裂纹。裂隙张开又合拢，像狼牙一般咔嚓作响。可那东西歇下的地方，有一堆零散旧冰块，隆起来五十英尺高，纹丝不动。科图科猛地向前一跃，把女孩拖在后面，爬到冰丘脚下。冰在四周说话的声音愈来愈响，冰丘却牢牢立着。女孩望着他，他便把右肘向外向上一抬，那是因纽特人表示岛屿陆地的手势。那一瘸一拐的八脚怪真把他俩领到了陆地！近海一座小岛，花岗岩顶，沙滩围边，冰给它套了鞋，裹了身，戴了面具，谁也看不出它和大冰原有什么区别。可底下是踏实的土，不是漂移的冰！搁浅、碎裂的冰排撞上又弹开，把岛屿的边缘划了出来。一道友善的浅滩延伸向北，将最沉最猛的冲冰从两侧拨开，像犁铧翻开沃土。当然，万一哪块冰原受压太大，猛冲上海滩，整个岛顶都有给它一刨刨平的危险。但当科图科和女孩搭起雪屋，开始吃东西，听冰块沿海滩猛击疾滑时，这已不使他们忧虑。那东西已经消失。科图科蹲在灯旁，兴奋地谈起自己驾驭神灵的力量。就在他讲得神乎其神之际，女孩开始发笑，前仰后合。

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: Behind her shoulder, crawling into the hut crawl by crawl, there were two heads, one yellow and one black, that belonged to two of the most sorrowful and ashamed dogs that ever you saw. Kotuko the dog was one, and the black leader was the other. Both were now fat, well-looking, and quite restored to their proper minds, but coupled to each other in an extraordinary fashion. When the black leader ran off, you remember, his harness was still on him. He must have met Kotuko the dog, and played or fought with him, for his shoulder-loop had caught in the plaited copper wire of Kotuko’s collar, and had drawn tight, so that neither could get at the trace to gnaw it apart, but each was fastened sidelong to his neighbour’s neck. That, with the freedom of hunting on their own account, must have helped to cure their madness. They were very sober.
原译: 在她的肩膀后面爬进小屋爬行有两个头一个黄色一个黑色属于你见过的最悲伤和最羞耻的狗。一只狗叫科图科另一只是黑人头目。两者现在都非常胖，长得漂亮，并且完全恢复了正常的思维，但是以非凡的方式相互结合。黑人领袖逃跑的时候你记得他的绳子还在他身上。他一定是遇到了狗科图科，和他玩耍或打架，因为他的肩膀被夹在科图科的项圈上的铜丝上，并拉紧了，那样谁也无法追踪到它，但每个人都被绑在邻居的脖子上。有了他们自己的狩猎自由一定帮助治愈了他们的疯狂。他们非常清醒。
现译: 她的肩膀后面，有两个脑袋，一黄一黑，正一步一步爬进屋来。它们属于世上你能见到的最愁苦、最羞愧的两条狗。一条是狗科图科，一条是从前的大黑领头狗。两条如今都肥壮精神，神志完全正常，却用很古怪的方式连在一起。你记得，大黑狗逃走的时候还穿着挽具。想必它后来碰上了狗科图科，或者玩，或者打，肩套就勾进科图科那副铜丝编的项圈，越扯越紧，弄到谁也扭不过头去咬断挽绳，两个家伙各自侧贴着邻居的脖子拴在一起。大约就是这回事，加上能自由自在自己打猎，使它们从疯狂里缓过来。眼下两位安分得很。

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: Kotuko cut them free, and they fell into his arms, yellow and black together, trying to explain how they had got their senses back again. Kotuko ran a hand down their ribs, which were round and well clothed. “They have found food,” he said, with a grin. “I do not think we shall go to Sedna so soon. My tornaq sent these. The sickness has left them.”
原译: 科图科把他们解脱了他们一起掉进他的怀里黄色和黑色的试图解释他们如何再次恢复了知觉。科图科用手伸下肋骨肋骨是圆的衣服很好。他说“他们找到了食物” 笑着说。我不认为我们会这么快就去塞德纳。我的托纳克寄来了这些，疾病使他们离开了。

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: As soon as they had greeted Kotuko, these two, who had been forced to sleep and eat and hunt together for the past few weeks, flew at each other’s throat, and there was a beautiful battle in the snow-house. “Empty dogs do not fight,” Kotuko said. “They have found the seal. 中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: When they waked there was open water on the north beach of the island, and all the loosened ice had been driven landward. The first sound of the surf is one of the most delightful that the Inuit can hear, for it means that spring is on the road. Kotuko and the girl took hold of hands and smiled, for the clear, full roar of the surge among the ice reminded them of salmon and reindeer time and the smell of blossoming ground-willows. Even as they looked, the sea began to skim over between the floating cakes of ice, so intense was the cold; but on the horizon there was a vast red glare, and that was the light of the sunken sun. It was more like hearing him yawn in his sleep than seeing him rise, and the glare lasted for only a few minutes, but it marked the turn of the year. Nothing, they felt, could alter that.
原译: 当他们醒来时岛上北边的海滩有开阔的水所有的松开的冰都被推向陆地。冲浪的第一声是因努伊特人能听到的最令人愉快的声音之一，因为它意味着春天正在路上。科图科和那女孩举起手来微笑，因为冰块中涌出潮流的清晰而全面的咆哮，提醒他们注意鲑鱼和驯鹿的时间，以及开花的地柳的气味。即使在他们看的时候，海也开始在冰的浮饼之间滑动，寒冷是如此的强烈；但是在地平线上，有巨大的红色光亮，那就是沉没的太阳的光。更像是在睡梦中听到他打哈欠而不是看到他站起来光线只持续了几分钟但它标志着一年的到来。他们觉得没有什么能改变这一点。
现译: 醒来时，小岛北滩已露出一带无冰的水，所有松动的海冰全被推向了岸。因纽特人最爱听的声音之一，就是第一阵浪涛声，因为那意味着春天上了路。科图科和女孩牵起手来，笑了。浪在碎冰间涌起，澄净、浑厚的轰鸣提醒他们，捕鲑鱼、追驯鹿的时节，矮柳开花的香味，都会来。他们眼看着严寒让海面在冰饼间又罩上一层薄壳。但地平线上却横着一道巨大的红光，那是还在地平线下的太阳发的光。与其说看见它升起，更像听见它在梦里打个呵欠。红光只留了几分钟，可是年景已到转折处。他们觉得，什么也改变不了这一点。

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: Kotuko found the dogs fighting over a fresh-killed seal who was following the fish that a gale always disturbs. He was the first of some twenty or thirty seal that landed on the island in the course of the day, and till the sea froze hard there were hundreds of keen black heads rejoicing in the shallow free water and floating about with the floating ice.

现译: 科图科发现两条狗正争夺一头新杀的海豹。海豹是跟着风暴惊动的鱼群游来的。那天之中有二三十头登上小岛，它是第一头。在海面重新冻硬之前，几百颗机警的黑脑袋在无冰的浅水中欢游，随漂浮的冰块一起荡来荡去。

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: It was good to eat seal-liver again; to fill the lamps recklessly with blubber, and watch the flame blaze three feet in the air; but as soon as the new sea-ice bore, Kotuko and the girl loaded the hand-sleigh, and made the two dogs pull as they had never pulled in their lives, for they feared what might have happened in their village. The weather was as pitiless as usual; but it is easier to draw a sleigh loaded with good food than to hunt starving. They left five-and-twenty seal carcasses buried in the ice of the beach, all ready for use, and hurried back to their people. The dogs showed them the way as soon as Kotuko told them what was expected, and though there was no sign of a landmark, in two days they were giving tongue outside Kadlu’s house. Only three dogs answered them; the others had been eaten, and the houses were all dark. But when Kotuko shouted, “Ojo!” (boiled meat), weak voices replied, and when he called the muster of the village name by name, very distinctly, there were no gaps in it.
原译: 很高兴再次吃海豹，鲁莽地把灯装满了鲸脂，看着火焰在空中点燃三英尺；但当新海冰吹过，科图科和女孩就装上雪橇。天气和往常一样冷酷无情；但是，抽一只装满好食物的雪橇比打猎更容易。他们留下五块二十块海豹尸体埋在海边的冰里都准备就绪供使用。当科图科告诉他们什么是预期的，虽然没有标志的迹象，但两天后，他们就在Kadlu家外用舌头向他们展示了道路。只有三只狗回答他们，其他的被吃掉，房屋一片漆黑。当科图科喊道：“Ojo！”时，声音很弱，当他叫起村庄的名称时，非常明显地，它没有空隙。
现译: 再吃到海豹肝，多好啊。毫不心疼地把灯添满油，看着火苗蹿起三英尺高，那又多好。可是新冻的海冰一承得住重量，科图科和女孩便把手橇装上货，让两条狗使出生平没有使过的力气往回拉。他们害怕村子里已经出了什么事。天候同往日一般无情，不过拉着满载好吃的雪橇，比饿着去找猎物容易得多。他们留下二十五头猎好的海豹埋在滩冰中，随时可取，赶着回族人那儿去。狗一懂得科图科要它们做什么，便认准方向。一路不见半个路标，两天以后，它们已在卡德卢门外放声吠叫。回应它们的只剩三条狗，其余的都给吃了。屋子间间漆黑。然而科图科一喊“奥约！”——白煮肉！——便响起了虚弱的应声。当他清清楚楚把全村人的名字一一点到，一个也没缺。

中文章名: 奎奎恩

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: Amoraq jumped from the bench where she sat, and began to sweep things into the girl’s lap--stone lamps, iron skin-scrapers, tin kettles, deer-skins embroidered with musk-ox teeth, and real canvas-needles such as sailors use--the finest dowry that has ever been given on the far edge of the Arctic Circle, and the girl from the North bowed her head down to the very floor.

中文章名: 奎奎恩

原译: “啊，”说安格科克，与一个重要的咳嗽，似乎他一直在想这一切。科图科离开村子后，我就去了Singing-House 唱了魔术，我唱了很久并呼唤驯鹿的精神。我的歌声使大风吹过冰，把两只狗拉到科图科，冰就会粉碎他的骨头。我的歌声把海豹拉到破碎的冰后面。我的身体仍然躺在石灰里，但我的精神却在冰上奔跑。并引导科图科和狗们做他们所做的一切，我做到了。”

中文章名: 奎奎恩
英文证据: Now Kotuko, who drew very well in the Inuit fashion, scratched pictures of all these adventures on a long, flat piece of ivory with a hole at one end. For the rush through the mist, and the quarry blind-started!
For the cry of our mates when the sambhur has wheeled and is
standing at bay,
For the risk and the riot of night!
For the sleep at the lair-mouth by day,
It is met, and we go to the fight.
Bay! O Bay!
原译:
为了我们的白色和美妙的夜晚..。 为我们的夜晚
快速运行。
开阔的距离，远处看，良好的狩猎，确实狡猾！
因为黎明的气味，没有污秽的，露珠已经离开！
急于穿过雾，采石场开始盲目！
当桑伯尔人转身时我们的伴侣们的哀号
站在海湾，
为了风险和夜间的暴动！
白天在巢穴里睡觉
我们相遇了，我们去打仗。
湾！
现译:
为咱们皎白、快意的长夜，为疾奔的那些夜晚！
为巡游称心，为目光远，为狩猎顺遂、机谋不爽！
为露水未干、干净如初的黎明气息！
为冲过雾，为猎物惊起、盲目奔逸！
为水鹿回身负隅之时，伙伴们的呼喊，
为长夜的险与欢！
为白天窝口一场好睡，
应战了，咱们奔赴战场。
嗥吧！嗥吧！

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: It was after the letting in of the Jungle that the pleasantest part of Mowgli’s life began. He had the good conscience that comes from paying debts; all the Jungle was his friend, and just a little afraid of him. The things that he did and saw and heard when he was wandering from one people to another, with or without his four companions, would make many many stories, each as long as this one. So you will never be told how he met the Mad Elephant of Mandla, who killed two-and-twenty bullocks drawing eleven carts of coined silver to the Government Treasury, and scattered the shiny rupees in the dust; how he fought Jacala, the Crocodile, all one long night in the Marshes of the North, and broke his skinning-knife on the brute’s back-plates; how he found a new and longer knife round the neck of a man who had been killed by a wild boar, and how he tracked that boar and killed him as a fair price for the knife; how he was caught up once in the Great Famine, by the moving of the deer, and nearly crushed to death in the swaying hot herds; how he saved Hathi the Silent from being once more trapped in a pit with a stake at the bottom, and how, next day, he himself fell into a very cunning leopard-trap, and how Hathi broke the thick wooden bars to pieces above him; how he milked the wild buffaloes in the swamp, and how----
原译: 毛格利生命中最愉快的部分开始于丛林中。他有良好的良心，来自偿还债务；所有的丛林都是他的朋友，只是有点害怕他。无论他有没有四个同伴，他所做的事和所看到的和听到的都会做很多故事，每个故事都和这个故事一样长。所以，你永远也不会被告知他如何遇见曼德拉的疯象他杀了两二十只公牛给政府财政部画了11辆银车将闪亮的卢比撒在尘里并打破了他的皮刀在野兽的后盘上；他如何发现新的和更长的刀脖子上一个人被野猪杀死，他如何跟踪那头野猪几乎被压死在摇晃的热群中；他如何拯救哈蒂沉默者不再被困在一个坑与木桩在底部，第二天，他自己如何跌入一个非常狡猾的豹陷阱，和如何 - - - - -
现译: 让丛林进了村子以后，毛格利一生中最快活的时光才开始。欠账都还清了，心中坦然。全丛林跟他是朋友，也都有那么一点怕他。他在各族之间往来，有时领着四个伙伴，有时独行，所做、所见、所闻，能写成许多许多故事，每一个都跟眼前这个一样长。所以呀，你永远听不到他怎样遇上曼德拉那头疯象。那象杀了二十二头拉车的公牛，它们拖着十一辆要送进政府金库的银币车，亮晶晶的卢比撒了一地。你也听不到他如何在北方沼泽与鳄鱼贾卡拉斗了整整一长夜，剥皮刀折在那家伙的背甲上。后来他在一个被野猪拱死的人颈间找到一把更长的新刀，又怎样追上那头猪，杀猪抵偿这把刀的公道价钱。有一回大饥荒，鹿群移动，他怎样被卷进摇晃滚烫的兽群，几乎给挤死。他如何把沉默的哈蒂救下来，免得大象再次落进底下带尖桩的陷阱。第二天自己却落入一个精巧无比的捕豹套，哈蒂又如何把他上方的粗木栏一根根捣碎。他怎样在沼泽里挤野水牛的奶，又怎样——

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: But we must tell one tale at a time. Father and Mother Wolf died, and Mowgli rolled a big boulder against the mouth of their cave, and cried the Death Song over them; Baloo grew very old and stiff, and even Bagheera, whose nerves were steel and whose muscles were iron, was a shade slower on the kill than he had been. Akela turned from gray to milky white with pure age; his ribs stuck out, and he walked as though he had been made of wood, and Mowgli killed for him. But the young wolves, the children of the disbanded Seeonee Pack, throve and increased, and when there were about forty of them, masterless, full-voiced, clean-footed five-year-olds, Akela told them that they ought to gather themselves together and follow the Law, and run under one head, as befitted the Free People.
原译: 但是我们必须一次讲一个故事。父亲和母亲沃尔夫死了，毛格利把一块大石头翻到洞穴的嘴边，喊着死亡之歌，巴鲁人变得非常老了，僵硬，甚至巴希拉人的神经是钢铁，肌肉是铁铁的，他们的杀戮的阴影比他更慢。阿克拉从灰色变为纯年白种的乳白色；他的肋骨卡住了，他走路好像是木做的，毛格利为他而死。但是年轻的狼群，被解散的西奥尼包的孩子们却在节奏和增加当他们中有大约40个无主的满口胡言满足的五岁小孩时 Akera告诉他们他们应该聚集起来遵守法律。
现译: 不过，故事得一回讲一个。狼爸爸和狼妈妈都死了。毛格利滚了块巨石来封住洞口，为他们唱起送死者的歌。巴鲁老得身子僵了，就连筋似钢、肉似铁的巴希拉，扑杀时也比从前稍稍迟了一点。阿克拉年岁太长，一身灰毛变成乳白，肋条一根根高耸，走路像个木头拼的架子。毛格利替他捕猎。至于那些年幼的狼，当年解散的西奥尼狼群的后代，却越长越兴旺。等到一群五岁上下、嗓门洪亮、双足利落的狼有了四十来个，还没有首领，阿克拉告诉他们，该聚在一块，遵从法则，跟着一个首领去跑，这才合乎自由之民的身份。

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: This was not a question in which Mowgli concerned himself, for, as he said, he had eaten sour fruit, and he knew the tree it hung from; but when Phao, son of Phaona (his father was the Gray Tracker in the days of Akela’s headship), fought his way to the leadership of the Pack, according to the Jungle Law, and the old calls and songs began to ring under the stars once more, Mowgli came to the Council Rock for memory’s sake. When he chose to speak the Pack waited till he had finished, and he sat at Akela’s side on the rock above Phao. Those were days of good hunting and good sleeping. No stranger cared to break into the jungles that belonged to Mowgli’s people, as they called the Pack, and the young wolves grew fat and strong, and there were many cubs to bring to the Looking-over. Mowgli always attended a Looking-over, remembering the night when a black panther bought a naked brown baby into the pack, and the long call, “Look, look well, O Wolves,” made his heart flutter. Otherwise, he would be far away in the Jungle with his four brothers, tasting, touching, seeing, and feeling new things.
原译: 这不是毛格利关心自己的问题，因为正如他说的，他吃过酸果子，他知道那棵树上挂着的树；但是，当Phaona的儿子法奥(他父亲是阿克拉当年的首领时)，根据《丛林法》，他向全党领导人战斗时，旧的歌声再次响起毛格利来到了摇滚议会以纪念它。当他选择说包直到他完成，他坐在阿克拉的一侧在法奥的岩石上。那些日子是好狩猎好睡觉好日子。没有一个陌生人愿意闯进毛格利的人的丛林，他们称之为包，年轻的狼体变胖和强壮。毛格利总是参加一个“寻找”活动记得那晚黑豹在包里买了个裸体棕色宝宝长喊“看好看啊狼人” 使他的心跳加速。否则，他将远在丛林里和他的四个兄弟，尝尝、摸摸、看到和感觉新事物。
现译: 毛格利不愿插手这件事，照他的话说，自己吃过酸果，也认得挂酸果子的树。可等法奥，法奥纳的儿子，依丛林法则凭战斗取得首领地位，熟悉的呼唤和歌声再次响在星空下，他为怀念旧日，还是到了议事岩。法奥的父亲，就是阿克拉当首领时那位灰毛追踪手。毛格利想开口的时候，全群等他讲完。他坐在岩上阿克拉身旁，比法奥还高。那些日子，打猎打得好，睡也睡得好。外来的动物没有谁爱闯进“毛格利族人”的丛林，他们如今这样称呼狼群。年轻的狼越长越壮、越长越肥，有许多幼崽带到认崽会上亮相。每逢认崽会，毛格利必到。他记得，黑豹曾付出代价，让一个褐色的光身娃娃加入狼群。那一声长喊“看仔细了，看仔细了，狼们啊！”一响，他的心还会怦怦跳。不在议事岩的时候，他便同四个兄弟去遥远的林中，尝新鲜东西，摸新鲜东西，看新鲜东西，感觉新鲜东西。

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: One twilight when he was trotting leisurely across the ranges to give Akela the half of a buck that he had killed, while the Four jogged behind him, sparring a little, and tumbling one another over for joy of being alive, he heard a cry that had never been heard since the bad days of Shere Khan. It was what they call in the Jungle the pheeal, a hideous kind of shriek that the jackal gives when he is hunting behind a tiger, or when there is a big killing afoot. If you can imagine a mixture of hate, triumph, fear, and despair, with a kind of leer running through it, you will get some notion of the pheeal that rose and sank and wavered and quavered far away across the Waingunga. The Four stopped at once, bristling and growling. Mowgli’s hand went to his knife, and he checked, the blood in his face, his eyebrows knotted.
原译: 一次微弱的瞬间，他横跨山脉，向Akera赠送他所杀的那半块钱，而四人则在他身后慢跑，挥舞一小步，互相摇晃，以换取活着的喜悦，他听到一声自谢尔汗的不幸时代以来从未听到的呼声。这就是他们在丛林里叫的蜂鸣声，一种可怕的尖叫，胡狼给予当他打猎老虎，或有一个大屠宰脚。如果你能想象出仇恨、胜利、恐惧和绝望的混合体，带着一种灵精，穿过它，你就会得到一些概念那种花朵，升起，沉睡，摇晃，震动，震动，远离瓦因贡加河。四个人立刻停下来哭叫叫着。毛格利的手伸到刀上，他检查，血在他的脸上，他的眉毛结。
现译: 一个黄昏，他不慌不忙小跑过山岭，去给阿克拉送自己猎的半头公鹿。四个兄弟在后面颠着步子，一路小打小闹，互相掀个跟头，只为活着高兴。忽然，他听见一声惨叫。自从谢尔汗作恶的年头过去，这声音再没响过。丛林管它叫“菲哀声”，是胡狼在老虎屁股后面跟着觅食，或有什么大屠杀要发生时，发出的一种怕人的尖叫。你要能把仇恨、得意、恐惧、绝望揉成一团，里面再穿上一丝阴笑，多少就明白了瓦因贡加河远远那头的菲哀声怎样起落、摇晃、发颤。四匹狼立刻站住，竖毛低吼。毛格利的手伸向刀柄。他也刹住了步子，面孔充血，眉头紧锁。

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: It broke out again, half sobbing and half chuckling, just as though the jackal had soft human lips. 中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: They could hear nothing except the Waingunga rushing and gurgling in the dark, and the light evening winds among the tree-tops, till suddenly across the river a wolf called. It was no wolf of the Pack, for they were all at the Rock. The note changed to a long, despairing bay; and “Dhole!” it said, “Dhole! dhole! dhole!” They heard tired feet on the rocks, and a gaunt wolf, streaked with red on his flanks, his right fore-paw useless, and his jaws white with foam, flung himself into the circle and lay gasping at Mowgli’s feet.

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: “Good hunting! Won-tolla am I,” was the answer. He meant that he was a solitary wolf, fending for himself, his mate, and his cubs in some lonely lair, as do many wolves in the south. Won-tolla means an Outlier--one who lies out from any Pack. Then he panted, and they could see his heart-beats shake him backward and forward.

中文章名: 红狗

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: “The dhole, the dhole of the Dekkan--Red Dog, the Killer! They came north from the south saying the Dekkan was empty and killing out by the way. When this moon was new there were four to me--my mate and three cubs. She would teach them to kill on the grass plains, hiding to drive the buck, as we do who are of the open. 中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: The split and weatherworn rocks of the gorge of the Waingunga had been used since the beginning of the Jungle by the Little People of the Rocks--the busy, furious, black wild bees of India; and, as Mowgli knew well, all trails turned off half a mile before they reached the gorge. For centuries the Little People had hived and swarmed from cleft to cleft, and swarmed again, staining the white marble with stale honey, and made their combs tall and deep in the dark of the inner caves, where neither man nor beast nor fire nor water had ever touched them. The length of the gorge on both siaes was hung as it were with black shimmery velvet curtains, and Mowgli sank as he looked, for those were the clotted millions of the sleeping bees. There were other lumps and festoons and things like decayed tree-trunks studded on the face of the rock, the old combs of past years, or new cities built in the shadow of the windless gorge, and huge masses of spongy, rotten trash had rolled down and stuck among the trees and creepers that clung to the rock-face. As he listened he heard more than once the rustle and slide of a honey-loaded comb turning over or failing away somewhere in the dark galleries; then a booming of angry wings, and the sullen drip, drip, drip, of the wasted honey, guttering along till it lipped over some ledge in the open air and sluggishly trickled down on the twigs. There was a tiny little beach, not five feet broad, on one side of the river, and that was piled high with the rubbish of uncounted years. There were dead bees, drones, sweepings, and stale combs, and wings of marauding moths that had strayed in after honey, all tumbled in smooth piles of the finest black dust. The mere sharp smell of it was enough to frighten anything that had no wings, and knew what the Little People were.
原译: 华贡加峡谷的碎石和结冰石从一开始就被岩礁小矮人使用过印度的繁忙、愤怒、黑野蜜蜂。几个世纪以来，小人们一直从裂缝到裂缝之间蜂拥而至，再次摇动，用陈旧的蜂蜜染上白大理石，在深洞的黑暗中把梳子高高高高高地竖起，在那里，人、兽、火、水都没有触碰过他们。两个岛的峡谷长着黑闪闪闪的天鹅绒窗帘和毛格利在寻找时沉没了因为那些是数以百万计的沉睡蜜蜂。还有其他的块状块和骨架，以及一些东西，比如腐烂的树枝在岩石的脸上，过去的旧梳子，或者在无风峡谷的阴影下建造的新城市，以及大量的海绵，腐烂的垃圾滚落下来，并被困在与岩石面交织的树木和爬行者之中。当他听到不止一次听到蜂蜜梳子翻转或掉落在黑暗的画廊中时，他听到的就是蜂蜜梳子的生锈和滑动；然后，愤怒的翅膀和枯萎的蜂蜜的滴水、滴水、滴水、流水，都发抖，直到它从露天的冰盖上掉下来，慢慢地滑到树枝上。在河的一边有个小海滩，不是五英尺宽的，上面堆积着数不清的岁月的垃圾。蜜蜂死亡无人机扫荡腐烂的梳子以及蜂蜜之后漂流的飞蛾翅膀都沉入了最优的黑尘中。光是尖锐的气味就足以吓唬任何没有翅膀的人并且知道小人是什么。
现译: 打丛林诞生起，瓦因贡加河峡谷间这些裂开、风化的岩石就归岩石的小民住，就是印度那些忙碌、暴烈的黑野蜂。毛格利很清楚，所有兽道在离峡谷还有半英里的地方就已拐开。几百年来，蜂群在一处岩缝筑巢，分群，迁去另一处，再分群，陈蜜把白大理石浸出了斑。里面无光的洞穴里，一层层的蜂房又高又深，没人，没兽，没有火，也没有水曾经触及。两边的整段峡壁都像垂着微微闪光的黑绒帘。毛格利一面望，一面把身子往水下沉。那是数百万只野蜂团团挤着睡觉。崖面还嵌着一坨坨、一串串的东西，有的像烂树干，是过去许多年的旧蜂房，或是生在避风的谷影里的一座座新城。大堆海绵般松朽的废物滚下来，卡在攀附石壁的树木和藤蔓之间。他竖耳细听，不止一次听见黑暗的洞廊深处，有哪一片盛满蜜的蜂房翻身或掉落，发出沙沙滑动的声音。接着，是怒翅的轰响，是白白淌走的蜜汁闷闷地滴，滴，滴，汇成小沟，溢过某一块露天的石沿，再慢吞吞淌到细枝上。河的一侧有条不足五英尺宽的小滩，堆高了不可计数的岁月攒下的废物。死蜂、雄蜂、扫出窝的碎屑、陈蜂房，还有误闯进去偷蜜的飞蛾的翅膀，全层层倒下，积成极细的黑尘，表面光滑。只这一股刺鼻的味道，就足以吓走一切不长翅膀、又知道小民厉害的动物。

中文章名: 红狗

中文章名: 红狗

From the last tree to the low scrub of the Bee Rocks was open country, where there was hardly cover enough to hide a wolf. Mowgli trotted along under the trees, judging distances between branch and branch, occasionally climbing up a trunk and taking a trial leap from one tree to another till he came to the open ground, which he studied very carefully for an hour. Then he turned, picked up Won-tolla’s trail where he had left it, settled himself in a tree with an outrunning branch some eight feet from the ground, and sat still, sharpening his knife on the sole of his foot and singing to himself.
原译: 原图拉的足迹全都是黑血点被一棵厚厚的树所包围向东北伸展。从最后一棵树到低层的蜜蜂岩石都开阔了，那里几乎没有遮蔽来隐藏一只狼。毛格利在树下走来走去判断树枝和树枝之间的距离偶尔爬上树干尝试从一棵树跳到另一棵树直到他来到露天的地上。然后他转过身，捡起元图拉留下的踪迹，安顿在树上，离地约8英尺处的树枝旁，坐着不动，将刀子磨在脚底，唱歌给自己听。

The dholes are a very silent people as a rule, and they have no manners even in their own Jungle. Fully two hundred must have gathered below him, but he could see that the leaders sniffed hungrily on Won-tolla’s trail, and tried to drag the Pack forward. That would never do, or they would be at the Lairs in broad daylight, and Mowgli meant to hold them under his tree till dusk.
原译: 野蛮人抬头看，他的同伴在后面停下来成百上千的红狗尾巴低，肩膀重，身体虚弱，嘴唇血腥。水坑是一个非常沉默的人，作为一个规则，他们没有礼貌，即使是在自己的丛林。整整200人聚集在他下面但他可以看到头目们在元图拉的踪迹上嗅到了烟雾。那样是绝对不行的，或者他们白天在莱尔家，毛格利打算把他们放在树下直到黄昏。
现译: 那野兽抬头，伙伴们纷纷在后面停住。红狗一群接一群，低垂的尾巴，沉重的肩，单薄的后身，血淋淋的嘴。豺族平时很沉默，哪怕在自家丛林里也不懂一点礼貌。树下少说已聚了整整两百只，可毛格利看得见领头的几位还饥饿地嗅着离群狼的足迹，想把整群再往前带。那可不行。不然，它们大白天就会到狼窝。毛格利存心留它们在树下直等黄昏。

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: “All Jungles are our Jungle,” was the reply, and the dhole that gave it bared his white teeth. Mowgli looked down with a smile, and imitated perfectly the sharp chitter-chatter of Chikai, the leaping rat of the Dekkan, meaning the dholes to understand that he considered them no better than Chikai. The Pack closed up round the tree-trunk and the leader bayed savagely, calling Mowgli a tree-ape. For an answer Mowgli stretched down one naked leg and wriggled his bare toes just above the leader’s head. That was enough, and more than enough, to wake the Pack to stupid rage. Those who have hair between their toes do not care to be reminded of it. Mowgli caught his foot away as the leader leaped up, and said sweetly: “Dog, red dog! Go back to the Dekkan and eat lizards. Go to Chikai thy brother--dog, dog--red, red dog! There is hair between every toe!” He twiddled his toes a second time.
原译: “所有的丛林都是我们的”是答案，和洞给它擦白了他的白牙。毛格利笑着看模仿了奇凯的尖利小舌头德卡恩河的飞鼠意思是洞穴能明白他认为它们比奇卡伊好不到哪去。包包把树枝围起来头领野蛮地把毛格利称为树猿。为了回答一个问题毛格利把一条赤脚伸下来扭动他的赤脚脚趾正好在领袖头上。足够了足够了足以唤醒那帮人发疯。那些脚趾之间有毛的人并不想被提醒。毛格利的脚在领袖跳跃时伸出来，他甜美地说：红狗狗啊！你回去吃蜥蜴吧！你的兄弟、红狗、红狗，到奇凯去吧！每只脚趾之间，都有毛！他第二次乱动脚趾。
现译: “凡是丛林，都是我们的丛林。”作答的豺龇出了白牙。毛格利低头一笑，惟妙惟肖地学起德干小跳鼠奇凯尖细的吱喳声，好让它们听明白，在他眼里，豺跟那小耗子一个身价。豺群朝树身围紧，领头的凶狠地吠叫，骂毛格利是个树猿。毛格利垂下一条光腿作答，赤脚趾头就在领头狗头顶扭来扭去。这已足够，远不止足够，把全群气得发蠢。趾缝间长毛的家伙，可不爱旁人提起这件事。领头狗跃起时，毛格利脚一收，甜甜地说：“狗呀，红狗！滚回德干吃蜥蜴吧。找你兄弟奇凯去。狗，狗，红的，红狗！每个脚趾缝都长着毛！”又把脚趾转了一遍。

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: “Come down ere we starve thee out, hairless ape!” yelled the Pack, and this was exactly what Mowgli wanted. He laid himself down along the branch, his cheek to the bark, his right arm free, and there he told the Pack what he thought and knew about them, their manners, their customs, their mates, and their puppies. There is no speech in the world so rancorous and so stinging as the language the Jungle People use to show scorn and contempt. When you come to think of it you will see how this must be so. As Mowgli told Kaa, he had many little thorns under his tongue, and slowly and deliberately he drove the dholes from silence to growls, from growls to yells, and from yells to hoarse slavery ravings. They tried to answer his taunts, but a cub might as well have tried to answer Kaa in a rage; and all the while Mowgli’s right hand lay crooked at his side, ready for action, his feet locked round the branch. The big bay leader had leaped many times in the air, but Mowgli dared not risk a false blow. At last, made furious beyond his natural strength, he bounded up seven or eight feet clear of the ground. Then Mowgli’s hand shot out like the head of a tree-snake, and gripped him by the scruff of his neck, and the branch shook with the jar as his weight fell back, almost wrenching Mowgli to the ground. But he never loosed his grip, and inch by inch he hauled the beast, hanging like a drowned jackal, up on the branch. With his left hand he reached for his knife and cut off the red, bushy tail, flinging the dhole back to earth again. That was all he needed. The Pack would not go forward on Won-tolla’s trail now till they had killed Mowgli or Mowgli had killed them. He saw them settle down in circles with a quiver of the haunches that meant they were going to stay, and so he climbed to a higher crotch, settled his back comfortably, and went to sleep.
原译: “在我们饿死你之前快下来吧，无毛的猩猩！” 大叫着包，这就是毛格利想要的。他躺在树枝边，脸朝树皮，右臂自由，在那里，他告诉了包包，他所想和了解他们，他们的举止，他们的习俗，他们的伴侣，以及他们的小狗。世界上没有比丛林人民用来表达鄙视和鄙视的语言更令人发指的演讲了。当你想到它的时候，你会明白这一定是。正如毛格利告诉卡亚的那样，他舌下有许多小刺，他缓慢和蓄意地把洞从沉默赶到咆哮，从咆哮到叫喊，从喊叫到粗鲁的奴役狂怒。他们试图回答他的嘲讽，但幼崽可能也试图回答卡亚愤怒；和所有当毛格利的右手弯曲在他的身边，准备行动，他的脚锁在树枝上。大海湾头目多次飞过空中但毛格利不敢冒一个错误的打击。他终于超越了自然力量将七八英尺的距离连在一起。然后毛格利的手像砍树头一样被射杀，被他的脖子的绞痕抓住，树枝被罐子震动，他的体重倒了，几乎把毛格利扳倒在地上。但他从不松手，一寸一寸地拖着野兽吊着像淹死的胡狼，吊在树枝上。他用左手伸手拿起刀，砍掉红色的、粗糙的尾巴，又把水坑扔回地上。这就是他所需要的。直到他们杀了毛格利或者毛格利杀了他们。他看见他们与一阵阵阵阵阵阵的怒吼一起在圈子里安顿下来意味着他们要留下来于是他爬到高处舒适地安稳地安稳地躺着睡着。
现译: “下来！没毛的猿猴！不然我们在这里等着饿死你！”豺群喊。这正是毛格利要的。他沿枝干趴好，脸颊贴树皮，右臂留出来，给豺群讲了一通他对它们、它们的礼数、习性、母狗和幼崽的所思所知。丛林之民用来蔑视、羞辱别人的话，世上再没有更狠毒、更扎人的。你仔细一想，自然就懂得为什么。正如毛格利告诉卡阿，他舌底藏着许多小刺。他不慌不忙，一根根扎，把豺群从默不作声逼到低吼，再从低吼逼到叫喊，从叫喊逼到哑着喉咙淌着涎水乱吠一气。它们想还嘴，可那跟小狼崽向动了怒的卡阿还嘴一样徒劳。毛格利的右手始终弯在身侧，准备出动，两脚牢牢勾住树枝。红褐色头犬跳起已有多次，毛格利却不敢出手落空。终于，它怒到了超过天生的力气，身子整个拔高，跳离地面足有七八英尺。毛格利的手像树蛇的脑袋飞出，一把攥住它后颈的皮。它的分量往下一坠，震得树枝一晃，差点把毛格利扯下去。但他的手指一点未松，竟一寸一寸把那家伙拖上枝来，它挂在那里像只淹死的胡狼。毛格利左手抽刀，割掉那条红蓬蓬的大尾巴，把它丢回地上。他要的已经到手。现在不杀了毛格利，或者不让毛格利杀掉，这群豺再也不会沿着离群狼的血迹往前走。他见它们排成圈坐下，后腿肌肉一抖摆定，知道它们准备久守，就爬到更高的枝杈，找个舒服的地方把背靠好，睡了起来。

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: After three or four hours he waked and counted the Pack. They were all there, silent, husky, and dry, with eyes of steel. The sun was beginning to sink. In half an hour the Little People of the Rocks would be ending their labours, and, as you know, the dhole does not fight best in the twilight.
原译: 三四个小时后，他醒来数了包。他们都在那里，沉默，霍斯基，和干，眼睛是钢铁。太阳开始下沉了。半个小时后，小岩石的人将结束他们的劳动，和，如你所知，水坑不是最好的战斗在黄昏。

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: “I did not need such faithful watchers,” he said politely, standing up on a branch, “but I will remember this. Ye be true dholes, but to my thinking over much of one kind. For that reason I do not give the big lizard-eater his tail again. Art thou not pleased, Red Dog?”
原译: 他说：我的确不需要这种忠实的观察者，我的确要站在树枝上，但我的确要记住。你们确是一个洞，但我只凭一种思维，我不把尾巴给那只大蜥蜴。你不高兴吗，红狗？
现译: “我倒用不着这样忠心的守卫，”他立在树枝上，客客气气地说，“不过我会记着这份情。你们都是真豺，只不过在我看来，未免都长得太像。所以那位吃大蜥蜴的，我就不把尾巴还给它了。红狗，你高兴吧？”

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: “Nay, but consider, wise rat of the Dekkan. There will now be many litters of little tailless red dogs, yea, with raw red stumps that sting when the sand is hot. Go home, Red Dog, and cry that an ape has done this. Ye will not go? Come, then, with me, and I will make you very wise!”
原译: 不然！你们想一想德卡恩的聪明老鼠吧！现在有许多无尾小红狗的垃圾，当沙子热的时候，他们生来就吃红树桩，你们回家去吧，红狗，你们为一只猩猩做这件事而哭泣吧。你们不走吗？你们跟我走吧，我将使你们聪明！

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: He moved, Bandar-log fashion, into the next tree, and so on into the next and the next, the Pack following with lifted hungry heads. Now and then he would pretend to fall, and the Pack would tumble one over the other in their haste to be at the death. It was a curious sight--the boy with the knife that shone in the low sunlight as it sifted through the upper branches, and the silent Pack with their red coats all aflame, huddling and following below. When he came to the last tree he took the garlic and rubbed himself all over carefully, and the dholes yelled with scorn. “Ape with a wolf’s tongue, dost thou think to cover thy scent?” they said. “We follow to the death.”
原译: 他移动，班达罗时尚，进入下一棵树，等到下一棵树，包装后举起饥饿的头。之后他假装摔倒包裹会匆匆忙忙忙地倒在另一个上面。令人好奇的是拿着刀子的男孩在低光下射穿了树枝静默的包装着红大衣。当他来到最后一棵树，他拿大蒜和擦擦自己仔细，和洞大声的嘲讽。“用狼舌头的猩猩，你认为可以遮住你的气味吗？” 他们说。“我们跟随死亡。”
现译: 他学猴民的样子过到邻树，再过一棵，又一棵。豺群仰着饥饿的脑袋一路追。他不时假装要掉下去，豺群争抢着赶去看他死，自己互相绊翻。倒是幅奇景：斜阳从高枝间筛过，男孩手里的刀一闪一闪。下方，沉默的豺群一身红毛全似火烧，挤成一团尾随。走到最后一棵树，他拿出野蒜，仔细擦遍全身。豺群轻蔑地叫起：“长狼舌头的猿猴，你还想盖住你的气味吗？我们一路追到死。”

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: They gave one deep howl, and settled down to the long, lobbing canter that can at the last run down anything that runs. Mowgli knew their pack-pace to be much slower than that of the wolves, or he would never have risked a two-mile run in full sight. They were sure that the boy was theirs at last, and he was sure that he held them to play with as he pleased. All his trouble was to keep them sufficiently hot behind him to prevent their turning off too soon. He ran cleanly, evenly, and springily; the tailless leader not five yards behind him; and the Pack tailing out over perhaps a quarter of a mile of ground, crazy and blind with the rage of slaughter. So he kept his distance by ear, reserving his last effort for the rush across the Bee Rocks.
原译: 他们打了一声深嚎沉浸在漫漫长夜挥舞着拐杖最终可以击落任何运行的物体。毛格利知道他们的背包速度比狼慢得多，否则他绝不会冒着两英里的险跑在全天候。他们确信这孩子最终是他们的了他确信他能随心所欲地带着他们玩耍。他所有的烦恼是让他们有足够的热身在他身后防止他们关闭太快。他跑得干净、平和、温和；没有尾巴的领导人离他不到五码；背包在四分之一英里长的地上尾行，疯狂和盲目地狂暴地屠杀。所以他保持了距离保留了最后的精力穿过蜜蜂摇滚。
现译: 它们发出一声深嗥，跑成那种长距离颠扑的慢跑。凡是会跑的东西，经它们这么个跑法，到末了都能赶上。毛格利知道，豺群集体行进比狼群慢得多，否则他不敢冒险在众目睽睽下跑这两英里。它们认定男孩已落到自己手里，他也认定它们任自己摆弄。他唯一的难处，是要叫身后那些追兵足够热切，才不会过早拐开。他的脚步干净，均匀，起落有弹性。断尾头犬就在五码不到的身后，豺群则拖成长约四分之一英里的队伍，个个杀红了眼，疯狂而盲目。他只用耳朵掌握距离，留着最后一口力气，好冲过蜂岩。

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: The Little People had gone to sleep in the early twilight, for it was not the season of late blossoming flowers; but as Mowgli’s first foot-falls rang hollow on the hollow ground he heard a sound as though all the earth were humming. Then he ran as he had never run in his life before, spurned aside one--two--three of the piles of stones into the dark, sweet-smelling gullies; heard a roar like the roar of the sea in a cave; saw with the tail of his eye the air grow dark behind him; saw the current of the Waingunga far below, and a flat, diamond-shaped head in the water; leaped outward with all his strength, the tailless dhole snapping at his shoulder in mid-air, and dropped feet first to the safety of the river, breathless and triumphant. There was not a sting upon him, for the smell of the garlic had checked the Little People for just the few seconds that he was among them. When he rose Kaa’s coils were steadying him and things were bounding over the edge of the cliff--great lumps, it seemed, of clustered bees falling like plummets; but before any lump touched water the bees flew upward and the body of a dhole whirled down-stream. Overhead they could hear furious short yells that were drowned in a roar like breakers--the roar of the wings of the Little People of the Rocks. Some of the dholes, too, had fallen into the gullies that communicated with the underground caves, and there choked and fought and snapped among the tumbled honeycombs, and at last, borne up, even when they were dead, on the heaving waves of bees beneath them, shot out of some hole in the river-face, to roll over on the black rubbish-heaps. There were dholes who had leaped short into the trees on the cliffs, and the bees blotted out their shapes; but the greater number of them, maddened by the stings, had flung themselves into the river; and, as Kaa said, the Waingunga was hungry water.
原译: 幼虫们在黎明时睡了觉，因为这不是晚开花的季节；但是当毛格利第一次脚踏地时，他听到一个声音，仿佛整个地球都在哼着。他奔跑，前世从未跑过，他把一堆石头扔到黑暗的、甜美的海沟里，听到山洞里大吼大叫，他的眼睛尾巴中，空气在黑暗中增长；他看见下面的瓦因贡加河河水流，和平坦的，钻石形的头在水中；跳出用他的所有力量，无尾孔在他的肩膀断裂在空中。他身上没有刺伤，因为大蒜的味道检查了小人仅仅几秒钟，他是他们中的。当他举起卡亚的圈子紧紧地固定着他东西被绑在悬崖的边缘巨大的肿块，它似乎，聚集的蜜蜂跌倒了。头顶上他们可以听到愤怒的短喊声被淹没在咆哮像断路器 - 咆哮的翅膀小岩石的人的翅膀。有些洞也掉进了与地下洞穴沟通的沟里，在那里，在倒塌的蜂窝中窒息、战斗和断裂，最终，即使他们死了，也在下面的蜂群堆积起来，从河面的一个洞里射出来，翻过黑垃圾堆。有些洞洞跳到悬崖上的树上，蜜蜂擦破了他们的形状；但更多的蜜蜂因刺痛而发疯，被扔进河里；而且，正如卡亚所说，瓦因贡加河人饿得要命。
现译: 黄昏初到，岩石的小民已经入睡，因为不是花朵迟开的季节。毛格利的头几个脚步在空空的地下甬洞上踏出空响，他就听得好像整个大地都在嗡嗡作声。于是他跑了起来，一生从没跑过那么快。他踢掉一堆，两堆，三堆石头，送它们落入黝黑、带甜味的深沟。听见一声吼，如海潮在洞穴中轰鸣。眼角瞥见背后天空变黑了，又看见远在下方流动的瓦因贡加河，看见水里一颗扁扁的菱形脑袋。他用尽全力飞身跃出，断尾豺紧随在半空中冲他肩头一咬。他双脚先入水，落入救命的河流，上气不接下气，大获全胜。身上没有一处蜇伤，原来就在他穿过蜂群的那短短几秒里，野蒜味使小民们略一迟疑。他浮上来，卡阿已用身子把他托稳。崖缘上一个个东西跳出来，大团密集的蜂，铅锤般坠下。每一团将要沾水时，蜂群却往上飞，一具豺尸便打着旋流下去。头上响着愤怒短促的惨叫，又让碎浪般的吼声淹没，那正是岩石小民翼下的吼声。也有些豺掉进和地下洞穴相通的深沟，在翻倒的蜂房之间窒息、挣扎、乱咬。最后，底下翻腾的蜂浪托着它们，即便已经死了，也还托着，从朝河开的某一个洞里喷出去，翻滚在黑色碎屑堆上。还有的豺没跳够远，掉在崖面的树上，蜂群把它们的形状全涂没了。然而大多数给蜇得发疯，一头扑进河里。正如卡阿所说，瓦因贡加河的水是饿的。

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: Nearly half the pack had seen the trap their fellows rushed into, and turning sharp aside had flung themselves into the water where the gorge broke down in steep banks. Their cries of rage and their threats against the “tree-ape” who had brought them to their shame mixed with the yells and growls of those who had been punished by the Little People. To remain ashore was death, and every dhole knew it. Their pack was swept along the current, down to the deep eddies of the Peace Pool, but even there the angry Little People followed and forced them to the water again. Mowgli could hear the voice of the tailless leader bidding his people hold on and kill out every wolf in Seeonee. But he did not waste his time in listening.
原译: 几乎一半的人群看到他们的人冲进的陷阱，他们把尖锐的一面扔进峡谷破碎在陡峭的岸边的水里。他们愤怒的呼喊和对“树猿”的威胁，他们使他们蒙羞，他们与那些被小人民惩罚的人的呼喊和咆哮混在一起。留在岸上是死亡每个洞都知道。他们的背包被水流冲到和平池深处，但即使在那里愤怒的小人们跟随并迫使他们再次到水里。毛格利可以听到无尾头领袖的呼声要求他的族人坚持并杀死西欧尼的狼。但是他没有浪费时间去听。

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: Then they saw their mistake. They should have landed half a mile higher up, and rushed the wolves on dry ground. Now it was too late. The bank was lined with burning eyes, and except for the horrible pheeal that had never stopped since sundown, there was no sound in the Jungle. It seemed as though Won-tolla were fawning on them to come ashore; and “Turn and take hold!” said the leader of the dholes. The entire Pack flung themselves at the shore, threshing and squattering through the shoal water, till the face of the Waingunga was all white and torn, and the great ripples went from side to side, like bow-waves from a boat. Mowgli followed the rush, stabbing and slicing as the dholes, huddled together, rushed up the river-beach in one wave.

中文章名: 红狗
英文证据: Then the long fight began, heaving and straining and splitting and scattering and narrowing and broadening along the red, wet sands, and over and between the tangled tree-roots, and through and among the bushes, and in and out of the grass clumps; for even now the dholes were two to one. But they met wolves fighting for all that made the Pack, and not only the short, high, deep-chested, white-tusked hunters of the Pack, but the anxious-eyed lahinis--the she-wolves of the lair, as the saying is--fighting for their litters, with here and there a yearling wolf, his first coat still half woolly, tugging and grappling by their sides. A wolf, you must know, flies at the throat or snaps at the flank, while a dhole, by preference, bites at the belly; so when the dholes were struggling out of the water and had to raise their heads, the odds were with the wolves. On dry land the wolves suffered; but in the water or ashore, Mowgli’s knife came and went without ceasing. The Four had worried their way to his side. Gray Brother, crouched between the boy’s knees, was protecting his stomach, while the others guarded his back and either side, or stood over him when the shock of a leaping, yelling dhole who had thrown himself full on the steady blade bore him down. For the rest, it was one tangled confusion--a locked and swaying mob that moved from right to left and from left to right along the bank; and also ground round and round slowly on its own centre. Here would be a heaving mound, like a water-blister in a whirlpool, which would break like a water-blister, and throw up four or five mangled dogs, each striving to get back to the centre; here would be a single wolf borne down by two or three dholes, laboriously dragging them forward, and sinking the while; here a yearling cub would be held up by the pressure round him, though he had been killed early, while his mother, crazed with dumb rage, rolled over and over, snapping, and passing on; and in the middle of the thickest press, perhaps, one wolf and one dhole, forgetting everything else, would be manoeuvring for first hold till they were whirled away by a rush of furious fighters. Once Mowgli passed Akela, a dhole on either flank, and his all but toothless jaws closed over the loins of a third; and once he saw Phao, his teeth set in the throat of a dhole, tugging the unwilling beast forward till the yearlings could finish him. But the bulk of the fight was blind flurry and smother in the dark; hit, trip, and tumble, yelp, groan, and worry-worry-worry, round him and behind him and above him. As the night wore on, the quick, giddy-go-round motion increased. The dholes were cowed and afraid to attack the stronger wolves, but did not yet dare to run away. Mowgli felt that the end was coming soon, and contented himself with striking merely to cripple. The yearlings were growing bolder; there was time now and again to breathe, and pass a word to a friend, and the mere flicker of the knife would sometimes turn a dog aside.
原译: 然后，漫长的战斗开始，堆积起来，散开，散开，缩小，扩大沿着红色，湿润的沙子，和和在缠绕的树根之间，和穿过和穿过灌木，和进出草堆；但他们遇到了那些为群体利益而战的狼——不仅仅是那短身、高胸、深胸、白牙的猎手，还有那眼神焦虑的母狼——正如人们所说，是巢穴中的母狼——它们也在为自己的幼崽而战，偶尔还能看到一只一岁左右的幼狼。他的第一身大衣仍然半毛不整，拉着他们的两侧，你必须知道，一只狼在喉咙上飞，或在侧翼上飞，而一个洞则偏爱咬肚子；所以当洞从水中冲出来，不得不抬起头来时，与狼的距离就大了。在干燥的土地上，狼遭受了痛苦；毛格利的刀来来来去去都不停了。他俩担心自己到他身边去。盖瑞兄弟跪在男孩的膝盖之间，保护他的胃，而其他人则保护他的背部和两侧，或在跳跃时站在他身上。大声喊叫的恶狗，将自己完全扑在稳定的刀刃上，导致他被击倒。其余的则是一团混乱——一群纠缠不清的人群，在岸上从右到左、从左到右移动；同时也在自身中心缓慢地旋转。这里将有一个山丘，就像一个水泡在水流中，它像水泡一样破裂，扔出四五只狗，每只狗都要努力赶回中心。 一只狼被两三个洞所淹没，辛苦地拖着它们前进，并沉没在水里；在这里，一个年幼的幼崽将被压住他身边的压力，尽管他早死了，而他的母亲疯狂愚蠢的愤怒，翻滚和翻转，崩溃和传递；将机动先行直到他们被暴躁的战斗机冲走。当毛格利穿过阿克拉时，他两侧都有一个洞，他的下巴除牙外，都关在第三个洞的腰上；他一看到法奥，牙齿就塞进一个洞的喉咙，拉着不情愿的野兽向前，直到长春树结束他。但这场战斗大部分是盲目而昏暗的；打、打、打、闹、呻吟、担心、担心、担心，围绕着他，绕在他身后和上方。随着夜晚的过去快速的旋转的动作增加了。水坑被吓坏了害怕攻击更强壮的狼，但还没有敢逃跑。毛格利觉得结局很快会结束并且满足于打击只是为了残废。年青越来越大胆；有时间时不时地呼吸，向朋友说几句话，刀子的闪烁有时会使狗置之不理。
现译: 漫长的一仗开始了。湿红的沙地上，纠结的树根上，树根间，灌木里外，草墩边缘，战团翻涌、绷紧、分裂、四散、收窄、拉宽，因为到了这时，豺的数目仍是狼的两倍。可是迎敌的狼在保卫使狼群之所以为狼群的一切。除了那些身短、腿高、胸深、牙白的猎手，还有眼里盛着忧虑的“拉希妮”，也就是守窝的母狼。她们为自己一窝幼崽战斗，偶尔身边还有一头周岁的狼，头一身毛还半是绒毛，也在牵扯、撕打。你得知道，狼或直扑喉咙，或向侧腹出牙。豺最爱咬的是肚皮。因此豺从水里挣扎出来，不得不抬起头的时候，狼就占着上风。一到干地，狼便吃亏。无论水里、岸上，毛格利的刀没有一刻不在来回。四个兄弟一口口咬开路来到他身边。灰兄弟蹲在男孩双膝之间，护他的腹部，其余三只守住后背和两侧。有时，一只厉叫的豺纵身直扑横持的刀刃，那冲势把毛格利撞倒，兄弟们就站到他身上方去。别的一切是一团分不清的乱战，一大堆锁在一起，摇摆着，沿岸从右到左，又从左到右，还绕着自身的中央慢慢研磨打转。这里隆起一座肉山，像漩涡中鼓出的水泡，又像水泡破裂，抛出四五条遍体鳞伤的狗，每一条还挣扎着要重回中央。那里一匹狼被两三头豺压住，一边往下陷，一边还费力拖着它们往前。这里有一头周岁幼狼，早就丢了命，身体却仍受四周挤压直立。他的母亲悲愤得一句叫不出，翻滚不停，咬过一口，又往前去。就在最拥挤的中央，也许还有一狼一豺把别的一切统统忘掉，专注地盘旋着争头一口，直到被一股狂怒的战士卷走。有一次毛格利经过阿克拉，两胁各咬着一只豺，那副几乎没牙的嘴却仍锁在第三只豺的腰上。有一次，他见法奥叼住一只豺的喉咙，硬拖着不情不愿的对手往前，好让周岁的幼狼结果它。但大半场战斗都是黑暗里的一团扑打和窒息。在他四周、身后、头顶，撞，绊，摔，尖叫，呻吟，又咬，又撕，又扯。夜越深，那种叫人晕眩的转圈越快。豺渐渐胆怯，不敢再冲强壮的狼出击，却还没有逃跑的胆子。毛格利感觉结局将近，这会儿出手，便只打到使其失去行动能力。周岁的狼愈来愈大胆。现在偶尔已能喘口气，跟朋友说句话，有时刀身仅仅一闪，就吓得一条狗闪开。

中文章名: 春日奔行

He looked older, for hard exercise, the best of good eating, and baths whenever he felt in the least hot or dusty, had given him strength and growth far beyond his age. He could swing by one hand from a top branch for half an hour at a time, when he had occasion to look along the tree-roads. He could stop a young buck in mid-gallop and throw him sideways by the head. He could even jerk over the big, blue wild boars that lived in the Marshes of the North. The Jungle People who used to fear him for his wits feared him now for his strength, and when he moved quietly on his own affairs the mere whisper of his coming cleared the wood-paths. And yet the look in his eyes was always gentle. Even when he fought, his eyes never blazed as Bagheera’s did. They only grew more and more interested and excited; and that was one of the things that Bagheera himself did not understand.
原译: 与红狗大打一场后第二年和阿克拉的死亡，毛格利一定是将近17岁。他看起来年纪大了锻炼力强饮食最美味只要他觉得自己最不热或灰尘不浓时都会洗澡给他的体力和成长远远超过他这个年龄。他可以一次从顶部的树枝上挥手半小时，当时他有机会沿着树道看。他可以阻止一只小公鸡在中盖洛普并扔他的头侧。他甚至可以替北方沼泽地的蓝野猪打手枪。丛林里的人曾经因为他的智慧而害怕他现在担心他的力量，当他悄悄地为自己的事务行动时，轻轻地说，他来了就清除了木路。但是他的眼睛总是温柔的。即使他打的时候他的眼睛也从来没有像巴希拉那样亮过。他们只是越来越感兴趣和兴奋；这是巴希拉自己不明白的事情之一。

中文章名: 春日奔行
英文证据: In an Indian Jungle the seasons slide one into the other almost without division. There seem to be only two--the wet and the dry; but if you look closely below the torrents of rain and the clouds of char and dust you will find all four going round in their regular ring. Spring is the most wonderful, because she has not to cover a clean, bare field with new leaves and flowers, but to drive before her and to put away the hanging-on, over-surviving raffle of half-green things which the gentle winter has suffered to live, and to make the partly-dressed stale earth feel new and young once more. And this she does so well that there is no spring in the world like the Jungle spring.
原译: 在印度的丛林中季节将一个滑向另一个几乎没有分裂。似乎只有两颗湿的和干过的但是如果你仔细观察雨的暴风雨和焦炭和尘埃的云下。春天是最奇妙的，因为它不会用新叶和花朵来覆盖干净、光秃的田野，而是将那些在温柔的冬天中勉强存活的半绿植物清除掉，让那些尚未完全长好的旧土重新感受到新鲜与年轻。她做的很好世界上没有像丛林泉那样的春天。
现译: 印度丛林的季节几乎不分界，此一季就滑入彼一季。似乎只有两个季节，旱季和雨季。可要是透过倾泻的暴雨、腾腾的灰烬和尘土留心往深处找，你仍会发现四季按着他们自己那只轮子规律地旋转。春天最有奇迹。她来的时候，任务可不是在一片赤裸干净的大地铺盖新叶新花。温和的冬天饶过一大堆半绿不绿、拖拖拉拉不肯死的旧东西，她得赶在前面，把那些残余收拾走，使仍半穿着旧衣、陈腐的土地重新觉得自己年轻新鲜。这件事她做得太好，世上再也没有像丛林之春的春天。

中文章名: 春日奔行
英文证据: There is one day when all things are tired, and the very smells, as they drift on the heavy air, are old and used. One cannot explain this, but it feels so. Then there is another day--to the eye nothing whatever has changed--when all the smells are new and delightful, and the whiskers of the Jungle People quiver to their roots, and the winter hair comes away from their sides in long, draggled locks. Then, perhaps, a little rain falls, and all the trees and the bushes and the bamboos and the mosses and the juicy-leaved plants wake with a noise of growing that you can almost hear, and under this noise runs, day and night, a deep hum. THAT is the noise of the spring--a vibrating boom which is neither bees, nor falling water, nor the wind in tree-tops, but the purring of the warm, happy world.
原译: 有一天，所有的东西都累了，和气味，当它们漂浮在沉重的空气，旧的和使用的。无法解释这一点，但感觉如此。然后还有一天眼里什么也没有改变当所有的气味都是新的令人愉快的丛林人民的胡须都从他们的根上跳出来冬发从他们的侧面长长的拖拉的锁里流出来。然后，也许有小雨落下，所有树木，灌木丛，竹子，苔胱，和多汁的植物，以一种生长的噪音醒来，你几乎可以听到，在这种噪音下，一天到晚，一个深的哼声。这是春天的响声震动的繁荣既不是蜜蜂，也不是落水也不是树顶的风而是温暖快乐的世界的呼唤。
现译: 有那么一天，一切都倦了。甚至连那些在沉闷空气中漂流的气味都是旧的，用过的。解释不出，就是这种感觉。又有那么一天，眼睛看去，一切毫无改变，可世上所有气味都新鲜可喜。丛林之民的胡须一直颤到根，冬毛一长绺一长绺，蓬乱着从两胁脱落。也许还会落点细雨，乔木、灌木、竹子、苔藓和多汁的阔叶草木，一齐醒来，滋长的声音几乎听得见。在这一切声响底下，日日夜夜，有一种低沉的嗡鸣。那就是春天的声音。一阵震动的轰响，不是蜜蜂，不是落水，不是风吹树梢，是这暖融融的快活世界在打呼噜。

中文章名: 春日奔行
英文证据: Up to this year Mowgli had always delighted in the turn of the seasons. It was he who generally saw the first Eye-of-the-Spring deep down among the grasses, and the first bank of spring clouds, which are like nothing else in the Jungle. His voice could be heard in all sorts of wet, star-lighted, blossoming places, helping the big frogs through their choruses, or mocking the little upside-down owls that hoot through the white nights. Like all his people, spring was the season he chose for his flittings--moving, for the mere joy of rushing through the warm air, thirty, forty, or fifty miles between twilight and the morning star, and coming back panting and laughing and wreathed with strange flowers. The Four did not follow him on these wild ringings of the Jungle, but went off to sing songs with other wolves. The Jungle People are very busy in the spring, and Mowgli could hear them grunting and screaming and whistling according to their kind. Their voices then are different from their voices at other times of the year, and that is one of the reasons why spring in the Jungle is called the Time of New Talk.
原译: 直至今年，毛格利一直对季节之交感到高兴。他一般都看到了草丛中第一道闪烁的眼线和第一棵春云，与丛林中别无二致。他的声音可以在各种湿润、星光照亮、开花的地方听到，帮助大青蛙穿过它们的花圈，或嘲笑那些在白夜里摇晃的小反向猫头鹰。和他所有的人民一样，春天是他选择的季节飞翔的季节仅仅是为了在温暖的空气中奔驰 30、40或50英里。四个人没有跟着他走在丛林的狂野铃声上，但去唱着其他狼的歌。丛林人民在春天非常忙碌，毛格利可以听到他们叫喊尖叫和吹口哨与他们同类。他们的呼声与每年其他时间的声音不同，这就是为什么在丛林中春天被称为新对话时代的原因之一。
现译: 在这一年以前，每次季节交替，毛格利都爱得很。草丛深处第一朵春之眼，往往是他先看见。第一层春云，在丛林里绝不像其他任何一样东西，也是他先看见。星光打湿、百花绽放的所在，四下都听到他的声音，替大青蛙们撑起合唱的场面，或模仿那些倒挂着、彻夜在白亮月光里啼叫的小猫头鹰。他跟族人们一样，最爱选春天四处游荡。纯粹为了迎着暖风飞奔的喜悦，他会在黄昏到晨星升起之间跑过三十、四十、五十英里，喘着气，笑着，身上绕满奇花回来。四兄弟不跟着他这样绕丛林疯跑，转去找其他的狼唱歌。春天丛林之民都很忙，毛格利能听见各族各依各的习性，呼噜，尖叫，吹口哨。这时它们的声音不同于一年中其他时节。因此，丛林才把春天叫作新语时节。

中文章名: 春日奔行
英文证据: But that spring, as he told Bagheera, his stomach was changed in him. Ever since the bamboo shoots turned spotty-brown he had been looking forward to the morning when the smells should change. But when the morning came, and Mor the Peacock, blazing in bronze and blue and gold, cried it aloud all along the misty woods, and Mowgli opened his mouth to send on the cry, the words choked between his teeth, and a feeling came over him that began at his toes and ended in his hair--a feeling of pure unhappiness, so that he looked himself over to be sure that he had not trod on a thorn. Mor cried the new smells, the other birds took it over, and from the rocks by the Waingunga he heard Bagheera’s hoarse scream--something between the scream of an eagle and the neighing of a horse. There was a yelling and scattering of Bandar-log in the new-budding branches above, and there stood Mowgli, his chest, filled to answer Mor, sinking in little gasps as the breath was driven out of it by this unhappiness.

中文章名: 春日奔行
英文证据: “I have eaten good food,” he said to himself. “I have drunk good water. Nor does my throat burn and grow small, as it did when I bit the blue-spotted root that Oo the Turtle said was clean food. But my stomach is heavy, and I have given very bad talk to Bagheera and others, people of the Jungle and my people. Now, too, I am hot and now I am cold, and now I am neither hot nor cold, but angry with that which I cannot see. Huhu! It is time to make a running! To-night I will cross the ranges; yes, I will make a spring running to the Marshes of the North, and back again. I have hunted too easily too long. The Four shall come with me, for they grow as fat as white grubs.”
原译: 他对自己说，“我吃过好吃的食物”。“我喝过好水，喉咙也烧焦了，变小了，就像我咬了乌龟说的蓝斑的根。但是我的胃很重，我对巴希拉和其他人，丛林的人和我的族人都说了很多话。现在，我也很热，现在又很冷，现在我既不热，也不冷，但我生我所不能见的气。你告诉我吧，我今晚要穿过山岳，我要从山岳中跑出一条泉水，再往北奔走，我猎猎的时间太长了。四人将随我而来，因为他们长得像白猪一样肥。

中文章名: 春日奔行
英文证据: He called, but never one of the Four answered. They were far beyond earshot, singing over the spring songs--the Moon and Sambhur Songs--with the wolves of the pack; for in the spring-time the Jungle People make very little difference between the day and the night. He gave the sharp, barking note, but his only answer was the mocking maiou of the little spotted tree-cat winding in and out among the branches for early birds’ nests. At this he shook all over with rage, and half drew his knife. Then he became very haughty, though there was no one to see him, and stalked severely down the hillside, chin up and eyebrows down. But never a single one of his people asked him a question, for they were all too busy with their own affairs.
原译: 他打过电话但四个人中没有一个接过。歌唱着春天的歌 -- 月亮和Sambhur Songs -- 与狼群同在；因为春天，丛林人民在白天和黑夜之间几乎没有什么区别。他给了尖锐的叫声，但他唯一的答案是嘲笑maiou 小斑斑斑的树猫。此时他愤怒地摇摇欲坠一半人拔出了他的刀。然后他变得很傲慢，虽然没有人看见他，并严重地从山坡上走下来，抬起头来，眉毛朝下。但他的族人中从来没有一个人问过他一个问题，因为他们都忙于自己的事务。

中文章名: 春日奔行
英文证据: A couple of young wolves of the Pack were cantering down a path, looking for open ground in which to fight. (You will remember that the Law of the Jungle forbids fighting where the Pack can see.) Their neck-bristles were as stiff as wire, and they bayed furiously, crouching for the first grapple. Mowgli leaped forward, caught one outstretched throat in either hand, expecting to fling the creatures backward as he had often done in games or Pack hunts. 中文章名: 春日奔行
英文证据: He killed early that evening and ate but little, so as to be in good fettle for his spring running, and he ate alone because all the Jungle People were away singing or fighting. It was a perfect white night, as they call it. All green things seemed to have made a month’s growth since the morning. The branch that was yellow-leaved the day before dripped sap when Mowgli broke it. The mosses curled deep and warm over his feet, the young grass had no cutting edges, and all the voices of the Jungle boomed like one deep harp-string touched by the moon--the Moon of New Talk, who splashed her light full on rock and pool, slipped it between trunk and creeper, and sifted it through a million leaves. Forgetting his unhappiness, Mowgli sang aloud with pure delight as he settled into his stride. It was more like flying than anything else, for he had chosen the long downward slope that leads to the Northern Marshes through the heart of the main Jungle, where the springy ground deadened the fall of his feet. A man-taught man would have picked his way with many stumbles through the cheating moonlight, but Mowgli’s muscles, trained by years of experience, bore him up as though he were a feather. When a rotten log or a hidden stone turned under his foot he saved himself, never checking his pace, without effort and without thought. When he tired of ground-going he threw up his hands monkey-fashion to the nearest creeper, and seemed to float rather than to climb up into the thin branches, whence he would follow a tree-road till his mood changed, and he shot downward in a long, leafy curve to the levels again. There were still, hot hollows surrounded by wet rocks where he could hardly breathe for the heavy scents of the night flowers and the bloom along the creeper buds; dark avenues where the moonlight lay in belts as regular as checkered marbles in a church aisle; thickets where the wet young growth stood breast-high about him and threw its arms round his waist; and hilltops crowned with broken rock, where he leaped from stone to stone above the lairs of the frightened little foxes. He would hear, very faint and far off, the chug-drug of a boar sharpening his tusks on a bole; and would come across the great gray brute all alone, scribing and rending the bark of a tall tree, his mouth dripping with foam, and his eyes blazing like fire. Or he would turn aside to the sound of clashing horns and hissing grunts, and dash past a couple of furious sambhur, staggering to and fro with lowered heads, striped with blood that showed black in the moonlight. Or at some rushing ford he would hear Jacala the Crocodile bellowing like a bull, or disturb a twined knot of the Poison People, but before they could strike he would be away and across the glistening shingle, and deep in the Jungle again.
原译: 那天晚上他早点杀人，吃得很少，所以为了他的春天跑步，他独自吃，因为所有的丛林人民都在外唱歌或战斗。那是个完美的白夜，就像他们所说的。所有绿色的东西似乎已经一个月的增长从早上开始。树枝是黄色的，在毛格利弄坏时，树苗滴落的前一天。青草没有前锋丛林的声音都像被月亮-新谈之月触动的竖琴一样闪烁在岩石和游泳池上滑落在树干和爬行器之间。毛格利忘了他不快乐的时候，大声地歌唱，满怀喜悦，沉浸在自己的足迹中。更像是飞翔因为他选择了漫长的向下斜坡通往北方沼泽地穿过大丛林的心脏。男人教的会选择他的方式与许多绊倒通过欺骗的月光，但毛格利的肌肉，训练多年的经验，使他觉得自己像一个羽毛。当一根烂木或一块隐藏的石头在他脚下翻转时，他救了自己，从不检查他的步伐，不费吹灰之力，不考虑。当他厌倦了跳地时，他把手的猴子时装扔到最接近的爬行者身上，似乎漂浮起来，而不是爬到薄枝上，在那里，他会沿着树道走，直到他的情绪发生变化，然后他又向下射击在一个长长的叶状弯曲上向下向下向上飞。仍然有热的空洞，四周是湿的岩石，他几乎无法呼吸，因为夜花的香味很重，而且花花在爬虫芽上开花开花；黑暗的通道，月光像在教堂过道上弹珠一样固定在皮带里；厚厚的厚的厚厚，年轻湿润的生长在他身上，将他的手臂围在腰上；和山顶与破碎的岩石，在那里，他跳从石头到石头之上被吓坏的小狐狸的巢穴。他将听到，非常微弱和遥远的，野猪的酸液，磨磨他的牙，并且独自穿过大灰色的野兽，给一棵高树的树打字和树皮，他的嘴里滴着泡沫，他的眼睛像火一样闪耀。或者他会转过身去听一听角和呼噜声的响声冲过一对愤怒的桑伯尔人摇晃晃晃晃头低落沾满了月光下黑血。或是在某个匆忙的叉子上他会听到鳄鱼的铃声像公牛一样响起或打乱毒民的绳结但是在他们袭击之前。
现译: 那天傍晚，他早早猎了食物却只吃一点，好让身子轻快，去作春日奔行。他是一个人吃的，因为丛林之民全都唱歌或斗打去了。照他们的说法，这是个十全十美的白夜。自早晨以来，所有青绿的东西仿佛都长过了一个月。昨天还黄着叶的枝条，毛格利一掰就滴出树汁。苔藓暖洋洋地在他脚面上卷得深厚，嫩草叶缘还不割人。全丛林的声音一起轰鸣，仿佛月亮拨响一根深沉的竖琴弦。那是新语之月，把满怀清光泼上岩石、池潭，让它从树干与藤蔓之间偷偷滑过，再经由百万片叶子筛落。毛格利忘掉难过，跑开了步子，纯为高兴，放声唱歌。这实在更像飞行。他特地选了贯穿丛林腹心、一直往下通到北方沼泽的长坡，富有弹性的土地消去了脚步落地的震动。若是人训练出来的人，要在这骗眼睛的月光里摸路，早不知跌过几回。毛格利那身肌肉经多年的经验训练，把他托得像一根羽毛。腐木或暗石在他脚下一滚，他自然稳住身形，既不减速，也不用费力，更不必动念头。地上走乏了，他学猴子伸手攀最近的藤蔓，与其说“爬”，不如说“飘”进了纤细的枝桠，再顺着树间道路走上一程。等心境又变，便沿一道长长的绿叶弧线直射回平地。有潮湿岩石围着的静热低洼，夜花和藤芽上的花香浓得几乎叫人透不过气。有幽暗的林荫道，月光带带落在地上，整齐如教堂走道里的方格大理石。有稠密的树丛，湿嫩的新条齐胸高，伸臂搂住他的腰。也有破石戴冠的山顶，他在受惊小狐狸的洞顶上由一块石跃向另一块。他会听见远远的吭哧吭哧，是野猪在树干上磨尖牙。再往前，果然就碰上孤伶伶一头灰大野猪，犁破、撕扯一棵高树的皮，嘴里滴白沫，双眼燃着火。或是循着角相撞的声响和咝咝的低吼拐去，从两头盛怒的水鹿身边冲过，它们低着头踉跄来去，身上道道血迹在月下成了黑色。也许在一个水急的浅渡，他会听到鳄鱼贾卡拉像公牛般吼叫，或惊起一团扭结的毒牙一族。可还没等它们出击，他已越过发亮的砾石滩，又入了深林。

The marsh was awake all round him, for in the spring the Bird People sleep very lightly, and companies of them were coming or going the night through. But no one took any notice of Mowgli sitting among the tall reeds humming songs without words, and looking at the soles of his hard brown feet in case of neglected thorns. 中文章名: 春日奔行
英文证据: “I have surely eaten poison,” he said in an awe-stricken voice. “It must be that carelessly I have eaten poison, and my strength is going from me. I was afraid--and yet it was not _I_ that was afraid--Mowgli was afraid when the two wolves fought. Akela, or even Phao, would have silenced them; yet Mowgli was afraid. That is true sign I have eaten poison.... But what do they care in the Jungle? They sing and howl and fight, and run in companies under the moon, and I--Hai-mai!--I am dying in the marshes, of that poison which I have eaten.” He was so sorry for himself that he nearly wept. “And after,” he went on, “they will find me lying in the black water. 原译: 他的言辞被咆哮和坠落在下面，巴希拉，光，强大和可怕的，一如既往，站在他面前。
现译: 他的话被下方矮树丛中一声咆哮、一阵撞响截断。轻捷、雄健，又一如往日可畏的巴希拉站到了他面前。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 春日奔行
英文证据: “Therefore,” he said, stretching out a dripping right paw, “I did not come. It was a long hunt, but he lies dead in the bushes now--a bull in his second year--the Bull that frees thee, Little Brother. All debts are paid now. For the rest, my word is Baloo’s word.” He licked Mowgli’s foot. “Remember, Bagheera loved thee,” he cried, and bounded away. At the foot of the hill he cried again long and loud, “Good hunting on a new trail, Master of the Jungle! Remember, Bagheera loved thee.”
原译: 他说：我的确没有到来，但现在他死在灌木丛里。他第二年的牛牛救了你。弟弟，现在所有的债务都还清了。我的话就是巴鲁的话。他舔毛格利的脚。“记住，巴希拉爱你” 他哭喊着，并被包围了。在山脚上，他又长又大声地喊道：“丛林大师，捕猎的好，记住，巴希拉爱你。”
现译: “我先前没来，就是为这个，”巴希拉伸出湿淋淋的右爪。“这一场猎用了好久，可它如今已死，在矮树丛里。一头两岁不到的公牛。小兄弟，这就是叫你自由的那头牛。如今所有的债都已还清。至于其余的，巴鲁的话就是我的话。”他舔了舔毛格利的脚。“记着，巴希拉爱过你！”他一跃而去。到山脚，又长长地、高声地叫了一句：“丛林之主，祝你在新的道路上狩猎顺遂！记着，巴希拉爱过你！”
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 春日奔行
英文证据: “Thou hast heard,” said Baloo. “There is no more. Go now; but first come to me. O wise Little Frog, come to me!”
原译: 巴鲁说“你听说了。”“没有了，现在走，但先来见我，聪明的小青蛙，来见我！”
现译: “你都听见了，”巴鲁说。“没有别的话。现在去吧。不过先到我跟前来。我那聪明的小青蛙呀，到我跟前来！”
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 春日奔行
英文证据: “It is hard to cast the skin,” said Kaa as Mowgli sobbed and sobbed, with his head on the blind bear’s side and his arms round his neck, while Baloo tried feebly to lick his feet.
原译: 卡阿说“很难抛出皮肤，因为毛格利感到哭泣和哭泣，头部在盲熊的身边，手部围在脖子上，而巴鲁却费劲地舔脚。
现译: “蜕去一层皮是艰难的。”卡阿说。毛格利把头埋在盲眼老熊的身边，两臂搂住他的脖子，哭了又哭。巴鲁力不从心，还试着去舔他的脚。
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。

中文章名: 春日奔行
英文证据: “The stars are thin,” said Gray Brother, snuffing at the dawn wind. “Where shall we lair to-day? for from now, we follow new trails.”
原译: 灰哥说“星星是薄的” 黎明的风会窒息。今天我们该去哪里藏身呢？因为从现在起，我们将走新的路线。
现译: “星星稀了。”灰兄弟闻着黎明的风说。“今天我们在哪里安窝呢？今后，咱们可要走新的路了。”
修改判断: 按所附英文核对全段并重译或修订，保留原文的说话人、细节和叙事语气。
