中文章名: 下部 / 第10章　海底煤矿
英文证据: At every turn of the path we were following, the lake appeared in all its length and breadth. The lantern lit up the whole of its peaceable surface, which knew neither ripple nor wave. The _Nautilus_ remained perfectly immovable. On the platform, and on the mountain, the ship’s crew were working like black shadows clearly carved against the luminous atmosphere. We were now going round the highest crest of the first layers of rock which upheld the roof. I then saw that bees were not the only representatives of the animal kingdom in the interior of this volcano. Birds of prey hovered here and there in the shadows, or fled from their nests on the top of the rocks. There were sparrow hawks, with white breasts, and kestrels, and down the slopes scampered, with their long legs, several fine fat bustards. I leave anyone to imagine the covetousness of the Canadian at the sight of this savoury game, and whether he did not regret having no gun. But he did his best to replace the lead by stones, and, after several fruitless attempts, he succeeded in wounding a magnificent bird. To say that he risked his life twenty times before reaching it is but the truth; but he managed so well that the creature joined the honey-cakes in his bag. We were now obliged to descend toward the shore, the crest becoming impracticable. Above us the crater seemed to gape like the mouth of a well. From this place the sky could be clearly seen, and clouds, dissipated by the west wind, leaving behind them, even on the summit of the mountain, their misty remnants—certain proof that they were only moderately high, for the volcano did not rise more than eight hundred feet above the level of the ocean. Half an hour after the Canadian’s last exploit we had regained the inner shore. Here the flora was represented by large carpets of marine crystal, a little umbelliferous plant very good to pickle, which also bears the name of pierce-stone and sea-fennel. Conseil gathered some bundles of it. As to the fauna, it might be counted by thousands of crustacea of all sorts, lobsters, crabs, spider-crabs, chameleon shrimps, and a large number of shells, rockfish, and limpets. Three-quarters of an hour later we had finished our circuitous walk and were on board. The crew had just finished loading the sodium, and the _Nautilus_ could have left that instant. But Captain Nemo gave no order. Did he wish to wait until night, and leave the submarine passage secretly? Perhaps so. Whatever it might be, the next day, the _Nautilus_, having left its port, steered clear of all land at a few yards beneath the waves of the Atlantic.
原译: 在我们所遵循的道路的每一个转弯，湖面的长度和广度都出现了。灯笼照亮了整个和平的表面既不了解波浪也不了解波浪。鹦鹉螺号仍然完全不动。在平台上，在山上，船的船员工作像黑色的阴影明显刻在光亮的大气。我们正绕着头层岩石的顶峰绕过屋顶。然后我发现蜜蜂不是火山内地动物王国的唯一代表。猎物鸟盘旋在这里和在那里的阴影，或逃离他们的巢在岩石的顶部。有麻雀鹰，白色的乳房，和海雀，和下坡骗，他们的长腿，几个漂亮的肥猪。我让大家想象一下加拿大人在这美妙的游戏面前的贪婪，以及他是否对没有枪不后悔。但是他尽力用石头取代铅经过几次徒劳的尝试他成功地伤害了一只壮观的鸟。说到他生命危险二十次才到手，但事实并非如此；但是他做得如此好，以至于他把蜂蜜蛋糕塞进他的包里。我们现在不得不向岸边下山山顶变得不切实际。在我们上面弹坑似乎像一口井的嘴一样裂开。从这里可以清楚地看到天空，云层被西风散去，留下，甚至在山顶上，留下的迷雾残留物-- 某些证据表明它们只有中等高度，因为火山并没有超过海洋的800英尺。加拿大人上次开采后半个小时我们重获了内岸。这里的植物是由大片海洋水晶地毯代表的，一种对咸菜非常有益的微薄的植物，也带有刺石和海螺的名称。康塞尔收集了一些包。至于动物，可以计数成千的甲壳类动物，龙虾，螃蟹，蜘蛛蟹，变色龙虾，以及大量的贝壳，岩石鱼和瘸子。3/4小时后，我们完成了我们绕行的行走，并上了船。机组人员刚刚装完钠鹦鹉螺号可能马上离开了。但是尼摩船长没有下命令。他想等到晚上偷偷离开潜艇通道吗？也许吧。不管它是什么，第二天，鹦鹉螺号离开港口，在大西洋海浪下几码处离开所有陆地。
现译:
我们沿小路每转一个弯，眼前就会展出湖面从头到尾、从这岸到那岸的全貌。大灯照亮整片平静的水面，那湖既不识风浪，也不知涟漪为何物。“鹦鹉螺号”始终纹丝不动。船员在平台上、在山上工作，一条条黑影清楚地剪在明亮的空气中。我们此刻正绕行支撑穹顶的第一层岩石的最高脊线。
于是我看出，蜜蜂并非这火山腹中动物界的唯一代表。猛禽时而在阴影中盘旋，时而从石顶的巢里飞走。有白胸雀鹰，有红隼，斜坡上还奔下好几只又肥又壮的鸨，迈着长腿飞快地跑。看见这种肉香味浓的野味，加拿大人的渴望如何，是否遗憾没带枪，谁都不妨设想。然而他尽力用石块顶替铅弹，空了几次之后，终于打伤一只壮鸟。我说他为了追到它，前后冒了二十回性命的危险，并不是夸张。但他终究干得漂亮，那鸟便进了他的包，去跟做蜜饼的材料作伴。
现在脊线不能再走，逼得我们朝岸边往下。头顶火山口仿佛张开的井口。从这里能清楚看见天空，西风把云吹散，连山顶上都留下雾一般的残絮。这是再确切不过的证据，说明那些云并不太高，因为火山超出海面还不到八百英尺。加拿大人最后那次立功之后半小时，我们又回到了湖的内岸。植物界在这里的代表，是铺成大片地毯的海茴香，一种很适宜腌制的伞形科小草，又名穿石草。康塞尔采了好几束。至于动物，各类甲壳动物数以千计，有龙虾、蟹、蜘蛛蟹、善变颜色的小虾，以及大量贝类、岩栖鱼和笠贝。再过三刻钟，环湖全程走完，我们已在船上。船员也刚把钠装完。“鹦鹉螺号”当时就能出发，尼摩船长却没下令。莫非他愿等夜色降临，好秘密通过海底通道？也许是。无论如何，到了次日，“鹦鹉螺号”已从港里驶出，在大西洋浪面下几码深处开向远离一切陆地的地方。

中文章名: 下部 / 第11章　马尾藻海
英文证据: That day the _Nautilus_ crossed a singular part of the Atlantic Ocean. No one can be ignorant of the existence of a current of warm water known by the name of the Gulf Stream. After leaving the Gulf of Florida, we went in the direction of Spitzbergen. But before entering the Gulf of Mexico, about 45° of N. lat., this current divides into two arms, the principal one going towards the coast of Ireland and Norway, whilst the second bends to the south about the height of the Azores; then, touching the African shore, and describing a lengthened oval, returns to the Antilles. This second arm—it is rather a collar than an arm—surrounds with its circles of warm water that portion of the cold, quiet, immovable ocean called the Sargasso Sea, a perfect lake in the open Atlantic: it takes no less than three years for the great current to pass round it. Such was the region the _Nautilus_ was now visiting, a perfect meadow, a close carpet of seaweed, fucus, and tropical berries, so thick and so compact that the stem of a vessel could hardly tear its way through it. And Captain Nemo, not wishing to entangle his screw in this herbaceous mass, kept some yards beneath the surface of the waves. The name Sargasso comes from the Spanish word “sargazzo” which signifies kelp. This kelp, or berry-plant, is the principal formation of this immense bank. And this is the reason why these plants unite in the peaceful basin of the Atlantic. The only explanation which can be given, he says, seems to me to result from the experience known to all the world. Place in a vase some fragments of cork or other floating body, and give to the water in the vase a circular movement, the scattered fragments will unite in a group in the centre of the liquid surface, that is to say, in the part least agitated. In the phenomenon we are considering, the Atlantic is the vase, the Gulf Stream the circular current, and the Sargasso Sea the central point at which the floating bodies unite.
原译: 那天鹦鹉螺号越过大西洋的单一部分。任何人都不能不知道存在以海湾流为名的暖水流。离开佛罗里达湾后，我们朝斯皮兹贝根的方向去了。但进入墨西哥湾之前大约是北纬45度。这条洋流分成两条胳膊，一条主要向爱尔兰和挪威海岸飞去，另一条向南弯曲，大约在亚速尔群岛的高度；然后，触摸非洲海岸，描述一个长长的奥瓦尔，返回安的列斯群岛。第二只手臂 -- -- 与其说是项圈，不如说是一只臂 -- -- 环绕着它的温暖水圈，在寒冷、宁静、不可移动的海洋中，有一部分被称为Sargasso海，这是大西洋开放中完美的湖：大海流经过它至少需要三年时间。鹦鹉螺现在所到之地一片完美的草原一片海藻乌豆热带浆果厚厚而紧凑以至于一艘船的干叶几乎无法穿过它。尼摩船长不想把螺丝缠在疯狂的弥撒中却把几码子放在海浪表面下面。Sargasso的名字来自西班牙的“sargazzo”一词，它代表着海藻。这个海藻，或果冻，是这个巨大的银行的主要组成。这就是为什么这些植物团结在大西洋的和平盆地。他说，在我看来，唯一可以给出的解释似乎来自全世界所知道的经验。在花瓶中放置一些软体或其他漂浮体的碎片，并将一个圆形运动交给花瓶中的水体，分散的碎片将集中在液体表面的中心，也就是说，在最不激动的部分。我们正在考虑的现象是，大西洋是花瓶，海湾是圆环流，而萨尔加索海是漂浮体凝聚的中心点。
现译:
那天，“鹦鹉螺号”横穿了大西洋上一个奇特的区域。想必谁都知道，海上有股暖流叫作墨西哥湾流。离开佛罗里达湾之后，我们取道斯匹次卑尔根的方向。不过还没进入墨西哥湾，约在北纬四十五度处，这股洋流分出两臂。主流向着爱尔兰和挪威的海岸，另一臂在与亚速尔群岛相平处转向南方，触及非洲海岸，再画一个长长的椭圆，转回安的列斯群岛。这第二臂，其实与其说是臂，不如说是一只颈圈，以环绕的暖水围住了一片又冷又静、几乎不动的海洋。那地方叫马尾藻海，是开阔的大西洋上一个真正的湖。外面的大洋流要绕它一圈，至少得花三年。
眼下“鹦鹉螺号”探访的正是这片地方。海面俨然一座牧场，一张铺得密密的地毯，由海草、褐藻和热带长着小浆果般圆囊的藻草织成。它紧密厚实到连船首也很难撕开一条路。尼摩船长不愿叫螺旋桨缠进这团草丛，便把船保持在浪下几码。马尾藻海的名字出自西班牙词“sargazzo”，意为海藻。长着小浆果般气囊的这种海藻，正是构成这片巨大草滩的主要材料。
它们怎么会聚到大西洋这个平静的盆地里？莫里认为，唯一说得通的解释，来自人人熟悉的一项试验。往容器里的水面放些碎软木或别的浮物，再让里面的水打转，散落的碎片就会聚作一团，集中于液面中央，也就是受到搅动最小的地方。眼前这种现象，道理相同。大西洋是容器，墨西哥湾流是旋转的水，而马尾藻海便是浮物聚集的中心。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第11章　马尾藻海
英文证据: I share Maury’s opinion, and I was able to study the phenomenon in the very midst, where vessels rarely penetrate. Above us floated products of all kinds, heaped up among these brownish plants; trunks of trees torn from the Andes or the Rocky Mountains, and floated by the Amazon or the Mississippi; numerous wrecks, remains of keels, or ships’ bottoms, side-planks stove in, and so weighted with shells and barnacles that they could not again rise to the surface. And time will one day justify Maury’s other opinion, that these substances thus accumulated for ages will become petrified by the action of the water and will then form inexhaustible coal-mines—a precious reserve prepared by far-seeing Nature for the moment when men shall have exhausted the mines of continents.
原译: 我同意莫里的观点，我研究过这一现象，在那里，船只很少穿透。上面浮着各种产品，堆积在这些棕色植物中；树干从安第斯山脉或落基山脉撕裂，由亚马逊河或密西西比河漂浮；大量残骸，残骸，或船底，侧板炉，如此重量的贝壳和谷仓无法再次升到地表。有一天，时间会证明莫里的另一个观点，即这些古老积累的物质将会被水流所淹没，并形成无穷无尽的煤矿 -- 一种宝贵的储备，由远视的自然所制成，在人类将用尽各大洲的矿山的时候。
现译: 我赞同莫里的见解，如今更能身临其境，在极少有船能闯进的中央察看这个现象。在我们头顶，各色东西堆在那些褐色藻草间一起漂浮。有从安第斯山或落基山脉被冲走、经亚马孙河或密西西比河漂来的树干；有众多船骸，龙骨和船底的残片，被撞破的舷板。壳和藤壶在上面附生得太多，压得有些东西再也浮不到水面。有一天，时间还将证明莫里的另一种见解：这些堆积了许多世纪的物质，会在水的作用下石化，继而形成取之不尽的煤矿。等人们耗尽大陆上的矿产时，有远见的大自然已为他们备好了这份宝贵的储藏。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第11章　马尾藻海
英文证据: In the midst of this inextricable mass of plants and sea weed, I noticed some charming pink halcyons and actiniae, with their long tentacles trailing after them, and medusæ, green, red, and blue.
原译: 这片杂草中我发现了一些迷人的粉红色的海参和动作它们的长触角跟着它们以及绿、红和蓝的海观。
现译: 在这团分也分不开的水草和海藻之间，我注意到可爱的粉红色软珊瑚和海葵，身后拖着长长的触手，还有碧绿、鲜红、湛蓝的水母。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第11章　马尾藻海
英文证据: All the day of the 22nd of February we passed in the Sargasso Sea, where such fish as are partial to marine plants find abundant nourishment. The next, the ocean had returned to its accustomed aspect. From this time for nineteen days, from the 23rd of February to the 12th of March, the _Nautilus_ kept in the middle of the Atlantic, carrying us at a constant speed of a hundred leagues in twenty-four hours. Captain Nemo evidently intended accomplishing his submarine programme, and I imagined that he intended, after doubling Cape Horn, to return to the Australian seas of the Pacific. Ned Land had cause for fear. In these large seas, void of islands, we could not attempt to leave the boat. Nor had we any means of opposing Captain Nemo’s will. Our only course was to submit; but what we could neither gain by force nor cunning, I liked to think might be obtained by persuasion. This voyage ended, would he not consent to restore our liberty, under an oath never to reveal his existence?—an oath of honour which we should have religiously kept. But we must consider that delicate question with the Captain. But was I free to claim this liberty? Had he not himself said from the beginning, in the firmest manner, that the secret of his life exacted from him our lasting imprisonment on board the _Nautilus?_ And would not my four months’ silence appear to him a tacit acceptance of our situation? And would not a return to the subject result in raising suspicions which might be hurtful to our projects, if at some future time a favourable opportunity offered to return to them?
原译: 2月22日的一整天我们在Sargasso海经过在那里，海洋植物中的一部分鱼类发现了丰富的营养。接下来，海洋又回到了老生常谈的方面。从2月23日到3月12日的十九天鹦鹉螺号一直停留在大西洋中部 24小时内以100里的速度一直以100里的速度载我们。尼摩船长显然打算完成他的潜艇计划，我想象，在把合恩角翻一番之后，他打算返回澳大利亚太平洋海域。尼德·兰德有恐惧的原因。在这些大海中，没有岛屿，我们不能试图离开船。我们也没有办法对抗尼摩船长的意志。我们唯一的方向是屈服；但是，我们既不能靠武力，也不能靠狡猾获得，我更希望通过说服获得。这场航行结束了，他不会同意恢复我们的自由，发誓永远不透露他的存在吗？- 我们本该遵守的荣誉誓言。但是我们必须和船长考虑这个微妙的问题。但我能自由要求这种自由吗？难道他自己不是一开始就以最坚定的方式说，他生命的秘密使我们在鹦鹉螺号船上长期被监禁吗？难道我四个月的沉默对他来说不是暗中接受我们的处境吗？如果今后某个时候有机会回到我们的项目上，回到这个问题上不会引起对我们的项目有害的怀疑吗？
现译: 整个二月二十二日，我们都是在马尾藻海中度过的。偏爱海草的鱼类，在这里实在不愁缺乏食物。第二天，大洋恢复了平常的面貌。从二月二十三日到三月十二日，此后十九天，“鹦鹉螺号”始终行驶在大西洋中部，载我们以每二十四小时一百里格的恒定速度前进。尼摩船长显然打算贯彻自己的海底行程。我猜想，他是要绕过合恩角，回到太平洋的南方水域。尼德·兰德确实有理由害怕：在这片没有岛屿的茫茫外海，我们无从离船，也没有办法抗拒尼摩船长的意志。所能做的只有顺从。不过靠武力和计谋拿不到的东西，我宁愿设想或许能用劝说争取。这一趟航行结束之后，假如我们敢起誓永不泄露他的存在，而且一定会把这名誉上的誓约守得严严实实，他能不能同意还我们自由？要谈这桩微妙的问题，终究还得同船长谈。可是我当真有资格开口索取自由吗？打从一开头，他不就以最坚定的口气说过，他生活的秘密要求我们长久囚居在“鹦鹉螺号”上吗？我的四个月沉默，在他看来难道不正像默许了处境？现在重提此事，要是引起了他的猜疑，日后真有好机会再实行计划时，岂不反而受害？
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第11章　马尾藻海
英文证据: During the nineteen days mentioned above, no incident of any kind happened to signalise our voyage. I saw little of the Captain; he was at work. In the library I often found his books left open, especially those on natural history. My work on submarine depths, conned over by him, was covered with marginal notes, often contradicting my theories and systems; but the Captain contented himself with thus purging my work; it was very rare for him to discuss it with me. Sometimes I heard the melancholy tones of his organ; but only at night, in the midst of the deepest obscurity, when the _Nautilus_ slept upon the deserted ocean. During this part of our voyage we sailed whole days on the surface of the waves. The sea seemed abandoned. A few sailing-vessels, on the road to India, were making for the Cape of Good Hope. One day we were followed by the boats of a whaler, who, no doubt, took us for some enormous whale of great price; but Captain Nemo did not wish the worthy fellows to lose their time and trouble, so ended the chase by plunging under the water. Our navigation continued until the 13th of March; that day the _Nautilus_ was employed in taking soundings, which greatly interested me. We had then made about 13,000 leagues since our departure from the high seas of the Pacific. The bearings gave us 45° 37′ S. lat., and 37° 53′ W. long. It was the same water in which Captain Denham of the Herald sounded 7,000 fathoms without finding the bottom. There, too, Lieutenant Parker, of the American frigate Congress, could not touch the bottom with 15,140 fathoms. Captain Nemo intended seeking the bottom of the ocean by a diagonal sufficiently lengthened by means of lateral planes placed at an angle of 45° with the water-line of the _Nautilus_. Then the screw set to work at its maximum speed, its four blades beating the waves with in describable force. Under this powerful pressure, the hull of the _Nautilus_ quivered like a sonorous chord and sank regularly under the water.
原译: 在上述19天中，没有任何事件表明我们的航行。我很少见到船长，他在工作。在图书馆里，我经常发现他的书还开着特别是那些关于自然历史的书。我在海底深处的工作，被他骗了，被边际的笔记覆盖，常常与我的理论和制度相矛盾；但是船长满足于这样洗刷我的工作；他很少和我讨论此事。有时我听到他器官的忧郁音调，但只在晚上，在最深的模糊中，当鹦鹉螺在荒漠的海洋上睡觉。在这部分航行期间，我们在海浪表面航行了一整天。海洋似乎被抛弃了。在去印度的路上，几艘帆船正在驶往好望角。有一天，我们被捕鲸者的船跟踪，他无疑把我们带到了一艘价格高昂的巨型鲸鱼身上；但是尼摩船长不希望那些优秀的船员们失去时间和麻烦，因此，在水下倾注，结束了追逐。我们的航行一直持续到3月13日；当天，鹦鹉螺号公司被雇用拍摄声音，我对此非常感兴趣。自从我们离开太平洋公海以来，我们共做了大约13 000里拉。方位给了我们45度37分。和37°53'W. 长。和《先驱报》的登纳姆船长听到的7000条法度却找不到底部的一样。在那里，Parker中尉，美国护卫舰国会，无法触摸底部 15,140英尺。尼摩船长打算用一个斜角，通过将平面置于鹦鹉螺号河水线45度角上，以足够长的平面，寻找海底。然后螺丝以最大速度运转 4把刀片用不可磨灭的力量击打波浪。在这种强大的压力下鹦鹉螺的船体像一首高音的合唱经常沉在水下。
现译:
在上述十九天中，航程平静，什么值得特记的意外也没发生。我难得见到船长，他忙着工作。我常在图书室瞧见他摊开的书，尤其是自然史一类。我那本论海洋深处的著作，已经被他反复研读，书边密密写满批注，常反对我的理论和分类。可船长满足于这样给书补正，极少当面跟我辩论。有时我听得见他那管风琴忧伤的音色，但总在夜里，在最深的黑暗中，在“鹦鹉螺号”沉睡于荒寂大洋的时候。
这段行程里，我们往往整天都航行在浪面。海像给人抛弃了，只有几条往印度去的帆船向好望角赶路。有一天，一条捕鲸船放下小艇追我们，显然把我们当成一头价格非凡的巨鲸。尼摩船长不愿叫那些好伙计白白费时费力，便潜入水下，结束了追逐。
这样的航行一直持续到三月十三日。这天“鹦鹉螺号”从事测深，使我大为感兴趣。从太平洋外海出发以来，我们约已走过一万三千里格。测出的船位是南纬四十五度三十七分、西经三十七度五十三分。正是在同一片水域，“先驱号”的德纳姆船长曾放下七千英寻测索而未见底。美国巡防舰“国会号”的帕克中尉也没能探到底，尽管他用了足足一万五千一百四十英寻的索。尼摩船长想亲自寻找洋底。他要将两侧舵面同“鹦鹉螺号”的水线成四十五度角，沿一道足够长的斜线往下驶。螺旋桨随即以最高转速运转，四片桨叶用无法形容的力量击水。巨力推压之下，“鹦鹉螺号”的船壳像一根发声的弦似的颤动，平稳地向水下沉去。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第11章　马尾藻海
英文证据: At 7,000 fathoms I saw some blackish tops rising from the midst of the waters; but these summits might belong to high mountains like the Himalayas or Mont Blanc, even higher; and the depth of the abyss remained incalculable. The _Nautilus_ descended still lower, in spite of the great pressure. I felt the steel plates tremble at the fastenings of the bolts; its bars bent, its partitions groaned; the windows of the saloon seemed to curve under the pressure of the waters. And this firm structure would doubtless have yielded, if, as its Captain had said, it had not been capable of resistance like a solid block. We had attained a depth of 16,000 yards (four leagues), and the sides of the _Nautilus_ then bore a pressure of 1,600 atmospheres, that is to say, 3,200 lbs. to each square two-fifths of an inch of its surface.
原译: 7000平方英尺时，我看到一些黑的顶部从水中升起；但这些顶峰可能属于喜马拉雅山或勃朗峰等高山，甚至更高；深渊的深度仍然无法估量。鹦鹉螺鱼尽管受到很大压力，但降幅仍然较低。我感到钢板在螺栓的紧紧处颤抖；它的铁棒弯曲，它的分区呻吟；酒馆的窗户似乎在水压下弯曲。毫无疑问，这种坚固的结构会有所收效，如果正如船长所说，它无法像一个坚固的块一样进行抵抗的话。我们达到了16 000码的深度(四里格)，鹦鹉螺号两边随后承受了1 600个大气压力，也就是说，3 200磅。以每平方的五分之二的表面。
现译: 到七千英寻深处，我看见水中耸出几座黝黑的山头。但这些山头也许属于喜马拉雅或勃朗峰一般、甚至更高的山脉，深渊到底多深，还是无法估量。“鹦鹉螺号”不顾巨压，继续下潜。我感觉钢板在螺栓紧固处颤动，支架弯曲，舱壁呻吟，客厅的玻璃也仿佛给水压得弯了。这坚实的构造，无疑早就屈服，若不是果真如船长所言，它能像一整块实心金属那样抵抗。我们已经潜到一万六千码，即四里格的深度。此刻“鹦鹉螺号”的侧壁承受着一千六百个大气压，按它的表面算，每五分之二平方英寸压着三千二百磅。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第11章　马尾藻海
英文证据: “What a situation to be in!” I exclaimed. “To overrun these deep regions where man has never trod! Look, Captain, look at these magnificent rocks, these uninhabited grottoes, these lowest receptacles of the globe, where life is no longer possible! What unknown sights are here! Why should we be unable to preserve a remembrance of them?”
原译: “情况真糟糕！”我宣布了。“要征服这些人类从未涉足的深奥地域！看吧，船长，看看这些壮丽的岩石，这些无人居住的洞穴，这些地球最底层的空间，那里已经不再有生命存在！这里有着多么未知的奇观！我们为何不能记住它们呢？”
现译: “这是置身怎样的境地啊！”我叫道，“竟能漫游在人从没踏足的深层世界！看呀，船长，看那些壮丽的岩石，那些无人居住的洞穴；地球最底下的这些容器，连生命都再不可能存在！这里有多少人不知道的景色！为什么我们不能保存一份纪念呢？”
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第11章　马尾藻海
英文证据: “Would you like to carry away more than the remembrance?” said Captain Nemo.
原译: 尼摩船长说 “你想带走的不只是纪念吗？”
现译: “您想带走的，还有比记忆更多的东西吗？”尼摩船长问。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第11章　马尾藻海

英文证据: “I mean to say that nothing is easier than to make a photographic view of this submarine region.”

现译: “我是说，把眼前这片海底世界照一张相，是再容易不过的事。”
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第11章　马尾藻海
英文证据: I had not time to express my surprise at this new proposition, when, at Captain Nemo’s call, an objective was brought into the saloon. Through the widely-opened panel, the liquid mass was bright with electricity, which was distributed with such uniformity that not a shadow, not a gradation, was to be seen in our manufactured light. The _Nautilus_ remained motionless, the force of its screw subdued by the inclination of its planes: the instrument was propped on the bottom of the oceanic site, and in a few seconds we had obtained a perfect negative.
原译: 我没有时间对这一新的提议表示惊讶，当时，在尼摩船长的号召下，有人把一个目标带到酒馆。通过开阔的面板，液体质量与电力相当明亮，电流分布统一，不能在我们的制造光线上看到阴影，不能看到变异。鹦鹉螺号没有动静，其螺丝的力量被其飞机的倾角所压抑：该仪器被压在海洋遗址的底部，在几秒钟内，我们获得了完美的负数。
现译: 这新建议带来的惊讶还没来得及说出口，尼摩船长一声吩咐，已有人把摄影镜头拿进客厅。舷窗的护板敞开着，海水在电光里通体明亮。人造光分布得太均匀，一点阴影、一层明暗也没有。“鹦鹉螺号”静止不动，螺旋桨的冲力被倾斜舵板抵住。照相机架稳，对准这海底景致；几秒后，我们就得到了一张完美的底片。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第11章　马尾藻海
英文证据: But, the operation being over, Captain Nemo said, “Let us go up; we must not abuse our position, nor expose the _Nautilus_ too long to such great pressure.”
原译: 但是，这次行动已经结束了，尼摩船长说，“让我们上去，我们决不能滥用我们的位置，也不能让鹦鹉螺船承受如此巨大的压力。”
现译: 可照相刚一完，尼摩船长便说：“上去吧。咱们不能滥用这番处境，让‘鹦鹉螺号’过久暴露在这样强的压力下。”
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第11章　马尾藻海
英文证据: “Go up again!” I exclaimed.
原译: “又上来了！” 我被赞美了。
现译: “再往上去！”我叫道。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第11章　马尾藻海
英文证据: I had not time to understand why the Captain cautioned me thus, when I was thrown forward on to the carpet. At a signal from the Captain, its screw was shipped, and its blades raised vertically; the _Nautilus_ shot into the air like a balloon, rising with stunning rapidity, and cutting the mass of waters with a sonorous agitation. Nothing was visible; and in four minutes it had shot through the four leagues which separated it from the ocean, and, after emerging like a flying-fish, fell, making the waves rebound to an enormous height.
原译: 我没有时间去理解为什么船长这样警告我，当我被扔到地毯上的时候。在船长发出信号后，它的螺丝被运走了，刀片垂直上升；鹦鹉螺像气球一样射入空中，飞速上升，以响亮的振动声切断了大片水域。没有什么是可见的；在四分钟内，它射穿了四里格将它与海洋隔开，在像飞鱼一样出现后，坠落，使海浪反弹到一个巨大的高度。
现译: 船长为何这样告诫，我还没来得及弄明白，就已经朝前跌在了地毯上。他信号一发，螺旋桨收住，桨叶竖起。“鹦鹉螺号”如同一只气球腾空，以令人晕眩的速度上升，激起洪亮的水声，剖开了上面的海水。什么也看不清。只用四分钟，它便射穿与洋面相隔的四里格水层，像一条飞鱼似的跃出水面，又重重跌下，把波浪弹到惊人的高处。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第12章　抹香鲸和鲸群
英文证据: During the nights of the 13th and 14th of March, the _Nautilus_ returned to its southerly course. I fancied that, when on a level with Cape Horn, he would turn the helm westward, in order to beat the Pacific seas, and so complete the tour of the world. He did nothing of the kind, but continued on his way to the southern regions. Where was he going to? To the pole? It was madness! I began to think that the Captain’s temerity justified Ned Land’s fears. For some time past the Canadian had not spoken to me of his projects of flight; he was less communicative, almost silent. I could see that this lengthened imprisonment was weighing upon him, and I felt that rage was burning within him. When he met the Captain, his eyes lit up with suppressed anger; and I feared that his natural violence would lead him into some extreme. That day, the 14th of March, Conseil and he came to me in my room. I inquired the cause of their visit.
原译: 在3月13日和14日的夜晚，鹦鹉螺号返回了南方。我幻想，当他和合恩角的高度向西转舵，以击败太平洋，并完成世界之旅。他没有做任何这类事，但继续前往南部地区。他准备去哪儿？到电线杆？简直是疯了！我开始觉得船长的暴躁证明尼德·兰德的恐惧是有道理的。过去一段时间，加拿大人没有和我谈他的飞行项目；他不太通情达理，几乎保持沉默。我可以看到，这种延长的监禁对他来说是沉重的，我觉得愤怒正在燃烧在他体内。当他见到船长时，他的眼睛被压抑的愤怒照亮；我担心他的自然暴力会把他引向极端。那天 3月14日康塞尔和他到我房间来。我询问了他们访问的原因。
现译:
三月十三日到十四日的夜里，“鹦鹉螺号”重新向南。我原以为，等到了与合恩角相平的地方，船长就会向西转舵，进入太平洋巡游，完成环球一周。他却毫无此意，仍往南方的海域驶。究竟要去哪里？南极吗？简直疯狂！我开始觉得，船长这样敢冒险，尼德·兰德的恐惧确有道理。有一阵子，加拿大人没再跟我提逃跑计划了；他比平常更不肯敞开心，几乎不开口。我看得出，长久的囚禁压得他透不过气，也感觉到怒火在他心里燃烧。遇上船长时，他眼睛里总会闪出压抑的愤怒。我怕他天生火爆，将来难免走到哪一步极端。
三月十四日这天，他和康塞尔到我的房间里来。我问他们为了什么事。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

原译: “一个简单的问题问你，先生，” 回答加拿大人。

中文章名: 下部 / 第12章　抹香鲸和鲸群
英文证据: “Why?” I replied, looking fixedly at Ned Land, whose meaning was easy to guess. “Because,” I added, “if my surmises are correct, and if I have well understood the Captain’s existence, the _Nautilus_ is not only a vessel: it is also a place of refuge for those who, like its commander, have broken every tie upon earth.”
原译: “为什么？”我回答说，固定地看着尼德·兰德，其意义很容易猜到。因为，我补充说，“如果我的假象是正确的，如果我非常了解船长的存在，鹦鹉螺号不仅是一艘船，也是那些像它的指挥官一样打破了地球上每条领带的人的避难所。”

中文章名: 下部 / 第12章　抹香鲸和鲸群
英文证据: Mouth and teeth! No one could better describe the macrocephalous cachalot, which is sometimes more than seventy-five feet long. Its enormous head occupies one-third of its entire body. Better armed than the whale, whose upper jaw is furnished only with whalebone, it is supplied with twenty-five large tusks, about eight inches long, cylindrical and conical at the top, each weighing two pounds. It is in the upper part of this enormous head, in great cavities divided by cartilages, that is to be found from six to eight hundred pounds of that precious oil called spermaceti. The cachalot is a disagreeable creature, more tadpole than fish, according to Fredol’s description. It is badly formed, the whole of its left side being (if we may say it), a “failure,” and being only able to see with its right eye. But the formidable troop was nearing us. They had seen the whales and were preparing to attack them. One could judge beforehand that the cachalots would be victorious, not only because they were better built for attack than their inoffensive adversaries, but also because they could remain longer under water without coming to the surface. There was only just time to go to the help of the whales. The _Nautilus_ went under water. Conseil, Ned Land, and I took our places before the window in the saloon, and Captain Nemo joined the pilot in his cage to work his apparatus as an engine of destruction. Soon I felt the beatings of the screw quicken, and our speed increased. The battle between the cachalots and the whales had already begun when the _Nautilus_ arrived. They did not at first show any fear at the sight of this new monster joining in the conflict. But they soon had to guard against its blows. What a battle! The _Nautilus_ was nothing but a formidable harpoon, brandished by the hand of its Captain. It hurled itself against the fleshy mass, passing through from one part to the other, leaving behind it two quivering halves of the animal. It could not feel the formidable blows from their tails upon its sides, nor the shock which it produced itself, much more. One cachalot killed, it ran at the next, tacked on the spot that it might not miss its prey, going forwards and backwards, answering to its helm, plunging when the cetacean dived into the deep waters, coming up with it when it returned to the surface, striking it front or sideways, cutting or tearing in all directions and at any pace, piercing it with its terrible spur. What carnage! What a noise on the surface of the waves! What sharp hissing, and what snorting peculiar to these enraged animals! In the midst of these waters, generally so peaceful, their tails made perfect billows. For one hour this wholesale massacre continued, from which the cachalots could not escape. Several times ten or twelve united tried to crush the _Nautilus_ by their weight. From the window we could see their enormous mouths, studded with tusks, and their formidable eyes. Ned Land could not contain himself; he threatened and swore at them. We could feel them clinging to our vessel like dogs worrying a wild boar in a copse. But the _Nautilus_, working its screw, carried them here and there, or to the upper levels of the ocean, without caring for their enormous weight, nor the powerful strain on the vessel. At length the mass of cachalots broke up, the waves became quiet, and I felt that we were rising to the surface. The panel opened, and we hurried on to the platform. The sea was covered with mutilated bodies. A formidable explosion could not have divided and torn this fleshy mass with more violence. We were floating amid gigantic bodies, bluish on the back and white underneath, covered with enormous protuberances. Some terrified cachalots were flying towards the horizon. The waves were dyed red for several miles, and the _Nautilus_ floated in a sea of blood: Captain Nemo joined us.
原译: 嘴和牙齿！没有人能更清楚地描述大脑积层，有时超过75英尺。其巨大的头部占据了整个身体的三分之一。比鲸鱼的上下巴只有鲸骨，更配有武器，它有25个大象牙，大约8英寸长，圆柱形和锥形在顶部，每只重两磅。正是在这个巨大的头部的上部，巨大的洞穴被软体分开，发现有6到800磅的珍贵的油叫做精子。根据Fredol的描述，卡恰罗是一个令人讨厌的生物，比鱼更美味。它的左面是坏的，它是“失败的”，只能用右眼看见。但是，强大的部队正在接近我们。他们看到了鲸鱼并准备攻击它们。人们可以事先判断，卡查洛人将获胜，这不仅是因为他们比不进攻的对手更适合进攻，而且还因为他们可以在水下停留更长的时间，而不到地表。当时只有时间去帮助那些鲸鱼。鹦鹉螺号被水淹没了。尼摩船长加入他的笼子里的飞行员将他的机器作为毁灭的引擎。很快我感受到了螺丝的殴打快速，我们的速度加快。鹦鹉螺号到达时鱼群和鲸鱼之间的战斗已经开始了。他们一开始没有在看到这个新的怪物加入冲突时表现出任何恐惧。但他们很快就要防范它的打击了。多么精彩的战斗啊！鹦鹉螺只是一只巨大的鱼叉被船长的手挥舞。它向肉群投掷，从一个部分经过另一个部分，留下两股动物的颤抖。它无法感受到它们尾巴的沉重打击，也无法感受到它本身造成的冲击，更难以感受到。一只鲸鱼被杀死，然后跑到另一边，当场说，它可能不会错过猎物，向前或向后，对着船头，在鲸目动物跳进深水中时滑倒，当鲸目动物返回地表时，它会带着它爬上，它会正面或侧面撞击它，从各个方向和任何速度切开或撕裂，用可怕的刺激刺穿它。简直是大屠杀！海浪表面的声音真吵！多么尖锐的刺痛，和什么呼呼特别为这些愤怒的动物！在这片平和的水域里它们的尾巴造出了完美的烟囱。整个大屠杀持续了一个小时，卡查洛人无法逃脱。数倍于10或12个联合试图粉碎鹦鹉螺的重量。我们从窗户可以看到他们巨大的嘴被海象缠住眼神也非常可怕。尼德·兰德无法控制自己；他对他们进行威胁并发过誓。我们能感觉到他们像狗一样紧紧缠在船上担心一只野猪在条子里。但是鹦鹉螺把它们带到了这里和那里或海洋的上层却不关心它们的巨大重量也不关心对船的强大压力。长长的木匠的重量散开，波浪变得安静，我觉得我们正在上升到表面。面板打开了，我们匆忙赶到平台上。海面上布满了残骸。一场可怕的爆炸不可能以更多的暴力分裂和撕裂这块肉群。我们漂浮在巨大的身体中，背部的浮肿和下面的白色，覆盖着巨大的繁荣。一些恐怖的匪徒飞向地平线。海浪染红了几英里鹦鹉螺漂浮在血海中尼摩船长加入我们。
现译:
一张嘴，一口牙！再没有更贴切的话来形容这种大头抹香鲸了。它有时长过七十五英尺，硕大的头占整个身子的三分之一。普通鲸的上颌只长鲸须，它却有一副更便于搏斗的武器：二十五枚粗牙，每枚约八英寸长，牙身成圆柱状，顶端呈圆锥形，各重两磅。巨大头部的上方，有几个由软骨隔开的宽阔空腔，可以从中取得六到八百磅名叫鲸蜡的贵重油脂。按弗雷多尔的描写，抹香鲸长得不好看，与其说像鱼，不如说更像蝌蚪。它形体不匀称，整个左侧恕我说一句，简直像“做坏了”，只能够用右眼看东西。
可那班来势可怕的鲸已经逼近。它们看见了南方鲸，正要进攻。谁都事先看得出抹香鲸准能取胜，不只因为它们身上的构造比那些温顺的对手更适于攻击，还因为它们在水下待得更久，不必上浮换气。要救鲸群，恰恰还来得及。“鹦鹉螺号”潜入水下。我和康塞尔、尼德·兰德在客厅舷窗前各就各位；尼摩船长进舵手室与舵手会合，要将机器用作杀伤的工具。不久我觉得螺旋桨搏动加快，船速也提高了。“鹦鹉螺号”赶到时，抹香鲸和南方鲸的战斗已经开始。这头新的怪兽插入战阵，它们起先并未显出惧怕，不久却非提防它的冲撞不可。
好一场厮杀！“鹦鹉螺号”整艘化作一柄可怕的捕鲸叉，由船长的手挥动。它猛然投向血肉之躯，从这一侧贯穿到另一侧，只留下动物颤抖的两半。鲸尾猛烈地击打船舷，它几乎没有感觉；它自己冲上去的撞击，似乎也并没多大感受。杀掉一头抹香鲸，立刻又去冲下一头。为使猎物不致落空，它原地调转方向，忽进忽退，听舵灵便。鲸潜水，它也跟着下潜；鲸浮出，它也一同上升。迎头去撞也好，横侧去击也好，以任何速度、从任何方向切割撕裂，用可怕的撞角穿透。何等的屠杀！浪面何等的喧腾！这些发怒的动物特有的尖嘶和喷鼻之声，又是何等刺耳！在这片平日如此安宁的水域，它们挥舞的尾巴掀起真正的巨浪。
整整一个钟头，这场无从逃脱的大屠杀持续着。好几次，有十来头合到一起，要靠体重压碎“鹦鹉螺号”。从舷窗望出去，我们看得见它们嵌着长牙的巨口，看得见它们吓人的眼睛。尼德·兰德控制不住，向它们挥拳，冲它们咒骂。那些大家伙紧咬着我们的船，好像林中的一群狗围咬一头野猪，我们能感觉得到。可是“鹦鹉螺号”仍开着螺旋桨，它们再沉，施在船身上的力再大，也只能给它带着东奔西走，或者给带到海洋的上层。
终于，抹香鲸的阵势溃散了。水面平息，我们往上浮去。舱口开了，我们飞奔到平台上。海面上到处是残缺的尸体。就算发生一场可怕的爆炸，这些血肉也不能给分裂、撕碎得更猛烈了。巨尸之间，我们缓缓浮行。它们背部发蓝、腹部苍白，身上突着巨大的瘤块。几头受了惊的抹香鲸正在向地平线逃去。方圆几英里的海浪全被染红了。“鹦鹉螺号”浮在一片血海中。尼摩船长过来同我们站到一处。

英文证据: I feared he would commit some act of violence, which would end in sad consequences. But his anger was turned by the sight of a whale which the _Nautilus_ had just come up with. The creature had not quite escaped from the cachalot’s teeth. I recognised the southern whale by its flat head, which is entirely black. Anatomically, it is distinguished from the white whale and the North Cape whale by the seven cervical vertebrae, and it has two more ribs than its congeners. The unfortunate cetacean was lying on its side, riddled with holes from the bites, and quite dead. From its mutilated fin still hung a young whale which it could not save from the massacre. Its open mouth let the water flow in and out, murmuring like the waves breaking on the shore. Captain Nemo steered close to the corpse of the creature. Two of his men mounted its side, and I saw, not without surprise, that they were drawing from its breasts all the milk which they contained, that is to say, about two or three tons. The Captain offered me a cup of the milk, which was still warm. I could not help showing my repugnance to the drink; but he assured me that it was excellent, and not to be distinguished from cow’s milk. I tasted it, and was of his opinion. It was a useful reserve to us, for in the shape of salt butter or cheese it would form an agreeable variety from our ordinary food. From that day I noticed with uneasiness that Ned Land’s ill-will towards Captain Nemo increased, and I resolved to watch the Canadian’s gestures closely.
原译: 我担心他会犯下某种暴力行为，结果将悲惨地结束。但他的愤怒被一只鲸鱼的目光所驱散鹦鹉螺号刚刚发现了它。怪物并没有从卡恰洛的牙齿里逃出来。我用平头认出了南鲸完全黑了。从解剖学上讲，它与白鲸和北开普鲸有7个宫颈脊椎的区别，比同族体多两根肋骨。不幸的鲸目动物躺在它的侧面，满是洞从咬，和相当死亡。一只年轻的鲸鱼被断裂的鳍吊起来无法幸免大屠杀。它张开的嘴让水流进进出出像海浪在岸上破裂一样低语。尼摩船长靠近那生物的尸体。他的两个手下架起侧面，我毫不惊讶地看到，他们从乳房里抽出所有牛奶，也就是说，大约两到三吨。船长给我一杯牛奶，它还是热的。我忍不住要展示我对饮料的厌恶；但他向我保证，饮料是极好的，不能与牛奶区分开来。我尝过，也是他的看法。对我们而言，它是一个有用的保留地，因为以盐黄油或奶酪的形式，它会形成一种与我们普通食物相容的品种。从那天起，我不安地注意到尼德·兰德对尼摩船长的恶意增加，我决心密切注视加拿大人的姿态。
现译:
我担心他会做出激烈行为，酿成悲剧。但有一头鲸的景象转移了这场怒火。“鹦鹉螺号”刚驶到它旁边。那动物终究没能完全逃过抹香鲸的利齿。我凭它扁平、通黑的头认出是南方鲸。按解剖构造，它的七节颈椎可以同白鲸和北角鲸区别开来，肋骨又比那些近亲多两根。这头不幸的鲸侧身漂着，周身让撕咬穿出了许多洞，已经死透。残损的鳍上还贴着一头幼鲸，它终究没能把孩子从屠杀中救出来。大嘴张着，水流进又流出，低低作响，像波浪在岸上拍碎。
尼摩船长使船贴近尸身。两名船员爬上鲸的侧腹。我惊奇地发现，他们正从它乳腺里汲取全部乳汁，约有两三吨。船长递给我一杯，奶尚有余温。我忍不住露出对这饮料的厌恶，他却向我保证味道极好，跟牛奶分不出来。我尝了尝，倒也认同他的见解。这对我们是一份有用的储备，做成咸黄油或奶酪，便能使每日的伙食添点称心的变化。从这天开始，我不安地看出尼德·兰德对尼摩船长的敌意正在加深，于是下决心，仔细留心加拿大人的一举一动。

中文章名: 下部 / 第13章　冰山
英文证据: The _Nautilus_ was steadily pursuing its southerly course, following the fiftieth meridian with considerable speed. Did he wish to reach the pole? I did not think so, for every attempt to reach that point had hitherto failed. Again, the season was far advanced, for in the Antarctic regions the 13th of March corresponds with the 13th of September of northern regions, which begin at the equinoctial season. On the 14th of March I saw floating ice in latitude 55°, merely pale bits of debris from twenty to twenty-five feet long, forming banks over which the sea curled. The _Nautilus_ remained on the surface of the ocean. Ned Land, who had fished in the Arctic Seas, was familiar with its icebergs; but Conseil and I admired them for the first time. In the atmosphere towards the southern horizon stretched a white dazzling band. English whalers have given it the name of “ice blink.” However thick the clouds may be, it is always visible, and announces the presence of an ice pack or bank. Accordingly, larger blocks soon appeared, whose brilliancy changed with the caprices of the fog. Some of these masses showed green veins, as if long undulating lines had been traced with sulphate of copper; others resembled enormous amethysts with the light shining through them. Some reflected the light of day upon a thousand crystal facets. Others shaded with vivid calcareous reflections resembled a perfect town of marble. The more we neared the south the more these floating islands increased both in number and importance.
原译: 鹦鹉螺号以相当快的速度沿着第50度线稳步向南前进。他想要到电线杆吗？我不这么认为，因为迄今为达到这一点所作的一切努力都失败了。南极地区3月13日与北方地区9月13日相对应，从季季开始，因此，季节也大大加快。3月14日，我看到纬度55度的浮冰，仅仅从20英尺到25英尺的微小碎片，形成海卷起的河岸。鹦鹉螺号留在海洋表面。在北极海域捕鱼的尼德·兰德熟悉其冰山；但是，我和康塞尔首次钦佩这些冰山。在向南地平线的大气中展露出一个白色的光芒。英国捕鲸者把它命名为“冰眨眼。”不论云层多厚，它总是可见的，并宣布存在一个冰块或银行。因此，大块块很快出现，其光彩随着雾的热潮而改变。其中一些物质表现出绿色的静脉，仿佛长长的无线线是用铜硫酸盐追踪的；另一些物质则类似于巨大的含硫酸盐，其光线照亮。有些反射着光芒出现在千晶面上。其他人的阴暗的阴暗的反射仿佛一个完美的大理石城。我们越接近南方，这些漂浮岛屿的数量和重要性都越大。
现译: “鹦鹉螺号”沿第五十度经线以相当快的速度稳稳南行。船长真想抵达南极？我不这么以为，因为此前每一次前往极点的尝试都失败了。何况季节已经很晚。南极地区的三月十三日，相当于北方的九月十三日，已是秋分前后的时节。三月十四日，在南纬五十五度，我看见了浮冰。最先只是些苍白的碎片，长二十至二十五英尺，聚成一片片小冰滩，浪头在上面卷起。“鹦鹉螺号”仍停在海面。尼德·兰德曾在北冰洋捕鲸，冰山是他的熟相识；我和康塞尔却是第一次欣赏。南方地平线上空横着一道耀眼的白带。英国捕鲸人给它取名“冰光”。云再厚也能望见，它预告着浮冰群或冰岸的存在。果然，很快就出现了更大的冰块，光彩随雾气的无常变化。有的冰体带着绿色纹脉，像有人用硫酸铜描上长长的波纹；有的像硕大的紫水晶，透着光。有些冰在成千上万的晶面上反射日光。有的在明亮的白垩色光影中深浅错落，简直像一座大理石的城市。越向南行，这些漂浮的岛屿不但数量增多，体积也越来越大。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

英文证据: At 60° lat. every pass had disappeared. But, seeking carefully, Captain Nemo soon found a narrow opening, through which he boldly slipped, knowing, however, that it would close behind him. Thus, guided by this clever hand, the _Nautilus_ passed through all the ice with a precision which quite charmed Conseil; icebergs or mountains, ice-fields or smooth plains, seeming to have no limits, drift-ice or floating ice-packs, plains broken up, called palchs when they are circular, and streams when they are made up of long strips. The temperature was very low; the thermometer exposed to the air marked 2 deg. or 3° below zero, but we were warmly clad with fur, at the expense of the sea-bear and seal. The interior of the _Nautilus_, warmed regularly by its electric apparatus, defied the most intense cold. Besides, it would only have been necessary to go some yards beneath the waves to find a more bearable temperature. Two months earlier we should have had perpetual daylight in these latitudes; but already we had had three or four hours of night, and by and by there would be six months of darkness in these circumpolar regions. On the 15th of March we were in the latitude of New Shetland and South Orkney. The Captain told me that formerly numerous tribes of seals inhabited them; but that English and American whalers, in their rage for destruction, massacred both old and young; thus, where there was once life and animation, they had left silence and death.

英文证据: About eight o’clock on the morning of the 16th of March the _Nautilus_, following the fifty-fifth meridian, cut the Antarctic polar circle. Ice surrounded us on all sides, and closed the horizon. But Captain Nemo went from one opening to another, still going higher. I cannot express my astonishment at the beauties of these new regions. The ice took most surprising forms. Here the grouping formed an oriental town, with innumerable mosques and minarets; there a fallen city thrown to the earth, as it were, by some convulsion of nature. The whole aspect was constantly changed by the oblique rays of the sun, or lost in the greyish fog amidst hurricanes of snow. Detonations and falls were heard on all sides, great overthrows of icebergs, which altered the whole landscape like a diorama. Often seeing no exit, I thought we were definitely prisoners; but, instinct guiding him at the slightest indication, Captain Nemo would discover a new pass. He was never mistaken when he saw the thin threads of bluish water trickling along the ice-fields; and I had no doubt that he had already ventured into the midst of these Antarctic seas before. On the 16th of March, however, the ice-fields absolutely blocked our road. It was not the iceberg itself, as yet, but vast fields cemented by the cold. But this obstacle could not stop Captain Nemo: he hurled himself against it with frightful violence. The _Nautilus_ entered the brittle mass like a wedge, and split it with frightful crackings. It was the battering ram of the ancients hurled by infinite strength. The ice, thrown high in the air, fell like hail around us. By its own power of impulsion our apparatus made a canal for itself; some times carried away by its own impetus, it lodged on the ice-field, crushing it with its weight, and sometimes buried beneath it, dividing it by a simple pitching movement, producing large rents in it. Violent gales assailed us at this time, accompanied by thick fogs, through which, from one end of the platform to the other, we could see nothing. The wind blew sharply from all parts of the compass, and the snow lay in such hard heaps that we had to break it with blows of a pickaxe. The temperature was always at 5 deg. below zero; every outward part of the _Nautilus_ was covered with ice. A rigged vessel would have been entangled in the blocked up gorges. A vessel without sails, with electricity for its motive power, and wanting no coal, could alone brave such high latitudes. At length, on the 18th of March, after many useless assaults, the _Nautilus_ was positively blocked. It was no longer either streams, packs, or ice-fields, but an interminable and immovable barrier, formed by mountains soldered together.
原译: 3月16日早上八点左右南瓜特卢斯在第五十五度后切断了南极极圈。冰环绕着我们四面并关闭了地平线。但尼摩船长从一个开口跑到另一个开口还在往上爬。我不能对这些新区域的美貌表示惊讶。冰层呈现出令人吃惊的形式。这群人在这里组成了一个东方城镇，有许多清真寺和尖塔；一个城市倒塌，象它一样，由于自然的震动而倒塌。整个方面都因太阳的斜线而不断改变，或者在暴风雪中灰雾中消失。到处都听到爆炸声和瀑布声冰山被大肆推翻整个地貌都变了。通常看不到出口，我以为我们绝对是囚犯但是，本能的指引他丝毫的暗示，尼摩船长会发现新的通行证。他从没有错过，他看到冰块上流着薄薄的水线；我毫不怀疑，他以前曾冒险进入这些南极海洋。然而在3月16日冰原完全封锁了我们的道路。现在不是冰山本身而是被寒冷凝固的大片土地。但这个障碍无法阻止尼摩船长：他以可怕的暴力向尼摩船长投掷自己。鹦鹉螺号像一个小矮人一样进入了小矮人体内并用可怕的裂缝把它分割开来。这是古代人被无穷力量所驱赶的撞击性公羊。冰块在空中飘浮落得像冰雹般。我们的机器靠自己冲动的力量为自己制造了一条运河；有时它被自己的动力冲走了，它沉到冰地上，用它的重量压碎它，有时埋在冰地下面，被一个简单的投球运动分割开来，产生巨大的租金。暴力的暴风雪伴随着浓雾从平台的一端到另一端我们什么都看不见。风从罗盘的每个部分急剧吹散，雪堆如此坚硬的堆积，我们不得不打破它由一粒摘轴的打击。温度总是在5度。不到零；鹦鹉螺的每一个外部都覆盖着冰。被操纵的船会被困在峡谷里。一艘没有船帆的船拥有动力的电力并且不需要煤炭能够单枪匹马地勇敢地走这么高的纬度。3月18日，在经过许多无谓的攻击后，鹦鹉螺号号遭到积极封锁。它不再是溪流，包，或冰地，而是由山脉叠合而成的永恒和不可移动的屏障。
现译:
三月十六日上午约八点，“鹦鹉螺号”沿第五十五度经线越过南极圈。四面为冰所围，天边也被封闭。但尼摩船长从一道缺口找到另一道缺口，仍向更高纬度挺进。这陌生地区的美叫我惊异到无从形容。冰块结成最出奇的形态。这一堆像东方城市，清真寺和宣礼塔多得数不过来；那一丛像一座倾覆的城池，仿佛一场自然界的痉挛将它推倒在地。太阳斜射，整幅图画随时都给改了一副面貌，又会在雪暴之中隐没于灰蒙蒙的雾气里。四下响着爆裂和崩坠的声音。大冰山一翻，整片风景便被改换，像活动景片换了一幕。经常眼看找不到出口，我以为我们已彻底成了囚徒，尼摩船长却能凭一点点征兆，让直觉领他找出新通路。他从来没有看错过冰原上蜿蜒而行的细线般的蓝水。我毫不怀疑，他从前已经冒险进入过这些南极海域。
然而就在三月十六日，冰原终于将道路完全封住了。还不是冰山本身横在面前，而是一片又一片叫严寒黏合起来的广大冰原。这个障碍却仍挡不住尼摩船长。他以吓人的猛劲冲上去。“鹦鹉螺号”像楔子那样插入易脆的冰体，在可怕的劈啪声中豁开一条口子。活像古人的攻城槌，有无穷的力量将它掷出。冰给掀到半空，雹子似的掉在我们周围。我们这台机器只凭冲劲，竟给自己开出一条航道。有时被自己的冲力推得骑上冰原，用体重把冰压碎；有时又一头钻到冰底，船首只须上下点动，便将冰分开，造成宽大的裂缝。
这当口，我们同时遭到狂风和浓雾的袭击，从平台的一头向另一头，竟看不见东西。风从罗盘的各个方向凶猛地吹，积雪堆得硬实，非用十字镐才能敲开。气温始终在零下五度，“鹦鹉螺号”露在外面的每一处都封了冰。寻常装帆挂索的船，必定会在堵塞的冰峡里缠得动弹不得。只有不用帆、不用煤、以电力推动的船才能在这样高的纬度冒险。终于到了三月十八日，在一次次冲击都无结果以后，“鹦鹉螺号”真正给堵住了。面前已不是条状浮冰、冰群或冰原，而是一道看不到尽头、也推不动的屏障，整座整座冰山焊成了一体。

The sun appearing for an instant at noon, Captain Nemo took an observation as near as possible, which gave our situation at 51° 30′ long. and 67° 39′ of S. lat. We had advanced one degree more in this Antarctic region. Of the liquid surface of the sea there was no longer a glimpse. Under the spur of the _Nautilus_ lay stretched a vast plain, entangled with confused blocks. Here and there sharp points and slender needles rising to a height of 200 feet; further on a steep shore, hewn as it were with an axe and clothed with greyish tints; huge mirrors, reflecting a few rays of sunshine, half drowned in the fog. And over this desolate face of nature a stern silence reigned, scarcely broken by the flapping of the wings of petrels and puffins. Everything was frozen—even the noise. The _Nautilus_ was then obliged to stop in its adventurous course amid these fields of ice. In spite of our efforts, in spite of the powerful means employed to break up the ice, the _Nautilus_ remained immovable. Generally, when we can proceed no further, we have return still open to us; but here return was as impossible as advance, for every pass had closed behind us; and for the few moments when we were stationary, we were likely to be entirely blocked, which did indeed happen about two o’clock in the afternoon, the fresh ice forming around its sides with astonishing rapidity. I was obliged to admit that Captain Nemo was more than imprudent. I was on the platform at that moment. The Captain had been observing our situation for some time past, when he said to me:

L. 。 。 。我们在这个南极地区取得了更高一等的成绩。海洋的液体表面不再有一瞥。在鹦鹉螺的刺激下伸展了一片广阔的平原与混杂的石块纠缠在一起。这里和那里有尖点和细针，高到200英尺；在陡峭的海岸上，用斧头和灰色的灰色色色色衣服割下母鸡；巨大的镜子，反映几条阳光，一半被雾淹没。在这种荒凉的自然面容上严酷的沉默统治着很少被海燕和海绵的翅膀打碎。所有的东西都被冻住了甚至噪音。鹦鹉螺号被迫在这些冰层中停止冒险。尽管我们作出了努力，尽管为打破冰层采取了强有力的手段，但鹦鹉螺河仍然是不可移动的。一般来说，当我们无法继续前进时，我们仍然可以返回；但是，这里的返回是不可能的，因为每一个通道都关闭在我们身后；在我们处于静止状态的片刻，我们很可能完全被封锁，而下午两点左右确实发生了这种情况，在冰面两侧以惊人的速度形成新的冰块。我不得不承认尼摩船长不仅仅是轻率。我当时在平台上。船长观察我们的情况已经有一段时间了当他对我说：
现译:
我知道，在尼德·兰德和我们之前所有海员的眼里，这都是无法越过的一道障碍。正午太阳露了片刻。尼摩船长尽可能准确地作了观测，得知船位是经度五十一度三十分、南纬六十七度三十九分。我们在南极地区又深入了一度。液态的海面一眼也看不见。“鹦鹉螺号”的撞角底下，延伸着一片巨大的平原，杂乱的冰块交结在一起。这里那里，有尖峰和冰针伸上两百英尺高空；更远是一处斧削般的陡岸，披着灰影；又有些巨镜，将半淹在雾里的几缕日光反射回来。大自然这一派荒寒面容上，笼罩着严厉的寂静，偶尔才被海燕和海鹦扑动翅膀的声音打破。一切都冻住了，连声音都像结了冰。
“鹦鹉螺号”这时不得不停下冰原间的冒险行程。不管我们怎样努力，采用多么强有力的破冰手段，它还是纹丝不动。平常前面走不通，总还容得下往回走，可在这里后退和前进一样不可能，因为来路上每一道水隙都已在身后关闭。只消停驻片刻，我们就可能被完全封死。下午约两点，事情真就如此发生了。新冰以惊人的速度，在船的四周合拢。我不得不承认，尼摩船长已不是“不够谨慎”这几个字就能形容的了。当时我正在平台上。船长注视我们的处境已有一阵，忽然向我开了口。

英文证据: Yes, I knew that. I knew that this man was bold, even to rashness. 中文章名: 下部 / 第13章　冰山

The weather was clear, the atmosphere pure enough, the cold very great, being 12° below zero; but, the wind having gone down, this temperature was not so unbearable. The operation was quickly performed, for the fresh ice was still very thin. We all went below. The usual reservoirs were filled with the newly-liberated water, and the _Nautilus_ soon descended. I had taken my place with Conseil in the saloon; through the open window we could see the lower beds of the Southern Ocean. The thermometer went up, the needle of the compass deviated on the dial. At about 900 feet, as Captain Nemo had foreseen, we were floating beneath the undulating bottom of the iceberg. But the _Nautilus_ went lower still—it went to the depth of four hundred fathoms. Our pace was rapid; we could feel it by the quivering of the long steel body. About two in the morning I took some hours’ repose, and Conseil did the same. In crossing the waist I did not meet Captain Nemo: I supposed him to be in the pilot’s cage. The next morning, the 19th of March, I took my post once more in the saloon. The electric log told me that the speed of the _Nautilus_ had been slackened. It was then going towards the surface; but prudently emptying its reservoirs very slowly. My heart beat fast. Were we going to emerge and regain the open polar atmosphere? No! A shock told me that the _Nautilus_ had struck the bottom of the iceberg, still very thick, judging from the deadened sound. We had in deed “struck,” to use a sea expression, but in an inverse sense, and at a thousand feet deep. This would give three thousand feet of ice above us; one thousand being above the water-mark. The iceberg was then higher than at its borders—not a very reassuring fact. Several times that day the _Nautilus_ tried again, and every time it struck the wall which lay like a ceiling above it. Sometimes it met with but 900 yards, only 200 of which rose above the surface. It was twice the height it was when the _Nautilus_ had gone under the waves. I carefully noted the different depths, and thus obtained a submarine profile of the chain as it was developed under the water. That night no change had taken place in our situation. Still ice between four and five hundred yards in depth! It was evidently diminishing, but, still, what a thickness between us and the surface of the ocean! It was then eight. According to the daily custom on board the _Nautilus_, its air should have been renewed four hours ago; but I did not suffer much, although Captain Nemo had not yet made any demand upon his reserve of oxygen. My sleep was painful that night; hope and fear besieged me by turns: I rose several times. The groping of the _Nautilus_ continued. About three in the morning, I noticed that the lower surface of the iceberg was only about fifty feet deep. One hundred and fifty feet now separated us from the surface of the waters. The iceberg was by degrees becoming an ice-field, the mountain a plain. My eyes never left the manometer. We were still rising diagonally to the surface, which sparkled under the electric rays. The iceberg was stretching both above and beneath into lengthening slopes; mile after mile it was getting thinner. At length, at six in the morning of that memorable day, the 19th of March, the door of the saloon opened, and Captain Nemo appeared.
原译: 晚上有一段时间情况很新奇把我们关在窗户边。海洋是用电灯照亮的；但是它却被遗弃了；这些被囚禁的水域里没有鱼逗留；它们只找到一条通道，从南极海洋带它们到开阔的极海。我们的步伐很快，我们从长钢体的颤抖中可以感觉到它。大约凌晨两点我休息了几个小时康塞尔也做了同样的事。越过腰部时，我没有见到尼摩船长：我以为他是在飞行员的笼子里。第二天早上，即3月19日，我再次在酒馆任职。电线记录告诉我鹦鹉螺号的速度已经减慢了。然后，它朝向表面，但谨慎地将其水库清空得非常缓慢。我的心跳得飞快。我们是不是要浮出水面重获开阔的极地大气？不！不！不！不！No！惊吓告诉我鹦鹉螺已经击中了冰山底部仍然很厚从死声来看。我们用“击落”来表达海洋，但从反面来说，在千尺深处。这能给我们三千英尺高的冰能在水印上加一千英尺高。冰山当时比边界高 -- -- 并不是一个非常令人欣慰的事实。那天，鹦鹉螺再次试了几次，每次撞到墙上，墙上像天花板一样。有时遇到900码，其中只有200码升到表面之上。这是鹦鹉螺号在海浪下高度的两倍。我仔细地注意到了不同的深度，并因此获得了海底的剖面图在水下开发。那天晚上，我们的情况没有变化。冰层在四五百码深之间！它显然在缩小，但是，我们和海洋表面之间的厚度仍然如此之大！那时是八岁。根据鹦鹉螺号号上每天的习惯，它的空气应在四小时前更新；但我没有遭受多大痛苦，尽管尼摩船长尚未对其氧气储备提出任何要求。那天晚上，我的睡眠很痛苦；希望和恐惧轮流缠着我：我升了好几圈。鹦鹉螺号人的摸索还在继续。大约凌晨三点，我注意到冰山下层只有50英尺深。150英尺的海面把我们分开了。冰山的冰山是冰原，变成冰原，山是平原。我的眼睛从来没有离开压力计。我们仍在对角上升地表，它在电光下点燃。冰山在上下伸展到延展的斜坡上；每英里的冰山越变越薄。长时间以来，在那个令人难忘的日子的早上6点，3月19日，酒馆的门打开了，尼摩船长就出现了。
现译:
夜里有好长一段，我们被处境的新奇吸引，舍不得离开窗口。海水给电灯照得明亮，却空空荡荡。鱼儿不栖身在这样受禁锢的海里，只是借它作一条通道，从南大洋游到开放的极地海洋中去。我们速度很快，长长的钢制船身发着颤，能感觉得出。凌晨约两点，我才去休息几个钟头，康塞尔也一样。经过船腰通道时，我没有遇见尼摩船长，猜他在舵手室里。
次日，三月十九日早晨，我又回到客厅里自己的岗位。电动计程仪告诉我，“鹦鹉螺号”已减速。它正朝水面升去，不过极为谨慎，水舱里的水一点点才抽出。我的心怦怦跳。我们要冲出水面，重新呼吸极地开放的空气了吗？不！一次撞击告诉我，“鹦鹉螺号”碰到了冰山的底面。撞声沉闷，那冰想来仍很厚。照水手的说法，我们的确“触礁”了，却是颠倒着触的礁，而且在一千英尺深处。照这个算法，我们头顶上方有三千英尺的冰，其中一千英尺在水线以上。冰山在这里比边缘还高，这可不是令人安心的事。
那天“鹦鹉螺号”又试过几回，每一次都撞上那道天花板一样盖在头顶的墙。有时量得冰厚只有九百码，露出水面的只占两百码。它的高度已是“鹦鹉螺号”下潜之初的两倍。我把每一次测得的深度仔细记下，竟能画出这道冰山链在水下起伏的剖面图。到了夜里，处境仍旧未变。冰层厚度还有四五百码！分明是在减薄，可我们与洋面之间，依旧隔着那么厚的一层！
当时是八点。按“鹦鹉螺号”平时的习惯，早在四个钟头以前就该换气。虽然船长还没动用储氧，我倒也没有觉得十分难受。这一夜我睡得很苦，希望和恐惧轮番围攻，好几次爬起身。“鹦鹉螺号”一路摸索着。凌晨约三点，我留意到冰底伸下去已只有约五十英尺。现在我们与海面之间隔着一百五十英尺。冰山渐变为冰原，高山渐变为平地。我的眼睛一刻不离压力计。我们仍斜向上升，接近电光下闪亮的表面。冰的上下两面都延伸成越来越长的缓坡，每过一英里，厚度便又减一点。终于，在那值得纪念的三月十九日早晨六点，客厅的门开了，尼摩船长出现。

英文证据: I rushed on to the platform. Yes! the open sea, with but a few scattered pieces of ice and moving icebergs—a long stretch of sea; a world of birds in the air, and myriads of fishes under those waters, which varied from intense blue to olive green, according to the bottom. The thermometer marked 3° C. above zero. It was comparatively spring, shut up as we were behind this iceberg, whose lengthened mass was dimly seen on our northern horizon.

英文证据: About ten miles south a solitary island rose to a height of one hundred and four yards. We made for it, but carefully, for the sea might be strewn with banks. One hour afterwards we had reached it, two hours later we had made the round of it. It measured four or five miles in circumference. A narrow canal separated it from a considerable stretch of land, perhaps a continent, for we could not see its limits. The existence of this land seemed to give some colour to Maury’s theory. The ingenious American has remarked that, between the South Pole and the sixtieth parallel, the sea is covered with floating ice of enormous size, which is never met with in the North Atlantic. From this fact he has drawn the conclusion that the Antarctic Circle encloses considerable continents, as icebergs cannot form in open sea, but only on the coasts. According to these calculations, the mass of ice surrounding the southern pole forms a vast cap, the circumference of which must be, at least, 2,500 miles. But the _Nautilus_, for fear of running aground, had stopped about three cable-lengths from a strand over which reared a superb heap of rocks. The boat was launched; the Captain, two of his men, bearing instruments, Conseil, and myself were in it. It was ten in the morning. I had not seen Ned Land. 原译: 孤岛以南大约十英里升至104码高地。我为它做了，但小心，因为海洋可能堆满了银行。一个小时后我们到达了它，两个小时后我们完成了它的回合。它测量了四五英里的环形。一条狭窄的运河将它与相当大片的土地，或许是一个大陆分隔开来，因为我们看不到它的极限。这片土地的存在似乎使莫里理论有些色彩。聪明的美国人说，在南极和60度平行之间，海洋被巨大的浮冰覆盖，北大西洋从未遇到过这种冰块。从这一事实中他得出的结论是，南极圈覆盖着相当多的大陆，因为冰山不可能在公海形成，而只能形成在海岸上。根据这些计算，南极周围的冰块形成一个巨大的盖子，其环绕范围必须至少2 500英里。但鹦鹉螺由于害怕落地已经从一股长约三根电缆支撑了一大堆岩石。船已经开动了船长和他的两个手下带着仪器康塞尔和我。那天早上十点。我没见过尼德·兰德。毫无疑问，加拿大人不愿意承认南极的存在。划了几下船桨把我们带到沙滩上我们上岸了。我把他挡在后面的时候康塞尔要跳到陆地上去。
现译: 南边大约十英里处，一座孤岛耸立在海上，高一百零四码。我们朝它驶去，走得很小心，因为海里可能到处有浅滩。一小时后，我们到达岛边。又过两小时，我们已经绕岛一周。岛的周长四五英里，一道窄水道把它同一大片陆地隔开。那也许是块大陆，因为我们根本望不到它的尽头。这片陆地的存在，似乎给莫里的学说添了一点依据。那位颇有见地的美国人曾经指出，南极点到南纬六十度之间，海上遍布巨大浮冰，北大西洋却看不到那种规模。他由此推断，南极圈内一定有相当广阔的大陆，因为冰山只能沿海岸形成，不能在外海中凭空长出来。照这样推算，南极四周的冰体构成一个巨大的冰盖，周长至少有二千五百英里。“鹦鹉螺号”怕搁浅，在离海滩约三链的地方停下。滩头耸立着壮观的石堆。小艇放下水去，船长、两个携带仪器的船员、康塞尔和我都坐了进去。那时是上午十点。我没见着尼德·兰德，想必这加拿大人不肯承认脚下当真有个南极点。几桨划去，小艇直上沙滩。康塞尔正要跳上陆地，我伸手拉住了他。

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极
英文证据: I landed, followed by Conseil, leaving the two men in the boat. For a long way the soil was composed of a reddish sandy stone, something like crushed brick, scoriae, streams of lava, and pumice-stones. One could not mistake its volcanic origin. In some parts, slight curls of smoke emitted a sulphurous smell, proving that the internal fires had lost nothing of their expansive powers, though, having climbed a high acclivity, I could see no volcano for a radius of several miles. We know that in those Antarctic countries, James Ross found two craters, the Erebus and Terror, in full activity, on the 167th meridian, latitude 77° 32′. The vegetation of this desolate continent seemed to me much restricted. Some lichens lay upon the black rocks; some microscopic plants, rudimentary diatomas, a kind of cells placed between two quartz shells; long purple and scarlet weed, supported on little swimming bladders, which the breaking of the waves brought to the shore. These constituted the meagre flora of this region. The shore was strewn with molluscs, little mussels, and limpets. I also saw myriads of northern clios, one-and-a-quarter inches long, of which a whale would swallow a whole world at a mouthful; and some perfect sea-butterflies, animating the waters on the skirts of the shore.
原译: 我降落了之后是康塞尔将两个人留在船上。土壤由一块红沙石组成像是碎砖、石灰、熔岩流和石块。人们不能误判其火山起源。在某些地方，微小的烟卷释放出硫气味，证明内部大火没有失去任何扩张力，不过，在攀升高度的广度之后，我可以看到半径数英里的火山。我们知道，在南极国家，詹姆斯·罗斯发现两个弹坑，埃雷布斯和恐怖号，在北纬77度32分的第167度间距上充分活动。在我看来，这片荒凉的大陆的植被似乎非常有限。一些地衣落在黑石上；一些微小植物，原始的地表，一种放在两个石英壳之间的细胞；长紫色和红色的杂草，用小游泳囊支撑，波浪的破碎将之带到海岸。这些植物是该地区微薄的植物。岸上满是软体动物小贝类和瘸子。我还看到了无数的北冰洋长一英寸和四分之一英寸鲸鱼会吞下一个满嘴的整个世界。
现译: 我上了岸，康塞尔随后，那两个水手留在小艇里。很长一段地面全由微红的砂岩构成，像是碎砖，另有火山渣、一道道凝固的熔岩和浮石。这里出于火山作用，一望即知。有些地方冒着几缕带硫黄味的轻烟，足以证明地下的火仍蕴着当初向外喷发的力量。可是我登上一处高坡，放眼周围几英里内，却看不见火山。我们知道，詹姆斯·罗斯曾在南极一带、东经一百六十七度、南纬七十七度三十二分的地方，发现过两个正在活动的火山口，即埃里伯斯和特罗尔。这片荒凉大陆的植物，在我看来实在有限。黑岩上附着些地衣，另有几种显微镜下才看得见的植物，是些结构简单的硅藻，仿佛细胞夹在两片石英质的壳中；还有紫色和猩红色的长藻，靠小浮囊托起，被浪花推上岸。这便是此地稀薄的植物面貌。滩上散布着软体动物，小小的贻贝和帽贝。我还见到成千上万的北方裸海蝶，每个一又四分之一英寸长，鲸只消一口就能吞去整整一个世界。近岸的水中还有真正如蝶的翼足类，将一带海水点缀得生意盎然。

英文证据: There appeared on the high bottoms some coral shrubs, of the kind which, according to James Ross, live in the Antarctic seas to the depth of more than 1,000 yards. Then there were little kingfishers and starfish studding the soil. But where life abounded most was in the air. There thousands of birds fluttered and flew of all kinds, deafening us with their cries; others crowded the rock, looking at us as we passed by without fear, and pressing familiarly close by our feet. There were penguins, so agile in the water, heavy and awkward as they are on the ground; they were uttering harsh cries, a large assembly, sober in gesture, but extravagant in clamour. Albatrosses passed in the air, the expanse of their wings being at least four yards and a half, and justly called the vultures of the ocean; some gigantic petrels, and some damiers, a kind of small duck, the underpart of whose body is black and white; then there were a whole series of petrels, some whitish, with brown-bordered wings, others blue, peculiar to the Antarctic seas, and so oily, as I told Conseil, that the inhabitants of the Ferroe Islands had nothing to do before lighting them but to put a wick in.
原译: 在海底出现了一些珊瑚灌木詹姆斯·罗斯说，这种灌木生活在南极海深达一千码。然后有小海王鱼和海星挖土。但生命中最繁忙的地方却在空中。成千上万的鸟儿在飞动和飞动，用他们的呼喊使我们震耳欲聋；其他人挤满了岩石，看着我们无所畏惧地经过，并熟悉地紧紧地靠着我们的脚。有企鹅，在水中如此敏捷，沉重的和尴尬的，因为他们在地面上；他们大声地喊叫，一个巨大的集合，清醒的手势，却在大声地叫喊。信天翁在空中飞过，翅膀的宽度至少是四码半，并被正确地称为海洋秃鹫；一些巨大的海燕，和一些达米埃人，一种小鸭子，以棕色边框的翅膀其他蓝色的南极海域特有的和如此油腻，正如我告诉康塞尔。
现译: 浅水处的海底，冒出一些灌木般的珊瑚。据詹姆斯·罗斯说，这类珊瑚生活在南极海中，深处可到一千多码。又有小翠鸟，海星则星星点点，撒满地面。但最具生气的地方还在空中。各种各样的鸟，有成千只在那里振翅飞舞，叫得我们耳朵发聋。还有些挤满岩石，见我们经过也不害怕，反倒很熟络地挤到脚边。企鹅在地上笨拙沉重，入了水却那么灵活。它们聚成一大群，动作庄重不多，发出的刺耳叫嚷可一点也不肯节省。信天翁掠过天空，双翼展开至少四码半，无怪人们叫它海洋的秃鹫。也有巨大的海燕，有名叫棋盘鸟的小鸭，身体下方黑白相间。再有各种海燕，有的微白，翼缘是棕色，有的是南极海域特有的蓝色品种。我告诉康塞尔，那些鸟油脂多到什么地步呢？在法罗群岛，人们要拿它们照明，只须添一根灯芯，划火点着就是了。

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极
英文证据: About half a mile farther on the soil was riddled with ruffs’ nests, a sort of laying-ground, out of which many birds were issuing. Captain Nemo had some hundreds hunted. They uttered a cry like the braying of an ass, were about the size of a goose, slate-colour on the body, white beneath, with a yellow line round their throats; they allowed themselves to be killed with a stone, never trying to escape. But the fog did not lift, and at eleven the sun had not yet shown itself. Its absence made me uneasy. Without it no observations were possible. How, then, could we decide whether we had reached the pole? When I rejoined Captain Nemo, I found him leaning on a piece of rock, silently watching the sky. He seemed impatient and vexed. But what was to be done? This rash and powerful man could not command the sun as he did the sea. Noon arrived without the orb of day showing itself for an instant. We could not even tell its position behind the curtain of fog; and soon the fog turned to snow.
原译: 土壤上大约半英里处满是蜂窝一种埋地很多鸟儿都从中发出来。尼摩船长猎杀过几百人。他们大喊大叫，就像屁股的胸罩一样，几乎是一只鹅的大小，身上的白色，下面是白的，喉咙上有一条黄线；他们任由自己被石头打死，从来不试图逃跑。但雾没起 11点太阳还没露出来。它的缺席让我不安。没有它，就不可能进行观察。那么，我们如何决定我们是否到达了极点？当我重新加入尼摩船长时我发现他躺在一块石头上静静地看着天空。他看起来急躁不安。但是该怎么做呢？这个暴躁又有权势的人无法像在海中一样指挥太阳。中午到达时，没有一天的球体显示自己一瞬间。我们甚至无法分辨出雾幕后面的位置，很快雾就变成雪。
现译: 再向前约半英里，地面布满流苏鹬的巢穴，好像一片产卵场，许多鸟正从里面钻出。尼摩船长让人猎取了几百只。它们叫得像驴嘶，个头跟鹅差不多，身披石板灰的羽毛，腹部白色，喉间围着一圈黄线。拿石头便能打死，竟不知要跑。雾却不散。十一点了，太阳还没露面。我为它迟迟不出着起急来。没有太阳便不能观测，我们靠什么来确定究竟到没到极点？我回到尼摩船长身边时，他正倚着一块岩石，默默望天，看来也有些不耐烦，有些烦恼。可又能怎么办？这人胆子再大，力量再强，也只能指挥大海，不能指挥太阳。正午到了，白日的光轮一瞬也没露。我们甚至辨不出它藏在雾幕后什么方位。没过多久，雾又变成了雪。

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极
英文证据: The tempest of snow continued till the next day. It was impossible to remain on the platform. From the saloon, where I was taking notes of incidents happening during this excursion to the polar continent, I could hear the cries of petrels and albatrosses sporting in the midst of this violent storm. The _Nautilus_ did not remain motionless, but skirted the coast, advancing ten miles more to the south in the half-light left by the sun as it skirted the edge of the horizon. The next day, the 20th of March, the snow had ceased. The cold was a little greater, the thermometer showing 2° below zero. The fog was rising, and I hoped that that day our observations might be taken. Captain Nemo not having yet appeared, the boat took Conseil and myself to land. The soil was still of the same volcanic nature; everywhere were traces of lava, scoriae, and basalt; but the crater which had vomited them I could not see. Here, as lower down, this continent was alive with myriads of birds. But their rule was now divided with large troops of sea-mammals, looking at us with their soft eyes. There were several kinds of seals, some stretched on the earth, some on flakes of ice, many going in and out of the sea. They did not flee at our approach, never having had anything to do with man; and I reckoned that there were provisions there for hundreds of vessels.
原译: 暴风雪持续到第二天。不可能留在平台上。从这个酒吧，我注意到了在这次极地大陆的探险中发生的事件，我能听到海燕和信天翁的呼喊声，在这场暴风雨中。鹦鹉螺号并不无动于衷，而是绕过海岸，在太阳绕过地平线边缘时，太阳的半光线向南推进了10英里。第二天，即3月20日，雪停了下来。温度计显示在零下2度以下。雾在上升，我希望那一天，我们的观察可以采取。尼摩船长还没出现船载我和康塞尔登陆。土壤仍然具有同样的火山性质；到处都是熔岩、石灰和巴萨尔特的痕迹；但是，我看不到那些呕吐的弹坑。这里，作为低端，这个大陆是活下来的无数的鸟类。但他们的统治现在被海哺乳动物的庞大部队所分割，以他们的柔软的眼睛看着我们。有几种海豹，有些在地球上伸展，有些在冰块上，许多进出海洋。他们没有在我们接近我们的时候逃跑，他们从未与人有任何关系；我估计那里有数百艘船。
现译: 暴雪下到次日。平台上没法立足。我在客厅里笔录这次南极大陆之行的见闻，从那里还能听见海燕和信天翁在暴风雪里嬉游的叫声。“鹦鹉螺号”并没有停着不动。太阳贴着地平线走过，剩下一点微光，船就在这微光中沿岸又往南驶了十英里。次日，三月二十日，雪停了。天气更冷了一点，温度计指在零下二度。雾正往上散，我盼着今天有望进行观测。尼摩船长还没出现，小艇便先送康塞尔和我上岸。地面依旧是火山造就的，到处是熔岩、火山渣和玄武岩的痕迹，唯独喷出这些东西的火山口，我无从看见。这里和下边那一带一样，陆上挤满了鸟。不过如今分掌地盘的还有一大群一大群海生哺乳动物，都用温和的眼睛望着我们。海豹有好几种，有的卧在地上，有的卧在浮冰上，许多在海里出出进进。我们走近也没惊走它们，这些动物根本没有跟人打过交道。我心里算了算，眼前这些就够几百艘船备足给养。

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极
英文证据: It was now eight in the morning. Four hours remained to us before the sun could be observed with advantage. I directed our steps towards a vast bay cut in the steep granite shore. There, I can aver that earth and ice were lost to sight by the numbers of sea-mammals covering them, and I involuntarily sought for old Proteus, the mythological shepherd who watched these immense flocks of Neptune. There were more seals than anything else, forming distinct groups, male and female, the father watching over his family, the mother suckling her little ones, some already strong enough to go a few steps. When they wished to change their place, they took little jumps, made by the contraction of their bodies, and helped awkwardly enough by their imperfect fin, which, as with the lamantin, their cousins, forms a perfect forearm. I should say that, in the water, which is their element—the spine of these creatures is flexible; with smooth and close skin and webbed feet—they swim admirably. In resting on the earth they take the most graceful attitudes. Thus the ancients, observing their soft and expressive looks, which cannot be surpassed by the most beautiful look a woman can give, their clear voluptuous eyes, their charming positions, and the poetry of their manners, metamorphosed them, the male into a triton and the female into a mermaid. I made Conseil notice the considerable development of the lobes of the brain in these interesting cetaceans. No mammal, except man, has such a quantity of brain matter; they are also capable of receiving a certain amount of education, are easily domesticated, and I think, with other naturalists, that if properly taught they would be of great service as fishing-dogs. The greater part of them slept on the rocks or on the sand. Amongst these seals, properly so called, which have no external ears (in which they differ from the otter, whose ears are prominent), I noticed several varieties of seals about three yards long, with a white coat, bulldog heads, armed with teeth in both jaws, four incisors at the top and four at the bottom, and two large canine teeth in the shape of a fleur-de-lis. Amongst them glided sea-elephants, a kind of seal, with short, flexible trunks. The giants of this species measured twenty feet round and ten yards and a half in length; but they did not move as we approached.
原译: 现在是早上八点。太阳在观察之前还剩下四小时。我将我们的脚步指向陡峭的花岗岩岸上的一个巨大的海湾。在那里，我可以肯定地说，由于覆盖着它们的海哺乳动物的数量，地球和冰失去了视线，我非自愿地寻找古老的普罗特斯，那个神话牧人，他看着海王星的庞大的群落。印章比其他任何东西都多，形成不同的群体，男性和女性，父亲照顾他的家人，母亲吸她的小的，有些已经足够强大能够走几步。当他们想换位的时候，他们通过身体的收缩略微跳跃，并且用不完美的鳍来帮助他们，和他们的表兄弟们一样，这形成了完美的前臂。我要说，在水中，这是它们元素 -- -- 这些生物的脊椎是灵活的；光滑和紧贴的皮肤和网床脚 -- -- 它们游得令人钦佩。沉睡在地上时，他们的态度最优雅。因此，古代人，观察他们的柔软和表情，无法超越一个女人最美的表情，他们清晰的挥发性的眼睛，他们的迷人姿势，和他们的诗歌他们的举止，改变他们，男性变成三重奏，女性变成美人鱼。我让康塞尔注意到这些有趣的鲸目动物大脑叶子的巨大发展。哺乳动物，除了人之外，都没有如此多的大脑物质；它们也能够接受一定程度的教育，很容易被驯化，而且我认为，与其他自然学家一起，如果适当教育它们，它们作为捕鱼犬将发挥很大的作用。大部分人睡在石头上或沙子上。这些封条，名副其实的，没有外耳( 与耳尖的水蚤不同，耳尖尖)，我注意到几种海豹，长约三码，白色大衣，牛头，配有牙齿的两头，顶部四口，底部四口，和两口大犬牙，形状像树脂脱脂。其中有滑翔的海象，一种海豹，短短的、灵活的内裤。这个物种的巨人测量了20英尺圆10码半的长度但它们没有在我们接近时移动。
现译: 这时才早晨八点。离观测太阳的好时辰还有四个钟头。我领着康塞尔往一道宽阔的海湾走，那湾深嵌在陡峭的花岗岩岸间。我敢说，到了那里，陆地也看不见，冰也看不见，统统让无数海生哺乳动物盖住了。我不由自主寻望起老普罗透斯来，神话里正是这位牧者看守海神涅普顿的浩大畜群。最多的还是海豹，雌雄自成一簇簇的家族，父亲守卫全家，母亲哺育幼儿，有几个小家伙已经强壮到能自己挪上几步。它们要换地方，就把身子一缩，一小跳一小跳地向前，笨拙地借发育不全的鳍帮忙。这鳍和它们的亲戚海牛一样，其实是一条完整的前肢。话虽这样，在水中——那才是它们的天地——它们脊骨柔韧，皮肤光滑紧密，脚有蹼，游起来妙极了。在陆地上休息时，姿态又那么优雅。难怪古人见了它们那温柔传情、连最美的女子也难以超越的目光，看见亮而妩媚的眼睛，迷人的姿势，富于诗意的举止，便把雄的想象成特里同海神，把雌的想象成人鱼。我还指给康塞尔看，这些有趣的鲸类动物，大脑的脑叶发育得多么充分。除了人，没有哪种哺乳动物有这么多脑质。它们也能受相当程度的教育，很容易驯养。我和另一些博物学家都以为，加以适当训练，它们一定很能充作帮人捕鱼的猎犬。大部分海豹睡在岩上或沙地上。真正的海豹没有外耳，和耳朵突出的水獭不同。我在其中认出几个品种，体长约三码，白毛，脑袋像斗牛犬，上下两颚都长着牙齿，上四枚门齿，下四枚门齿，又有两枚百合花形的大犬齿。象海豹也滑行在其间，这一类海豹长着短短的、灵活的鼻子。最大的一头身围二十英尺，从头到尾十码半，我们走近时，它们却纹丝不动。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极
英文证据: Two miles farther on we were stopped by the promontory which shelters the bay from the southerly winds. Beyond it we heard loud bellowings such as a troop of ruminants would produce.
原译: 离我们两英里远的地方被挡住了海湾远离南风的预兆。之后，我们听到一些响亮的鸣叫声，比如一群反贼会生产。
现译: 又走了两英里，挡住我们去路的是一座岬角。海湾所以不受南风侵袭，靠的便是它。岬角另一边传来震耳的吼声，像一群反刍的牲畜同时开了嗓。

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极
英文证据: We now began to climb the blackish rocks, amid unforeseen stumbles, and over stones which the ice made slippery. More than once I rolled over at the expense of my loins. Conseil, more prudent or more steady, did not stumble, and helped me up, saying:

现译: “先生若肯把步子迈得再宽些，平衡也就比较容易保住了。”
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极
英文证据: Arrived at the upper ridge of the promontory, I saw a vast white plain covered with morses. They were playing amongst themselves, and what we heard were bellowings of pleasure, not of anger.
原译: 到达口令山顶时我看到一片满是灰烬的白色平原。他们互相玩耍我们听到的是欢乐而不是愤怒。
现译: 登上岬角的高脊，我望见一大片白色平原，上面全是海象。它们确实在彼此嬉戏，我们听到的吼叫不是愤怒，而是欢喜。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极
英文证据: As I passed these curious animals I could examine them leisurely, for they did not move. Their skins were thick and rugged, of a yellowish tint, approaching to red; their hair was short and scant. Some of them were four yards and a quarter long. Quieter and less timid than their cousins of the north, they did not, like them, place sentinels round the outskirts of their encampment. After examining this city of morses, I began to think of returning. It was eleven o’clock, and, if Captain Nemo found the conditions favourable for observations, I wished to be present at the operation. We followed a narrow pathway running along the summit of the steep shore. At half-past eleven we had reached the place where we landed. The boat had run aground, bringing the Captain. I saw him standing on a block of basalt, his instruments near him, his eyes fixed on the northern horizon, near which the sun was then describing a lengthened curve. I took my place beside him, and waited without speaking. Noon arrived, and, as before, the sun did not appear. It was a fatality. Observations were still wanting. If not accomplished to-morrow, we must give up all idea of taking any. We were indeed exactly at the 20th of March. To-morrow, the 21st, would be the equinox; the sun would disappear behind the horizon for six months, and with its disappearance the long polar night would begin. Since the September equinox it had emerged from the northern horizon, rising by lengthened spirals up to the 21st of December. At this period, the summer solstice of the northern regions, it had begun to descend; and to-morrow was to shed its last rays upon them. I communicated my fears and observations to Captain Nemo.
原译: 当我通过这些好奇动物时我可以轻松地检查它们因为它们没有移动。他们的皮肤很厚，很粗糙，有黄色，接近红色；他们的头发短短，很少。其中一些是四码长四分之一长。他们比北方的表弟们更安静，更胆小，没有像他们一样，在营地外围安放哨兵。检查了这个城市的灰烬，我开始想着返回。11点了如果尼摩船长发现观察条件有利我想参加这次行动。我们沿着陡峭海岸的峰顶走着一条狭窄的道路。11点半我们到达了降落的地方。船已经搁浅了，把船长带来了。我看见他站在一块玄武石上，他身边的乐器，他的眼睛固定在北平线上，太阳在那附近，描述了一个长长的曲线。我在他身边占了位子等不及说话了。中午到了和以前一样太阳没出现。这是致命的。意见仍然不足。如果明天没有完成，我们就必须放弃任何选择的想法。我们确实在3月20日。明天，即21号，将是春分；太阳将在地平线后消失六个月，随着它的消失，漫长的极地之夜将开始。自9月的五分制以来，它从北方地平线上浮现出来，随着螺旋上升，一直持续到12月21日。在此期间，北部地区的夏令营开始下降；明天是向这些地区撒下最后的光线。我向尼摩船长传达了我的恐惧和观察。
现译: 这些有趣的动物一动不动，我从它们身旁经过，尽可以从容端详。皮厚而粗糙，黄中泛红，体毛短且稀疏。有些体长四又四分之一码。比起北方的亲戚来，这些海象更安静，也不那么胆怯。它们不像北方海象那样，要在营地外围布置岗哨。考察完这座海象城，我想该回去了。已是十一点，假如天气许可船长观测，我希望在场亲眼看一看。我们沿峭岸顶上的一条窄径往回走。十一点半，就到了先前登陆的地方。船长乘来的小艇已经冲上沙滩。我看见他站在一块玄武岩上，仪器就放在近旁，双眼盯着北方的地平线，太阳这时正贴着那一带划出一道长弧。我站到他身边，默默等待。正午到了，太阳仍像上回一样，不肯露面。真像有意跟我们过不去！我们还是缺少观测。明天再做不成，就得放弃一切观测的念头。因为今天恰好是三月二十日，明天二十一日，便是昼夜平分之日。太阳将沉在地平线后，一去六个月，与之同来的，是漫长的极夜。自从九月昼夜平分之日，太阳从北方地平线升起，沿着一圈又一圈细长的螺线往高处爬，一直升到十二月二十一日。那时正值北部地区的夏至，它便开始下降；明天，它将向这些地方洒下最后的光芒。我向尼摩船长讲了自己的观察与忧虑。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极
英文证据: “You are right, M. Aronnax,” said he; “if to-morrow I cannot take the altitude of the sun, I shall not be able to do it for six months. But precisely because chance has led me into these seas on the 21st of March, my bearings will be easy to take, if at twelve we can see the sun.”
原译: 他说：阿龙纳斯先生，你说得对。如果明天我不能升上太阳的高度，六个月内我就无法升上太阳。但正因为3月21日有机会把我带入海洋，所以如果在12时看到太阳，我的方位将很容易走动。
现译: “阿龙纳斯先生，您说得对，”他说，“假如明天不能测到太阳的高度，我就得等六个月才能再做这件事。不过，既然机缘恰在三月二十一日把我引到这片海上，那么只要十二点能看见太阳，测定船位其实会相当容易。”
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极
英文证据: “I shall only use my chronometer,” replied Captain Nemo. “If to-morrow, the 21st of March, the disc of the sun, allowing for refraction, is exactly cut by the northern horizon, it will show that I am at the South Pole.”

现译: “我只用航海精密时计，”尼摩船长答，“假如明天，三月二十一日，把折射的影响算进去，太阳圆面正好被北方地平线切为两半，那便表明我已身在南极点。”

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极
英文证据: “Just so,” said I. “But this statement is not mathematically correct, because the equinox does not necessarily begin at noon.”

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极
英文证据: Captain Nemo returned on board. Conseil and I remained to survey the shore, observing and studying until five o’clock. Then I went to bed, not, however, without invoking, like the Indian, the favour of the radiant orb. The next day, the 21st of March, at five in the morning, I mounted the platform. I found Captain Nemo there.
原译: 尼摩船长回到船上了。康塞尔和我一直到5点观察和研究海岸。然后，我上床睡觉了，不过，不是没有像印度人一样，援引光辉的球体的恩惠。第二天，3月21日，早上5点，我搭起平台。我发现尼摩船长在那里。
现译: 尼摩船长回到艇上。我和康塞尔留下来探勘海岸，一边观察，一边研究，直到五点。我这才上床，睡前也忘不了像印度人那样，祈求这轮光辉的太阳眷顾我们。次日，三月二十一日，清晨五点，我登上平台，看见尼摩船长已在那里。

中文章名: 下部 / 第14章　南极
英文证据: “The weather is lightening a little,” said he. “I have some hope. After breakfast we will go on shore and choose a post for observation.”

英文证据: I led him to the room where the crew of the _Nautilus_ were putting on their cork-jackets. I told the Captain of Ned’s proposal, which he accepted. The Canadian put on his sea-costume, and was ready as soon as his companions. When Ned was dressed, I re-entered the drawing-room, where the panes of glass were open, and, posted near Conseil, I examined the ambient beds that supported the _Nautilus_. Some instants after, we saw a dozen of the crew set foot on the bank of ice, and among them Ned Land, easily known by his stature. Captain Nemo was with them. Before proceeding to dig the walls, he took the soundings, to be sure of working in the right direction. Long sounding lines were sunk in the side walls, but after fifteen yards they were again stopped by the thick wall. It was useless to attack it on the ceiling-like surface, since the iceberg itself measured more than 400 yards in height. Captain Nemo then sounded the lower surface. There ten yards of wall separated us from the water, so great was the thickness of the ice-field. It was necessary, therefore, to cut from it a piece equal in extent to the waterline of the _Nautilus_. There were about 6,000 cubic yards to detach, so as to dig a hole by which we could descend to the ice-field. The work had begun immediately and carried on with indefatigable energy. Instead of digging round the _Nautilus_ which would have involved greater difficulty, Captain Nemo had an immense trench made at eight yards from the port-quarter. Then the men set to work simultaneously with their screws on several points of its circumference. Presently the pickaxe attacked this compact matter vigorously, and large blocks were detached from the mass. By a curious effect of specific gravity, these blocks, lighter than water, fled, so to speak, to the vault of the tunnel, that increased in thickness at the top in proportion as it diminished at the base. But that mattered little, so long as the lower part grew thinner. After two hours’ hard work, Ned Land came in exhausted. He and his comrades were replaced by new workers, whom Conseil and I joined. The second lieutenant of the _Nautilus_ superintended us. The water seemed singularly cold, but I soon got warm handling the pickaxe. My movements were free enough, although they were made under a pressure of thirty atmospheres. When I re-entered, after working two hours, to take some food and rest, I found a perceptible difference between the pure fluid with which the Rouquayrol engine supplied me and the atmosphere of the _Nautilus_, already charged with carbonic acid. The air had not been renewed for forty-eight hours, and its vivifying qualities were considerably enfeebled. However, after a lapse of twelve hours, we had only raised a block of ice one yard thick, on the marked surface, which was about 600 cubic yards! Reckoning that it took twelve hours to accomplish this much it would take five nights and four days to bring this enterprise to a satisfactory conclusion. Five nights and four days! And we have only air enough for two days in the reservoirs! “Without taking into account,” said Ned, “that, even if we get out of this infernal prison, we shall also be imprisoned under the iceberg, shut out from all possible communication with the atmosphere.” True enough! Who could then foresee the minimum of time necessary for our deliverance? We might be suffocated before the _Nautilus_ could regain the surface of the waves? Was it destined to perish in this ice-tomb, with all those it enclosed? The situation was terrible. But everyone had looked the danger in the face, and each was determined to do his duty to the last.
原译: 我把他带到了鹦鹉螺号号的船员穿衣衣的房间。我告诉了尼德的提议，他接受了。加拿大人穿上了船装准备就绪。尼德穿衣时，我重新进入了画室，玻璃板打开了，并在康塞尔附近张贴，我检查了支持鹦鹉螺的周围床位。不久之后，我们看到十几个船员踏上冰岸，其中有尼德·兰德，他的地位很容易知道。尼摩船长和他们在一起。在开始挖掘墙壁之前，他采取了声音，以确保工作方向正确。长长的测音线被沉入侧墙，但15码后，又被厚墙拦住。在像天花板的表面攻击它没用因为冰山本身的高度超过400码。尼摩船长然后听到低面的声音。10码长的墙把我们从水中隔开冰层的厚度是如此之大。因此，有必要从中削减一个与鹦鹉螺号河水系相等的片段。大约有6000立方码要拆开以便挖一个洞我们能从这个洞中掉到冰层上。这项工作立即开始，并以不屈不挠的能量继续进行。尼摩船长没有在鹦鹉螺号河周围挖洞，而是在离港口点8码处建造了一个巨大的战壕。然后男人们同时用他们的螺丝在它的周长的几个点上工作。目前，帕卡克斯强烈地攻击了这一紧凑物质，大块块与质量分离。这些比水还轻的区块以特定引力的奇特效应逃到隧道的保险箱里厚度随着底部的缩小而增大。但是，只要低端部分变薄，这没什么关系。经过两个小时的辛勤工作尼德·兰德精疲力尽了。他和他的战友被新工人取代了，我和康塞尔都加入了这些工人。鹦鹉螺号的第二副队长顶替了我们。水看起来有点冷但我很快就热到处理采摘器了。我的行动已经足够自由了虽然是在30个大气的压力下进行的。当我在工作了两个小时后再次进入那里吃东西休息时，我发现鲁夸罗尔发动机给我供应的纯液与已经充含碳酸的鹦鹉螺的大气之间有明显的差别。空气没有更新48小时，其生机勃勃的品质已大为充斥。然而，经过12个小时的磨损，我们只举起一块冰一个院子厚，在标记的表面，大约600立方码！据推测，要完成这些任务需要12小时，要完成这一任务需要5晚4天才能令人满意。五夜四天！水库里只有两天的空气！尼德说，“没有考虑到，即使我们走出这个地狱的监狱，我们也会被囚禁在冰山之下，与大气层之间无法进行任何交流。”说得没错！那么，谁能预见到我们交付援助所需的最短时间？等鹦鹉螺号重获海浪表面我们可能会窒息吗？它注定要死在这个冰堆里吗？情况很糟。但每个人都看清了危险，每个人都决心履行他的责任。
现译: 我领他走进更衣舱，“鹦鹉螺号”的船员们正在那里穿软木潜水服。我把尼德的提议告诉船长，他接受了。加拿大人套上海底装备，跟同伴们同时准备停当。见他穿戴好了，我就回了客厅。舷窗挡板已经拉开。我在康塞尔身边立定，隔着玻璃细看那些托住艇身、围住它的冰层。片刻后，只见十来名船员踏上冰床，尼德·兰德也在其中，他那个头一眼便认得出。尼摩船长也在。凿冰之前，他先要探测，好把力气用对方向。长长的探具扎进两侧冰墙，到十五码处却仍是坚冰，探不透。头顶天花板似的冰面不必考虑，因为那冰山自身就高出四百码有余。尼摩船长随即转向下方测探。那一面冰厚十码，凿穿这十码，下面才是开阔的水。于是得沿冰床凿开一个洞，开口的面积不能小于“鹦鹉螺号”的水线面。总共约须清除六千立方码的冰，我们才能打通冰原向下脱身。凿冰马上开始，大伙儿以不知疲倦的劲头做起来。绕艇一圈去挖会平添困难，尼摩船长便叫人到左舷后方八码远处开一条巨槽。人们沿槽的周线，同时在几处用螺旋冰钻下手。接着，鹤嘴镐有力地啄进严密的冰体，大块大块的冰被敲离。由于比重的奇妙作用，这些冰块轻过水，一脱离底部就像逃跑一般，直往隧道顶上窜。下面的冰薄了多少，上面的冰就相应厚了多少。只要底下在变薄，别的都不要紧。苦干两小时后，尼德·兰德精疲力竭地回来了。他和同伴换了班，康塞尔和我也加入下一批。带我们下去的是“鹦鹉螺号”的二副。水冷得异乎寻常，可挥起镐来，我身上很快就暖和了。虽说承受着三十个大气压，手脚倒还活动自如。我干了两个钟头回艇吃饭休息，立刻感到鲁凯罗尔呼吸器供应的清新空气，同“鹦鹉螺号”里已充满二氧化碳的空气有多大分别。舱里已经四十八小时没有换气，空气中能叫人振作的那份力量已经弱了许多。可是足足过了十二个钟头，我们只在划定的范围内削去一码厚的冰，也就是约六百立方码！照十二小时才做得出这些来算，要完成整项工程，足得四个白天、五个黑夜。五夜四天！而储气罐里的空气只够两天！“这还没算一件事，”尼德说，“就算钻出了这座要命的监牢，咱们还关在冰山底下，跟外头的大气照样不通。”一点不错！这样一来，谁能预料我们最少还得多久才可脱险？说不定“鹦鹉螺号”还没有重见水面，我们就已窒息而死。难道它命中注定，要载着它收藏在腹中的所有人，一道葬身在冰墓？处境十分可怕。但人人都已经正眼望过危险，人人都拿定了主意，要尽责到底。

英文证据: On this day for several hours I used my pickaxe vigorously. The work kept me up. Besides, to work was to quit the _Nautilus_, and breathe directly the pure air drawn from the reservoirs, and supplied by our apparatus, and to quit the impoverished and vitiated atmosphere. Towards evening the trench was dug one yard deeper. When I returned on board, I was nearly suffocated by the carbonic acid with which the air was filled—ah! if we had only the chemical means to drive away this deleterious gas. We had plenty of oxygen; all this water contained a considerable quantity, and by dissolving it with our powerful piles, it would restore the vivifying fluid. I had thought well over it; but of what good was that, since the carbonic acid produced by our respiration had invaded every part of the vessel? To absorb it, it was necessary to fill some jars with caustic potash, and to shake them incessantly. Now this substance was wanting on board, and nothing could replace it. On that evening, Captain Nemo ought to open the taps of his reservoirs, and let some pure air into the interior of the _Nautilus;_ without this precaution we could not get rid of the sense of suffocation. The next day, March 26th, I resumed my miner’s work in beginning the fifth yard. The side walls and the lower surface of the iceberg thickened visibly. It was evident that they would meet before the _Nautilus_ was able to disengage itself. Despair seized me for an instant; my pickaxe nearly fell from my hands. What was the good of digging if I must be suffocated, crushed by the water that was turning into stone?—a punishment that the ferocity of the savages even would not have invented! Just then Captain Nemo passed near me. I touched his hand and showed him the walls of our prison. The wall to port had advanced to at least four yards from the hull of the _Nautilus_. The Captain understood me, and signed me to follow him. We went on board. I took off my cork-jacket and accompanied him into the drawing-room.
原译: 今天我用了几小时用力用我的皮卡克斯。工作使我无法休息。此外，工作就是退出鹦鹉螺号，直接呼吸从水库抽出的纯空气，由我们的机器提供，并摆脱贫乏和虚弱的气氛。晚上，战壕被挖得更深。当我回到船上时，我几乎窒息于空气中的碳酸 -- -- 啊！如果我们只有化学手段来驱走这种有害的气体，我们有足够的氧气；所有这些水都含有相当数量的氧气，并且通过用我们强大的堆积物溶解，它将恢复活性液体。我已对此深思熟虑；但有什么好处呢，因为我们呼吸产生的碳酸侵入了船的每一个部分？为了吸收它，必须用腐蚀的药瓶充填一些罐子，并不停地摇动它们。现在，这种物质在船上是需要的，没有任何东西可以取代它。当晚，尼摩船长应该打开水库的水龙头，让一些纯净的空气进入鹦鹉螺的内部，没有这种预防措施，我们无法摆脱窒息感。我恢复了矿工在第五个院子的工作。 冰山的侧壁和下层表面明显变厚。 很明显，他们会在鹦鹉螺号人能够自行脱离之前相遇。 绝望瞬间抓住了我；我的手几乎掉下来了。 挖洞有什么好处呢？如果我必须窒息，被那变成石头的水压碎了？野蛮人甚至不会发明这种惩罚！尼摩船长刚刚走近我我摸了他的手给他看了监狱的墙壁。通往港口的墙已经推进到离鹦鹉螺号船体至少四码处。船长理解我，并签名我跟随他。我们上船了。我脱掉了衣物带他去画室。
现译: 那天，我使劲挥着鹤嘴镐，足足干了好几个钟头。活计撑住了我的精神。况且，出工就能离开“鹦鹉螺号”，离开艇中稀薄败坏的空气，用呼吸器直接吸取储气罐里的纯净空气。傍晚，冰槽又加深一码。我回到艇内，简直快给充塞在空气里的二氧化碳憋死了。啊！要是我们有化学办法驱走这种有害的气体该多好！氧气我们并不缺，四周这些水里就含着大量的氧。用强力电池分解海水，便能取回那维系生命的气体。我早已反复想过这个办法。可我们呼吸出来的二氧化碳已经侵入船上每一个角落，光这样做又有什么用？要吸收它，得用罐子盛上苛性钾，再不停摇晃。偏偏船上少的就是这种东西，又没有什么可以代替。当天晚上，尼摩船长应当打开储气罐的阀门，让些新鲜空气进入“鹦鹉螺号”。不采取这一步，我们就摆不脱窒息的感觉。次日三月二十六日，我又投入矿工般的活计，开始挖第五码。两侧冰墙和上方冰山的底面都在变厚，肉眼就能看见。显而易见，“鹦鹉螺号”还没脱身，它们就会合拢。有一刻，绝望攫住了我，鹤嘴镐差点从手里掉下去。等着我的若是憋死，是让硬得如石头的水活活压碎，再挖还有什么用？连最残酷的野蛮人也想不出这样的刑罚！就在这时，尼摩船长从我身旁经过。我碰碰他的手，指给他看监牢的墙。左舷那道墙已经逼到离艇壳不过四码处。船长明白了我的意思，打手势叫我跟他走。我们回到艇上。我脱下软木潜水服，同他一起进了客厅。

中文章名: 下部 / 第16章　缺少空气

中文章名: 下部 / 第16章　缺少空气
英文证据: By his orders the vessel was lightened, that is to say, raised from the ice-bed by a change of specific gravity. When it floated they towed it so as to bring it above the immense trench made on the level of the water-line. Then, filling his reservoirs of water, he descended and shut himself up in the hole.
原译: 根据他的命令船被点亮了也就是说由冰盖由特定引力的变化而起。当它漂浮的时候，他们拖着它，以便把它拖上水线上的巨大沟渠。然后，他填满了水库，下降并把自己关在洞里。

中文章名: 下部 / 第16章　缺少空气
英文证据: Just then all the crew came on board, and the double door of communication was shut. The _Nautilus_ then rested on the bed of ice, which was not one yard thick, and which the sounding leads had perforated in a thousand places. The taps of the reservoirs were then opened, and a hundred cubic yards of water was let in, increasing the weight of the _Nautilus_ to 1,800 tons. We waited, we listened, forgetting our sufferings in hope. Our safety depended on this last chance. Notwithstanding the buzzing in my head, I soon heard the humming sound under the hull of the _Nautilus_. The ice cracked with a singular noise, like tearing paper, and the _Nautilus_ sank.
原译: 就在那时，所有船员都上船了，双层通讯门被关闭了。鹦鹉螺号号然后躺在冰层上，冰层不是一院厚的，而且探测线索在一千个地方穿透了。水库的水龙头打开，100立方码的水被放入水中，鹦鹉螺号的重量增加到1 800吨。我们等待着，我们倾听着，怀着希望忘记了我们的痛苦。我们的安全取决于这最后的机会。尽管我脑子里有嗡嗡声我很快听到鹦鹉螺号船壳下的嗡嗡声。冰块破裂时有奇异的噪音比如撕碎纸鹦鹉螺沉了。
现译: 就在这时，船员全部归艇，用于进出的双层舱门合上。“鹦鹉螺号”如今压在冰床上，冰厚已不足一码，又被探锤在上千处打穿了小孔。压载水舱的阀门随即开启，放进一百立方码的水，把“鹦鹉螺号”的总重提高到一千八百吨。我们等待，倾听，怀着希望，把身上的苦都忘了。这是最后一次机会，人人的性命都悬在上面。尽管我脑子里嗡嗡响，过不多时，还是听见“鹦鹉螺号”的船底下传来一阵低鸣。冰面伴着异样的声音裂了，像是一张纸被撕开。“鹦鹉螺号”沉了下去。

中文章名: 下部 / 第16章　缺少空气
英文证据: I could not answer him. I seized his hand, and pressed it convulsively. All at once, carried away by its frightful overcharge, the _Nautilus_ sank like a bullet under the waters, that is to say, it fell as if it was in a vacuum. Then all the electric force was put on the pumps, that soon began to let the water out of the reservoirs. After some minutes, our fall was stopped. Soon, too, the manometer indicated an ascending movement. The screw, going at full speed, made the iron hull tremble to its very bolts and drew us towards the north. But if this floating under the iceberg is to last another day before we reach the open sea, I shall be dead first.
原译: 我无法回答他。我抓住了他的手，并按了它抽筋。纳乌特卢斯被它可怕的超载瞬间就消失了纳乌特卢斯像一颗子弹一样沉在水下也就是说，它倒在真空中。然后所有的电力都放在水泵上，很快开始让水从水库里流出来。几分钟后，我们的跌倒就停止了。很快，压力计也显示有上升趋势。螺丝以全速前进使铁壳颤抖到螺栓上把我们引向北方。但是如果冰山下漂浮的船还要在我们到达大海之前再漂一天我就先死了。

中文章名: 下部 / 第16章　缺少空气
英文证据: Half stretched upon a divan in the library, I was suffocating. My face was purple, my lips blue, my faculties suspended. I neither saw nor heard. All notion of time had gone from my mind. My muscles could not contract. I do not know how many hours passed thus, but I was conscious of the agony that was coming over me. I felt as if I was going to die. Suddenly I came to. Some breaths of air penetrated my lungs. Had we risen to the surface of the waves? Were we free of the iceberg? No! Ned and Conseil, my two brave friends, were sacrificing themselves to save me. Some particles of air still remained at the bottom of one apparatus. Instead of using it, they had kept it for me, and, while they were being suffocated, they gave me life, drop by drop. I wanted to push back the thing; they held my hands, and for some moments I breathed freely. I looked at the clock; it was eleven in the morning. It ought to be the 28th of March. The _Nautilus_ went at a frightful pace, forty miles an hour. It literally tore through the water. Where was Captain Nemo? Had he succumbed? Were his companions dead with him? At the moment the manometer indicated that we were not more than twenty feet from the surface. A mere plate of ice separated us from the atmosphere. Could we not break it? Perhaps. In any case the _Nautilus_ was going to attempt it. I felt that it was in an oblique position, lowering the stern, and raising the bows. The introduction of water had been the means of disturbing its equilibrium. Then, impelled by its powerful screw, it attacked the ice-field from beneath like a formidable battering-ram. It broke it by backing and then rushing forward against the field, which gradually gave way; and at last, dashing suddenly against it, shot forwards on the ice-field, that crushed beneath its weight. The panel was opened—one might say torn off—and the pure air came in in abundance to all parts of the _Nautilus_.
原译: 图书馆里有一半的床垫我快窒息了。我的脸是紫色的，我的嘴唇蓝色，我的功能悬浮。我既没看见也没听说。时间的概念都从我脑海中消失了。我的肌肉不能收缩。我不知道这样过了多少小时，但我意识到我的痛苦正在降临，我感觉好像我快要死了。突然间我就来了。呼吸一些空气进入我的肺。我们升到海浪表面了吗？我们没有冰山吗？不！不！不！不！No！我的两个勇敢的朋友尼德和康特为了救我牺牲了自己。一些空气颗粒仍留在一个装置的底部。他们没有使用它，而是为我保存，当他们窒息时，他们给了我生命，下降。我想把东西推回去，他们握住我的手，我有时可以自由呼吸。我看着时钟，是早上11点。应该是3月28日。鹦鹉螺队以惊人的速度前进时速40英里。它真的撕裂了整个水。尼摩船长在哪？他死了吗？他的同伴和他一起死了吗？目前，压力计显示，我们距离地面不到20英尺。冰块把我们与大气层隔开。我们能不打破它吗？也许吧。无论如何，鹦鹉螺会尝试。我觉得它处于斜坡位置降低船尾抬起船首。引进水是破坏其平衡的手段。然后，它被强大的螺丝所驱使，从下面攻击冰场，就像一个巨大的击打架。它通过背部打破它，然后冲向逐渐退让的田地；最终，它突然冲向它，向冰地前进，压在它的重量之下。面板被打开 -- -- 可以说是撕开的 -- -- 纯空气充斥在鹦鹉螺的所有地区。
现译: 我半躺在图书室的长沙发上，正在窒息。脸已发紫，嘴唇乌青，感官停止了作用。我拿眼看不见，拿耳听不到。脑中连时间的概念也消失了。肌肉不能收缩。我不知道这样过了多少小时，只觉死亡的痛苦正向我袭来。我想自己要死了。忽然，我苏醒过来，几口能呼吸的空气进了肺里。我们升到水面了？已经脱离冰山了？没有！是尼德和康塞尔，我的两位勇敢的朋友，正在舍己救我。一个呼吸器的底部还剩下一点气，他们自己一口没用，给我留了下来。当他们自己也正窒息的时候，他们一滴一滴把生命给了我。我想推开呼吸器，两人却握住我的双手。就这么过了一会儿，我得以自在呼吸。我看了钟。上午十一点。今天该是三月二十八日。“鹦鹉螺号”正以每小时四十英里的骇人速度前进，真像把水撕裂了。尼摩船长在哪里？难道他已经倒下？其他船员也都同他一道死了？此刻压力表显示，我们离海面不超过二十英尺。只剩一片冰板挡在我们和大气之间。能不能打破它？兴许可以。无论如何，“鹦鹉螺号”要试一试了。我觉出艇身倾斜，船尾向下，船首翘起。这是利用注入的水改变了艇的平衡。随后，在强劲的螺旋桨推动下，它像一具可怕的破城槌，从下方向冰原进攻。它先向后退，再猛冲向前，一次次撞上冰去。冰渐渐支持不住了。最后它发力一冲，艇身蹿上冰原，冰在它的重量下碎裂。舱盖打开——简直该说是被扯开——清新的空气滚滚而入，一直涌进“鹦鹉螺号”的每一个角落。
修改判断: 逐句对照英文，按叙述者与角色语气重译。

中文章名: 下部 / 第17章　从合恩角到亚马孙河

My two companions were getting drunk with the fresh particles. The other unhappy men had been so long without food, that they could not with impunity indulge in the simplest aliments that were given them. We, on the contrary, had no end to restrain ourselves; we could draw this air freely into our lungs, and it was the breeze, the breeze alone, that filled us with this keen enjoyment.

中文章名: 下部 / 第17章　从合恩角到亚马孙河
英文证据: The first words I spoke were words of gratitude and thankfulness to my two companions. Ned and Conseil had prolonged my life during the last hours of this long agony. All my gratitude could not repay such devotion.

中文章名: 下部 / 第17章　从合恩角到亚马孙河
